Illinois Learning Standards for Science

E22750F794854E20ACEA80C79EBF6D64.description: Evaluate claims derived from purported scientific studies used in advertising and marketing strategies.

8ECEDDE9882942F8AF98E6093C39DEFF.description: Analyze local examples of resource use, technology use or conservation programs; document findings; and make recommendations for improvements.

D41485F80CD6473289EFDEE135FD36DB.description: Analyze ways that resource management and technology can be used to accommodate population trends.

627F06E9B2A44B7C86801F0C5DC12D40.description: Analyze a particular occupation to identify decisions that may be influenced by a knowledge of science.

227E978F2AAA4A7382B61B7B712D6739.description: Compare and contrast scientific inquiry and technological design as pure and applied sciences.

2348812DBC7F433FB5C43908173ADDFE.description: Know and apply concepts that describe the interaction between science, technology and society.

779120954734458889A23634F336ACFA.description: Explain how peer review helps to assure the accurate use of data and improves the scientific process.

69BAABC883C44643AF3781FA6D4F46F1.description: Describe how scientific knowledge, explanations and technological designs may change with new information over time (e.g., the understanding of DNA, the design of computers).

0B1073737AFD4ED4820408BF2F2F0688.description: Assess the validity of scientific data by analyzing the results, sample set, sample size, similar previous experimentation, possible misrepresentation of data presented and potential sources of error.

326C46D4703A41379FF147773F580D5D.description: Estimate and suggest ways to reduce the degree of risk involved in science activities.

A7739C5642EF45979156B5F8316D6EC9.description: Know and apply the accepted practices of science.

F4977F1054124A5A812A8B82984FDE19.description: Understand the relationships among science, technology and society in historical and contemporary contexts.
comments: Understanding the nature and practices of science such as ensuring the validity and replicability of results, building upon the work of others and recognizing risks involved in experimentation gives learners a useful sense of the scientific enterprise. In addition, the relationships among science, technology and society give humans the ability to change and improve their surroundings. Learners who understand this relationship will be able to appreciate the efforts and effects of scientific discovery and applications of technology on their own lives and on the society in which we live.

1A9BC35CA08548D1B66A8097F481A5C0.description: Describe and compare the chemical and physical characteristics of galaxies and objects within galaxies (e.g., pulsars, nebulae, black holes, dark matter, stars).

B7A6ED0862B347E694E2D50979FBEB9E.description: Explain theories, past and present, for changes observed in the universe.

92421B5748D54F599D7DA4E91FC34714.description: Know and apply concepts that explain the composition and structure of the universe and Earth's place in it.

F26DE121B76748FFAACF803438743861.description: Describe how rock sequences and fossil remains are used to interpret the age and changes in the Earth.

06EC61BAF6C74E48964C0C3B40C6F261.description: Explain how external and internal energy sources drive Earth processes (e.g., solar energy drives weather patterns; internal heat drives plate tectonics).

C716B5B149A84D29B78AE81A900C2157.description: Know and apply concepts that describe the features and processes of the Earth and its resources.

5A03236D486C4105AEB7B38D2FDEECDD.description: Describe the effects of electromagnetic and nuclear forces including atomic and molecular bonding, capacitance and nuclear reactions.

CB7602D1CB31466981474BD8B43CE7C9.description: Explain and predict motions in inertial and accelerated frames of reference.

15769E1D86F941AE8DB339EAE1F1CCCB.description: Know and apply concepts that describe force and motion and the principles that explain them.

FCACF82E27BF4F119E4611AD6CD08FCC.description: Analyze and explain the atomic and nuclear structure of matter.

A589D92F2E0C40D6A54425EE55AD9295.description: Use kinetic theory, wave theory, quantum theory and the laws of thermodynamics to explain energy transformations.

70EDE6955EDE4C4381AB8BE812E7A4D4.description: Know and apply concepts that describe properties of matter and energy and the interactions between them.

A9A896757B4B4F9FBEE9348A55CC5828.description: Simulate and analyze factors that influence the size and stability of populations within ecosystems (e.g., birth rate, death rate, predation, migration patterns).

5F6055ECDA464B55B5743BD156311F0F.description: Compare physical, ecological and behavioral factors that influence interactions and interdependence of organisms.

8F672215514F4900A336E193F8E65801.description: Know and apply concepts that describe how living things interact with each other and with their environment.

935C752DC04E43BAAAC21314FAA69AC1.description: Describe processes by which organisms change over time using evidence from comparative anatomy and physiology, embryology, the fossil record, genetics and biochemistry.

E6CC40379FD0444F85639B63D727AF22.description: Describe the structures and organization of cells and tissues that underlie basic life functions including nutrition, respiration, cellular transport, biosynthesis and reproduction.

E1EC4E82634B42369FAC3B20C31EC50A.description: Explain how genetic combinations produce visible effects and variations among physical features and cellular functions of organisms.

8FC77D7EC85944AD83C5561AFC9247E8.description: Know and apply concepts that explain how living things function, adapt and change.

B1581B22A1CB478D9FD726AEA84C0F49.description: Understand the fundamental concepts, principles and interconnections of the life, physical and earth/space sciences.
comments: This goal is comprised of key concepts and principles in the life, physical and earth/space sciences that have considerable explanatory and predictive power for scientists and non-scientists alike. These ideas have been thoroughly studied and have stood the test of time. Knowing and being able to apply these concepts, principles and processes help students understand what they observe in nature and through scientific experimentation. A working knowledge of these concepts and principles allows students to relate new subject matter to material previously learned and to create deeper and more meaningful levels of understanding.

36C7D303E4AC44F8A8F3DA4BA9C9FE6D.description: Using available technology, report to an audience the relative success of the design based on the test results and criteria.

6F3FFE40BA384AA2B1D61CC4BCFA257A.description: Evaluate the test results based on established criteria, note sources of error and recommend improvements.

CD3F72E7CD9E445BA10E28841992A7BE.description: Develop and test a prototype or simulation of the solution design using available materials, instruments and technology.

3F6D66A16DDA47049C5A84518D100BAE.description: Determine the criteria upon which the designs will be judged, identify advantages and disadvantages of the designs and select the most promising design.

49EA8B65887249E5A28154725E1697A5.description: Develop working visualizations of the proposed solution designs (e.g., blueprints, schematics, flowcharts, cad-cam, animations).

471C2C5A6343459FBA8517A39564B723.description: Propose and compare different solution designs to the design problem based upon given constraints including available tools, materials and time.

58D542B6CEEE4913AE72775BFF4DA1FD.description: Identify a technological design problem inherent in a commonly used product.

858D00B9EF614A3EB3DF54BBE29714A1.description: Know and apply the concepts, principles and processes of technological design.

E62CECC1341D45B79A02524A38F8E409.description: Using available technology, report, display and defend to an audience conclusions drawn from investigations.

48A25271CFA64908B3981E286F80EA9F.description: Formulate alternative hypotheses to explain unexpected results.

503339CEF3C74BD4A72DD7D15287FA0A.description: Apply statistical methods to the data to reach and support conclusions.

AE7ADFBC31CF4E03880DA8D266CBA982.description: Collect, organize and analyze data accurately and precisely.

7FFA5BF8C3CE41328830F3582479AC42.description: Conduct controlled experiments or simulations to test hypotheses.

91ABA2632ABA43D78DA2FDDBF7C2594F.description: Formulate hypotheses referencing prior research and knowledge.

6972A61844DC4C8C9E4CCEB7F9B97BEA.description: Know and apply the concepts, principles and processes of scientific inquiry.

E3920A276211493D83F0DC8FC21CCFF1.description: Understand the processes of scientific inquiry and technological design to investigate questions, conduct experiments and solve problems.
comments: The inquiry process prepares learners to engage in science and apply methods of technological design. This understanding will enable students to pose questions, use models to enhance understanding, make predictions, gather and work with data, use appropriate measurement methods, analyze results, draw conclusions based on evidence, communicate their methods and results, and think about the implications of scientific research and technological problem solving.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for English Language Arts

9E257470DFE501317AA568A86D17958E.description: Use print, nonprint, human and technological resources to acquire and use information.

9E25BAE0DFE501317AA668A86D17958E.description: Write letters, reports and stories based on acquired information.

9E252540DFE501317AA468A86D17958E.description: Apply acquired information, concepts and ideas to communicate in a variety of formats.

9E24D260DFE501317AA368A86D17958E.description: Select and organize information from various sources for a specific purpose.

9E243C70DFE501317AA168A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate information acquired from various sources.

9E239470DFE501317A9F68A86D17958E.description: Locate information using a variety of resources.

9E234A90DFE501317A9E68A86D17958E.description: Locate, organize, and use information from various sources to answer questions, solve problems and communicate ideas.

comments: To be successful in school and in the world of work, students must be able to use a wide variety of information resources (written, visual and electronic). They must also know how to frame questions for inquiry, identify and organize relevant information and communicate it effectively in a variety of formats. These skills are critical in school across all learning areas and are key to successful career and lifelong learning experiences.
9E22F900DFE501317A9D68A86D17958E.description: Use the language arts to acquire, assess and communicate information.

9E2688E0DFE501317AA968A86D17958E.description: Participate in discussions around a common topic.

9E26D560DFE501317AAA68A86D17958E.description: Present brief oral reports, using language and vocabulary appropriate to the message and audience (e.g., show and tell).

9E264690DFE501317AA868A86D17958E.description: Speak effectively using language appropriate to the situation and audience.

9E27C570DFE501317AAD68A86D17958E.description: Use visually oriented and auditorily based media.

9E277A30DFE501317AAC68A86D17958E.description: Ask questions and respond to questions from the teacher and from group members to improve comprehension.

9E280930DFE501317AAE68A86D17958E.description: Listen attentively by facing the speaker, making eye contact and paraphrasing what is said.

9E272F90DFE501317AAB68A86D17958E.description: Listen effectively in formal and informal situations.

9E25FF90DFE501317AA768A86D17958E.description: Listen and speak effectively in a variety of situations.
comments: Of all the language arts, listening and speaking are those most often used on a daily basis at home, school and work or in the community. Skill in speaking is universally recognized as a primary indicator of a person's knowledge, skill and credibility. In person, by phone or through video, good listening and speaking skills are essential to sending, receiving and understanding messages. To understand messages spoken by others, students must be able to listen carefully, using specific techniques to clarify what they have heard. For speaking properly and making messages understood, grammar, sentence structure, tone, expression and emphasis must be part of students' repertoires.

9E1AE390DFE501317A8068A86D17958E.description: Create media compositions or productions which convey meaning visually for a variety of purposes.

9E1B3410DFE501317A8168A86D17958E.description: Write for a variety of purposes including description, information, explanation, persuasion and narration.

9E1A8F30DFE501317A7F68A86D17958E.description: Communicate ideas in writing to accomplish a variety of purposes.

9E19F190DFE501317A7D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate focus, organization, elaboration and integration in written compositions (e.g., short stories, letters, essays, reports).

9E1A3FB0DFE501317A7E68A86D17958E.description: Use prewriting strategies to generate and organize ideas (e.g., focus on one topic; organize writing to include a beginning, middle and end; use descriptive words when writing about people, places, things, events).

9E199B10DFE501317A7C68A86D17958E.description: Compose well-organized and coherent writing for specific purposes and audiences.

9E1BB530DFE501317A8368A86D17958E.description: Construct complete sentences which demonstrate subject/verb agreement; appropriate capitalization and punctuation; correct spelling of appropriate, high-frequency words; and appropriate use of the eight parts of speech.

9E1B7630DFE501317A8268A86D17958E.description: Use correct grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization and structure.

9E193D90DFE501317A7B68A86D17958E.description: Write to communicate for a variety of purposes.
comments: The ability to write clearly is essential to any person's effective communications. Students with high-level writing skills can produce documents that show planning and organization and effectively convey the intended message and meaning. Clear writing is critical to employment and production in today's world. Individuals must be capable of writing for a variety of audiences in differing styles, including standard rhetoric themes, business letters and reports, financial proposals and technical and professional communications. Students should be able to use word processors and computers to enhance their writing proficiency and improve their career opportunities.

9E1DC1B0DFE501317A8B68A86D17958E.description: Relate character, setting and plot to real-life situations.

9E1D8380DFE501317A8A68A86D17958E.description: Identify common themes in literature from a variety of eras.

9E1E00E0DFE501317A8C68A86D17958E.description: Respond to literary materials by connecting them to their own experience and communicate those responses to others.

9E1D4580DFE501317A8968A86D17958E.description: Read and interpret a variety of literary works.

9E1C6F30DFE501317A8668A86D17958E.description: Describe differences between prose and poetry.

9E1CBD60DFE501317A8768A86D17958E.description: Classify literary works as fiction or nonfiction.

9E1D05F0DFE501317A8868A86D17958E.description: Identify the literary elements of theme, setting, plot and character within literary works.

9E1C3300DFE501317A8568A86D17958E.description: Understand how literary elements and techniques are used to convey meaning.

9E1BF340DFE501317A8468A86D17958E.description: Read and understand literature representative of various societies, eras and ideas.
comments: Literature transmits ideas, reflects societies and eras and expresses the human imagination. It brings understanding, enrichment and joy. Appreciating literature and recognizing its many forms enable students to learn and respond to ideas, issues, perspectives and actions of others. Literature study includes understanding the structure and intent of a short poem or a long, complex book. By exploring the techniques that authors use to convey messages and evoke responses, students connect literature to their own lives and daily experiences.

9E1F53B0DFE501317A9068A86D17958E.description: Use information presented in simple tables, maps and charts to form an interpretation.

9E1F01C0DFE501317A8F68A86D17958E.description: Identify how authors and illustrators express their ideas in text and graphics (e.g., dialogue, conflict, shape, color, characters).

9E208FB0DFE501317A9468A86D17958E.description: Summarize content of reading material using text organization (e.g., story, sequence).

9E204BC0DFE501317A9368A86D17958E.description: Use information to form questions and verify predictions.

9E1EBA90DFE501317A8E68A86D17958E.description: Comprehend a broad range of reading materials.

9E219BE0DFE501317A9868A86D17958E.description: Read age-appropriate material aloud with fluency and accuracy.

9E2151A0DFE501317A9768A86D17958E.description: Continuously check and clarify for understanding (e.g., reread, read ahead, use visual and context clues, ask questions, retell, use meaningful substitutions).

9E211000DFE501317A9668A86D17958E.description: Identify genres (forms and purposes) of fiction, nonfiction, poetry and electronic literary forms.

9E21E590DFE501317A9968A86D17958E.description: Establish purposes for reading, make predictions, connect important ideas, and link text to previous experiences and knowledge.

9E20CFA0DFE501317A9568A86D17958E.description: Apply reading strategies to improve understanding and fluency.

9E22B2A0DFE501317A9C68A86D17958E.description: Comprehend unfamiliar words using context clues and prior knowledge; verify meanings with resource materials.

9E226F50DFE501317A9B68A86D17958E.description: Apply word analysis skills (e.g., phonics, word patterns) to recognize new words.

9E222C20DFE501317A9A68A86D17958E.description: Apply word analysis and vocabulary skills to comprehend selections.

comments: Reading is essential. It is the process by which people gain information and ideas from books, newspapers, manuals, letters, contracts, advertisements and a host of other materials. Using strategies for constructing meaning before, during and after reading will help students connect what they read now with what they have learned in the past. Students who read well and widely build a strong foundation for learning in all areas of life.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for English Language Arts

9E5A7E60DFE501317B1368A86D17958E.description: Take notes, conduct interviews, organize and report information in oral, visual and electronic formats.

9E5B1410DFE501317B1568A86D17958E.description: Prepare and orally present original work (e.g., poems, monologues, reports, plays, stories) supported by research.

9E5ACED0DFE501317B1468A86D17958E.description: Plan, compose, edit and revise documents that synthesize new meaining gleaned from multiple sources.

9E5A3290DFE501317B1268A86D17958E.description: Apply acquired information, concepts and ideas to communicate in a variety of formats.

9E59E270DFE501317B1168A86D17958E.description: Identify, evaluate and cite primary sources.

9E599340DFE501317B1068A86D17958E.description: Choose and analyze information sources for individual, academic and functional purposes.

9E593EA0DFE501317B0F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate information acquired from various sources.

9E58E6D0DFE501317B0E68A86D17958E.description: Design a project related to contemporary issues (e.g., real-world math, career development, community service) using multiple sources.

9E586E60DFE501317B0D68A86D17958E.description: Identify appropriate resources to solve problems or answer questions through research.

9E582100DFE501317B0C68A86D17958E.description: Locate, organize, and use information from various sources to answer questions, solve problems and communicate ideas.

9E57D290DFE501317B0B68A86D17958E.description: Use the language arts to acquire, assess and communicate information.
comments: To be successful in school and in the world of work, students must be able to use a wide variety of information resources (written, visual and electronic). They must also know how to frame questions for inquiry, identify and organize relevant information and communicate it effectively in a variety of formats. These skills are critical in school across all learning areas and are key to successful career and lifelong learning experiences.

9E5BE7B0DFE501317B1868A86D17958E.description: Use verbal and nonverbal communication strategies to maintain communications and to resolve conflict.

9E5CA640DFE501317B1B68A86D17958E.description: Develop strategies to manage or overcome communication anxiety and apprehension (e.g., sentence outlining, note cards).

9E5C6820DFE501317B1A68A86D17958E.description: Design and produce reports and multimedia compositions that represent group projects.

9E5C27F0DFE501317B1968A86D17958E.description: Deliver planned oral presentations using language and vocabulary appropriate to the purpose, message and audience; provide details and supporting information that clarify main ideas; and use visual aids and contemporary technology as support.

9E5BA670DFE501317B1768A86D17958E.description: Speak effectively using language appropriate to the situation and audience.

9E5DB080DFE501317B1F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to identify and manage barriers to listening (e.g., noise, speaker credibility, environmental distractions).

9E5DEE00DFE501317B2068A86D17958E.description: Restate and carry out multistep oral instructions.

9E5D2E80DFE501317B1D68A86D17958E.description: Compare a speaker's verbal and nonverbal messages.

9E5D7060DFE501317B1E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ways (e.g., ask probing questions, provide feedback to a speaker, summarize and paraphrase complex spoken messages) that listening attentively can improve comprehension.

9E5CE4C0DFE501317B1C68A86D17958E.description: Listen effectively in formal and informal situations.

9E5B6040DFE501317B1668A86D17958E.description: Listen and speak effectively in a variety of situations.
comments: Of all the language arts, listening and speaking are those most often used on a daily basis at home, school and work or in the community. Skill in speaking is universally recognized as a primary indicator of a person's knowledge, skill and credibility. In person, by phone or through video, good listening and speaking skills are essential to sending, receiving and understanding messages. To understand messages spoken by others, students must be able to listen carefully, using specific techniques to clarify what they have heard. For speaking properly and making messages understood, grammar, sentence structure, tone, expression and emphasis must be part of students' repertoires.

9E4F1200DFE501317AED68A86D17958E.description: Using available technology, produce compositions and multimedia works for specified audiences.

9E4F5340DFE501317AEE68A86D17958E.description: Compose narrative, informative, and persuasive writings (e.g., in addition to previous writings, literature reviews, instructions, news articles, correspondence) for a specified audience.

9E4ED180DFE501317AEC68A86D17958E.description: Communicate ideas in writing to accomplish a variety of purposes.

9E4E9020DFE501317AEB68A86D17958E.description: Edit and revise for word choice, organization, consistent point of view and transitions among paragraphs using contemporary technology and formats suitable for submission and/or publication.

9E4E4EE0DFE501317AEA68A86D17958E.description: Produce documents that convey a clear understanding and interpretation of ideas and information and display focus, organization, elaboration and coherence.

9E4E0AC0DFE501317AE968A86D17958E.description: Compose well-organized and coherent writing for specific purposes and audiences.

9E4FF8B0DFE501317AF068A86D17958E.description: Write compositions that contain complete sentences and effective paragraphs using English conventions.

9E4FAD90DFE501317AEF68A86D17958E.description: Use correct grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization and structure.

9E4DBC40DFE501317AE868A86D17958E.description: Write to communicate for a variety of purposes.
comments: The ability to write clearly is essential to any person's effective communications. Students with high-level writing skills can produce documents that show planning and organization and effectively convey the intended message and meaning. Clear writing is critical to employment and production in today's world. Individuals must be capable of writing for a variety of audiences in differing styles, including standard rhetoric themes, business letters and reports, financial proposals and technical and professional communications. Students should be able to use word processors and computers to enhance their writing proficiency and improve their career opportunities.

9E522EC0DFE501317AF868A86D17958E.description: Analyze how characters in literature deal with conflict, solve problems and relate to real-life situations.

9E52C070DFE501317AFA68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast common literary themes across various societies and eras.

9E527200DFE501317AF968A86D17958E.description: Respond to literary material from personal, creative and critical points of view.

9E51EA80DFE501317AF768A86D17958E.description: Read and interpret a variety of literary works.

9E50C7D0DFE501317AF368A86D17958E.description: Identify ways that an author uses language structure, word choice and style to convey the author's viewpoint.

9E51A510DFE501317AF668A86D17958E.description: Identify characteristics and authors of various literary forms (e.g., short stories, novels, drama, fables, biographies, documentaries, poetry, science fiction).

9E5119F0DFE501317AF468A86D17958E.description: Describe how the development of theme, character, plot and setting contribute to the overall impact of a piece of literature.

9E516100DFE501317AF568A86D17958E.description: Identify and analyze a variety of literary techniques (e.g., figurative language, allusion, dialogue, description, word choice, dialect) within classical and contemporary works representing a variety of genres.

9E5082C0DFE501317AF268A86D17958E.description: Understand how literary elements and techniques are used to convey meaning.

9E503C00DFE501317AF168A86D17958E.description: Read and understand literature representative of various societies, eras and ideas.
comments: Literature transmits ideas, reflects societies and eras and expresses the human imagination. It brings understanding, enrichment and joy. Appreciating literature and recognizing its many forms enable students to learn and respond to ideas, issues, perspectives and actions of others. Literature study includes understanding the structure and intent of a short poem or a long, complex book. By exploring the techniques that authors use to convey messages and evoke responses, students connect literature to their own lives and daily experiences.

9E54B5A0DFE501317B0068A86D17958E.description: Interpret tables that display textual information and data in visual formats.

9E546480DFE501317AFF68A86D17958E.description: Compare how authors and illustrators use text and art across materials to express their ideas (e.g., foreshadowing, flashbacks, color, strong verbs, language that inspires).

9E555480DFE501317B0268A86D17958E.description: Summarize and make generalizations from content and relate them to the purpose of the material.

9E541DC0DFE501317AFE68A86D17958E.description: Compare, contrast and evaluate ideas and information from various sources and genres.

9E53D7A0DFE501317AFD68A86D17958E.description: Interpret and analyze entire narrative text using story elements, point of view and theme.

9E5507C0DFE501317B0168A86D17958E.description: Use information to form, explain and support questions and predictions.

9E5394A0DFE501317AFC68A86D17958E.description: Comprehend a broad range of reading materials.

9E55E870DFE501317B0468A86D17958E.description: Read age-appropriate material with fluency and accuracy.

9E567C10DFE501317B0668A86D17958E.description: Continuously check and clarify for understanding (e.g., in addition to previous skills, draw comparisons to other readings).

9E5635E0DFE501317B0568A86D17958E.description: Identify text structure and create a visual representation (e.g., graphic organizer, outline, drawing) to use while reading.

9E56C030DFE501317B0768A86D17958E.description: Preview reading materials, make predictions and relate reading to information from other sources.

9E55A1E0DFE501317B0368A86D17958E.description: Apply reading strategies to improve understanding and fluency.

9E578820DFE501317B0A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the meaning of words and phrases in their context.

9E5745F0DFE501317B0968A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of word origins and derivations to comprehend words used in specific content areas (e.g., scientific, political, literary, mathematical).

9E5702F0DFE501317B0868A86D17958E.description: Apply word analysis and vocabulary skills to comprehend selections.

comments: Reading is essential. It is the process by which people gain information and ideas from books, newspapers, manuals, letters, contracts, advertisements and a host of other materials. Using strategies for constructing meaning before, during and after reading will help students connect what they read now with what they have learned in the past. Students who read well and widely build a strong foundation for learning in all areas of life.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Science

5A29A4A5C73C4E10BF9A237E69287B21.description: Analyze how specific personal and societal choices that humans make affect local, regional and global ecosystems (e.g., lawn and garden care, mass transit).

CD49EF94894E4934835C93EE82F9270D.description: Identify and explain ways that technology changes ecosystems (e.g., dams, highways, buildings, communication networks, power plants).

69C4CEA334604304B4434E64B2D73E96.description: Compare the relative effectiveness of reducing, reusing and recycling in actual situations.

69B0A7347AEB46A7AD067CC770B9597C.description: Identify and explain ways that science and technology influence the lives and careers of people.

9871C00685524F8E835FEC119436BFC0.description: Describe the effects on society of scientific and technological innovations (e.g., antibiotics, steam engine, digital computer).

58FCBA1DE8A043FFBD6CA7D0390EDDBB.description: Explain how technology is used in science for a variety of purposes (e.g., sample collection, storage and treatment; measurement; data collection, storage and retrieval; communication of information).

5BE3589E46CE40E5BAFC1470197FC7F5.description: Know and apply concepts that describe the interaction between science, technology and society.

73E6F240502E4D078BA84877C590A8B2.description: Explain why keeping accurate and detailed records is important.

27ED7148206A4521B3AAE8CABAA26D74.description: Explain why similar investigations may not produce similar results.

82DED94726A04DF9AED2860D672A891C.description: Demonstrate ways to avoid injury when conducting science activities (e.g., wearing goggles, fire extinguisher use).

F514333BD8DA4AE2B5ABEEAEC44C1ED5.description: Know and apply the accepted practices of science.

45B69C811D03454DAAB77EE86F6825A9.description: Understand the relationships among science, technology and society in historical and contemporary contexts.
comments: Understanding the nature and practices of science such as ensuring the validity and replicability of results, building upon the work of others and recognizing risks involved in experimentation gives learners a useful sense of the scientific enterprise. In addition, the relationships among science, technology and society give humans the ability to change and improve their surroundings. Learners who understand this relationship will be able to appreciate the efforts and effects of scientific discovery and applications of technology on their own lives and on the society in which we live.

7219BE7A1340496DB7B83E28799AFE4D.description: Identify easily recognizable star patterns (e.g., the Big Dipper, constellations).

3C06AD18E6B34139BA638F3536C8AF4C.description: Explain the apparent motion of the sun and stars.

1CC175B3977A4712AB063E7D1F6CA755.description: Identify and explain natural cycles and patterns in the solar system (e.g., order of the planets; moon phases; seasons as related to Earth's tilt, one's latitude, and where Earth is in its yearly orbit around the sun).

D9AA8CB51D8648699F36FF814B147C9C.description: Know and apply concepts that explain the composition and structure of the universe and Earth's place in it.

F602505AC32448E88C12182A4105A094.description: Describe and explain short-term and long-term interactions of the Earth's components (e.g., earthquakes, types of erosion).

E321BDA2D76842229538A6588D38EA2B.description: Identify and explain natural cycles of the Earth's land, water and atmospheric systems (e.g., rock cycle, water cycle, weather patterns).

2B7461B5006B4910BF41D08A682822BA.description: Know and apply concepts that describe the features and processes of the Earth and its resources.

EA7A31988E41486FA0A0D11E56DD320A.description: Demonstrate and explain ways that forces cause actions and reactions (e.g., magnets attracting and repelling; objects falling, rolling and bouncing).

FAA7AA9783654EBE9DF1C9B56932E176.description: Explain constant, variable and periodic motions.

5281189BF0DE448294A9AD4BA029EF7B.description: Know and apply concepts that describe force and motion and the principles that explain them.

C4D4DB5B3C5D4EA3823ECCAC2FA6B635.description: Describe and explain the properties of solids, liquids and gases.

D6023BF00C9A4165837EE89540793382.description: Describe and compare types of energy including light, heat, sound, electrical and mechanical.

2C7650792221412F8E4339F4C0DE2F93.description: Know and apply concepts that describe properties of matter and energy and the interactions between them.

233E246F0233401B91FF3585ACEEA494.description: Identify physical features of plants and animals that help them live in different environments (e.g., specialized teeth for eating certain foods, thorns for protection, insulation for cold temperature).

5F9B61E9EEB74849A8298AFA09A2F3D7.description: Describe relationships among various organisms in their environments (e.g., predator/prey, parasite/host, food chains and food webs).

E2F246AA14FC4F7ABB31CC66823D3092.description: Know and apply concepts that describe how living things interact with each other and with their environment.

ADD7E1C2A3CA4FB98DCD08C0F421FAF7.description: Categorize features as either inherited or learned (e.g., flower color or eye color is inherited; language is learned).

A2DF27291D7746A8A3EDC2B64202DF46.description: Describe simple life cycles of plants and animals and the similarities and differences in their offspring.

8446979765CB499289BBCDE37BE777A9.description: Know and apply concepts that explain how living things function, adapt and change.

6811B26449624813A5AC3B97CDA93E59.description: Understand the fundamental concepts, principles and interconnections of the life, physical and earth/space sciences.
comments: This goal is comprised of key concepts and principles in the life, physical and earth/space sciences that have considerable explanatory and predictive power for scientists and non-scientists alike. These ideas have been thoroughly studied and have stood the test of time. Knowing and being able to apply these concepts, principles and processes help students understand what they observe in nature and through scientific experimentation. A working knowledge of these concepts and principles allows students to relate new subject matter to material previously learned and to create deeper and more meaningful levels of understanding.

6249461173594F20B269ACFF1EC17A1A.description: Report test design, test process and test results.

B8680E87E09D4C4F8E9191070681FD84.description: Assess test results and the effectiveness of the design using given criteria and noting possible sources of error.

58C512CE1C0947E196A4180492F5B7A9.description: Test the prototype using suitable instruments, techniques and quantitative measurements to record data.

7F64F9E69FB64D708E4438A99C52C238.description: Build a prototype of the design using available tools and materials.

66D1FF4890ED4F508EAFB1D98D6CF27E.description: Develop a plan, design and procedure to address the problem identifying constraints (e.g., time, materials, technology).

FFD6939F95CD4B2398DB7F5448F4EC65.description: Identify a design problem and propose possible solutions.

2C9C18F5A5364D6B9E770E356F6F6AA9.description: Know and apply the concepts, principles and processes of technological design.

2004A3AA96974D5D87954CC693EF07D6.description: Report and display the results of individual and group investigations.

B4CFFB2CFBEA4E81A80041AFC3E57014.description: Use data to produce reasonable explanations.

B59CE6B7E5624AC28AD170A41066B8B4.description: Construct charts and visualizations to display data.

068B1A2FA0D8496A8D274F5A35BDC9DA.description: Collect data for investigations using scientific process skills including observing, estimating and measuring.

4284D81BEAF649668857573777B3CF4D.description: Formulate questions on a specific science topic and choose the steps needed to answer the questions.

0574330BBC9D420E9590DE077B45EAF7.description: Know and apply the concepts, principles and processes of scientific inquiry.

8FCCB625D9FD4D74960A92155B908D69.description: Understand the processes of scientific inquiry and technological design to investigate questions, conduct experiments and solve problems.
comments: The inquiry process prepares learners to engage in science and apply methods of technological design. This understanding will enable students to pose questions, use models to enhance understanding, make predictions, gather and work with data, use appropriate measurement methods, analyze results, draw conclusions based on evidence, communicate their methods and results, and think about the implications of scientific research and technological problem solving.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Mathematics

9D9D9FB0DFE50131799C68A86D17958E.description: Systematically list all possible outcomes of a simple one-stage experiment (e.g., the flip of one coin, the toss of one die, the spin of a spinner).

9D9D4EF0DFE50131799B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the concept of probability in relationship to likelihood and chance.

9D9D0880DFE50131799A68A86D17958E.description: Determine, describe and apply the probabilities of events.

9D9CC610DFE50131799968A86D17958E.description: Analyze data, draw conclusions and communicate the results.

9D9C07D0DFE50131799768A86D17958E.description: Collect, organize and describe data using pictures, tallies, tables, charts or bar graphs.

9D9C77D0DFE50131799868A86D17958E.description: Formulate questions of interest and design surveys or experiments to gather data.

9D9BB360DFE50131799668A86D17958E.description: Formulate questions, design data collection methods, gather and analyze data and communicate findings.

9D9B3200DFE50131799468A86D17958E.description: Answer questions and make predictions based on given data.

9D9B72E0DFE50131799568A86D17958E.description: Organize and display data using pictures, tallies, tables, charts or bar graphs.

9D9AEE90DFE50131799368A86D17958E.description: Organize, describe and make predictions from existing data.

9D9A9F00DFE50131799268A86D17958E.description: Collect, organize and analyze data using statistical methods; predict results; and interpret uncertainty using concepts of probability.
comments: The ability to understand and interpret data (e.g., opinion polls, stock prices, tax rates, crime statistics, scientific studies, weather reports) grows more important each day. Students must be able to organize data, make sense of variables and patterns, and judge the logical reasonableness of any claims and interpretations made. Even very young students can count objects and communicate their findings with charts and graphs. Students of all ages can collect, display and interpret data to answer specific questions. They also must construct and analyze arguments that involve data and its interpretation. All students need to understand and apply the role probability plays in data collection and decision making. Data analysis and use are important abilities necessary for all careers.

9DA43B90DFE50131799F68A86D17958E.description: Draw logical conclusions and communicate reasoning about simple geometric figures and patterns using concrete materials, diagrams and contemporary technology.

9DA3F2C0DFE50131799E68A86D17958E.description: Construct convincing arguments and proofs to solve problems.

9DA559F0DFE5013179A368A86D17958E.description: Identify lines of symmetry in simple figures and construct symmetrical figures using various concrete materials.

9DA51100DFE5013179A268A86D17958E.description: Sort, classify and compare familiar shapes.

9DA4C560DFE5013179A168A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe characteristics, similarities and differences of geometric shapes.

9DA48070DFE5013179A068A86D17958E.description: Identify, describe, classify and compare relationships using points, lines, planes and solids.

9DA5FF40DFE5013179A568A86D17958E.description: Identify related two- and three-dimensional shapes including circle-sphere, square-cube, triangle-pyramid, rectangle-rectangular prism and their basic properties.

9DA5B5D0DFE5013179A468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and apply geometric concepts involving points, lines, planes and space.

comments: Geometry provides important methods for reasoning and solving problems with points, lines, planes and space. The word "geometry" comes from Greek words meaning "measurement of the Earth." While we use modern technology and employ a wider variety of mathematical tools today, we still study geometry to understand the shapes and dimensions of our world. The applications of geometry are widespread in construction, engineering, architecture, mapmaking and art. Historically, geometry is a way to develop skill in forming convincing arguments and proofs. This goal of developing a means of argument and validation remains an important part of our reasons for studying geometry today.
9D9DEB80DFE50131799D68A86D17958E.description: Use geometric methods to analyze, categorize and draw conclusions about points, lines, planes and space.

9D9307B0DFE50131797768A86D17958E.description: Find the unknown numbers in whole-number addition, subtraction, multiplication and division situations.

9D92BB50DFE50131797668A86D17958E.description: Use algebraic concepts and procedures to represent and solve problems.

9D942230DFE50131797B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the basic arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) orally, in writing and using concrete materials and drawings.

9D93E1F0DFE50131797A68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using systems of numbers and their properties.

9D93A1B0DFE50131797968A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving pattern identification and completion of patterns.

9D935B60DFE50131797868A86D17958E.description: Interpret and describe numerical relationships using tables, graphs and symbols.

9D9273D0DFE50131797568A86D17958E.description: Identify, describe and extend simple geometric and numeric patterns.

9D91E220DFE50131797368A86D17958E.description: Describe numerical relationships using variables and patterns.

9D918520DFE50131797268A86D17958E.description: Use algebraic and analytical methods to identify and describe patterns and relationships in data, solve problems and predict results.
comments: Algebra unites patterns and quantities in patterns with the means of describing change through the use of variables and functions. Its concepts and analytical methods allow people to consider general solutions to problems with common characteristics and develop related formulas. Algebra provides verbal, symbolic and graphical formats for discussing and representing settings as diverse as the pricing patterns of merchandise in a store, the behavior of a car as it accelerates or slows down, the changes in two chemicals as they react with one another, or the type of variation existing in a comparison of two factors in the economy. All people must be able to use algebraic methods to construct and examine tables of values; to interpret the relationships expressed by patterns in these tables; to relate change and variation in graphs and formulas; to reason about changes in quantities and the relationships involved in changes; and to find solutions to everyday problems using algebra's symbolic manipulation and formulas.

9D980D30DFE50131798968A86D17958E.description: Determine perimeter and area using concrete materials (e.g., geoboards, square tiles, grids, measurement instruments).

9D97CB10DFE50131798868A86D17958E.description: Select and use appropriate technology, instruments and formulas to solve problems, interpret results and communicate findings.

9D9A1190DFE50131799068A86D17958E.description: Compare estimated measures to actual measures taken with appropriate measuring instruments.

9D9A5270DFE50131799168A86D17958E.description: Given a problem, describe possible methods for estimating a given measure.

9D99CF30DFE50131798F68A86D17958E.description: Estimate measurements and determine acceptable levels of accuracy.

9D998C80DFE50131798E68A86D17958E.description: Read temperatures to the nearest degree from Celsius and Fahrenheit thermometers.

9D990320DFE50131798C68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the relative values and relationships among coins and solve addition and subtraction problems using currency.

9D994950DFE50131798D68A86D17958E.description: Measure units of time using appropriate instruments (e.g., calendars, clocks, watches--both analog and digital).

9D98B110DFE50131798B68A86D17958E.description: Measure length, volume and weight/mass using rulers, scales and other appropriate measuring instruments in the customary and metric systems.

9D985B10DFE50131798A68A86D17958E.description: Measure and compare quantities using appropriate units, instruments and methods.

9D977ED0DFE50131798768A86D17958E.description: Estimate, make and use measurements of objects, quantities and relationships and determine acceptable levels of accuracy.
comments: Measurement provides a way to answer questions about "how many," "how much" and "how far." It is an indispensable component of business, manufacturing, art, medicine and many other aspects of daily life. We describe the sizes, capacities and values of many things, from the large distances involved in space travel, to the very small quantities in computer design and microbiology, to the varying values of currencies in international monetary exchange. All people must be able to choose an appropriate level of accuracy for a measurement; to select what measuring instruments to use and to correctly determine the measures of objects, space and time. These activities require people to be able to use standard instruments including rulers, volume and capacity measures, timers and emerging measurement technologies found in the home and workplace.

9D94F280DFE50131797E68A86D17958E.description: Compare the numbers of objects in groups.

9D94B210DFE50131797D68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using comparison of quantities, ratios, proportions and percents.

9D958100DFE50131798068A86D17958E.description: Show evidence that whole number computational results are correct and/or that estimates are reasonable.

9D95C090DFE50131798168A86D17958E.description: Select and perform computational procedures to solve problems with whole numbers.

9D953FA0DFE50131797F68A86D17958E.description: Compute and estimate using mental mathematics, paper-and-pencil methods, calculators and computers.

9D964640DFE50131798368A86D17958E.description: Solve one- and two-step problems with whole numbers using addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

9D960310DFE50131798268A86D17958E.description: Investigate, represent and solve problems using number facts, operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and their properties, algorithms and relationships.

9D96E6D0DFE50131798568A86D17958E.description: Identify and model fractions using concrete materials and pictorial representations.

9D973940DFE50131798668A86D17958E.description: Identify whole numbers and compare them using the symbols <, >, or = and the words "less than", "greater than", or "equal to", applying counting, grouping and place value concepts.

9D968C80DFE50131798468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge and use of numbers and their representations in a broad range of theoretical and practical settings.

comments: Numbers and operations on numbers play fundamental roles in helping us make sense of the world around us. Operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, as well as the ability to find powers and roots, extend the notion of numbers to create tools to model situations and solve problems in our everyday lives. Discussing and solving problems related to budgets, comparing prices on merchandise, understanding the nature of interest charges, measuring fuel consumption and calculating the trajectory for space travel would all be impossible without a sense of numbers and numerical operations. All people must develop this sense of numbers and operations and be able to use it to solve problems using mental computation, paper-and-pencil algorithms, calculators and computers.
9D9467E0DFE50131797C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and apply a knowledge and sense of numbers, including numeration and operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division), patterns, ratios and proportions.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for English Language Arts

9E3F8230DFE501317ADB68A86D17958E.description: Prepare and deliver oral presentations based on inquiry or research.

9E3FC400DFE501317ADC68A86D17958E.description: Create a variety of print and nonprint documents to communicate acqured information for specific audiences and purposes.

9E3F3EC0DFE501317ADA68A86D17958E.description: Apply acquired information, concepts and ideas to communicate in a variety of formats.

9E3EA6C0DFE501317AD868A86D17958E.description: Determine the accuracy, currency and reliability of materials from various sources.

9E3E5680DFE501317AD768A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate information acquired from various sources.

9E3DC3C0DFE501317AD568A86D17958E.description: Organize and integrate information from a variety of sources (e.g., books, interviews, library reference materials, websites, CD/ROMs).

9E3E0750DFE501317AD668A86D17958E.description: Formulate questions and construct a basic research plan.

9E3D8050DFE501317AD468A86D17958E.description: Locate, organize, and use information from various sources to answer questions, solve problems and communicate ideas.

9E3D3FA0DFE501317AD368A86D17958E.description: Use the language arts to acquire, assess and communicate information.
comments: To be successful in school and in the world of work, students must be able to use a wide variety of information resources (written, visual and electronic). They must also know how to frame questions for inquiry, identify and organize relevant information and communicate it effectively in a variety of formats. These skills are critical in school across all learning areas and are key to successful career and lifelong learning experiences.

9E40A440DFE501317ADF68A86D17958E.description: Identify main verbal and nonverbal communication elements and strategies to maintain communications and to resolve conflict.

9E4142A0DFE501317AE168A86D17958E.description: Identify methods to manage or overcome communication anxiety and apprehension (e.g., topic outlines, repetitive practice).

9E418A90DFE501317AE268A86D17958E.description: Use speaking skills and procedures to participate in group discussions.

9E40EEF0DFE501317AE068A86D17958E.description: Present oral reports to an audience using correct language and nonverbal expressions for the intended purpose and message within a suggested organizational format.

9E405640DFE501317ADE68A86D17958E.description: Speak effectively using language appropriate to the situation and audience.

9E426990DFE501317AE568A86D17958E.description: Restate and carry out a variety of oral instructions.

9E4223D0DFE501317AE468A86D17958E.description: Ask and respond to questions related to oral presentations and messages in small and large group settings.

9E42AD00DFE501317AE668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the listening process (e.g., sender, receiver, message) by summarizing and paraphrasing spoken messages orally and in writing in formal and informal situations.

9E41DB70DFE501317AE368A86D17958E.description: Listen effectively in formal and informal situations.

9E4008C0DFE501317ADD68A86D17958E.description: Listen and speak effectively in a variety of situations.
comments: Of all the language arts, listening and speaking are those most often used on a daily basis at home, school and work or in the community. Skill in speaking is universally recognized as a primary indicator of a person's knowledge, skill and credibility. In person, by phone or through video, good listening and speaking skills are essential to sending, receiving and understanding messages. To understand messages spoken by others, students must be able to listen carefully, using specific techniques to clarify what they have heard. For speaking properly and making messages understood, grammar, sentence structure, tone, expression and emphasis must be part of students' repertoires.

9E3544B0DFE501317AB668A86D17958E.description: Produce and format compositions for specified audiences using available technology.

9E358E40DFE501317AB768A86D17958E.description: Write for a variety of purposes and for specified audiences in a variety of forms including narrative (e.g., fiction, autobiography), expository (e.g., reports, essays) and persuasive writings (e.g., editorials, advertisements).

9E350440DFE501317AB568A86D17958E.description: Communicate ideas in writing to accomplish a variety of purposes.

9E347580DFE501317AB368A86D17958E.description: Establish central idea, organization, elaboration and unity in relation to purpose and audience.

9E34BC00DFE501317AB468A86D17958E.description: Generate and organize ideas using a variety of planning strategies (e.g., mapping, outlining, drafting).

9E342670DFE501317AB268A86D17958E.description: Compose well-organized and coherent writing for specific purposes and audiences.

9E361680DFE501317AB968A86D17958E.description: Write paragraphs that include a variety of sentence types; appropriate use of the eight parts of speech; and accurate spelling, capitalization and punctuation.

9E35D470DFE501317AB868A86D17958E.description: Use correct grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization and structure.

9E33D2C0DFE501317AB168A86D17958E.description: Write to communicate for a variety of purposes.
comments: The ability to write clearly is essential to any person's effective communications. Students with high-level writing skills can produce documents that show planning and organization and effectively convey the intended message and meaning. Clear writing is critical to employment and production in today's world. Individuals must be capable of writing for a variety of audiences in differing styles, including standard rhetoric themes, business letters and reports, financial proposals and technical and professional communications. Students should be able to use word processors and computers to enhance their writing proficiency and improve their career opportunities.

9E3829A0DFE501317AC168A86D17958E.description: Relate literary works and their characters, settings and plots to current and historical events, people and perspectives.

9E37E8F0DFE501317AC068A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain themes that have been explored in literature from different societies and eras.

9E386980DFE501317AC268A86D17958E.description: Respond to literary material by making inferences, drawing conclusions and comparing it to their own experience, prior knowledge and other texts.

9E37A830DFE501317ABF68A86D17958E.description: Read and interpret a variety of literary works.

9E371350DFE501317ABD68A86D17958E.description: Identify definitive features of literary forms (e.g., realistic fiction, historical fiction, fantasy, narrative, nonfiction, biography, plays, electronic literary forms).

9E36D510DFE501317ABC68A86D17958E.description: Describe how literary elements (e.g., theme, character, setting, plot, tone, conflict) are used in literature to create meaning.

9E376060DFE501317ABE68A86D17958E.description: Identify literary elements and literary techniques (e.g., characterization, use of narration, use of dialogue) in a variety of literary works.

9E3696F0DFE501317ABB68A86D17958E.description: Understand how literary elements and techniques are used to convey meaning.

9E365790DFE501317ABA68A86D17958E.description: Read and understand literature representative of various societies, eras and ideas.
comments: Literature transmits ideas, reflects societies and eras and expresses the human imagination. It brings understanding, enrichment and joy. Appreciating literature and recognizing its many forms enable students to learn and respond to ideas, issues, perspectives and actions of others. Literature study includes understanding the structure and intent of a short poem or a long, complex book. By exploring the techniques that authors use to convey messages and evoke responses, students connect literature to their own lives and daily experiences.

9E39AB20DFE501317AC668A86D17958E.description: Connect information presented in tables, maps and charts to printed or electronic text.

9E3A2C20DFE501317AC868A86D17958E.description: Explain how authors and illustrators use text and art to express their ideas (e.g., points of view, design hues, metaphor).

9E3A6AB0DFE501317AC968A86D17958E.description: Summarize and make generalizations from content and relate to purpose of material.

9E396380DFE501317AC568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the content and organization of selections.

9E3AAB30DFE501317ACA68A86D17958E.description: Make and support inferences and form interpretations about main themes and topics.

9E39EC60DFE501317AC768A86D17958E.description: Use information to form and refine questions and predictions.

9E38F830DFE501317AC468A86D17958E.description: Comprehend a broad range of reading materials.

9E3BDAA0DFE501317ACE68A86D17958E.description: Read age-appropriate material aloud with fluency and accuracy.

9E3C2AC0DFE501317ACF68A86D17958E.description: Continuously check and clarify for understanding (e.g., in addition to previous skills, clarify terminology, seek additional information).

9E3B8F00DFE501317ACD68A86D17958E.description: Identify structure (e.g., description, compare/contrast, cause and effect, sequence) of nonfiction texts to improve comprehension.

9E3B3970DFE501317ACC68A86D17958E.description: Establish purposes for reading; survey materials; ask questions; make predictions; connect, clarify and extend ideas.

9E3AF3B0DFE501317ACB68A86D17958E.description: Apply reading strategies to improve understanding and fluency.

9E3D0010DFE501317AD268A86D17958E.description: Clarify word meaning using context clues and a variety of resources including glossaries, dictionaries and thesauruses.

9E3CBFA0DFE501317AD168A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend unfamiliar words using root words, synonyms, antonyms, word origins and derivations.

9E3C7C90DFE501317AD068A86D17958E.description: Apply word analysis and vocabulary skills to comprehend selections.

comments: Reading is essential. It is the process by which people gain information and ideas from books, newspapers, manuals, letters, contracts, advertisements and a host of other materials. Using strategies for constructing meaning before, during and after reading will help students connect what they read now with what they have learned in the past. Students who read well and widely build a strong foundation for learning in all areas of life.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Mathematics

9E0B8FD0DFE501317A6E68A86D17958E.description: Make predictions using probabilities associated with normally distributed events.

9E0B4430DFE501317A6D68A86D17958E.description: Compute probabilities in counting situations involving permutations and combinations.

9E0BD710DFE501317A6F68A86D17958E.description: Compute conditional probabilities and the probabilities of independent events.

9E0B05A0DFE501317A6C68A86D17958E.description: Determine, describe and apply the probabilities of events.

9E0AC6D0DFE501317A6B68A86D17958E.description: Design a statistical experiment to answer a question about a realistic situation, conduct the experiment, use statistics to interpret the data, and communicate the results, individually and as members of a team.

9E0A8A20DFE501317A6A68A86D17958E.description: Formulate questions, design data collection methods, gather and analyze data and communicate findings.

9E0A4B80DFE501317A6968A86D17958E.description: Construct a statistics-based presentation, individually and as members of a team, to communicate and justify the results of a project.

9E0A0CC0DFE501317A6868A86D17958E.description: Organize, describe and make predictions from existing data.

comments: The ability to understand and interpret data (e.g., opinion polls, stock prices, tax rates, crime statistics, scientific studies, weather reports) grows more important each day. Students must be able to organize data, make sense of variables and patterns, and judge the logical reasonableness of any claims and interpretations made. Even very young students can count objects and communicate their findings with charts and graphs. Students of all ages can collect, display and interpret data to answer specific questions. They also must construct and analyze arguments that involve data and its interpretation. All students need to understand and apply the role probability plays in data collection and decision making. Data analysis and use are important abilities necessary for all careers.
9E09C2D0DFE501317A6768A86D17958E.description: Collect, organize and analyze data using statistical methods; predict results; and interpret uncertainty using concepts of probability.

9E0E2D70DFE501317A7768A86D17958E.description: Analyze and solve problems involving periodic patterns (e.g., sound waves, tide variations) using circular functions and communicate results orally and in writing.

9E0DEA00DFE501317A7668A86D17958E.description: Use trigonometric ratios and circular functions to solve problems.

9E0CACF0DFE501317A7268A86D17958E.description: Apply physical models, graphs, coordinate systems, networks and vectors to develop solutions in applied contexts (e.g., bus routing, areas of irregular shapes, describing forces and other physical quantities).

9E0CEE90DFE501317A7368A86D17958E.description: Perform and describe an original investigation of a geometric problem and verify the analysis and conclusions to an audience.

9E0C6C10DFE501317A7168A86D17958E.description: Construct convincing arguments and proofs to solve problems.

9E0DA2A0DFE501317A7568A86D17958E.description: Construct and use two- and three-dimensional models of objects that have practical applications (e.g., blueprints, topographical maps, scale models).

9E0D4400DFE501317A7468A86D17958E.description: Identify, describe, classify and compare relationships using points, lines, planes and solids.

9E0EB650DFE501317A7968A86D17958E.description: Use geometric figures and their properties to solve problems in the arts, the physical and life sciences and the building trades, with and without the use of technology.

9E0E7240DFE501317A7868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and apply geometric concepts involving points, lines, planes and space.

9E0C1F30DFE501317A7068A86D17958E.description: Use geometric methods to analyze, categorize and draw conclusions about points, lines, planes and space.
comments: Geometry provides important methods for reasoning and solving problems with points, lines, planes and space. The word "geometry" comes from Greek words meaning "measurement of the Earth." While we use modern technology and employ a wider variety of mathematical tools today, we still study geometry to understand the shapes and dimensions of our world. The applications of geometry are widespread in construction, engineering, architecture, mapmaking and art. Historically, geometry is a way to develop skill in forming convincing arguments and proofs. This goal of developing a means of argument and validation remains an important part of our reasons for studying geometry today.

9E034C30DFE501317A5168A86D17958E.description: Formulate and solve nonlinear equations and systems including problems involving inverse variation and exponential and logarithmic growth and decay.

9E030710DFE501317A5068A86D17958E.description: Use algebraic concepts and procedures to represent and solve problems.

9E046CD0DFE501317A5568A86D17958E.description: Use polynomial, exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions to model situations.

9E042A60DFE501317A5468A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using systems of numbers and their properties.

9E03DAF0DFE501317A5368A86D17958E.description: Use functions including exponential, polynomial, rational, parametric, logarithmic, and trigonometric to describe numerical relationships.

9E0397A0DFE501317A5268A86D17958E.description: Interpret and describe numerical relationships using tables, graphs and symbols.

9E02C6C0DFE501317A4F68A86D17958E.description: Solve mathematical problems involving recursive patterns and use models that employ such relationships.

9E0284C0DFE501317A4E68A86D17958E.description: Describe numerical relationships using variables and patterns.

9E023270DFE501317A4D68A86D17958E.description: Use algebraic and analytical methods to identify and describe patterns and relationships in data, solve problems and predict results.
comments: Algebra unites patterns and quantities in patterns with the means of describing change through the use of variables and functions. Its concepts and analytical methods allow people to consider general solutions to problems with common characteristics and develop related formulas. Algebra provides verbal, symbolic and graphical formats for discussing and representing settings as diverse as the pricing patterns of merchandise in a store, the behavior of a car as it accelerates or slows down, the changes in two chemicals as they react with one another, or the type of variation existing in a comparison of two factors in the economy. All people must be able to use algebraic methods to construct and examine tables of values; to interpret the relationships expressed by patterns in these tables; to relate change and variation in graphs and formulas; to reason about changes in quantities and the relationships involved in changes; and to find solutions to everyday problems using algebra's symbolic manipulation and formulas.

9E07FEB0DFE501317A6168A86D17958E.description: Determine how changes in one measure may affect other measures (e.g., what happens to the volume and surface area of a cube when the side of the cube is halved).

9E084CF0DFE501317A6268A86D17958E.description: Use dimensional analysis to determine units and check answers in applied measurement problems.

9E0799D0DFE501317A6068A86D17958E.description: Select and use appropriate technology, instruments and formulas to solve problems, interpret results and communicate findings.

9E097850DFE501317A6668A86D17958E.description: Estimate perimeter, area, volume, and capacity of irregular shapes, regions and solids and explain the reasoning supporting the estimate.

9E0934D0DFE501317A6568A86D17958E.description: Estimate measurements and determine acceptable levels of accuracy.

9E08EB40DFE501317A6468A86D17958E.description: Apply nonlinear scales (e.g., Richter, decibel, pH) to solve practical problems.

9E089DC0DFE501317A6368A86D17958E.description: Measure and compare quantities using appropriate units, instruments and methods.

9E072C70DFE501317A5F68A86D17958E.description: Estimate, make and use measurements of objects, quantities and relationships and determine acceptable levels of accuracy.
comments: Measurement provides a way to answer questions about "how many," "how much" and "how far." It is an indispensable component of business, manufacturing, art, medicine and many other aspects of daily life. We describe the sizes, capacities and values of many things, from the large distances involved in space travel, to the very small quantities in computer design and microbiology, to the varying values of currencies in international monetary exchange. All people must be able to choose an appropriate level of accuracy for a measurement; to select what measuring instruments to use and to correctly determine the measures of objects, space and time. These activities require people to be able to use standard instruments including rulers, volume and capacity measures, timers and emerging measurement technologies found in the home and workplace.

9E053BF0DFE501317A5868A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving loans, mortgages and other practical applications involving geometric patterns of growth.

9E04F9C0DFE501317A5768A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using comparison of quantities, ratios, proportions and percents.

9E05BEE0DFE501317A5A68A86D17958E.description: Determine the level of accuracy needed for computations involving measurement and irrational numbers.

9E057E70DFE501317A5968A86D17958E.description: Compute and estimate using mental mathematics, paper-and-pencil methods, calculators and computers.

9E065460DFE501317A5C68A86D17958E.description: Identify, represent and apply numbers expressed in exponential, logarithmic and scientific notation using contemporary technology.

9E060F20DFE501317A5B68A86D17958E.description: Investigate, represent and solve problems using number facts, operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and their properties, algorithms and relationships.

9E06E650DFE501317A5E68A86D17958E.description: Perform addition, subtraction and multiplication of complex numbers and graph the results in the complex plane.

9E069CA0DFE501317A5D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge and use of numbers and their representations in a broad range of theoretical and practical settings.

9E04AF20DFE501317A5668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and apply a knowledge and sense of numbers, including numeration and operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division), patterns, ratios and proportions.
comments: Numbers and operations on numbers play fundamental roles in helping us make sense of the world around us. Operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, as well as the ability to find powers and roots, extend the notion of numbers to create tools to model situations and solve problems in our everyday lives. Discussing and solving problems related to budgets, comparing prices on merchandise, understanding the nature of interest charges, measuring fuel consumption and calculating the trajectory for space travel would all be impossible without a sense of numbers and numerical operations. All people must develop this sense of numbers and operations and be able to use it to solve problems using mental computation, paper-and-pencil algorithms, calculators and computers.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Science

DE54A843D0C24AFA80B469B8771335DF.description: Demonstrate ways to reduce, reuse and recycle materials.

47734F259917481DA0936308817D2B80.description: Identify and describe ways that science and technology affect people's everyday lives (e.g., transportation, medicine, agriculture, sanitation, communication occupations).

ACFF8A16881048C28CC123CB4A261466.description: Describe contributions men and women have made to science and technology.

521A0F7C9B4040CBB2FB7A2EF1EF53AE.description: Explain how using measuring tools improves the accuracy of estimates.

2BCE68BBE1E747F0B2B5BEDFE5BA9D1B.description: Explain the uses of common scientific instruments (e.g., ruler, thermometer, balance, probe, computer).

95A7605D9399433B9C89D4F839E7DEBB.description: Know and apply concepts that describe the interaction between science, technology and society.

62375CDF12F34917ABF0BC7889F05603.description: Explain how knowledge can be gained by careful observation.

7B4904173AAC4747930EDDC35F23CF58.description: Explain why similar results are expected when procedures are done the same way.

AAF359D6CDFC48EE8A75A408F9D8C154.description: Use basic safety practices (e.g., not tasting materials without permission, "stop/drop/roll").

0FCF51BE891F477C91DC30FC24CEA60B.description: Know and apply the accepted practices of science.

374DFC69E8FB4F5F85ED7F06562483A4.description: Understand the relationships among science, technology and society in historical and contemporary contexts.
comments: Understanding the nature and practices of science such as ensuring the validity and replicability of results, building upon the work of others and recognizing risks involved in experimentation gives learners a useful sense of the scientific enterprise. In addition, the relationships among science, technology and society give humans the ability to change and improve their surroundings. Learners who understand this relationship will be able to appreciate the efforts and effects of scientific discovery and applications of technology on their own lives and on the society in which we live.

A7C90F3A68574013BA24CFADBA89710C.description: Identify daily, seasonal and annual patterns related to the Earth's rotation and revolution.

F4F0D0C86AE342A9A408C277635381B8.description: Identify and describe characteristics of the sun, Earth and moon as familiar objects in the solar system.

1E9A462483A64764A0DA18939705EFBF.description: Know and apply concepts that explain the composition and structure of the universe and Earth's place in it.

44D37F672F45445987DF1209A12EF40F.description: Identify renewable and nonrenewable natural resources.

D198D7F9622E41A683F67A974E454473.description: Identify and describe patterns of weather and seasonal change.

0AF9A75C6E2D4E4E84BEE849D899BC9E.description: Identify components and describe diverse features of the Earth's land, water and atmospheric systems.

A4321B1503404683BC631A91378E53A9.description: Know and apply concepts that describe the features and processes of the Earth and its resources.

473335C9819F4AFD87E1DA1F55EB5888.description: Identify observable forces in nature (e.g., pushes, pulls, gravity, magnetism).

3B69CD9C34B54360A7AE7BAC2101AC10.description: Identify examples of motion (e.g., moving in a straight line, vibrating, rotating).

B2283590C7BB4986961EB652A89D29D4.description: Know and apply concepts that describe force and motion and the principles that explain them.

21B6C056C30F4C8498DD273F7694CE1A.description: Compare large-scale physical properties of matter (e.g., size, shape, color, texture, odor).

4EDCC5111E1B498AA0CC8B7D4758205C.description: Identify and compare sources of energy (e.g., batteries, the sun).

FDC176B9E5C74BEB9253371195D78240.description: Know and apply concepts that describe properties of matter and energy and the interactions between them.

84E3FCC9ED914251B7EA9B4B58B81BC3.description: Describe how living things depend on one another for survival.

37425E04A6524D93A53EBEA2831950F7.description: Describe and compare characteristics of living things in relationship to their environments.

C39690CD99244E7C874CDFB5C73F796A.description: Know and apply concepts that describe how living things interact with each other and with their environment.

A84F741EC45F4586A3521ADB5EB122E6.description: Categorize living organisms using a variety of observable features (e.g., size, color, shape, backbone).

E666AD66740249DF9E9E29699D6CA066.description: Identify and describe the component parts of living things (e.g., birds have feathers; people have bones, blood, hair, skin) and their major functions.

6A6B04FEEB124AD68B620678F6469BC8.description: Know and apply concepts that explain how living things function, adapt and change.

47A8A922CF2E4EFA8088CCE4C804CEA5.description: Understand the fundamental concepts, principles and interconnections of the life, physical and earth/space sciences.
comments: This goal is comprised of key concepts and principles in the life, physical and earth/space sciences that have considerable explanatory and predictive power for scientists and non-scientists alike. These ideas have been thoroughly studied and have stood the test of time. Knowing and being able to apply these concepts, principles and processes help students understand what they observe in nature and through scientific experimentation. A working knowledge of these concepts and principles allows students to relate new subject matter to material previously learned and to create deeper and more meaningful levels of understanding.

C8241FFE7BC94EC39DFB16BCE0562914.description: Report the design of the device, the test process and the results in solving a given problem.

A5516DB6BB47468EA2C3A571E61EDC79.description: Test the device and record results using given instruments, techniques and measurement methods.

56ECEB645C7B4ADD9C0C00711C5B5615.description: Build the device using the materials and tools provided.

B0447E394C0D46208F87625D3FCCA76F.description: Design a device that will be useful in solving the problem.

F88672BAF8C04236A26FE5304B326498.description: Given a simple design problem, formulate possible solutions.

5B08D44DAD8147C3991A97B82569BE87.description: Know and apply the concepts, principles and processes of technological design.

55D5114F2BAB4087AC98566F83CE7428.description: Compare observations of individual and group results.

BE3B97B129B24BC5ACA69FD79364EA03.description: Arrange data into logical patterns and describe the patterns.

2A9DAA8E264144ABAC981E149AED488E.description: Record and store data using available technologies.

A6C744A453D44805886ABA13B50D1061.description: Collect data for investigations using measuring instruments and technologies.

BCB803EDD9174FEA9D57CBD0EDA0046B.description: Know and apply the concepts, principles and processes of scientific inquiry.

E009C43FA4804DD2B34DFF6E74BF5EC5.description: Understand the processes of scientific inquiry and technological design to investigate questions, conduct experiments and solve problems.
comments: The inquiry process prepares learners to engage in science and apply methods of technological design. This understanding will enable students to pose questions, use models to enhance understanding, make predictions, gather and work with data, use appropriate measurement methods, analyze results, draw conclusions based on evidence, communicate their methods and results, and think about the implications of scientific research and technological problem solving.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Science

900275733C4D4FDE94F3532395790A92.description: Assess how scientific and technological progress has affected other fields of study, careers and job markets and aspects of everyday life.
