5A428594180840AD92A219F66A376539.description: Analyze the costs, benefits and effects of scientific and technological policies at the local, state, national and global levels (e.g., genetic research, Internet access).

182D209A44244A38ADDE29EF210C6112.description: Design and conduct an environmental impact study, analyze findings and justify recommendations.

63806E72E3C04D8B87BD37E542693509.description: Analyze and describe the processes and effects of scientific and technological breakthroughs.

7F5EF61DCA4347B7BFAA95BE71C2E09F.description: Analyze challenges created by international competition for increases in scientific knowledge and technological capabilities (e.g., patent issues, industrial espionage, technology obsolescence).

36D8BAEF3F7B4DC59D85AC217321B36E.description: Know and apply concepts that describe the interaction between science, technology and society.

0216E4138F634DF288067A366CEAF6C0.description: Explain, using a practical example (e.g., cold fusion), why experimental replication and peer review are essential to scientific claims.

572E15562DEB476995179A76931C0A55.description: Explain the strengths, weaknesses and uses of research methodologies including observational studies, controlled laboratory experiments, computer modeling and statistical studies.

05C79353391D4C90A306A35AD362C1DD.description: Explain criteria that scientists use to evaluate the validity of scientific claims and theories.

3087613BF41642BEBB826AE7B8B10893.description: Design procedures and policies to eliminate or reduce risk in potentially hazardous science activities.

D90845FEB97F4C69914F42E81D8B16EC.description: Know and apply the accepted practices of science.

454F57E1B3DE44F0AF7BE0387515C64D.description: Understand the relationships among science, technology and society in historical and contemporary contexts.
comments: Understanding the nature and practices of science such as ensuring the validity and replicability of results, building upon the work of others and recognizing risks involved in experimentation gives learners a useful sense of the scientific enterprise. In addition, the relationships among science, technology and society give humans the ability to change and improve their surroundings. Learners who understand this relationship will be able to appreciate the efforts and effects of scientific discovery and applications of technology on their own lives and on the society in which we live.

B6C66EFE778D445C9C3AA8E70CB72E98.description: Describe the size and age of the universe and evaluate the supporting evidence (e.g., red-shift, Hubble's constant).

D44C3238693045AFBDA9328C3BE98A7C.description: Compare the processes involved in the life cycle of stars (e.g., gravitational collapse, thermonuclear fusion, nova) and evaluate the supporting evidence.

87ACBF66846A405A951F9240A941DFEB.description: Know and apply concepts that explain the composition and structure of the universe and Earth's place in it.

A7C6E6F28CF9449CA211B9074BCB748E.description: Analyze the processes involved in naturally occurring short-term and long-term Earth events (e.g., floods, ice ages, temperature, sea-level fluctuations).

02B175C60BAB40939C6B0E0E475E58E0.description: Know and apply concepts that describe the features and processes of the Earth and its resources.

FA12DAA64E354306AA6CCEEFEAC94E1B.description: Analyze the effects of gravitational, electromagnetic and nuclear forces on a physical system.

6B1F609D77F345F19BF3507BAB825F0C.description: Analyze factors that influence the relative motion of an object (e.g., friction, wind shear, cross currents, potential differences).

D7CC0D23892D4C9B841715DC008F58FF.description: Know and apply concepts that describe force and motion and the principles that explain them.

663475FD4C9E4FA59E8A67D16A25F21D.description: Analyze the properties of materials (e.g., mass, boiling point, melting point, hardness) in relation to their physical and/or chemical structures.

A102B609442C4FA7BCAAE0B524EFE13A.description: Analyze reactions (e.g., nuclear reactions, burning of fuel, decomposition of waste) in natural and man-made energy systems.

248A276ABB0944B68E6A2532246430F1.description: Know and apply concepts that describe properties of matter and energy and the interactions between them.

E92B6D4742F94DDCBEFD83D58453B0F5.description: Compare and predict how life forms can adapt to changes in the environment by applying concepts of change and constancy (e.g., variations within a population increase the likelihood of survival under new conditions).

5A1BD05AD07B4ADBBDB97179BB5D71A0.description: Analyze and explain biodiversity issues and the causes and effects of extinction.

EA0F6ED8765D47C189F9C3E805F154B0.description: Know and apply concepts that describe how living things interact with each other and with their environment.

5C3105BD64E14484B7917110FFC93C15.description: Analyze the transmission of genetic traits, diseases and defects.

79764BB219F14DB7A132C10B1C8ACD7F.description: Explain changes within cells and organisms in response to stimuli and changing environmental conditions (e.g., homeostasis, dormancy).

A151C59F5B4641DDA3BB018A2989865C.description: Know and apply concepts that explain how living things function, adapt and change.

AE4E5F868840483AA4A25F6BA9849E9E.description: Understand the fundamental concepts, principles and interconnections of the life, physical and earth/space sciences.
comments: This goal is comprised of key concepts and principles in the life, physical and earth/space sciences that have considerable explanatory and predictive power for scientists and non-scientists alike. These ideas have been thoroughly studied and have stood the test of time. Knowing and being able to apply these concepts, principles and processes help students understand what they observe in nature and through scientific experimentation. A working knowledge of these concepts and principles allows students to relate new subject matter to material previously learned and to create deeper and more meaningful levels of understanding.

75AD9D3A8EB145348C71DDB9D32EC96A.description: Using available technology, prepare and present findings of the tested design solution to an audience that may include professional and technical experts.

5EB81AAE02D041449BE07CAE0906637A.description: Apply established criteria to evaluate the suitability, acceptability, benefits, drawbacks and consequences for the tested design solution and recommend modifications and refinements.

D31ED7FD20BF45FDAACF1DF5E47E6B8F.description: Choose a model and refine its design based on the test results.

437EEBD5220F4610BCDB2656E9AED199.description: Build and test different models or simulations of the design solution using suitable materials, tools and technology.

E0983E9EB0744C298E8AF84FBC67813A.description: Select criteria for a successful design solution to the identified problem.

1475DD4AC17148F09B1DD0EF04132EEF.description: Identify a design problem that has practical applications and propose possible solutions, considering such constraints as available tools, materials, time and costs.

D8D85F1FD8CE42E8876591A601351BA0.description: Know and apply the concepts, principles and processes of technological design.

F4B6AE5D64AF4424A6B091F695014D00.description: Report, display and defend the results of investigations to audiences that may include professionals and technical experts.

41B5F7C2B5F24254BB036130E7DFF192.description: Apply statistical methods to make predictions and to test the accuracy of results.

C073C3FEDCD54F9FA0D8CE5B4D2E4D5B.description: Conduct systematic controlled experiments to test the selected hypotheses.

41A49134A223463D8E8B3E1F1A64B67E.description: Design procedures to test the selected hypotheses.

59158ED05DD64D13B49D194FD7493D19.description: Formulate hypotheses referencing prior research and knowledge.

1488534EC8164A6587A63AEDC31C8760.description: Know and apply the concepts, principles and processes of scientific inquiry.

ADC22A2925E149A48D9E57749057DB00.description: Understand the processes of scientific inquiry and technological design to investigate questions, conduct experiments and solve problems.
comments: The inquiry process prepares learners to engage in science and apply methods of technological design. This understanding will enable students to pose questions, use models to enhance understanding, make predictions, gather and work with data, use appropriate measurement methods, analyze results, draw conclusions based on evidence, communicate their methods and results, and think about the implications of scientific research and technological problem solving.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Mathematics

9DD98D20DFE501317A0768A86D17958E.description: Analyze problem situations (e.g., board games, grading scales) and make predictions about results.

9DD9DB60DFE501317A0868A86D17958E.description: Determine the probability and odds of events using fundamental counting principles.

9DD94870DFE501317A0668A86D17958E.description: Determine, describe and apply the probabilities of events.

9DD901E0DFE501317A0568A86D17958E.description: Formulate questions (e.g., relationships between car age and mileage, average incomes and years of schooling), devise and conduct experiments or simulations, gather data, draw conclusions and communicate results to an audience using traditional methods and contemporary technologies.

9DD8ACE0DFE501317A0468A86D17958E.description: Formulate questions, design data collection methods, gather and analyze data and communicate findings.

9DD85D40DFE501317A0368A86D17958E.description: Test the reasonableness of an argument based on data and communicate their findings.

9DD80530DFE501317A0268A86D17958E.description: Compare the mean, median, mode and range, with and without the use of technology.

9DD7B5B0DFE501317A0168A86D17958E.description: Construct, read and interpret tables, graphs (including circle graphs) and charts to organize and represent data.

9DD77060DFE501317A0068A86D17958E.description: Organize, describe and make predictions from existing data.

9DD720F0DFE5013179FF68A86D17958E.description: Collect, organize and analyze data using statistical methods; predict results; and interpret uncertainty using concepts of probability.
comments: The ability to understand and interpret data (e.g., opinion polls, stock prices, tax rates, crime statistics, scientific studies, weather reports) grows more important each day. Students must be able to organize data, make sense of variables and patterns, and judge the logical reasonableness of any claims and interpretations made. Even very young students can count objects and communicate their findings with charts and graphs. Students of all ages can collect, display and interpret data to answer specific questions. They also must construct and analyze arguments that involve data and its interpretation. All students need to understand and apply the role probability plays in data collection and decision making. Data analysis and use are important abilities necessary for all careers.

9DDC33A0DFE501317A1068A86D17958E.description: Compute distances, lengths and measures of angles using proportions, the Pythagorean theorem and its converse.

9DDBEF40DFE501317A0F68A86D17958E.description: Use trigonometric ratios and circular functions to solve problems.

9DDABA70DFE501317A0B68A86D17958E.description: Develop and solve problems using geometric relationships and models, with and without the use of technology.

9DDB04B0DFE501317A0C68A86D17958E.description: Construct, develop and communicate logical arguments (informal proofs) about geometric figures and patterns.

9DDA69F0DFE501317A0A68A86D17958E.description: Construct convincing arguments and proofs to solve problems.

9DDB9BB0DFE501317A0E68A86D17958E.description: Identify, describe, classify and compare two- and three-dimensional geometric figures and models according to their properties.

9DDB5150DFE501317A0D68A86D17958E.description: Identify, describe, classify and compare relationships using points, lines, planes and solids.

9DDD4BE0DFE501317A1468A86D17958E.description: Use concepts of symmetry, congruency, similarity, scale, perspective, and angles to describe and analyze two- and three-dimensional shapes found in practical applications (e.g., geodesic domes, A-frame houses, basketball courts, inclined planes, art forms, blueprints).

9DDD01F0DFE501317A1368A86D17958E.description: Draw transformation images of figures, with and without the use of technology.

9DDCBD90DFE501317A1268A86D17958E.description: Draw or construct two- or three- dimensional geometric figures including prisms, pyramids, cylinders and cones.

9DDC7800DFE501317A1168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and apply geometric concepts involving points, lines, planes and space.

9DDA20B0DFE501317A0968A86D17958E.description: Use geometric methods to analyze, categorize and draw conclusions about points, lines, planes and space.
comments: Geometry provides important methods for reasoning and solving problems with points, lines, planes and space. The word "geometry" comes from Greek words meaning "measurement of the Earth." While we use modern technology and employ a wider variety of mathematical tools today, we still study geometry to understand the shapes and dimensions of our world. The applications of geometry are widespread in construction, engineering, architecture, mapmaking and art. Historically, geometry is a way to develop skill in forming convincing arguments and proofs. This goal of developing a means of argument and validation remains an important part of our reasons for studying geometry today.

9DCF7FD0DFE5013179E468A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of powers, perfect squares and square roots.

9DCF3820DFE5013179E368A86D17958E.description: Propose and solve problems using proportions, formulas and linear functions.

9DCFC6E0DFE5013179E568A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using numeric, graphic or symbolic representations of variables, expressions, equations and inequalities.

9DCEF740DFE5013179E268A86D17958E.description: Use algebraic concepts and procedures to represent and solve problems.

9DD0D1B0DFE5013179E968A86D17958E.description: Apply the properties of numbers and operations including inverses in algebraic settings derived from economics, business and the sciences.

9DD08DA0DFE5013179E868A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using systems of numbers and their properties.

9DD04D10DFE5013179E768A86D17958E.description: Use graphing technology and algebraic methods to analyze and predict linear relationships and make generalizations from linear patterns.

9DD00A80DFE5013179E668A86D17958E.description: Interpret and describe numerical relationships using tables, graphs and symbols.

9DCE6B20DFE5013179E068A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using linear expressions, equations and inequalities.

9DCEB2F0DFE5013179E168A86D17958E.description: Apply the basic properties of commutative, associative, distributive, transitive, inverse, identity, zero, equality and order of operations to solve problems.

9DCE2770DFE5013179DF68A86D17958E.description: Describe numerical relationships using variables and patterns.

9DCDCA60DFE5013179DE68A86D17958E.description: Use algebraic and analytical methods to identify and describe patterns and relationships in data, solve problems and predict results.
comments: Algebra unites patterns and quantities in patterns with the means of describing change through the use of variables and functions. Its concepts and analytical methods allow people to consider general solutions to problems with common characteristics and develop related formulas. Algebra provides verbal, symbolic and graphical formats for discussing and representing settings as diverse as the pricing patterns of merchandise in a store, the behavior of a car as it accelerates or slows down, the changes in two chemicals as they react with one another, or the type of variation existing in a comparison of two factors in the economy. All people must be able to use algebraic methods to construct and examine tables of values; to interpret the relationships expressed by patterns in these tables; to relate change and variation in graphs and formulas; to reason about changes in quantities and the relationships involved in changes; and to find solutions to everyday problems using algebra's symbolic manipulation and formulas.

9DD53130DFE5013179F968A86D17958E.description: Use concrete and graphic models and appropriate formulas to find perimeters, areas, surface areas and volumes of two- and three-dimensional regions.

9DD4EFB0DFE5013179F868A86D17958E.description: Construct a simple scale drawing for a given situation.

9DD4A5A0DFE5013179F768A86D17958E.description: Select and use appropriate technology, instruments and formulas to solve problems, interpret results and communicate findings.

9DD6DA50DFE5013179FE68A86D17958E.description: Select and apply instruments including rulers and protractors and units of measure to the degree of accuracy required.

9DD694D0DFE5013179FD68A86D17958E.description: Estimate measurements and determine acceptable levels of accuracy.

9DD5F4F0DFE5013179FB68A86D17958E.description: Apply the concepts and attributes of length, capacity, weight/mass, perimeter, area, volume, time, temperature and angle measures in practical situations.

9DD64BF0DFE5013179FC68A86D17958E.description: Measure, length, capacity, weight/mass and angles using sophisticated instruments (e.g., compass, protractor, trundle wheel).

9DD589D0DFE5013179FA68A86D17958E.description: Measure and compare quantities using appropriate units, instruments and methods.

9DD45BE0DFE5013179F668A86D17958E.description: Estimate, make and use measurements of objects, quantities and relationships and determine acceptable levels of accuracy.
comments: Measurement provides a way to answer questions about "how many," "how much" and "how far." It is an indispensable component of business, manufacturing, art, medicine and many other aspects of daily life. We describe the sizes, capacities and values of many things, from the large distances involved in space travel, to the very small quantities in computer design and microbiology, to the varying values of currencies in international monetary exchange. All people must be able to choose an appropriate level of accuracy for a measurement; to select what measuring instruments to use and to correctly determine the measures of objects, space and time. These activities require people to be able to use standard instruments including rulers, volume and capacity measures, timers and emerging measurement technologies found in the home and workplace.

9DD1B4D0DFE5013179EC68A86D17958E.description: Apply ratios and proportions to solve practical problems.

9DD16F50DFE5013179EB68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using comparison of quantities, ratios, proportions and percents.

9DD23580DFE5013179EE68A86D17958E.description: Show evidence that computational results using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, percents and proportions are correct and/or that estimates are reasonable.

9DD27670DFE5013179EF68A86D17958E.description: Select computational procedures and solve problems with whole numbers, fractions, decimals, percents and proportions.

9DD1F580DFE5013179ED68A86D17958E.description: Compute and estimate using mental mathematics, paper-and-pencil methods, calculators and computers.

9DD398B0DFE5013179F368A86D17958E.description: Identify and apply properties of real numbers including pi, squares, and square roots.

9DD35590DFE5013179F268A86D17958E.description: Apply primes, factors, divisors, multiples, common factors and common multiples in solving problems.

9DD30530DFE5013179F168A86D17958E.description: Solve practical computation problems involving whole numbers, integers and rational numbers.

9DD2BB40DFE5013179F068A86D17958E.description: Investigate, represent and solve problems using number facts, operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and their properties, algorithms and relationships.

9DD41C30DFE5013179F568A86D17958E.description: Represent fractions, decimals, percentages, exponents and scientific notation in equivalent forms.

9DD3DAE0DFE5013179F468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge and use of numbers and their representations in a broad range of theoretical and practical settings.

9DD115A0DFE5013179EA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and apply a knowledge and sense of numbers, including numeration and operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division), patterns, ratios and proportions.
comments: Numbers and operations on numbers play fundamental roles in helping us make sense of the world around us. Operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, as well as the ability to find powers and roots, extend the notion of numbers to create tools to model situations and solve problems in our everyday lives. Discussing and solving problems related to budgets, comparing prices on merchandise, understanding the nature of interest charges, measuring fuel consumption and calculating the trajectory for space travel would all be impossible without a sense of numbers and numerical operations. All people must develop this sense of numbers and operations and be able to use it to solve problems using mental computation, paper-and-pencil algorithms, calculators and computers.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards Incorporating the Common Core English Language Arts

A01AFB20DFE501317E0B68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that night we went looking for them).

A01AAAD0DFE501317E0A68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).

A01A5360DFE501317E0968A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).

A01A0140DFE501317E0868A86D17958E.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

A019B3D0DFE501317E0768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

A0196010DFE501317E0668A86D17958E.description: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

A018FF40DFE501317E0568A86D17958E.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).

A018A620DFE501317E0468A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).

A0184E50DFE501317E0368A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

A017FCF0DFE501317E0268A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

A0175740DFE501317E0068A86D17958E.description: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.

A016FEF0DFE501317DFF68A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

A0169760DFE501317DFE68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

A015E7D0DFE501317DFC68A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

A01590F0DFE501317DFB68A86D17958E.description: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.

A0151290DFE501317DFA68A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).

A01472C0DFE501317DF868A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

A0135920DFE501317DF568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

A0130F80DFE501317DF468A86D17958E.description: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

A01271B0DFE501317DF268A86D17958E.description: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

A011CCA0DFE501317DF068A86D17958E.description: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.

A01177B0DFE501317DEF68A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.

A010CD40DFE501317DED68A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.

A0107EC0DFE501317DEC68A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.

A01023B0DFE501317DEB68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A00F3270DFE501317DE868A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

A00ED980DFE501317DE768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

A00E7B80DFE501317DE668A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

A00DB5D0DFE501317DE468A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

A00D15E0DFE501317DE268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

A00CCBB0DFE501317DE168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A00C25F0DFE501317DDF68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

A00BD630DFE501317DDE68A86D17958E.description: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

A00B81B0DFE501317DDD68A86D17958E.description: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.

A00B2BE0DFE501317DDC68A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.

A00A8EA0DFE501317DDA68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.

A00A36D0DFE501317DD968A86D17958E.description: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

A009E940DFE501317DD868A86D17958E.description: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

A00999A0DFE501317DD768A86D17958E.description: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.

A0094A90DFE501317DD668A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

A008F910DFE501317DD568A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

A008A010DFE501317DD468A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

A007A700DFE501317DD168A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

A0074E80DFE501317DD068A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

A006F2E0DFE501317DCF68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

A0063710DFE501317DCD68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

A005D380DFE501317DCC68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

A0055AC0DFE501317DCB68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

A004AA20DFE501317DC968A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

A0045BC0DFE501317DC868A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

A00372E0DFE501317DC568A86D17958E.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.

A0032110DFE501317DC468A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.

A002C720DFE501317DC368A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

A0027960DFE501317DC268A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.

A00224C0DFE501317DC168A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

A001C970DFE501317DC068A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
comments: (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1—3 above.)

A000C9C0DFE501317DBD68A86D17958E.description: Use temporal words and phrases to signal event order.

A0007D80DFE501317DBC68A86D17958E.description: Use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the response of characters to situations.

A0002890DFE501317DBB68A86D17958E.description: Establish a situation and introduce a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

9FFFD530DFE501317DBA68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

9FFF87D0DFE501317DB968A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

9FFF2A10DFE501317DB868A86D17958E.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., also, another, and, more, but) to connect ideas within categories of information.

9FFEC6A0DFE501317DB768A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details.

9FFE76B0DFE501317DB668A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic and group related information together; include illustrations when useful to aiding comprehension.

9FFE1870DFE501317DB568A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

9FFDC5D0DFE501317DB468A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

9FFD7240DFE501317DB368A86D17958E.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., because, therefore, since, for example) to connect opinion and reasons.

9FFD12C0DFE501317DB268A86D17958E.description: Provide reasons that support the opinion.

9FFCB6E0DFE501317DB168A86D17958E.description: Introduce the topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure that lists reasons.

9FFC5E00DFE501317DB068A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons.

9FFB6FA0DFE501317DAD68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

9FFAC9A0DFE501317DAB68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

9FFA6CC0DFE501317DAA68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

9FFA1840DFE501317DA968A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

9FF9B1B0DFE501317DA868A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

9FF96160DFE501317DA768A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

9FF90C90DFE501317DA668A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

9FF8BB80DFE501317DA568A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

9FF81200DFE501317DA368A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

9FF7AFA0DFE501317DA268A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

9FF757B0DFE501317DA168A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

9FF6B8B0DFE501317D9F68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

9FF661D0DFE501317D9E68A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

9FF61220DFE501317D9D68A86D17958E.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

9FF5B870DFE501317D9C68A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

9FF56EB0DFE501317D9B68A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

9FF43400DFE501317D9768A86D17958E.description: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.

9FF3D9A0DFE501317D9668A86D17958E.description: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.

9FF38CE0DFE501317D9568A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

9FF2A290DFE501317D9268A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 2—3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

9FF251C0DFE501317D9168A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

9FF1E810DFE501317D9068A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.

9FF19A50DFE501317D8F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (e.g., comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence).

9FF14BA0DFE501317D8E68A86D17958E.description: Use information gained from illustrations (e.g., maps, photographs) and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding of the text (e.g., where, when, why, and how key events occur).

9FF0AC60DFE501317D8C68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.

9FF05020DFE501317D8B68A86D17958E.description: Use text features and search tools (e.g., key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information relevant to a given topic efficiently.

9FEFEAA0DFE501317D8A68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.

9FEF3DF0DFE501317D8868A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.

9FEED2B0DFE501317D8768A86D17958E.description: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.

9FEE7120DFE501317D8668A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

9FED8650DFE501317D8368A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 2—3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

9FED38A0DFE501317D8268A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

9FEC9810DFE501317D8068A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the themes, settings, and plots of stories written by the same author about the same or similar characters (e.g., in books from a series).

9FEC40A0DFE501317D7F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how specific aspects of a text's illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story (e.g., create mood, emphasize aspects of a character or setting).

9FEB9D60DFE501317D7D68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or those of the characters.

9FEB3D50DFE501317D7C68A86D17958E.description: Refer to parts of stories, dramas, and poems when writing or speaking about a text, using terms such as chapter, scene, and stanza; describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections.

9FEAD9E0DFE501317D7B68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.

9FEA3630DFE501317D7968A86D17958E.description: Describe characters in a story (e.g., their traits, motivations, or feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.

9FE9E870DFE501317D7868A86D17958E.description: Recount stories, including fables, folktales, and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson, or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details in the text.

9FE99560DFE501317D7768A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

9FE89570DFE501317D7468A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

9FE84BA0DFE501317D7368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

9FE800D0DFE501317D7268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

9FE7B6A0DFE501317D7168A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

9FE76600DFE501317D7068A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

9FE6B6A0DFE501317D6E68A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

9FE66710DFE501317D6D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

9FE612C0DFE501317D6C68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

9FE56A40DFE501317D6A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

9FE51A60DFE501317D6968A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

9FE4CAC0DFE501317D6868A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

9FE3DAF0DFE501317D6668A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Mathematics

9DF34EC0DFE501317A3D68A86D17958E.description: Propose and interpret discrete probability distributions, with and without the use of technology.

9DF3D450DFE501317A3F68A86D17958E.description: Design and conduct simulations (e.g., waiting times at restaurant, probabilities of births, likelihood of game prizes), with and without the use of technology.

9DF39290DFE501317A3E68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems of chance using the principles of probability including conditional settings.

9DF30640DFE501317A3C68A86D17958E.description: Determine, describe and apply the probabilities of events.

9DF2A560DFE501317A3B68A86D17958E.description: Design and execute surveys or experiments, gather data to answer relevant questions, and communicate results and conclusions to an audience using traditional methods and contemporary technology.

9DF252C0DFE501317A3A68A86D17958E.description: Formulate questions, design data collection methods, gather and analyze data and communicate findings.

9DF1CDC0DFE501317A3868A86D17958E.description: Predict from data using interpolation, extrapolation and trend lines, with and without the use of technology.

9DF189E0DFE501317A3768A86D17958E.description: Analyze data using mean, median, mode, range, variance and standard deviation of a data set, with and without the use of technology.

9DF20F00DFE501317A3968A86D17958E.description: Represent and organize data by creating lists, charts, tables, frequency distributions, graphs, scatterplots and box-plots.

9DF142B0DFE501317A3668A86D17958E.description: Organize, describe and make predictions from existing data.

9DF0F260DFE501317A3568A86D17958E.description: Collect, organize and analyze data using statistical methods; predict results; and interpret uncertainty using concepts of probability.
comments: The ability to understand and interpret data (e.g., opinion polls, stock prices, tax rates, crime statistics, scientific studies, weather reports) grows more important each day. Students must be able to organize data, make sense of variables and patterns, and judge the logical reasonableness of any claims and interpretations made. Even very young students can count objects and communicate their findings with charts and graphs. Students of all ages can collect, display and interpret data to answer specific questions. They also must construct and analyze arguments that involve data and its interpretation. All students need to understand and apply the role probability plays in data collection and decision making. Data analysis and use are important abilities necessary for all careers.

9DF670E0DFE501317A4868A86D17958E.description: Analyze and solve problems involving triangles (e.g., distances which cannot be measured directly) using trigonometric ratios.

9DF622F0DFE501317A4768A86D17958E.description: Use trigonometric ratios and circular functions to solve problems.

9DF51740DFE501317A4368A86D17958E.description: Develop and communicate mathematical proofs (e.g., two-column, paragraph, indirect) and counter examples for geometric statements.

9DF55B10DFE501317A4468A86D17958E.description: Construct and communicate convincing arguments for geometric situations.

9DF4D230DFE501317A4268A86D17958E.description: Construct and test logical arguments for geometric situations using technology where appropriate.

9DF47EA0DFE501317A4168A86D17958E.description: Construct convincing arguments and proofs to solve problems.

9DF5E220DFE501317A4668A86D17958E.description: Recognize and apply relationships within and among geometric figures.

9DF5A1E0DFE501317A4568A86D17958E.description: Identify, describe, classify and compare relationships using points, lines, planes and solids.

9DF73620DFE501317A4B68A86D17958E.description: Make perspective drawings, tessellations and scale drawings, with and without the use of technology.

9DF6F630DFE501317A4A68A86D17958E.description: Construct a model of a three-dimensional figure from a two-dimensional pattern.

9DF6B510DFE501317A4968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and apply geometric concepts involving points, lines, planes and space.

comments: Geometry provides important methods for reasoning and solving problems with points, lines, planes and space. The word "geometry" comes from Greek words meaning "measurement of the Earth." While we use modern technology and employ a wider variety of mathematical tools today, we still study geometry to understand the shapes and dimensions of our world. The applications of geometry are widespread in construction, engineering, architecture, mapmaking and art. Historically, geometry is a way to develop skill in forming convincing arguments and proofs. This goal of developing a means of argument and validation remains an important part of our reasons for studying geometry today.
9DF424F0DFE501317A4068A86D17958E.description: Use geometric methods to analyze, categorize and draw conclusions about points, lines, planes and space.

9DE975C0DFE501317A1B68A86D17958E.description: Formulate and solve linear and quadratic equations and linear inequalities algebraically and investigate nonlinear inequalities using graphs, tables, calculators and computers.

9DE935E0DFE501317A1A68A86D17958E.description: Use algebraic concepts and procedures to represent and solve problems.

9DEB1740DFE501317A2168A86D17958E.description: Apply algebraic properties and procedures with matrices, vectors, functions and sequences using data found in business, industry and consumer situations.

9DEAD530DFE501317A2068A86D17958E.description: Analyze and report the effects of changing coefficients, exponents and other parameters on functions and their graphs.

9DEA93B0DFE501317A1F68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using systems of numbers and their properties.

9DEA5120DFE501317A1E68A86D17958E.description: Use the basic functions of absolute value, square root, linear, quadratic and step to describe numerical relationships.

9DEA0D00DFE501317A1D68A86D17958E.description: Represent algebraic concepts with physical materials, words, diagrams, tables, graphs, equations and inequalities and use appropriate technology.

9DE9C5A0DFE501317A1C68A86D17958E.description: Interpret and describe numerical relationships using tables, graphs and symbols.

9DE8F170DFE501317A1968A86D17958E.description: Represent mathematical patterns and describe their properties using variables and mathematical symbols.

9DE8AC70DFE501317A1868A86D17958E.description: Use algebraic methods to convert repeating decimals to fractions.

9DE86150DFE501317A1768A86D17958E.description: Describe numerical relationships using variables and patterns.

9DE7F270DFE501317A1668A86D17958E.description: Use algebraic and analytical methods to identify and describe patterns and relationships in data, solve problems and predict results.
comments: Algebra unites patterns and quantities in patterns with the means of describing change through the use of variables and functions. Its concepts and analytical methods allow people to consider general solutions to problems with common characteristics and develop related formulas. Algebra provides verbal, symbolic and graphical formats for discussing and representing settings as diverse as the pricing patterns of merchandise in a store, the behavior of a car as it accelerates or slows down, the changes in two chemicals as they react with one another, or the type of variation existing in a comparison of two factors in the economy. All people must be able to use algebraic methods to construct and examine tables of values; to interpret the relationships expressed by patterns in these tables; to relate change and variation in graphs and formulas; to reason about changes in quantities and the relationships involved in changes; and to find solutions to everyday problems using algebra's symbolic manipulation and formulas.

9DEED580DFE501317A2E68A86D17958E.description: Convert within and between measurement systems and monetary systems using technology where appropriate.

9DEF31A0DFE501317A2F68A86D17958E.description: Interpret scale drawings and models using maps and blueprints.

9DEE8790DFE501317A2D68A86D17958E.description: Make indirect measurements, including heights and distances, using proportions (e.g., finding the height of a tower by its shadow).

9DEE4760DFE501317A2C68A86D17958E.description: Select and use appropriate technology, instruments and formulas to solve problems, interpret results and communicate findings.

9DF0A190DFE501317A3468A86D17958E.description: Estimate and measure the magnitude and directions of physical quantities (e.g., velocity, force, slope) using rulers, protractors and other scientific instruments including timers, calculators and computers.

9DF05F00DFE501317A3368A86D17958E.description: Estimate measurements and determine acceptable levels of accuracy.

9DF01B60DFE501317A3268A86D17958E.description: Apply formulas in a wide variety of theoretical and practical real-world measurement applications involving perimeter, area, volume, angle, time, temperature, mass, speed, distance, density and monetary values.

9DEFD4F0DFE501317A3168A86D17958E.description: Apply units and scales to describe and compare numerical data and physical objects.

9DEF81A0DFE501317A3068A86D17958E.description: Measure and compare quantities using appropriate units, instruments and methods.

9DEDFDF0DFE501317A2B68A86D17958E.description: Estimate, make and use measurements of objects, quantities and relationships and determine acceptable levels of accuracy.
comments: Measurement provides a way to answer questions about "how many," "how much" and "how far." It is an indispensable component of business, manufacturing, art, medicine and many other aspects of daily life. We describe the sizes, capacities and values of many things, from the large distances involved in space travel, to the very small quantities in computer design and microbiology, to the varying values of currencies in international monetary exchange. All people must be able to choose an appropriate level of accuracy for a measurement; to select what measuring instruments to use and to correctly determine the measures of objects, space and time. These activities require people to be able to use standard instruments including rulers, volume and capacity measures, timers and emerging measurement technologies found in the home and workplace.

9DEBFA30DFE501317A2468A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving recipes or mixtures, financial calculations and geometric similarity using ratios, proportions and percents.

9DEBB380DFE501317A2368A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using comparison of quantities, ratios, proportions and percents.

9DEC8210DFE501317A2668A86D17958E.description: Determine whether exact values or approximations are appropriate (e.g., bid a job, determine gas mileage for a trip).

9DEC3D90DFE501317A2568A86D17958E.description: Compute and estimate using mental mathematics, paper-and-pencil methods, calculators and computers.

9DED09E0DFE501317A2868A86D17958E.description: Select and use appropriate arithmetic operations in practical situations including calculating wages after taxes, developing a budget and balancing a checkbook.

9DECC640DFE501317A2768A86D17958E.description: Investigate, represent and solve problems using number facts, operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and their properties, algorithms and relationships.

9DEDBB00DFE501317A2A68A86D17958E.description: Identify and apply the associative, commutative, distributive and identity properties of real numbers, including special numbers such as pi and square roots.

9DED7070DFE501317A2968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge and use of numbers and their representations in a broad range of theoretical and practical settings.

9DEB5890DFE501317A2268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and apply a knowledge and sense of numbers, including numeration and operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division), patterns, ratios and proportions.
comments: Numbers and operations on numbers play fundamental roles in helping us make sense of the world around us. Operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, as well as the ability to find powers and roots, extend the notion of numbers to create tools to model situations and solve problems in our everyday lives. Discussing and solving problems related to budgets, comparing prices on merchandise, understanding the nature of interest charges, measuring fuel consumption and calculating the trajectory for space travel would all be impossible without a sense of numbers and numerical operations. All people must develop this sense of numbers and operations and be able to use it to solve problems using mental computation, paper-and-pencil algorithms, calculators and computers.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Science

3B544721441245D2AC997EE486115E92.description: Apply classroom-developed criteria to determine the effects of policies on local science and technology issues (e.g., energy consumption, landfills, water quality).

97EC8CAC0C7445E3B2379D68395E0A21.description: Identify advantages and disadvantages of natural resource conservation and management programs.

ABD0DB57D69F4CF0938FABDAFCB31363.description: Analyze the interaction of resource acquisition, technological development and ecosystem impact (e.g., diamond, coal or gold mining; deforestation).

E7239B74C2A943338128F3AF638D7ABB.description: Describe how occupations use scientific and technological knowledge and skills.

992E5D2D3B7B44EE9748BCC2AB202151.description: Identify important contributions to science and technology that have been made by individuals and groups from various cultures.

AE94E7BF1B8C439DA312CB95F8E0C861.description: Identify and explain ways that scientific knowledge and economics drive technological development.

311ABFDE89264DB9B12E2AE2F3BEF0B3.description: Know and apply concepts that describe the interaction between science, technology and society.

1D73F63FC95C4F88B59EE6565434522C.description: Explain what is similar and different about observational and experimental investigations.

FD71C09073124A65A0EB5179A8161DC2.description: Analyze historical and contemporary cases in which the work of science has been affected by both valid and biased scientific practices.

8A59E3E56B11414DBBDAA9C670275B6B.description: Identify and reduce potential hazards in science activities (e.g., ventilation, handling chemicals).

2DE08468E2F54ABBA533424215BC7F11.description: Know and apply the accepted practices of science.

11550A2CC30F4CDF8CCF907088561B0C.description: Understand the relationships among science, technology and society in historical and contemporary contexts.
comments: Understanding the nature and practices of science such as ensuring the validity and replicability of results, building upon the work of others and recognizing risks involved in experimentation gives learners a useful sense of the scientific enterprise. In addition, the relationships among science, technology and society give humans the ability to change and improve their surroundings. Learners who understand this relationship will be able to appreciate the efforts and effects of scientific discovery and applications of technology on their own lives and on the society in which we live.

CA3C660B7B344130B70D773448BAA5F9.description: Compare and contrast the sun as a star with other objects in the Milky Way galaxy (e.g., nebulae, dust clouds, stars, black holes).

A8F0337EABA7405D843808ACAACA1EE2.description: Describe the organization and physical characteristics of the solar system (e.g., sun, planets, satellites, asteroids, comets).

46B612B893A6412C9CBC591076636F34.description: Simulate, analyze and explain the effects of gravitational force in the solar system (e.g., orbital shape and speed, tides, spherical shape of the planets and moons).

230DE6D1B40749C5B914619C48E309CC.description: Know and apply concepts that explain the composition and structure of the universe and Earth's place in it.

3BA78F0EE445474F83F7A82458D1BC24.description: Evaluate the biodegradability of renewable and nonrenewable natural resources.

1A504B30C02F4EC9BB7A8385DF2D47A4.description: Describe interactions between solid earth, oceans, atmosphere and organisms that have resulted in ongoing changes of Earth (e.g., erosion, El Nino).

AAE577E93D834947A63F46E57D4890A8.description: Analyze and explain large-scale dynamic forces, events and processes that affect the Earth's land, water and atmospheric systems (e.g., jetstream, hurricanes, plate tectonics).

E3571DD82AF94D1DAB7A80238A9F8960.description: Know and apply concepts that describe the features and processes of the Earth and its resources.

3069A25392D0442F84E87D3AD1BFB1DD.description: Explain the factors that affect the gravitational forces on objects (e.g., changes in mass, distance).

3F9953ABFF154A739C04EADDC6572110.description: Explain and demonstrate how forces affect motion (e.g., action/reaction, equilibrium conditions, free-falling objects).

049BE05E5A4B4658B31A597950074517.description: Know and apply concepts that describe force and motion and the principles that explain them.

CA474BBBCED9403D86CDDF985EAE7C8A.description: Model and describe the chemical and physical characteristics of matter (e.g., atoms, molecules, elements, compounds, mixtures).

1C8CA7B5286646739AC7044693D21768.description: Explain interactions of energy with matter including changes of state and conservation of mass and energy.

82A9CB7071FB4295823B0943FB22E1FB.description: Know and apply concepts that describe properties of matter and energy and the interactions between them.

42582AFEE6324E37BF4FF6B72A2B28F1.description: Compare and assess features of organisms for their adaptive, competitive and survival potential (e.g., appendages, reproductive rates, camouflage, defensive structures).

1C9675933F7C4F2DBAD6F18BC779BCA0.description: Identify and classify biotic and abiotic factors in an environment that affect population density, habitat and placement of organisms in an energy pyramid.

B7A6862F01DE40439D4F2CF14D2AE333.description: Know and apply concepts that describe how living things interact with each other and with their environment.

9CB4B8A6092F4A0F97E6B00D815E7D5E.description: Compare and contrast how different forms and structures reflect different functions (e.g., similarities and differences among animals that fly, walk or swim; structures of plant cells and animal cells).

365C9D7BC7394CFBAA6945A9AAA66A66.description: Compare characteristics of organisms produced from a single parent with those of organisms produced by two parents.

8ED4F5549A1A47B8B5BE7D1E401BF37B.description: Explain how cells function as "building blocks" of organisms and describe the requirements for cells to live.

6621E2062E914225B55B2E21129286A5.description: Know and apply concepts that explain how living things function, adapt and change.

B8134FB596274F93837D5D9D7795441E.description: Understand the fundamental concepts, principles and interconnections of the life, physical and earth/space sciences.
comments: This goal is comprised of key concepts and principles in the life, physical and earth/space sciences that have considerable explanatory and predictive power for scientists and non-scientists alike. These ideas have been thoroughly studied and have stood the test of time. Knowing and being able to apply these concepts, principles and processes help students understand what they observe in nature and through scientific experimentation. A working knowledge of these concepts and principles allows students to relate new subject matter to material previously learned and to create deeper and more meaningful levels of understanding.

F9C9D886ACDB4E728BE6E77392C5D595.description: Using available technology, report the relative success of the design based on the test results and criteria.

F5F81A5EB3A6477CBA7AEC65DFC8EDBE.description: Evaluate the test results based on established criteria, note sources of error and recommend improvements.

3ACD9E246D2341A7A853369B069C930A.description: Test the prototype using available materials, instruments and technology and record the data.

30BEC75CE60A46A0BDFDBD0874E2261F.description: Select the most appropriate design and build a prototype or simulation.

540FB130806E4DC4A6971A76F8A5D662.description: Sketch, propose and compare design solutions to the problem considering available materials, tools, cost effectiveness and safety.

0FD6CB6DAC0B41F0A354EFDB7A72EEA2.description: Identify an actual design problem and establish criteria for determining the success of a solution.

FD9623B319684DEA9090534806A1743E.description: Know and apply the concepts, principles and processes of technological design.

FB7122E48AEE45B08B95762ECFC6C2BD.description: Report and display the process and results of a scientific investigation.

6CD614F9631A4BBCA10F092A75004FC7.description: Interpret and represent results of analysis to produce findings.

407D19058C60451C8D6E54FDD5BB39DD.description: Use data manipulation tools and quantitative (e.g., mean, mode, simple equations) and representational methods (e.g., simulations, image processing) to analyze measurements.

86EE817073B14DBCA00E059428FCEA81.description: Explain the existence of unexpected results in a data set.

A12A275CD50049468617E9575EC5F21B.description: Collect and record data accurately using consistent measuring and recording techniques and media.

9FA954172F5C4D7180EDD145819E089A.description: Conduct scientific experiments that control all but one variable.

B21261325DA54D0789680E7ED7E6F61A.description: Formulate hypotheses that can be tested by collecting data.

AE24D1A61F5040C5B4342F04D55C60A2.description: Know and apply the concepts, principles and processes of scientific inquiry.

D83B24ABB3A94B24BC666227A06575B2.description: Understand the processes of scientific inquiry and technological design to investigate questions, conduct experiments and solve problems.
comments: The inquiry process prepares learners to engage in science and apply methods of technological design. This understanding will enable students to pose questions, use models to enhance understanding, make predictions, gather and work with data, use appropriate measurement methods, analyze results, draw conclusions based on evidence, communicate their methods and results, and think about the implications of scientific research and technological problem solving.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Physical Development and Health

A3290D20DFE5013183FC68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate basic refusal skills (e.g., "Just Say No", "Stranger Danger").

A328CAC0DFE5013183FB68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate skills essential to enhancing health and avoiding dangerous situations.

A3288600DFE5013183FA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize how choices can affect health (e.g., not brushing/tooth decay, smoking/risk of cancer and heart disease).

A32833F0DFE5013183F968A86D17958E.description: Apply decision-making skills related to the protection and promotion of individual health.

A327DAF0DFE5013183F868A86D17958E.description: Identify positive verbal and nonverbal communication skills (e.g., body language, manners, listening).

A3278A40DFE5013183F768A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between positive and negative behaviors (e.g., waiting your turn vs. pushing in line, honesty vs. lying).

A3274100DFE5013183F668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate procedures for communicating in positive ways, resolving differences and preventing conflict.

comments: From an early age, students need to know how to communicate their health needs and learn to take responsibility for their own health. They also need to know how and why personal decisions can affect their own health and well-being. Consideration for the needs of others becomes part of health promotion as well. Students who can clearly identify and communicate about health-related issues-and can make healthful personal decisions-will benefit as they grow and mature in school and into responsible workers and citizens.
A326D6B0DFE5013183F568A86D17958E.description: Promote and enhance health and well-being through the use of effective communication and decision-making skills.

A3267640DFE5013183F468A86D17958E.description: Identify individual differences in growth and development among people.

A3262E20DFE5013183F368A86D17958E.description: Describe factors that affect growth and development.

A325EB20DFE5013183F268A86D17958E.description: Identify healthy actions that influence the functions of the body (e.g., cleanliness, proper diet, exercise).

A3259FC0DFE5013183F168A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of health-related actions on the body systems.

A32554F0DFE5013183F068A86D17958E.description: Identify basic parts of body systems and their functions (e.g., heart, lungs, eyes).

A3251170DFE5013183EF68A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain the structure and functions of the human body systems and how they interrelate.

A324BF40DFE5013183EE68A86D17958E.description: Understand human body systems and factors that influence growth and development.
comments: To achieve healthful individual development, students need to understand human anatomy and physiology, nutrition, stages of growth and development, avoidance of harmful actions and the characteristics of good health habits. Early learners begin with basic recognition of body systems and growth stages. As students progress, they understand how systems work together and how individual actions affect health. As they themselves grow and develop, students can learn to enhance the process throughout their school years and later life.

A32477C0DFE5013183ED68A86D17958E.description: Identify sources and causes of environmental health risks (e.g., air, soil, sun, water, noise, food, chemicals).

A3243750DFE5013183EC68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the environment can affect health.

A323F4C0DFE5013183EB68A86D17958E.description: Encourage and support others in making positive health choices (e.g., eating practices, cleanliness, safety practices).

A323B590DFE5013183EA68A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain the factors that influence health among individuals, groups and communities.

A32373E0DFE5013183E968A86D17958E.description: Identify dangerous situations and safety methods to reduce risks (e.g., traffic, improper use of medicine and poisons, strangers).

A3231F30DFE5013183E868A86D17958E.description: Identify methods of health promotion and illness prevention (e.g., obtaining immuni-zations, hand washing, brushing and flossing teeth, eating practices, sleep, cleanliness).

A322C4A0DFE5013183E768A86D17958E.description: Identify general signs and symptoms of illness (e.g., fever, rashes, coughs, congestion).

A3227540DFE5013183E668A86D17958E.description: Explain the basic principles of health promotion, illness prevention and safety.

A3222BC0DFE5013183E568A86D17958E.description: Understand principles of health promotion and the prevention and treatment of illness and injury.
comments: Nutrition, exercise, rest, hygiene and safety are the bases for personal, family and occupational health. From an early age, students can recognize healthy habits and understand why they are important. As students become more sophisticated in their understanding, they learn and can adopt a variety of ways to minimize illness and enhance health. Learners will be able to apply the effects of health-related actions to success in the workplace. Students who develop an effective understanding of basic health promotion can establish the foundation for achieving and maintaining personal health and well-being by making informed wellness decisions now and throughout their lives.

A321E8A0DFE5013183E468A86D17958E.description: Work cooperatively with another to accomplish an assigned task.

A321A240DFE5013183E368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate cooperative skills during structured group physical activity.

A32145E0DFE5013183E268A86D17958E.description: Work independently on tasks for short periods of time.

A320F290DFE5013183E168A86D17958E.description: Use identified procedures and safe practices with little or no reinforcement during group physical activities.

A320A750DFE5013183E068A86D17958E.description: Follow directions and class procedures while participating in physical activities.

A3206640DFE5013183DF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate individual responsibility during group physical activities.

A32020D0DFE5013183DE68A86D17958E.description: Develop team-building skills by working with others through physical activity.
comments: As members of teams, students need to fill the role of leader at times and participant at other times. Knowing how to follow procedures, accept leadership from others, participate actively and lead when appropriate will serve the student on and off the playing field. Students need to know the elements of teamwork (communication, decision making, cooperation, leadership) and how to adjust individual needs to team needs. Students also need to be able to recognize each member's contributions, including their own.

A31F98B0DFE5013183DC68A86D17958E.description: Set goals based on fitness data and develop, implement and monitor an individual fitness improvement plan.

A31F3C80DFE5013183DB68A86D17958E.description: Describe immediate effects of physical activity on the body (e.g., faster heartbeat, increased pulse rate, increased breathing rate).

A31EBF80DFE5013183D968A86D17958E.description: Engage in sustained physical activity that causes increased heart rate, muscle strength and range of movement.

A31E7D20DFE5013183D868A86D17958E.description: Identify characteristics of health-related fitness (e.g., flexibility, muscular strength).

A31E3AC0DFE5013183D768A86D17958E.description: Know and apply the principles and components of health-related fitness.

A31DF140DFE5013183D668A86D17958E.description: Achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical fitness based upon continual self-assessment.
comments: Regular physical activity is necessary to sustain fitness and health. Students need to apply training principles-frequency, intensity, time and type (FITT)-to achieve their personal fitness goals. Fitness expectations need to be established on an individual basis; realistic goals need to be based on the health-related components of endurance, strength, flexibility, cardiorespiratory fitness and body composition. By learning and applying these concepts, students can develop lifelong understanding and good habits for overall health and fitness.

A31DA670DFE5013183D568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate safe movement in physical activities.

A31D5450DFE5013183D468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of rules, safety and strategies during physical activity.

A31D0AE0DFE5013183D368A86D17958E.description: Understand spatial awareness and relationships to objects and people.

A31CC120DFE5013183D268A86D17958E.description: Analyze various movement concepts and applications.

A31C7C10DFE5013183D168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate control when performing fundamental locomotor, non-locomotor and manipulative skills.

A31C3660DFE5013183D068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate physical competency in individual and team sports, creative movement and leisure and work-related activities.

A31BE640DFE5013183CF68A86D17958E.description: Acquire movement skills and understand concepts needed to engage in health-enhancing physical activity.
comments: Physical performance involves competency in a wide range of motor, non-motor and manipulative skills. Learning in this area is developmental, building simple movements into more complex patterns. Learning to follow directions and rules enhances enjoyment and success in both recreational and competitive sports. Working toward higher levels of competence, students learn how to maintain health and fitness as individuals and as members of teams.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for English Language Arts

9E754BA0DFE501317B4D68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate in formal debates.

9E759420DFE501317B4E68A86D17958E.description: Produce oral presentations and written documents using supportive research and incorporating contemporary technology.

9E75DC70DFE501317B4F68A86D17958E.description: Plan, compose, edit and revise information (e.g., brochures, formal reports, proposals, research summaries, analyses, editorials, articles, overheads, multimedia displays) for presentation to an audience.

9E74F9B0DFE501317B4C68A86D17958E.description: Apply acquired information, concepts and ideas to communicate in a variety of formats.

9E74B740DFE501317B4B68A86D17958E.description: Use multiple sources and multiple formats; cite according to standard style manuals.

9E747090DFE501317B4A68A86D17958E.description: Choose and evaluate primary and secondary sources (print and nonprint) for a variety of purposes.

9E742A80DFE501317B4968A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate information acquired from various sources.

9E739A30DFE501317B4768A86D17958E.description: Design and present a project (e.g., research report, scientific study, career/higher education opportunities) using various formats from multiple sources.

9E73E3B0DFE501317B4868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate a knowledge of strategies needed to prepare a credible research report (e.g., notes, planning sheets).

9E734DD0DFE501317B4668A86D17958E.description: Locate, organize, and use information from various sources to answer questions, solve problems and communicate ideas.

9E7307C0DFE501317B4568A86D17958E.description: Use the language arts to acquire, assess and communicate information.
comments: To be successful in school and in the world of work, students must be able to use a wide variety of information resources (written, visual and electronic). They must also know how to frame questions for inquiry, identify and organize relevant information and communicate it effectively in a variety of formats. These skills are critical in school across all learning areas and are key to successful career and lifelong learning experiences.

9E77AE60DFE501317B5568A86D17958E.description: Use verbal and nonverbal strategies to maintain communication and to resolve individual and group conflict.

9E76C830DFE501317B5268A86D17958E.description: Use strategies to manage or overcome communication anxiety and apprehension (e.g., developed outlines, notecards, practice).

9E772260DFE501317B5368A86D17958E.description: Use group discussion skills to assume leadership and participant roles within an assigned project or to reach a group goal.

9E7768A0DFE501317B5468A86D17958E.description: Deliver planned informative and persuasive oral presentations using visual aids and contemporary technology as individuals and members of a group; demonstrate organization, clarity, vocabulary, credible and accurate supporting evidence.

9E767960DFE501317B5168A86D17958E.description: Speak effectively using language appropriate to the situation and audience.

9E78E420DFE501317B5968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the relationship of verbal and nonverbal messages within a context (e.g., contradictory, supportive, repetitive, substitutive).

9E789480DFE501317B5868A86D17958E.description: Apply listening skills in practical settings (e.g., classroom note taking, interpersonal conflict situations, giving and receiving directions, evaluating persuasive messages).

9E784CB0DFE501317B5768A86D17958E.description: Apply listening skills as individuals and members of a group in a variety of settings (e.g., lectures, discussions, conversations, team projects, presentations, interviews).

9E77F3A0DFE501317B5668A86D17958E.description: Listen effectively in formal and informal situations.

9E762E50DFE501317B5068A86D17958E.description: Listen and speak effectively in a variety of situations.
comments: Of all the language arts, listening and speaking are those most often used on a daily basis at home, school and work or in the community. Skill in speaking is universally recognized as a primary indicator of a person's knowledge, skill and credibility. In person, by phone or through video, good listening and speaking skills are essential to sending, receiving and understanding messages. To understand messages spoken by others, students must be able to listen carefully, using specific techniques to clarify what they have heard. For speaking properly and making messages understood, grammar, sentence structure, tone, expression and emphasis must be part of students' repertoires.

9E6B2BB0DFE501317B2968A86D17958E.description: Using available technology, produce compositions and multimedia works for specified audiences.

9E6AE2B0DFE501317B2868A86D17958E.description: Write for real or potentially real situations in academic, professional and civic contexts (e.g., college applications, job applications, business letters, petitions).

9E6A9650DFE501317B2768A86D17958E.description: Communicate ideas in writing to accomplish a variety of purposes.
