9E6A5600DFE501317B2668A86D17958E.description: Evaluate written work for its effectiveness and make recommendations for its improvement.

9E69BEF0DFE501317B2468A86D17958E.description: Produce, edit, revise and format work for submission and/or publication (e.g., manuscript form, appropriate citation of sources) using contemporary technology.

9E6A1220DFE501317B2568A86D17958E.description: Produce documents that exhibit a range of writing techniques appropriate to purpose and audience, with clarity of focus, logic of organization, appropriate elaboration and suport and overall coherence.

9E696EB0DFE501317B2368A86D17958E.description: Compose well-organized and coherent writing for specific purposes and audiences.

9E6BACF0DFE501317B2B68A86D17958E.description: Use standard English to edit documents for clarity, subject/verb agreement, adverb and adjective agreement and verb tense; proofread for spelling, capitalization and punctuation; and ensure that documents are formatted in final form for submission and/or publication.

9E6B6DB0DFE501317B2A68A86D17958E.description: Use correct grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization and structure.

9E691A00DFE501317B2268A86D17958E.description: Write to communicate for a variety of purposes.
comments: The ability to write clearly is essential to any person's effective communications. Students with high-level writing skills can produce documents that show planning and organization and effectively convey the intended message and meaning. Clear writing is critical to employment and production in today's world. Individuals must be capable of writing for a variety of audiences in differing styles, including standard rhetoric themes, business letters and reports, financial proposals and technical and professional communications. Students should be able to use word processors and computers to enhance their writing proficiency and improve their career opportunities.

9E6E5EA0DFE501317B3568A86D17958E.description: Discuss and evaluate motive, resulting behavior and consequences demonstrated in literature.

9E6E04F0DFE501317B3468A86D17958E.description: Analyze form, content, purpose and major themes of American literature and literature of other countries in their historical perspectives.

9E6DC3C0DFE501317B3368A86D17958E.description: Critique ideas and impressions generated by oral, visual, written and electronic materials.

9E6D80D0DFE501317B3268A86D17958E.description: Read and interpret a variety of literary works.

9E6D3BE0DFE501317B3168A86D17958E.description: Describe the influence of the author's language structure and word choice to convey the author's viewpoint.

9E6CBAC0DFE501317B2F68A86D17958E.description: Describe relationships between the author's style, literary form (e.g., short stories, novels, drama, fables, biographies, documentaries, poetry, essays) and intended effect on the reader.

9E6C7150DFE501317B2E68A86D17958E.description: Explain relationships between and among literary elements including character, plot, setting, theme, conflict and resolution and their influence on the effectiveness of the literary piece.

9E6CFBC0DFE501317B3068A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate the effective use of literary techniques (e.g., figurative language, allusion, dialogue, description, symbolism, word choice, dialect) in classical and contemporary literature representing a variety of forms and media.

9E6C2F00DFE501317B2D68A86D17958E.description: Understand how literary elements and techniques are used to convey meaning.

9E6BEC40DFE501317B2C68A86D17958E.description: Read and understand literature representative of various societies, eras and ideas.
comments: Literature transmits ideas, reflects societies and eras and expresses the human imagination. It brings understanding, enrichment and joy. Appreciating literature and recognizing its many forms enable students to learn and respond to ideas, issues, perspectives and actions of others. Literature study includes understanding the structure and intent of a short poem or a long, complex book. By exploring the techniques that authors use to convey messages and evoke responses, students connect literature to their own lives and daily experiences.

9E70A010DFE501317B3D68A86D17958E.description: Interpret tables, graphs and maps in conjunction with related text.

9E6F8DF0DFE501317B3968A86D17958E.description: Analyze how authors and illustrators use text and art to express and emphasize their ideas (e.g., imagery, multiple points of view).

9E705CA0DFE501317B3C68A86D17958E.description: Summarize and make generalizations from content and relate them to the purpose of the material.

9E701610DFE501317B3B68A86D17958E.description: Interpret, evaluate and apply information from a variety of sources to other situations (e.g., academic, vocational, technical, personal).

9E6F4DE0DFE501317B3868A86D17958E.description: Explain and justify an interpretation of a text.

9E6FCDC0DFE501317B3A68A86D17958E.description: Use questions and predictions to guide reading.

9E6F0BC0DFE501317B3768A86D17958E.description: Comprehend a broad range of reading materials.

9E71EC40DFE501317B4168A86D17958E.description: Read age-appropriate material with fluency and accuracy.

9E718C60DFE501317B4068A86D17958E.description: Analyze, interpret and compare a variety of texts for purpose, structure, content, detail and effect.

9E713990DFE501317B3F68A86D17958E.description: Preview reading materials, clarify meaning, analyze overall themes and coherence, and relate reading with information from other sources.

9E70EDC0DFE501317B3E68A86D17958E.description: Apply reading strategies to improve understanding and fluency.

9E727950DFE501317B4368A86D17958E.description: Compare the meaning of words and phrases and use analogies to explain the relationships among them.

9E72C220DFE501317B4468A86D17958E.description: Expand knowledge of word origins and derivations and use idioms, analogies, metaphors and similes to extend vocabulary development.

9E723390DFE501317B4268A86D17958E.description: Apply word analysis and vocabulary skills to comprehend selections.

comments: Reading is essential. It is the process by which people gain information and ideas from books, newspapers, manuals, letters, contracts, advertisements and a host of other materials. Using strategies for constructing meaning before, during and after reading will help students connect what they read now with what they have learned in the past. Students who read well and widely build a strong foundation for learning in all areas of life.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Social/Emotional Development

A3D0DF50DFE50131854E68A86D17958E.description: Plan, implement, and evaluate one's participation in a group effort to contribute to one's local community.

A3D09000DFE50131854D68A86D17958E.description: Plan, implement, and evaluate one's participation in activities and organizations that improve school climate.

A3D04410DFE50131854C68A86D17958E.description: Contribute to the well-being of one's school and community.

A3CFF020DFE50131854B68A86D17958E.description: Apply decision-making skills to establish responsible social and work relationships.

A3CFA540DFE50131854A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate personal abilities to gather information, generate alternatives, and anticipate the consequences of decisions.

A3CF6060DFE50131854968A86D17958E.description: Apply decision-making skills to deal responsibly with daily academic and social situations.

A3CF0E20DFE50131854868A86D17958E.description: Evaluate how social norms and the expectations of authority influence personal decisions and actions.

A3CEC060DFE50131854768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate personal responsibility in making ethical decisions.

A3CE7C40DFE50131854668A86D17958E.description: Consider ethical, safety, and societal factors in making decisions.

A3CE3AE0DFE50131854568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate decision-making skills and responsible behaviors in personal, school, and community contexts.
comments: Promoting one's own health, avoiding risky behaviors, dealing honestly and fairly with others, and contributing to the good of one's classroom, school, family, community, and environment are essential to citizenship in a democratic society. Achieving these outcomes requires an ability to make decisions and solve problems on the basis of accurately defining decisions to be made, generating alternative solutions, anticipating the consequences of each, and evaluating and learning from one's decision making.

A3CDF8E0DFE50131854468A86D17958E.description: Analyze how conflict-resolution skills contribute to work within a group.

A3CD9F20DFE50131854368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how listening and talking accurately help in resolving conflicts.

A3CD35A0DFE50131854268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an ability to prevent, manage, and resolve interpersonal conflicts in constructive ways.

A3CCF820DFE50131854168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate one's contribution in groups as a member and leader.

A3CCBCB0DFE50131854068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the effects of requesting support from and providing support to others.

A3CC8150DFE50131853F68A86D17958E.description: Use communication and social skills to interact effectively with others.

A3CC44B0DFE50131853E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate respect for individuals from different social and cultural groups.

A3CC0370DFE50131853D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the origins and negative effects of stereotyping and prejudice.

A3CBAE60DFE50131853C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize individual and group similarities and differences.

A3CB71F0DFE50131853B68A86D17958E.description: Use conversation skills to understand others' feelings and perspectives.

A3CB36E0DFE50131853A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze similarities and differences between one's own and others' perspectives.

A3CAFB80DFE50131853968A86D17958E.description: Recognize the feelings and perspectives of others.

A3CABD70DFE50131853868A86D17958E.description: Use social-awareness and interpersonal skills to establish and maintain positive relationships.
comments: Building and maintaining positive relationships with others are central to success in school and life and require the ability to recognize the thoughts, feelings, and perspectives of others, including those different from one's own. In addition, establishing positive peer, family, and work relationships requires skills in cooperating, communicating respectfully, and constructively resolving conflicts with others.

A3CA81F0DFE50131853768A86D17958E.description: Apply strategies to overcome obstacles to goal achievement.

A3CA4120DFE50131853668A86D17958E.description: Identify strategies to make use of resources and overcome obstacles to achieve goals.

A3C9FD00DFE50131853568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate skills related to achieving personal and academic goals.

A3C9AEC0DFE50131853468A86D17958E.description: Analyze how positive adult role models and support systems contribute to school and life success.

A3C97160DFE50131853368A86D17958E.description: Set priorities in building on strengths and identifying areas for improvement.

A3C93240DFE50131853268A86D17958E.description: Recognize personal qualities and external supports.

A3C8EA00DFE50131853168A86D17958E.description: Generate ways to develop more positive attitudes.

A3C8AB90DFE50131853068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how thoughts and emotions affect decision making and responsible behavior.

A3C868A0DFE50131852F68A86D17958E.description: Identify and manage one's emotions and behavior.

A3C81CB0DFE50131852E68A86D17958E.description: Develop self-awareness and self-management skills to achieve school and life success.
comments: Several key sets of skills and attitudes provide a strong foundation for achieving school and life success. One involves knowing your emotions, how to manage them, and ways to express them constructively. This enables one to handle stress, control impulses, and motivate oneself to persevere in overcoming obstacles to goal achievement. A related set of skills involves accurately assessing your abilities and interests, building strengths, and making effective use of family, school, and community resources. Finally, it is critical for students to be able to establish and monitor their progress toward achieving academic and personal goals.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Fine Arts

A2D8D380DFE50131836C68A86D17958E.description: Know how images, sounds and movement convey stories about people, places and times.

A2D88830DFE50131836B68A86D17958E.description: Understand how the arts shape and reflect history, society and everyday life.

A2D847F0DFE50131836A68A86D17958E.description: Identify how the arts contribute to communication, celebrations, occupations and recreation.

A2D806F0DFE50131836968A86D17958E.description: Identify the distinctive roles of artists and audiences.

A2D7C330DFE50131836868A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the arts function in history, society and everyday life.

A2D760E0DFE50131836768A86D17958E.description: Understand the role of the arts in civilizations, past and present.
comments: The arts are a record of civilizations, past and present. Artists are influenced by-and influence-the times and places in which they live and work. As students learn through the arts about people and civilizations, they learn about others and themselves. Also, students learn about careers related to this goal (e.g., animator, curator, art historian, sound technician).

A2D70050DFE50131836668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge and skills to create visual works of art using manipulation, eye-hand coordination, building and imagination.

A2D6C500DFE50131836568A86D17958E.description: Sing or play on classroom instruments a variety of music representing diverse cultures and styles.

A2D688E0DFE50131836468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate individual skills (e.g., vocalizing, listening, moving, observing, concentrating) and group skills (e.g., decision making, planning, practicing, spacing) necessary to create or perform story elements and characterizations.

A2D64C00DFE50131836368A86D17958E.description: Perform basic locomotor, non-locomotor movements and traditional dance forms and create simple dance sequences.

A2D60E70DFE50131836268A86D17958E.description: Apply skills and knowledge necessary to create and perform in one or more of the arts.

A2D5CFD0DFE50131836168A86D17958E.description: Identify media and tools and how to use them in a safe and responsible manner when painting, drawing and constructing.

A2D58A80DFE50131836068A86D17958E.description: Relate symbol systems (e.g., icons, syllables, numbers and letters) to musical sounds.

A2D53C70DFE50131835F68A86D17958E.description: Identify a variety of sounds and sound sources (e.g., instruments, voices and environmental sounds).

A2D4FDE0DFE50131835E68A86D17958E.description: Understand the tools of body, mind, voice and simple visual/aural media and the processes of planning, practicing and collaborating used to create or perform drama/theatre.

A2D4C170DFE50131835D68A86D17958E.description: Understand that the body is the primary tool of dance and identify secondary tools (e.g., pictures, visual aids, words, props and recordings).

A2D483B0DFE50131835C68A86D17958E.description: Understand processes, traditional tools and modern technologies used in the arts.

A2D44310DFE50131835B68A86D17958E.description: Through creating and performing, understand how works of art are produced.
comments: Students acquire skills to produce and perform dance, drama, music and visual art. They learn to use media, tools and technologies. They learn to shape ideas and emotions into sounds, images and actions. As students create and perform their own artworks and review the works of others, they become more imaginative, strengthen their problem-solving skills and learn to respond to the creativity of others. Creating and performing are at the core of the fine arts. Students also learn about the role of the artist (e.g., dancer, painter, actor, director, scriptwriter, musician).

A2D40340DFE50131835A68A86D17958E.description: Identify similarities in and among the arts (e.g., pattern, sequence and mood).

A2D3B3B0DFE50131835968A86D17958E.description: Understand the similarities, distinctions and connections in and among the arts.

A2D36BE0DFE50131835868A86D17958E.description: Identify the elements of line, shape, space, color and texture; the principles of repetition and pattern; and the expressive qualities of mood, emotion and pictorial representation.

A2D32770DFE50131835768A86D17958E.description: Identify differences in elements and expressive qualities (e.g., between fast and slow tempo; loud and soft dynamics; high and low pitch/direction; long and short duration; same and different form, tone color or timbre, and beat).

A2D2E340DFE50131835668A86D17958E.description: Understand the elements of acting, locomotor and nonlocomotor move-ment, vocal and nonvocal sound, story making; the principles of plot, character, setting, problem/resolution and message; and the expressive characteristics of simple emotions.

A2D2A190DFE50131835568A86D17958E.description: Identify the elements of personal and shared space, direction in space, quick and slow speed, firm and fine force; the principles of AB choreographic form and sequence; and the expressive qualities of mood and emotion.

A2D25F80DFE50131835468A86D17958E.description: Understand the sensory elements, organizational principles and expressive qualities of the arts.

A2D20EA0DFE50131835368A86D17958E.description: Know the language of the arts.
comments: Through observation, discussion, interpretation and analysis, students learn the "language" of the arts. They learn to understand how others express ideas in dance, drama, music and visual art forms. In addition to acquiring knowledge essential to performance and production, students become arts consumers (e.g., attending live performances or movies, purchasing paintings or jewelry, or visiting museums) who understand the basic elements and principles underlying artworks and are able to critique them.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for English Language Arts

9E90B070DFE501317B8868A86D17958E.description: Support and defend a thesis statement using various references including media and electronic resources.

9E906AC0DFE501317B8768A86D17958E.description: Using contemporary technology, create a research presentation or prepare a documentary related to academic, technical or occupational topics and present the findings in oral or multimedia formats.

9E901C30DFE501317B8668A86D17958E.description: Apply acquired information, concepts and ideas to communicate in a variety of formats.

9E8F8B90DFE501317B8468A86D17958E.description: Credit primary and secondary sources in a form appropriate for presentation or publication for a particular audience.

9E8FD1E0DFE501317B8568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the usefulness of information, synthesize information to support a thesis, and present information in a logical manner in oral and written forms.

9E8F41F0DFE501317B8368A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate information acquired from various sources.

9E8EF640DFE501317B8268A86D17958E.description: Research, design and present a project to an academic, business or school community audience on a topic selected from among contemporary issues.

9E8EA9E0DFE501317B8168A86D17958E.description: Develop a research plan using multiple forms of data.

9E8E60E0DFE501317B8068A86D17958E.description: Locate, organize, and use information from various sources to answer questions, solve problems and communicate ideas.

9E8E20A0DFE501317B7F68A86D17958E.description: Use the language arts to acquire, assess and communicate information.
comments: To be successful in school and in the world of work, students must be able to use a wide variety of information resources (written, visual and electronic). They must also know how to frame questions for inquiry, identify and organize relevant information and communicate it effectively in a variety of formats. These skills are critical in school across all learning areas and are key to successful career and lifelong learning experiences.

9E91F030DFE501317B8D68A86D17958E.description: Use verbal and nonverbal strategies to maintain communication and to resolve individual, group and workplace conflict (e.g., mediation skills, formal and informal bargaining skills).

9E91AED0DFE501317B8C68A86D17958E.description: Implement learned strategies to self-monitor communication anxiety and apprehension (e.g., relaxation and transference techniques, scripting, extemporaneous outlining, repetitive practice).

9E924C20DFE501317B8E68A86D17958E.description: Use speaking skills to participate in and lead group discussions; analyze the effectiveness of the spoken interactions based upon the ability of the group to achieve its goals.

9E917130DFE501317B8B68A86D17958E.description: Deliver planned and impromptu oral presentations, as individuals and members of a group, conveying results of research, projects or literature studies to a variety of audiences (e.g., peers, community, business/industry, local organizations)using appropriate visual aids and available technology.

9E913310DFE501317B8A68A86D17958E.description: Speak effectively using language appropriate to the situation and audience.

9E92E2C0DFE501317B9068A86D17958E.description: Use techniques for analysis, synthesis, and evaluation of oral messages.

9E9326B0DFE501317B9168A86D17958E.description: Use criteria to evaluate a variety of speakers' verbal and nonverbal messages.

9E929700DFE501317B8F68A86D17958E.description: Listen effectively in formal and informal situations.

9E90F0E0DFE501317B8968A86D17958E.description: Listen and speak effectively in a variety of situations.
comments: Of all the language arts, listening and speaking are those most often used on a daily basis at home, school and work or in the community. Skill in speaking is universally recognized as a primary indicator of a person's knowledge, skill and credibility. In person, by phone or through video, good listening and speaking skills are essential to sending, receiving and understanding messages. To understand messages spoken by others, students must be able to listen carefully, using specific techniques to clarify what they have heard. For speaking properly and making messages understood, grammar, sentence structure, tone, expression and emphasis must be part of students' repertoires.

9E8650C0DFE501317B6368A86D17958E.description: Write for real or potentially real situations in academic, professional and civic contexts (e.g., applications, job applications, business letters, resume, petitions).

9E85E780DFE501317B6268A86D17958E.description: Communicate information and ideas in narrative, informative and persuasive writing with clarity and effectiveness in a variety of written forms using appropriate traditional and/or electronic formats; adapt content, vocabulary, voice and tone to the audience, purpose and situation.

9E858BF0DFE501317B6168A86D17958E.description: Communicate ideas in writing to accomplish a variety of purposes.

9E850BD0DFE501317B5F68A86D17958E.description: Edit documents for clarity, subjectivity, pronoun-antecedent agreement, adverb and adjective agreement and verb tense; proofread for spelling, capitalization and punctuation; and ensure that documents are formatted in final form for submission and/or publication.

9E854C60DFE501317B6068A86D17958E.description: Expand ideas by using modifiers, subordination and standard paragraph organization.

9E84CA60DFE501317B5E68A86D17958E.description: Using contemporary technology, produce documents of publication quality for specific purposes and audiences; exhibit clarity of focus, logic of organization, appropriate elaboration and support and overall coherence.

9E848540DFE501317B5D68A86D17958E.description: Compose well-organized and coherent writing for specific purposes and audiences.

9E86DD40DFE501317B6568A86D17958E.description: Produce grammatically correct documents using standard manuscript specifications for a variety of purposes and audiences.

9E8696F0DFE501317B6468A86D17958E.description: Use correct grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization and structure.

9E843560DFE501317B5C68A86D17958E.description: Write to communicate for a variety of purposes.
comments: The ability to write clearly is essential to any person's effective communications. Students with high-level writing skills can produce documents that show planning and organization and effectively convey the intended message and meaning. Clear writing is critical to employment and production in today's world. Individuals must be capable of writing for a variety of audiences in differing styles, including standard rhetoric themes, business letters and reports, financial proposals and technical and professional communications. Students should be able to use word processors and computers to enhance their writing proficiency and improve their career opportunities.

9E890960DFE501317B6D68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge gained from literature as a means of understanding contemporary and historical economic, social and political issues and perspectives.

9E895C00DFE501317B6E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and express an interpretation of literary work.

9E88C870DFE501317B6C68A86D17958E.description: Read and interpret a variety of literary works.

9E87F7A0DFE501317B6968A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the influence of historical context on form, style and point of view for a variety of literary works.

9E888370DFE501317B6B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the development of form (e.g., short stories, essays, speeches, poetry, plays, novels) and purpose in American literature and literature of other countries.

9E883A50DFE501317B6A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate relationships between and among character plot, setting, theme, conflict and resolution and their influence on the effectiveness of a literary piece.

9E87B5D0DFE501317B6868A86D17958E.description: Compare and evaluate oral, written or viewed works from various eras and traditions and analyze complex literary devices (e.g., structures, images, forms, foreshadowing, flashbacks, stream of consciousness).

9E876880DFE501317B6768A86D17958E.description: Understand how literary elements and techniques are used to convey meaning.

9E872410DFE501317B6668A86D17958E.description: Read and understand literature representative of various societies, eras and ideas.
comments: Literature transmits ideas, reflects societies and eras and expresses the human imagination. It brings understanding, enrichment and joy. Appreciating literature and recognizing its many forms enable students to learn and respond to ideas, issues, perspectives and actions of others. Literature study includes understanding the structure and intent of a short poem or a long, complex book. By exploring the techniques that authors use to convey messages and evoke responses, students connect literature to their own lives and daily experiences.

9E8B55A0DFE501317B7468A86D17958E.description: Use tables, graphs and maps to challenge arguments, defend conclusions, and persuade others.

9E8A5680DFE501317B7168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate how authors and illustrators use text and art across materials to express their ideas (e.g., complex dialogue, persuasive techniques).

9E8AAB90DFE501317B7268A86D17958E.description: Summarize and make generalizations from content and relate them to the purpose of the material.

9E8BD950DFE501317B7668A86D17958E.description: Critically evaluate information from multiple sources.

9E8B97C0DFE501317B7568A86D17958E.description: Analyze and defend an interpretation of text.

9E8B0050DFE501317B7368A86D17958E.description: Use questions and predictions to guide reading across complex materials.

9E8A0830DFE501317B7068A86D17958E.description: Comprehend a broad range of reading materials.

9E8C9560DFE501317B7968A86D17958E.description: Read age-appropriate material with fluency and accuracy.

9E8CDE00DFE501317B7A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a variety of compositions for purpose, structure, content and details for use in school or at work.

9E8C5700DFE501317B7868A86D17958E.description: Analyze the defining characteristics and structures of a variety of complex literary genres and describe how genre affects the meaning and function of the texts.

9E8D20C0DFE501317B7B68A86D17958E.description: Relate reading to prior knowledge and experience and make connections to related information.

9E8C18D0DFE501317B7768A86D17958E.description: Apply reading strategies to improve understanding and fluency.

9E8DA1A0DFE501317B7D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the meaning of abstract concepts and the effects of particular word and phrase choices.

9E8DE2C0DFE501317B7E68A86D17958E.description: Identify and analyze new terminology applying knowledge of word origins and derivations in a variety of practical settings.

9E8D6050DFE501317B7C68A86D17958E.description: Apply word analysis and vocabulary skills to comprehend selections.

comments: Reading is essential. It is the process by which people gain information and ideas from books, newspapers, manuals, letters, contracts, advertisements and a host of other materials. Using strategies for constructing meaning before, during and after reading will help students connect what they read now with what they have learned in the past. Students who read well and widely build a strong foundation for learning in all areas of life.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Mathematics

9DBFD540DFE5013179D368A86D17958E.description: Determine the probability of an event involving "and", "or", or "not".

9DBF8EF0DFE5013179D268A86D17958E.description: Compare the likelihood of events in terms of certain, more likely, less likely or impossible.

9DBF3B00DFE5013179D168A86D17958E.description: Calculate the probability of a simple event.

9DBEF700DFE5013179D068A86D17958E.description: Determine, describe and apply the probabilities of events.

9DBE6C20DFE5013179CE68A86D17958E.description: Interpret results or make relevant decisions based on the data gathered.

9DBDDBE0DFE5013179CC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the data using mean, median, mode and range, as appropriate, with or without the use of technology.

9DBE2970DFE5013179CD68A86D17958E.description: Collect, organize and display data using tables, charts, bar graphs, line graphs, circle graphs, line plots and stem-and-leaf graphs.

9DBEB2E0DFE5013179CF68A86D17958E.description: Formulate questions of interest and select methods to systematically collect data.

9DBD8BA0DFE5013179CB68A86D17958E.description: Formulate questions, design data collection methods, gather and analyze data and communicate findings.

9DBD4700DFE5013179CA68A86D17958E.description: Make predictions and decisions based on data and communicate their reasoning.

9DBCBAE0DFE5013179C868A86D17958E.description: Using a data set, determine mean, median, mode and range, with and without the use of technology.

9DBD0170DFE5013179C968A86D17958E.description: Organize and display data using pictures, tallies, tables, charts, bar graphs, line graphs, line plots and stem-and-leaf graphs.

9DBC7400DFE5013179C768A86D17958E.description: Organize, describe and make predictions from existing data.

9DBC1DF0DFE5013179C668A86D17958E.description: Collect, organize and analyze data using statistical methods; predict results; and interpret uncertainty using concepts of probability.
comments: The ability to understand and interpret data (e.g., opinion polls, stock prices, tax rates, crime statistics, scientific studies, weather reports) grows more important each day. Students must be able to organize data, make sense of variables and patterns, and judge the logical reasonableness of any claims and interpretations made. Even very young students can count objects and communicate their findings with charts and graphs. Students of all ages can collect, display and interpret data to answer specific questions. They also must construct and analyze arguments that involve data and its interpretation. All students need to understand and apply the role probability plays in data collection and decision making. Data analysis and use are important abilities necessary for all careers.

9DC0CB80DFE5013179D668A86D17958E.description: Formulate logical arguments about geometric figures and patterns and communicate reasoning.

9DC08690DFE5013179D568A86D17958E.description: Construct convincing arguments and proofs to solve problems.

9DC17000DFE5013179D868A86D17958E.description: Compare geometric figures and determine their properties including parallel, perpendicular, similar, congruent and line symmetry.

9DC11A10DFE5013179D768A86D17958E.description: Identify, describe, classify and compare relationships using points, lines, planes and solids.

9DC213D0DFE5013179DA68A86D17958E.description: Describe and draw representations of geometric relationships, patterns, symmetries, and designs in two- and three-dimensions with and without technology.

9DC25750DFE5013179DB68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe how geometric figures are used in practical settings (e.g., construction, art, advertising).

9DC298C0DFE5013179DC68A86D17958E.description: Build physical models of two- and three-dimensional shapes.

9DC1C240DFE5013179D968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and apply geometric concepts involving points, lines, planes and space.

9DC02290DFE5013179D468A86D17958E.description: Use geometric methods to analyze, categorize and draw conclusions about points, lines, planes and space.
comments: Geometry provides important methods for reasoning and solving problems with points, lines, planes and space. The word "geometry" comes from Greek words meaning "measurement of the Earth." While we use modern technology and employ a wider variety of mathematical tools today, we still study geometry to understand the shapes and dimensions of our world. The applications of geometry are widespread in construction, engineering, architecture, mapmaking and art. Historically, geometry is a way to develop skill in forming convincing arguments and proofs. This goal of developing a means of argument and validation remains an important part of our reasons for studying geometry today.

9DB4C3E0DFE5013179AD68A86D17958E.description: Solve linear equations involving whole numbers.

9DB466F0DFE5013179AC68A86D17958E.description: Use algebraic concepts and procedures to represent and solve problems.

9DB5DC70DFE5013179B168A86D17958E.description: Explain operations and number properties including commutative, associative, distributive, transitive, zero, equality and order of operations.

9DB59DF0DFE5013179B068A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using systems of numbers and their properties.

9DB55CE0DFE5013179AF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a geometric pattern and express the results numerically.

9DB51970DFE5013179AE68A86D17958E.description: Interpret and describe numerical relationships using tables, graphs and symbols.

9DB42670DFE5013179AB68A86D17958E.description: Construct and solve number sentences using a variable to represent an unknown quantity.

9DB3E350DFE5013179AA68A86D17958E.description: Identify, describe, extend and create geometric and numeric patterns.

9DB399E0DFE5013179A968A86D17958E.description: Describe numerical relationships using variables and patterns.

comments: Algebra unites patterns and quantities in patterns with the means of describing change through the use of variables and functions. Its concepts and analytical methods allow people to consider general solutions to problems with common characteristics and develop related formulas. Algebra provides verbal, symbolic and graphical formats for discussing and representing settings as diverse as the pricing patterns of merchandise in a store, the behavior of a car as it accelerates or slows down, the changes in two chemicals as they react with one another, or the type of variation existing in a comparison of two factors in the economy. All people must be able to use algebraic methods to construct and examine tables of values; to interpret the relationships expressed by patterns in these tables; to relate change and variation in graphs and formulas; to reason about changes in quantities and the relationships involved in changes; and to find solutions to everyday problems using algebra's symbolic manipulation and formulas.
9DB33D80DFE5013179A868A86D17958E.description: Use algebraic and analytical methods to identify and describe patterns and relationships in data, solve problems and predict results.

9DB9E3D0DFE5013179BF68A86D17958E.description: Construct or draw figures with given perimeters and areas.

9DB99F80DFE5013179BE68A86D17958E.description: Describe relationships in a simple scale drawing.

9DB95AF0DFE5013179BD68A86D17958E.description: Select and use appropriate technology, instruments and formulas to solve problems, interpret results and communicate findings.

9DBB82B0DFE5013179C468A86D17958E.description: Estimate conversions between measures within the customary and metric systems.

9DBBCB90DFE5013179C568A86D17958E.description: Determine and communicate possible methods for estimating a given measure, selecting proper units in both customary and metric systems.

9DBB3E10DFE5013179C368A86D17958E.description: Estimate measurements and determine acceptable levels of accuracy.

9DBA9FF0DFE5013179C168A86D17958E.description: Solve addition, subtraction, multiplication and division problems using currency.

9DBAF6D0DFE5013179C268A86D17958E.description: Calculate, compare and convert length, perimeter, area, weight/mass and volume within the customary and metric systems.

9DBA2D60DFE5013179C068A86D17958E.description: Measure and compare quantities using appropriate units, instruments and methods.

9DB90E00DFE5013179BC68A86D17958E.description: Estimate, make and use measurements of objects, quantities and relationships and determine acceptable levels of accuracy.
comments: Measurement provides a way to answer questions about "how many," "how much" and "how far." It is an indispensable component of business, manufacturing, art, medicine and many other aspects of daily life. We describe the sizes, capacities and values of many things, from the large distances involved in space travel, to the very small quantities in computer design and microbiology, to the varying values of currencies in international monetary exchange. All people must be able to choose an appropriate level of accuracy for a measurement; to select what measuring instruments to use and to correctly determine the measures of objects, space and time. These activities require people to be able to use standard instruments including rulers, volume and capacity measures, timers and emerging measurement technologies found in the home and workplace.

9DB6BC50DFE5013179B468A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between two sets of data using ratios and appropriate notations (e.g., a/b, a to b, a:b).

9DB66070DFE5013179B368A86D17958E.description: Solve problems using comparison of quantities, ratios, proportions and percents.

9DB7A980DFE5013179B768A86D17958E.description: Show evidence that computational results using whole numbers, fractions and decimals are correct and/or that estimates are reasonable.

9DB76030DFE5013179B668A86D17958E.description: Select and perform computational procedures to solve problems with whole numbers, fractions and decimals.

9DB71090DFE5013179B568A86D17958E.description: Compute and estimate using mental mathematics, paper-and-pencil methods, calculators and computers.

9DB82F90DFE5013179B968A86D17958E.description: Solve one- and two-step problems involving whole numbers, fractions and decimals using additon, subtraction, multiplication and division.

9DB7EEE0DFE5013179B868A86D17958E.description: Investigate, represent and solve problems using number facts, operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and their properties, algorithms and relationships.

9DB8C930DFE5013179BB68A86D17958E.description: Compare and order whole numbers, fractions and decimals using concrete materials, drawings and mathematical symbols.

9DB88120DFE5013179BA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge and use of numbers and their representations in a broad range of theoretical and practical settings.

9DB619D0DFE5013179B268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and apply a knowledge and sense of numbers, including numeration and operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division), patterns, ratios and proportions.
comments: Numbers and operations on numbers play fundamental roles in helping us make sense of the world around us. Operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, as well as the ability to find powers and roots, extend the notion of numbers to create tools to model situations and solve problems in our everyday lives. Discussing and solving problems related to budgets, comparing prices on merchandise, understanding the nature of interest charges, measuring fuel consumption and calculating the trajectory for space travel would all be impossible without a sense of numbers and numerical operations. All people must develop this sense of numbers and operations and be able to use it to solve problems using mental computation, paper-and-pencil algorithms, calculators and computers.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards Incorporating the Common Core Math

9C2211F0DFE50131770B68A86D17958E.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

9C21CEF0DFE50131770A68A86D17958E.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
comments: Example: express 3 in the form 3 = 3/1; recognize that 6/1 = 6.
Example: locate 4/4 and 1 at the same point of a number line diagram.

9C218990DFE50131770968A86D17958E.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., 1/2 = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3). Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

9C212890DFE50131770868A86D17958E.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.

9C20C850DFE50131770768A86D17958E.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

9C2083D0DFE50131770668A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

9C2040D0DFE50131770568A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

9C1FFDA0DFE50131770468A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

9C1FBC30DFE50131770368A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

9C1F7760DFE50131770268A86D17958E.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100
For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as 1/4 of the area of the shape.
9C1ECAC0DFE50131770068A86D17958E.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

9C1E77F0DFE5013176FF68A86D17958E.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

9C1E1FD0DFE5013176FE68A86D17958E.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

9C1DA1D0DFE5013176FC68A86D17958E.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

9C1D5FA0DFE5013176FB68A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

9C1D1380DFE5013176FA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

9C1CD2F0DFE5013176F968A86D17958E.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

9C1C9150DFE5013176F868A86D17958E.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

9C1C4D60DFE5013176F768A86D17958E.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

9C1C08A0DFE5013176F668A86D17958E.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

9C1BB970DFE5013176F568A86D17958E.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

9C1B7020DFE5013176F468A86D17958E.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

9C1B1740DFE5013176F368A86D17958E.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

9C1AD9A0DFE5013176F268A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

9C1A9B70DFE5013176F168A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

9C199220DFE5013176ED68A86D17958E.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units— whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

comments: For example, draw a bar graph in which each square in the bar graph might represent 5 pets.
9C1936C0DFE5013176EC68A86D17958E.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

comments: Excludes multiplicative comparison problems (problems involving notions of "times as much";
Excludes compound units such as cm³ and finding the geometric volume of a container.
9C1A5980DFE5013176F068A86D17958E.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.

9C1A19B0DFE5013176EF68A86D17958E.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

9C19D7B0DFE5013176EE68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

9C1878D0DFE5013176E968A86D17958E.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10—90 (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

9C183770DFE5013176E868A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

9C17F3D0DFE5013176E768A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

9C17AB90DFE5013176E668A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
comments: A range of algorithms may be used.

9C1754C0DFE5013176E568A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.
For example, observe that 4 times a number is always even, and explain why 4 times a number can be decomposed into two equal addends.
9C16FC40DFE5013176E468A86D17958E.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.

9C16A3D0DFE5013176E368A86D17958E.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
comments: This standard is limited to problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers; students should know how to perform operations in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

9C165AC0DFE5013176E268A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

9C1616C0DFE5013176E168A86D17958E.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 × 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

comments: For example, find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8.
9C1571A0DFE5013176DF68A86D17958E.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.

9C152B10DFE5013176DE68A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
comments: Students need not use formal terms for these properties.
Example: Knowing that 8 × 5 = 40 and 8 × 2 = 16, one can find 8 × 7 as 8 × (5 + 2) = (8 × 5) + (8 × 2) = 40 + 16 = 56. (Distributive property.)

Example: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known (Commutative property of multiplication.) 3 × 5 × 2 can be found by 3 × 5 = 15, then 15 × 2 = 30, or by 5 × 2 = 10, then 3 × 10 = 30. (Associative property of multiplication.)

9C14ECA0DFE5013176DD68A86D17958E.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

9C14A5B0DFE5013176DC68A86D17958E.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
comments: For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 × ? = 48, 5 = ÷ 3, 6 × 6 = ?.

9C146510DFE5013176DB68A86D17958E.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

comments: For example, describe a context in which a number of shares or a number of groups can be expressed as 56 ÷ 8.
9C142110DFE5013176DA68A86D17958E.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.

9C13D950DFE5013176D968A86D17958E.description: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.
comments: For example, describe a context in which a total number of objects can be expressed as 5 × 7.

9C138890DFE5013176D868A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

9C12F880DFE5013176D668A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

9C12AC10DFE5013176D568A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

9C113E60DFE5013176D168A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

9C10A1C0DFE5013176CF68A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Social Science

9AB15FA0DFE50131745868A86D17958E.description: Explain how diverse groups have contributed to U.S. social systems over time.

9AB11350DFE50131745768A86D17958E.description: Describe ways in which a diverse U.S. population has developed and maintained common beliefs (e.g., life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness; the Constitution and the Bill of Rights).

9AB0BB50DFE50131745668A86D17958E.description: Understand how social systems form and develop over time.

9AB06D90DFE50131745568A86D17958E.description: Explain how social institutions contribute to the development and transmission of culture.

9AB00D40DFE50131745468A86D17958E.description: Analyze how individuals and groups interact with and within institutions (e.g., educational, military).

9AAFBBD0DFE50131745368A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles and interactions of individuals and groups in society.

9AAF4E00DFE50131745268A86D17958E.description: Explain how language, literature, the arts, architecture and traditions contribute to the development and transmission of culture.

9AAEEF60DFE50131745168A86D17958E.description: Compare characteristics of culture as reflected in language, literature, the arts, traditions and institutions.

comments: A study of social systems has two important aspects that help people understand their roles as individuals and members of society. The first aspect is culture consisting of the language, literature, arts and traditions of various groups of people. Students should understand common characteristics of different cultures and explain how cultural contributions shape societies over time. The second aspect is the interaction among individuals, groups and institutions. Students should know how and why groups and institutions are formed, what roles they play in society, and how individuals and groups interact with and influence institutions.
9AAEAAE0DFE50131745068A86D17958E.description: Understand social systems, with an emphasis on the United States.

9AAE6820DFE50131744F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how interactions of geographic factors have shaped present conditions.

9AAE2180DFE50131744E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how and why spatial patterns of settlement change over time.

9AADD450DFE50131744D68A86D17958E.description: Understand the historical significance of geography.

9AAD7420DFE50131744C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how human processes influence settlement patterns including migration and population growth.

9AAD2690DFE50131744B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how patterns of resources are used throughout the world.

9AACD900DFE50131744A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how human activity is affected by geographic factors.

9AAC9050DFE50131744968A86D17958E.description: Understand relationships between geographic factors and society.

9AAC4950DFE50131744868A86D17958E.description: Explain how changes in components of an ecosystem affect the system overall.

9AAC0650DFE50131744768A86D17958E.description: Explain how physical processes including climate, plate tectonics, erosion, soil formation, water cycle, and circulation patterns in the ocean shape patterns in the environment and influence availability and quality of natural resources.

9AABC280DFE50131744668A86D17958E.description: Analyze and explain characteristics and interactions of the Earth's physical systems.

9AAB6F80DFE50131744568A86D17958E.description: Explain how to make and use geographic representations to provide and enhance spatial information including maps, graphs, charts, models, aerial photographs, satellite images.

9AAB29D0DFE50131744468A86D17958E.description: Explain how people use geographic markers and boundaries to analyze and navigate the Earth (e.g., hemispheres, meridians, continents, bodies of water).

9AAADA10DFE50131744368A86D17958E.description: Locate, describe and explain places, regions and features on the Earth.

9AAA8860DFE50131744268A86D17958E.description: Understand world geography and the effects of geography on society, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: The need for geographic literacy has never been greater or more obvious than in today's tightly interrelated world. Students must understand the world's physical features, how they blend with social systems and how they affect economies, politics and human interaction. Isolated geographic facts are not enough. To grasp geography and its effect on individuals and societies, students must know the broad concepts of spatial patterns, mapping, population and physical systems (land, air, water). The combination of geographic facts and broad concepts provides a deeper understanding of geography and its effects on individuals and societies.

9AAA3600DFE50131744168A86D17958E.description: Explain how expanded European and Asian contacts affected the environment of both continents, 1000 BCE - 1500 CE.

9AA9E620DFE50131744068A86D17958E.description: Describe how the people of the Huang He, Tigris-Euphrates, Nile and Indus river valleys shaped their environments during the agricultural revolution, 4000 - 1000 BCE.

9AA99750DFE50131743F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of urbanization and suburbanization, 1850 - present, on the environment.

9AA953E0DFE50131743E68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the largely rural population of the United States adapted, used and changed the environment after 1818.

9AA90E50DFE50131743D68A86D17958E.description: Describe how early settlers in Illinois and the United States adapted to, used and changed the environment prior to 1818.

9AA8C9B0DFE50131743C68A86D17958E.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world environmental history.

9AA87C00DFE50131743B68A86D17958E.description: Identify the origins and analyze consequences of events that have shaped world social history including famines, migrations, plagues, slave trading.

9AA81C90DFE50131743A68A86D17958E.description: Describe characteristics of different kinds of families in America during the colonial/frontier periods and the 19th century.

9AA7CA80DFE50131743968A86D17958E.description: Describe characteristics of different kinds of communities in various sections of America during the colonial/frontier periods and the 19th century.

9AA78A30DFE50131743868A86D17958E.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world social history.

9AA74740DFE50131743768A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of technology (e.g., weaponry, transportation, printing press, microchips) in different parts of the world, 1500 - present.

9AA704E0DFE50131743668A86D17958E.description: Describe the economic systems and trade patterns of North America, South America and Mesoamerica before the encounter with the Europeans.

9AA6C210DFE50131743568A86D17958E.description: Describe major economic trends from 1000 to 1500 CE including long distance trade, banking, specialization of labor, commercialization, urbanization and tech-nological and scientific progress.

9AA67C70DFE50131743468A86D17958E.description: Describe how economic developments and government policies after 1865 affected the country's economic institutions including corporations, banks and organized labor.

9AA62090DFE50131743368A86D17958E.description: Explain relationships among the American economy and slavery, immigration, industrialization, labor and urbanization, 1700-present.

9AA5D5B0DFE50131743268A86D17958E.description: Describe economic motivations that attracted Europeans and others to the Americas, 1500-1750.

9AA58500DFE50131743168A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of economic systems.

9AA53880DFE50131743068A86D17958E.description: Describe political effects of European exploration and expansion on the Americas, Asia, and Africa after 1500 CE.

9AA4E860DFE50131742F68A86D17958E.description: Identify causes and effects of European feudalism and the emergence of nation states between 500 CE and 1500 CE.

9AA49F10DFE50131742E68A86D17958E.description: Identify causes and effects of the decline of the Roman empire and other major world political events (e.g., rise of the Islamic empire, rise and decline of the T'ang dynasty, establishment of the kingdom of Ghana) between 500 CE and 1500 CE.

9AA45230DFE50131742D68A86D17958E.description: Compare the political characteristics of Greek and Roman civilizations with non-Western civilizations, including the early Han dynasty and Gupta empire, between 500 BCE and 500 CE.

9AA411E0DFE50131742C68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways in which the United States developed as a world political power.

9AA3D180DFE50131742B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the way the Constitution has changed over time as a result of amendments and Supreme Court decisions.

9AA38F90DFE50131742A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how and why the colonies fought for their independence and how the colonists' ideas are reflected in the Declaration of Independence and the United States Constitution.

9AA34D60DFE50131742968A86D17958E.description: Describe how different groups competed for power within the colonies and how that competition led to the development of political institutions during the early national period.

9AA309F0DFE50131742868A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of significant political events.

9AA2BDE0DFE50131742768A86D17958E.description: Identify the differences between historical fact and interpretation.

9AA24A10DFE50131742668A86D17958E.description: Make inferences about historical events and eras using historical maps and other historical sources.

9AA1F7C0DFE50131742568A86D17958E.description: Describe how historians use models for organizing historical interpretation (e.g., biographies, political events, issues and conflicts).

9AA1B6E0DFE50131742468A86D17958E.description: Apply the skills of historical analysis and interpretation.

9AA172D0DFE50131742368A86D17958E.description: Understand events, trends, individuals and movements shaping the history of Illinois, the United States and other nations.
comments: George Santayana said "those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it." In a broader sense, students who can examine and analyze the events of the past have a powerful tool for understanding the events of today and the future. They develop an understanding of how people, nations, actions and interactions have led to today's realities. In the process, they can better define their own roles as participating citizens.

9AA0D340DFE50131742168A86D17958E.description: Explain how laws and government policies (e.g., property rights, contract enforcement, standard weights/measurements) establish rules that help a market economy function effectively.

9AA09030DFE50131742068A86D17958E.description: Identify the types of taxes levied by differing levels of governments (e.g., income tax, sales tax, property tax).

9AA04D50DFE50131741F68A86D17958E.description: Understand the impact of government policies and decisions on production and consumption in the economy.

9AA00900DFE50131741E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how workers can affect their productivity through training and by using tools, machinery and technology.

9A9FC6C0DFE50131741D68A86D17958E.description: Explain how comparative advantage forms the basis for specialization and trade among nations.

9A9F81F0DFE50131741C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of increasing and declining imports and exports to an individual and to the nation's economy as a whole.

9A9F3760DFE50131741B68A86D17958E.description: Understand trade as an exchange of goods or services.

9A9EE710DFE50131741A68A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the effects of various incentives to produce a good or service.

9A9EA440DFE50131741968A86D17958E.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by producers.

9A9E5EF0DFE50131741868A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of choice and competition on individuals and the economy as a whole.

9A9E1140DFE50131741768A86D17958E.description: Describe the "market clearing price" of a good or service.

9A9DC670DFE50131741668A86D17958E.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by consumers.

9A9D6B20DFE50131741568A86D17958E.description: Describe the causes of unemployment (e.g., seasonal fluctuation in demand, changing jobs, changing skill requirements, national spending).

9A9D1060DFE50131741468A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between consumer purchases and businesses paying for productive resources.

9A9CBD00DFE50131741368A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between productivity and wages.

9A9C6ED0DFE50131741268A86D17958E.description: Explain how market prices signal producers about what, how and how much to produce.

9A9C2E50DFE50131741168A86D17958E.description: Understand how different economic systems operate in the exchange, production, distribution and consumption of goods and services.

9A9BE9C0DFE50131741068A86D17958E.description: Understand economic systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: Why This Goal Is Important: People's lives are directly affected by the economies of cities, states, nations and the world. All people engage in economic activity: buying, selling, trading, producing and consuming. By understanding economic systems-and how economics blends with other social sciences, students will be able to make more informed choices, prudently use resources and function as effective participants in the economies around them.

9A9BA1D0DFE50131740F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how United States political ideas and traditions were instituted in the Constitution and the Bill of Rights.

9A9B53D0DFE50131740E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze historical influences on the development of political ideas and practices as enumerated in the Declaration of Independence, the United States Constitution, the Bill of Rights and the Illinois Constitution.

9A9B12A0DFE50131740D68A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of United States political ideas and traditions.

9A9ACC00DFE50131740C68A86D17958E.description: Compare the basic principles of the United States and its international interests (e.g., territory, environment, trade, use of technology).

9A9A88E0DFE50131740B68A86D17958E.description: Understand United States foreign policy as it relates to other nations and international issues.

9A9A4570DFE50131740A68A86D17958E.description: Describe roles and influences of individuals, groups and media in shaping current Illinois and United States public policy (e.g., general public opinion, special interest groups, formal parties, media).

9A99FF40DFE50131740968A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles and influences of individuals and interest groups in the political systems of Illinois, the United States and other nations.

9A99B3A0DFE50131740868A86D17958E.description: Compare historical issues involving rights, roles and status of individuals in relation to municipalities, states and the nation.

9A993450DFE50131740768A86D17958E.description: Understand election processes and responsibilities of citizens.

9A98E990DFE50131740668A86D17958E.description: Identify and compare the basic political systems of Illinois and the United States as prescribed in their constitutions.

9A989E90DFE50131740568A86D17958E.description: Understand the structures and functions of the political systems of Illinois, the United States and other nations.

9A985490DFE50131740468A86D17958E.description: Describe how responsibilities are shared and limited by the United States and Illinois Constitutions and significant court decisions.

9A9805D0DFE50131740368A86D17958E.description: Understand and explain basic principles of the United States government.

9A97B470DFE50131740268A86D17958E.description: Understand political systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: The existence and advancement of a free society depend on the knowledge, skills and understanding of its citizenry. Through the study of various forms and levels of government and the documents and institutions of the United States, students will develop the skills and knowledge that they need to be contributing citizens, now and in the future.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Social Science

9AD5ED50DFE5013174A968A86D17958E.description: Analyze major contemporary cultural exchanges as influenced by worldwide communications.

9AD59AA0DFE5013174A868A86D17958E.description: Analyze major cultural exchanges of the past (e.g., Colombian exchange, the Silk Road, the Crusades).

9AD53EB0DFE5013174A768A86D17958E.description: Understand how social systems form and develop over time.

9AD4F350DFE5013174A668A86D17958E.description: Analyze various forms of institutions (e.g., educational, military, charitable, governmental).

9AD4B0E0DFE5013174A568A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles and interactions of individuals and groups in society.

9AD46F50DFE5013174A468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the influence of cultural factors including customs, traditions, language, media, art and architecture in developing pluralistic societies.

9AD42F60DFE5013174A368A86D17958E.description: Compare characteristics of culture as reflected in language, literature, the arts, traditions and institutions.
