9AD3EA40DFE5013174A268A86D17958E.description: Understand social systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: A study of social systems has two important aspects that help people understand their roles as individuals and members of society. The first aspect is culture consisting of the language, literature, arts and traditions of various groups of people. Students should understand common characteristics of different cultures and explain how cultural contributions shape societies over time. The second aspect is the interaction among individuals, groups and institutions. Students should know how and why groups and institutions are formed, what roles they play in society, and how individuals and groups interact with and influence institutions.

9AD39FB0DFE5013174A168A86D17958E.description: Explain how processes of spatial change have affected human history (e.g., resource development and use, natural disasters).

9AD35DF0DFE5013174A068A86D17958E.description: Understand the historical significance of geography.

9AD31EB0DFE50131749F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how places with various population distributions function as centers of economic activity (e.g., rural, suburban, urban).

9AD2DF00DFE50131749E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze growth trends in selected urban areas as they relate to geographic factors.

9AD29E10DFE50131749D68A86D17958E.description: Explain the ability of modern technology to alter geographic features and the impacts of these modifications on human activities.

9AD25D80DFE50131749C68A86D17958E.description: Understand relationships between geographic factors and society.

9AD21450DFE50131749B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze trends in world demographics as they relate to physical systems.

9AD1D380DFE50131749A68A86D17958E.description: Explain the dynamic interactions within and among the Earth's physical systems including variation, productivity and constructive and destructive processes.

9AD19370DFE50131749968A86D17958E.description: Analyze and explain characteristics and interactions of the Earth's physical systems.

9AD15280DFE50131749868A86D17958E.description: Use maps and other geographic instruments and technologies to analyze spatial patterns and distributions on earth.

9AD10720DFE50131749768A86D17958E.description: Use mental maps of physical features to answer complex geographic questions (e.g., how physical features have deterred or enabled migration).

9AD0B900DFE50131749668A86D17958E.description: Locate, describe and explain places, regions and features on the Earth.

9AD06540DFE50131749568A86D17958E.description: Understand world geography and the effects of geography on society, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: The need for geographic literacy has never been greater or more obvious than in today's tightly interrelated world. Students must understand the world's physical features, how they blend with social systems and how they affect economies, politics and human interaction. Isolated geographic facts are not enough. To grasp geography and its effect on individuals and societies, students must know the broad concepts of spatial patterns, mapping, population and physical systems (land, air, water). The combination of geographic facts and broad concepts provides a deeper understanding of geography and its effects on individuals and societies.

9AD01380DFE50131749468A86D17958E.description: Describe how migration has altered the world's environment since 1450.

9ACFBA80DFE50131749368A86D17958E.description: Describe how cultural encounters among peoples of the world (e.g., Colombian exchange, opening of China and Japan to external trade, building of Suez canal) affected the environment, 1500 - present.

9ACF4E90DFE50131749268A86D17958E.description: Describe different and sometimes competing views, as substantiated by scientific fact, that people in North America have historically held towards the environment (e.g., private and public land ownership and use, resource use vs. preservation).

9ACEFE00DFE50131749168A86D17958E.description: Describe the causes and effects of conservation and environmental movements in the United States, 1900 - present.

9ACEAC20DFE50131749068A86D17958E.description: Compare depictions of the natural environment that are found in myths, legends, folklore and traditions.

9ACE5D70DFE50131748F68A86D17958E.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world environmental history.

9ACE1AF0DFE50131748E68A86D17958E.description: Identify significant events and developments since 1500 that altered world social history in ways that persist today including colonization, Protestant Reformation, industrialization, the rise of technology and human rights movements.

9ACDD560DFE50131748D68A86D17958E.description: Describe unintended social consequences of political events in United States history (e.g., Civil War/emancipation, National Defense Highway Act/decline of inner cities, Vietnam War/anti-government activity).

9ACD9190DFE50131748C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the immediate and long-range social impacts of slavery.

9ACD46D0DFE50131748B68A86D17958E.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world social history.

9ACCF700DFE50131748A68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the maturing economies of Western Europe and Japan led to colonialism and imperialism.

9ACCAAA0DFE50131748968A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of key individuals/ideas from 1500 - present, including Adam Smith, Karl Marx and John Maynard Keynes.

9ACC6590DFE50131748868A86D17958E.description: Compare socialism and communism in Europe, America, Asia and Africa after 1815 CE.

9ACC20A0DFE50131748768A86D17958E.description: Describe the growing dominance of American and European capitalism and their institutions after 1500.

9ACBCE30DFE50131748668A86D17958E.description: Describe how American economic institutions were shaped by industrialists, union leaders and groups including Southern migrants, Dust Bowl refugees, agricultural workers from Mexico and female workers since 1914.

9ACB84B0DFE50131748568A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of westward expansion on the United States economy.

9ACB3590DFE50131748468A86D17958E.description: Explain how trade patterns developed between the Americas and the rest of the global economy, 1500 - 1840.

9ACAE520DFE50131748368A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of economic systems.

9ACAA350DFE50131748268A86D17958E.description: Identify political ideas from the early modern historical era to the present which have had worldwide impact (e.g., nationalism/Sun Yat-Sen, non-violence/Ghandi, independence/Kenyatta).

9ACA5F40DFE50131748168A86D17958E.description: Identify political ideas that began during the Renaissance and the Enlightenment and that persist today (e.g., church/state relationships).

9ACA0D30DFE50131748068A86D17958E.description: Identify political ideas that have dominated United States historical eras (e.g., Federalist, Jacksonian, Progressivist, New Deal, New Conservative).

9AC9AA30DFE50131747F68A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of significant political events.

9AC95B40DFE50131747E68A86D17958E.description: Compare competing historical interpretations of an event.

9AC90C30DFE50131747D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and report historical events to determine cause-and-effect relationships.

9AC8C800DFE50131747C68A86D17958E.description: Apply the skills of historical analysis and interpretation.

9AC88070DFE50131747B68A86D17958E.description: Understand events, trends, individuals and movements shaping the history of Illinois, the United States and other nations.
comments: George Santayana said "those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it." In a broader sense, students who can examine and analyze the events of the past have a powerful tool for understanding the events of today and the future. They develop an understanding of how people, nations, actions and interactions have led to today's realities. In the process, they can better define their own roles as participating citizens.

9AC839D0DFE50131747A68A86D17958E.description: Describe social and environmental benefits and consequences of production and con-sumption.

9AC7F000DFE50131747968A86D17958E.description: Explain why government may intervene in a market economy.

9AC7A620DFE50131747868A86D17958E.description: Understand the impact of government policies and decisions on production and consumption in the economy.

9AC74C30DFE50131747768A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of worker productivity (output per worker) on business, the worker and the consumer.

9AC70430DFE50131747668A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationships between the availability and price of a nation's resources and its comparative advantage in relation to other nations.

9AC6B680DFE50131747568A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning and importance of "balance of trade" and how trade surpluses and deficits between nations are determined.

9AC66D30DFE50131747468A86D17958E.description: Understand trade as an exchange of goods or services.

9AC61BF0DFE50131747368A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of research, development, invention, technology and entrepreneurship to the United States economy.

9AC5C4D0DFE50131747268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of political actions and natural phenomena (e.g., wars, legislation, natural disaster) on producers and production decisions.

9AC58140DFE50131747168A86D17958E.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by producers.

9AC54000DFE50131747068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of current events (e.g., weather/natural disasters, wars) on consumer prices.

9AC4FCC0DFE50131746F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the costs and benefits of making consumer purchases through differing means (e.g., credit, cash).

9AC4B710DFE50131746E68A86D17958E.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by consumers.

9AC46800DFE50131746D68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of unemployment on the economy.

9AC41F60DFE50131746C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of inflation on an individual and the economy as a whole.

9AC387F0DFE50131746A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how national economies vary in the extent that government and private markets help allocate goods, services and resources.

9AC34870DFE50131746968A86D17958E.description: Understand how different economic systems operate in the exchange, production, distribution and consumption of goods and services.

9AC30600DFE50131746868A86D17958E.description: Understand economic systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: Why This Goal Is Important: People's lives are directly affected by the economies of cities, states, nations and the world. All people engage in economic activity: buying, selling, trading, producing and consuming. By understanding economic systems-and how economics blends with other social sciences, students will be able to make more informed choices, prudently use resources and function as effective participants in the economies around them.

9AC2C540DFE50131746768A86D17958E.description: Describe how United States' political ideas, practices and technologies have extended rights for Americans in the 20th century (e.g., suffrage, civil rights, motor-voter registration).

9AC282D0DFE50131746668A86D17958E.description: Determine the historical events and processes that brought about changes in United States political ideas and traditions (e.g., the New Deal, Civil War).

9AC23310DFE50131746568A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of United States political ideas and traditions.

9AC1E750DFE50131746468A86D17958E.description: Analyze historical trends of United States foreign policy (e.g., emergence as a world leader - military, industrial, financial).

9AC1A1F0DFE50131746368A86D17958E.description: Understand United States foreign policy as it relates to other nations and international issues.

9AC15410DFE50131746268A86D17958E.description: Analyze roles and influences of individuals, groups and media in shaping current debates on state and national policies.

9AC10A70DFE50131746168A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles and influences of individuals and interest groups in the political systems of Illinois, the United States and other nations.

9AC0BC50DFE50131746068A86D17958E.description: Describe the meaning of participatory citizenship (e.g., volunteerism, voting) at all levels of government and society in the United States.

9AC06E10DFE50131745F68A86D17958E.description: Understand election processes and responsibilities of citizens.

9AC01E10DFE50131745E68A86D17958E.description: Compare the political systems of the United States to other nations.

9ABFCD10DFE50131745D68A86D17958E.description: Understand the structures and functions of the political systems of Illinois, the United States and other nations.

9ABF7340DFE50131745C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how local, state and national governments serve the purposes for which they were created.

9ABF2210DFE50131745B68A86D17958E.description: Understand and explain basic principles of the United States government.

9ABEC9F0DFE50131745A68A86D17958E.description: Understand political systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: The existence and advancement of a free society depend on the knowledge, skills and understanding of its citizenry. Through the study of various forms and levels of government and the documents and institutions of the United States, students will develop the skills and knowledge that they need to be contributing citizens, now and in the future.
