document.title: Illinois Learning Standards Incorporating the Common Core English Language Arts

9EDD30C0DFE501317C2B68A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts.

9EDCD940DFE501317C2A68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs describing the same general action (e.g., walk, march, strut, prance) by acting out the meanings.

9EDC8700DFE501317C2968A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at school that are colorful).

9EDC2F90DFE501317C2868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their opposites (antonyms).

9EDBD7A0DFE501317C2768A86D17958E.description: Sort common objects into categories (e.g., shapes, foods) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

9EDB8B60DFE501317C2668A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

9EDB3F90DFE501317C2568A86D17958E.description: Use the most frequently occurring inflections and affixes (e.g., -ed, -s, re-, un-, pre-, -ful, -less) as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word.

9EDAE750DFE501317C2468A86D17958E.description: Identify new meanings for familiar words and apply them accurately (e.g., knowing duck is a bird and learning the verb to duck).

9EDA9C30DFE501317C2368A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on kindergarten reading and content.

9ED95AB0DFE501317C1F68A86D17958E.description: Spell simple words phonetically, drawing on knowledge of sound-letter relationships.

9ED8DD90DFE501317C1E68A86D17958E.description: Write a letter or letters for most consonant and short-vowel sounds (phonemes).

9ED84620DFE501317C1C68A86D17958E.description: Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I.

9ED7FAF0DFE501317C1B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

9ED7AB20DFE501317C1A68A86D17958E.description: Produce and expand complete sentences in shared language activities.

9ED758E0DFE501317C1968A86D17958E.description: Use the most frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., to, from, in, out, on, off, for, of, by, with).

9ED70F20DFE501317C1868A86D17958E.description: Understand and use question words (interrogatives) (e.g., who, what, where, when, why, how).

9ED6C560DFE501317C1768A86D17958E.description: Form regular plural nouns orally by adding /s/ or /es/ (e.g., dog, dogs; wish, wishes).

9ED67D80DFE501317C1668A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring nouns and verbs.

9ED63440DFE501317C1568A86D17958E.description: Print many upper- and lowercase letters.

9ED5E390DFE501317C1468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

9ED4EDE0DFE501317C1168A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

9ED49880DFE501317C1068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

9ED43A20DFE501317C0F68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

9ED37650DFE501317C0D68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

9ED2B2E0DFE501317C0B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

9ED26440DFE501317C0A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

9ED1C760DFE501317C0868A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

9ED18040DFE501317C0768A86D17958E.description: Speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly.

9ED131F0DFE501317C0668A86D17958E.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions as desired to provide additional detail.

9ED0E760DFE501317C0568A86D17958E.description: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events and, with prompting and support, provide additional detail.

9ED04950DFE501317C0368A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.

9ED00030DFE501317C0268A86D17958E.description: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by asking and answering questions about key details and requesting clarification if something is not understood.

9ECFAAC0DFE501317C0168A86D17958E.description: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.

9ECF56A0DFE501317C0068A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking about the topics and texts under discussion).

9ECF00E0DFE501317BFF68A86D17958E.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about kindergarten topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

9ECE1480DFE501317BFC68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

9ECDBF50DFE501317BFB68A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

9ECD45E0DFE501317BFA68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

9ECC9510DFE501317BF868A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

9ECC4F50DFE501317BF768A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

9ECC0770DFE501317BF668A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

9ECB7220DFE501317BF468A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

9ECA1DF0DFE501317BF068A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

9EC9CB50DFE501317BEF68A86D17958E.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of books by a favorite author and express opinions about them).

9EC98120DFE501317BEE68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

9EC8D720DFE501317BEC68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

9EC88860DFE501317BEB68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

9EC7A320DFE501317BE968A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a single event or several loosely linked events, tell about the events in the order in which they occurred, and provide a reaction to what happened.

9EC73350DFE501317BE868A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative/explanatory texts in which they name what they are writing about and supply some information about the topic.

9EC6E400DFE501317BE768A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose opinion pieces in which they tell a reader the topic or the name of the book they are writing about and state an opinion or preference about the topic or book (e.g., My favorite book is…).

9EC5F760DFE501317BE468A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

9EC53850DFE501317BE268A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

9EC4DEB0DFE501317BE168A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

9EC49380DFE501317BE068A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

9EC447E0DFE501317BDF68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

9EC3F980DFE501317BDE68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

9EC3A8B0DFE501317BDD68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

9EC361A0DFE501317BDC68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

9EC2CE20DFE501317BDA68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

9EC27E40DFE501317BD968A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

9EC21310DFE501317BD868A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

9EC13050DFE501317BD668A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

9EC0D130DFE501317BD568A86D17958E.description: Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.

9EC02BF0DFE501317BD368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.

9EBFE550DFE501317BD268A86D17958E.description: Read common high-frequency words by sight (e.g., the, of, to, you, she, my, is, are, do, does).

9EBF9910DFE501317BD168A86D17958E.description: Associate the long and short sounds with common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.

9EBF4640DFE501317BD068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing the primary or many of the most frequent sound for each consonant.

9EBEF770DFE501317BCF68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

9EBE5330DFE501317BCD68A86D17958E.description: Add or substitute individual sounds (phonemes) in simple, one-syllable words to make new words.

9EBDF550DFE501317BCC68A86D17958E.description: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in three-phoneme (consonent-vowel-consonent, or CVC) words. (This does not include CVCs ending with /l/, /r/, or /x/.)

9EBD9130DFE501317BCB68A86D17958E.description: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.

9EBD3B70DFE501317BCA68A86D17958E.description: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.

9EBC7A60DFE501317BC868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

9EBBB790DFE501317BC668A86D17958E.description: Recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.

9EBB6BC0DFE501317BC568A86D17958E.description: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.

9EBB1EE0DFE501317BC468A86D17958E.description: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.

9EBAC860DFE501317BC368A86D17958E.description: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.

9EBA7C20DFE501317BC268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

9EB99420DFE501317BBF68A86D17958E.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

9EB93F40DFE501317BBE68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

9EB8CE50DFE501317BBD68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

9EB877C0DFE501317BBC68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

9EB81CF0DFE501317BBB68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear (e.g., what person, place, thing, or idea in the text an illustration depicts).

9EB77D70DFE501317BB968A86D17958E.description: Name the author and illustrator of a text and define the role of each in presenting the ideas or information in a text.

9EB72860DFE501317BB868A86D17958E.description: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.

9EB6D720DFE501317BB768A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

9EB632A0DFE501317BB568A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

9EB5DE50DFE501317BB468A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

9EB586C0DFE501317BB368A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

9EB4AFD0DFE501317BB068A86D17958E.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

9EB45E50DFE501317BAF68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

9EB3B6E0DFE501317BAD68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories.

9EB36470DFE501317BAC68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear (e.g., what moment in a story an illustration depicts).

9EB2C060DFE501317BAA68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, name the author and illustrator of a story and define the role of each in telling the story.

9EB27210DFE501317BA968A86D17958E.description: Recognize common types of texts (e.g., storybooks, poems).

9EB21620DFE501317BA868A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

9EB183B0DFE501317BA668A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and major events in a story.

9EB13240DFE501317BA568A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, retell familiar stories, including key details.

9EB0C200DFE501317BA468A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

9EAFDC20DFE501317BA168A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

9EAF9640DFE501317BA068A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

9EAF4DE0DFE501317B9F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

9EAF0350DFE501317B9E68A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

9EAEAAC0DFE501317B9D68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

9EAE1AE0DFE501317B9B68A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

9EADD070DFE501317B9A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

9EAD8550DFE501317B9968A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

9EACE230DFE501317B9768A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

9EAC93F0DFE501317B9668A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

9EAC3FF0DFE501317B9568A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

9EAB80A0DFE501317B9368A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Social/Emotional Development

A3E2A4B0DFE50131857068A86D17958E.description: Work cooperatively with others to plan, implement, and evaluate a project that addresses an identified need in the broader community.

A3E25760DFE50131856F68A86D17958E.description: Work cooperatively with others to plan, implement, and evaluate a project to meet an identified school need.

A3E216C0DFE50131856E68A86D17958E.description: Contribute to the well-being of one's school and community.

A3E1D550DFE50131856D68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate how responsible decision making affects interpersonal and group relationships.

A3E19260DFE50131856C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how present decision making affects college and career choices.

A3E14F60DFE50131856B68A86D17958E.description: Apply decision-making skills to deal responsibly with daily academic and social situations.

A3E10A00DFE50131856A68A86D17958E.description: Examine how the norms of different societies and cultures influence their members' decisions and behaviors.

A3E0C3C0DFE50131856968A86D17958E.description: Apply ethical reasoning to evaluate societal practices.

A3E07360DFE50131856868A86D17958E.description: Consider ethical, safety, and societal factors in making decisions.

A3E02D10DFE50131856768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate decision-making skills and responsible behaviors in personal, school, and community contexts.
comments: Promoting one's own health, avoiding risky behaviors, dealing honestly and fairly with others, and contributing to the good of one's classroom, school, family, community, and environment are essential to citizenship in a democratic society. Achieving these outcomes requires an ability to make decisions and solve problems on the basis of accurately defining decisions to be made, generating alternative solutions, anticipating the consequences of each, and evaluating and learning from one's decision making.

A3DFE560DFE50131856668A86D17958E.description: Evaluate current conflict-resolution skills and plan how to improve them.

A3DF9B40DFE50131856568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the effects of using negotiation skills to reach win-win solutions.

A3DF5060DFE50131856468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an ability to prevent, manage, and resolve interpersonal conflicts in constructive ways.

A3DEF2B0DFE50131856368A86D17958E.description: Plan, implement, and evaluate participation in a group project.

A3DE9FA0DFE50131856268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the application of communication and social skills in daily interactions with peers, teachers, and families.

A3DE5BB0DFE50131856168A86D17958E.description: Use communication and social skills to interact effectively with others.

A3DE1670DFE50131856068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate how advocacy for the rights of others contributes to the common good.

A3DDD140DFE50131855F68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate strategies for being respectful of others and opposing stereotyping and prejudice.

A3DD9500DFE50131855E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize individual and group similarities and differences.

A3DD5590DFE50131855D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ways to express empathy for others.

A3DCFDD0DFE50131855C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to express understanding of those who hold different opinions.

A3DCB770DFE50131855B68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the feelings and perspectives of others.

A3DC7360DFE50131855A68A86D17958E.description: Use social-awareness and interpersonal skills to establish and maintain positive relationships.
comments: Building and maintaining positive relationships with others are central to success in school and life and require the ability to recognize the thoughts, feelings, and perspectives of others, including those different from one's own. In addition, establishing positive peer, family, and work relationships requires skills in cooperating, communicating respectfully, and constructively resolving conflicts with others.

A3DC30E0DFE50131855968A86D17958E.description: Monitor progress toward achieving a goal, and evaluate one's performance against criteria.

A3DBEC40DFE50131855868A86D17958E.description: Set a post-secondary goal with action steps, timeframes, and criteria for evaluating achievement.

A3DBA800DFE50131855768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate skills related to achieving personal and academic goals.

A3DB60F0DFE50131855668A86D17958E.description: Evaluate how developing interests and filling useful roles support school and life success.

A3DAE9A0DFE50131855568A86D17958E.description: Implement a plan to build on a strength, meet a need, or address a challenge.

A3DA9CA0DFE50131855468A86D17958E.description: Recognize personal qualities and external supports.

A3DA4F80DFE50131855368A86D17958E.description: Evaluate how expressing more positive attitudes influences others.

A3DA0250DFE50131855268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate how expressing one's emotions in different situations affects others.

A3D9B580DFE50131855168A86D17958E.description: Identify and manage one's emotions and behavior.

comments: Several key sets of skills and attitudes provide a strong foundation for achieving school and life success. One involves knowing your emotions, how to manage them, and ways to express them constructively. This enables one to handle stress, control impulses, and motivate oneself to persevere in overcoming obstacles to goal achievement. A related set of skills involves accurately assessing your abilities and interests, building strengths, and making effective use of family, school, and community resources. Finally, it is critical for students to be able to establish and monitor their progress toward achieving academic and personal goals.
A3D954A0DFE50131855068A86D17958E.description: Develop self-awareness and self-management skills to achieve school and life success.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards Incorporating the Common Core Math

9C4848E0DFE50131774B68A86D17958E.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

9C480460DFE50131774A68A86D17958E.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.
comments: For example, rewrite 0.62 as 62/100; describe a length as 0.62 meters; locate 0.62 on a number line diagram.

9C47B300DFE50131774968A86D17958E.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.
comments: Students who can generate equivalent fractions can develop strategies for adding fractions with unlike denominators in general. But addition and subtraction with unlike denominators in general is not a requirement at this grade.
For example, express 3/10 as 30/100, and add 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100.

9C475E10DFE50131774868A86D17958E.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

comments: For example, if each person at a party will eat 3/8 of a pound of roast beef, and there will be 5 people at the party, how many pounds of roast beef will be needed? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?
9C470CF0DFE50131774768A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

9C46C250DFE50131774668A86D17958E.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to express 3 × (2/5) as 6 × (1/5), recognizing this product as 6/5. (In general, n × (a/b) = (n × a)/b.)

9C466080DFE50131774568A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to represent 5/4 as the product 5 × (1/4), recording the conclusion by the equation 5/4 = 5 × (1/4).

9C45E5A0DFE50131774468A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

9C459370DFE50131774368A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

9C455360DFE50131774268A86D17958E.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

9C4511B0DFE50131774168A86D17958E.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

9C44CEE0DFE50131774068A86D17958E.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

9C448AF0DFE50131773F68A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

9C444430DFE50131773E68A86D17958E.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

9C43F470DFE50131773D68A86D17958E.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

9C43A250DFE50131773C68A86D17958E.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

9C435DF0DFE50131773B68A86D17958E.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100

9C42C640DFE50131773968A86D17958E.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

9C427680DFE50131773868A86D17958E.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

9C4225E0DFE50131773768A86D17958E.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

9C41C7F0DFE50131773668A86D17958E.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

9C413970DFE50131773468A86D17958E.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

9C40F2D0DFE50131773368A86D17958E.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

9C409D50DFE50131773268A86D17958E.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

9C404700DFE50131773168A86D17958E.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

9C3FFE20DFE50131773068A86D17958E.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

9C3FBBE0DFE50131772F68A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

9C3E52A0DFE50131772A68A86D17958E.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.
comments: For example, from a line plot find and interpret the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in an insect collection.

9C3F7540DFE50131772E68A86D17958E.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.
comments: For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formula as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor.

9C3F2FD0DFE50131772D68A86D17958E.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

9C3EE840DFE50131772C68A86D17958E.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two column table.
comments: For example, know that 1 ft is 12 times as long as 1 in. Express the length of a 4 ft snake as 48 in. Generate a conversion table for feet and inches listing the number pairs (1, 12), (2, 24), (3, 36), …

9C3E94D0DFE50131772B68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

9C3C3A80DFE50131772368A86D17958E.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

9C3BF750DFE50131772268A86D17958E.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

9C3BB450DFE50131772168A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

9C3B6EE0DFE50131772068A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

9C3D8500DFE50131772768A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

9C3D36F0DFE50131772668A86D17958E.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

9C3CE660DFE50131772568A86D17958E.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
comments: For example, recognize that 700 ÷ 70 = 10 by applying concepts of place value and division.

9C3C80A0DFE50131772468A86D17958E.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

9C3B1090DFE50131771F68A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.

9C3AA210DFE50131771E68A86D17958E.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
comments: For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.

9C3A2170DFE50131771C68A86D17958E.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1—100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1—100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1—100 is prime or composite.

9C39E160DFE50131771B68A86D17958E.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

9C399DF0DFE50131771A68A86D17958E.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

9C395720DFE50131771968A86D17958E.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

9C3907D0DFE50131771868A86D17958E.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

9C38C670DFE50131771768A86D17958E.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

9C381690DFE50131771568A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

9C37BEB0DFE50131771468A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

9C367A90DFE50131771068A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.
9C35E190DFE50131770E68A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards Incorporating the Common Core Math

9BBA2CF0DFE50131766768A86D17958E.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes.
comments: For example, "Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?"

9BB9E460DFE50131766668A86D17958E.description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

9BB9A270DFE50131766568A86D17958E.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/"corners") and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

9BB96260DFE50131766468A86D17958E.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.

9BB917C0DFE50131766368A86D17958E.description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, "flat") or three-dimensional ("solid").

9BB8CD60DFE50131766268A86D17958E.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

9BB874A0DFE50131766168A86D17958E.description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

9BB81EE0DFE50131766068A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).

9BB77C30DFE50131765E68A86D17958E.description: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count.
comments: Limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10.

9BB73240DFE50131765D68A86D17958E.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.

9BB6EFA0DFE50131765C68A86D17958E.description: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has "more of"/"less of" the attribute, and describe the difference.
comments: For example, directly compare the heights of two children and describe one child as taller/shorter.

9BB6A320DFE50131765B68A86D17958E.description: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.

9BB5E4E0DFE50131765868A86D17958E.description: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

9BB5A400DFE50131765768A86D17958E.description: Work with numbers 11—19 to gain foundations for place value.

9BB560A0DFE50131765668A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.

9BB4BE20DFE50131765468A86D17958E.description: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.

9BB47540DFE50131765368A86D17958E.description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).

9BB42750DFE50131765268A86D17958E.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.

9BB3D0F0DFE50131765168A86D17958E.description: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
comments: Drawings need not show details, but should show the mathematics in the problem (This applies wherever drawings are mentioned in the Standards.)

9BB366F0DFE50131765068A86D17958E.description: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.

9BB2DB50DFE50131764E68A86D17958E.description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.

9BB299C0DFE50131764D68A86D17958E.description: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies.
comments: Include groups with up to ten objects.

9BB20DE0DFE50131764B68A86D17958E.description: Count to answer "how many?" questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1—20, count out that many objects.

9BB1B4F0DFE50131764A68A86D17958E.description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

9BB17150DFE50131764968A86D17958E.description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.

9BB13250DFE50131764868A86D17958E.description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.

9BB0F310DFE50131764768A86D17958E.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

9BB0B290DFE50131764668A86D17958E.description: Count to tell the number of objects.

9BB06E60DFE50131764568A86D17958E.description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

9BB02970DFE50131764468A86D17958E.description: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).

9BAFDB30DFE50131764368A86D17958E.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

9BAF95F0DFE50131764268A86D17958E.description: Know number names and the count sequence.

9BAF0410DFE50131764068A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

9BAEA4B0DFE50131763F68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.
9BAD4EB0DFE50131763B68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

comments: Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

9BACAF80DFE50131763968A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Physical Development and Health

A3423640DFE50131842F68A86D17958E.description: Describe situations where refusal skills are necessary (e.g., pressure to smoke, use alcohol and other drugs, join gangs; physical abuse and exploitation).

A341F230DFE50131842E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate skills essential to enhancing health and avoiding dangerous situations.

A341A510DFE50131842D68A86D17958E.description: Describe key elements of a decision-making process.

A3415C80DFE50131842C68A86D17958E.description: Apply decision-making skills related to the protection and promotion of individual health.

A340FF20DFE50131842B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate positive verbal and nonverbal communication skills (e.g., polite conversation, attentive listening, body language).

A340B170DFE50131842A68A86D17958E.description: Identify causes and consequences of conflict among youth.

A3407190DFE50131842968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate procedures for communicating in positive ways, resolving differences and preventing conflict.

A3402F30DFE50131842868A86D17958E.description: Promote and enhance health and well-being through the use of effective communication and decision-making skills.
comments: From an early age, students need to know how to communicate their health needs and learn to take responsibility for their own health. They also need to know how and why personal decisions can affect their own health and well-being. Consideration for the needs of others becomes part of health promotion as well. Students who can clearly identify and communicate about health-related issues-and can make healthful personal decisions-will benefit as they grow and mature in school and into responsible workers and citizens.

A33FEFD0DFE50131842768A86D17958E.description: Identify stages in growth and development (e.g., stages in the life cycle from infancy to old age).

A33FAF80DFE50131842668A86D17958E.description: Identify physical, mental, social and cultural factors affecting growth and develop-ment of children (e.g., nutrition, self-esteem, family and illness).

A33F6DF0DFE50131842568A86D17958E.description: Describe factors that affect growth and development.

A33F26A0DFE50131842468A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between positive and negative effects of health-related actions on body systems (e.g., drug use, exercise, diet).

A33EAD40DFE50131842368A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of health-related actions on the body systems.

A33E63C0DFE50131842268A86D17958E.description: Identify basic body systems and their functions (e.g., circulatory, respiratory, nervous).

A33E1EC0DFE50131842168A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain the structure and functions of the human body systems and how they interrelate.

comments: To achieve healthful individual development, students need to understand human anatomy and physiology, nutrition, stages of growth and development, avoidance of harmful actions and the characteristics of good health habits. Early learners begin with basic recognition of body systems and growth stages. As students progress, they understand how systems work together and how individual actions affect health. As they themselves grow and develop, students can learn to enhance the process throughout their school years and later life.
A33DD3D0DFE50131842068A86D17958E.description: Understand human body systems and factors that influence growth and development.

A33D8E90DFE50131841F68A86D17958E.description: Explain interrelationships between the environment and individual health (e.g., pollution and respiratory problems, sun and skin cancer).

A33D4AB0DFE50131841E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the environment can affect health.

A33CF850DFE50131841D68A86D17958E.description: Describe how individuals and groups influence the health of individuals (e.g., peer pressure, media and advertising).

A33CAAE0DFE50131841C68A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain the factors that influence health among individuals, groups and communities.

A33C3DD0DFE50131841B68A86D17958E.description: Describe and compare health and safety methods that reduce the risks associated with dangerous situations (e.g., wearing seat belts and helmets, using sunscreen).

A33BE6C0DFE50131841A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate strategies for the prevention and reduction of communicable and non-communicable disease (e.g., practicing cleanliness, making healthy food choices, understanding the importance of immunizations and regular health screenings).

A33BA7B0DFE50131841968A86D17958E.description: Describe benefits of early detection and treatment of illness.

A33B65A0DFE50131841868A86D17958E.description: Explain the basic principles of health promotion, illness prevention and safety.

A33B11A0DFE50131841768A86D17958E.description: Understand principles of health promotion and the prevention and treatment of illness and injury.
comments: Nutrition, exercise, rest, hygiene and safety are the bases for personal, family and occupational health. From an early age, students can recognize healthy habits and understand why they are important. As students become more sophisticated in their understanding, they learn and can adopt a variety of ways to minimize illness and enhance health. Learners will be able to apply the effects of health-related actions to success in the workplace. Students who develop an effective understanding of basic health promotion can establish the foundation for achieving and maintaining personal health and well-being by making informed wellness decisions now and throughout their lives.

A33AD2D0DFE50131841668A86D17958E.description: Work cooperatively with a partner or small group to reach a shared goal during physical activity.

A33A9390DFE50131841568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate cooperative skills during structured group physical activity.

A33A51B0DFE50131841468A86D17958E.description: Work independently on task until completed.

A33A0E90DFE50131841368A86D17958E.description: Use identified procedures and safe practices without reminders during group physical activities.

A339CB70DFE50131841268A86D17958E.description: Accept responsibility for their own actions in group physical activities.

A33981B0DFE50131841168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate individual responsibility during group physical activities.

comments: As members of teams, students need to fill the role of leader at times and participant at other times. Knowing how to follow procedures, accept leadership from others, participate actively and lead when appropriate will serve the student on and off the playing field. Students need to know the elements of teamwork (communication, decision making, cooperation, leadership) and how to adjust individual needs to team needs. Students also need to be able to recognize each member's contributions, including their own.
A3391650DFE50131841068A86D17958E.description: Develop team-building skills by working with others through physical activity.

A338CD70DFE50131840F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the relationship between movement and health-related fitness components (e.g., running/cardiorespiratory, tug-of-war/strength).

A3389020DFE50131840E68A86D17958E.description: Set a personal health-related fitness goal.

A33852A0DFE50131840D68A86D17958E.description: Set goals based on fitness data and develop, implement and monitor an individual fitness improvement plan.

A3381480DFE50131840C68A86D17958E.description: Match recognized assessments of health-related fitness (e.g., AAHPERED, AAU) to corresponding components of fitness.

A337CF80DFE50131840B68A86D17958E.description: Monitor individual heart rate before, during and after physical activity, with and without the use of technology.

A33742E0DFE50131840968A86D17958E.description: Regularly participate in physical activity for the purpose of sustaining or improving individual levels of health-related fitness.

A3370550DFE50131840868A86D17958E.description: Describe the benefits of maintaining a health-enhancing level of fitness.

A336C740DFE50131840768A86D17958E.description: Know and apply the principles and components of health-related fitness.

A3368520DFE50131840668A86D17958E.description: Achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical fitness based upon continual self-assessment.
comments: Regular physical activity is necessary to sustain fitness and health. Students need to apply training principles-frequency, intensity, time and type (FITT)-to achieve their personal fitness goals. Fitness expectations need to be established on an individual basis; realistic goals need to be based on the health-related components of endurance, strength, flexibility, cardiorespiratory fitness and body composition. By learning and applying these concepts, students can develop lifelong understanding and good habits for overall health and fitness.

A3364120DFE50131840568A86D17958E.description: Identify offensive, defensive and cooperative strategies in selected activities and games.

A335D900DFE50131840468A86D17958E.description: Identify and apply rules and safety procedures in physical activities.

A3356AB0DFE50131840368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of rules, safety and strategies during physical activity.

A3352790DFE50131840268A86D17958E.description: Identify the principles of movement (e.g., absorption and application of force, equilibrium).

A334E670DFE50131840168A86D17958E.description: Analyze various movement concepts and applications.

A334A190DFE50131840068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate control when performing combinations and sequences in locomotor, non locomotor and manipulative motor patterns.

A3345750DFE5013183FF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate physical competency in individual and team sports, creative movement and leisure and work-related activities.

comments: Physical performance involves competency in a wide range of motor, non-motor and manipulative skills. Learning in this area is developmental, building simple movements into more complex patterns. Learning to follow directions and rules enhances enjoyment and success in both recreational and competitive sports. Working toward higher levels of competence, students learn how to maintain health and fitness as individuals and as members of teams.
A3340790DFE5013183FE68A86D17958E.description: Acquire movement skills and understand concepts needed to engage in health-enhancing physical activity.
