A34E08F0DFE50131843668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of rules, safety and strategies during physical activity.

A34DC5B0DFE50131843568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast efficient and inefficient movement patterns.

A34D7E20DFE50131843468A86D17958E.description: Analyze various movement concepts and applications.

A34D3670DFE50131843368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate control when performing combinations and sequences of locomotor, non-locomotor and manipulative motor patterns in selected activities, games and sports.

A34CD9B0DFE50131843268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate physical competency in individual and team sports, creative movement and leisure and work-related activities.

A34C8140DFE50131843168A86D17958E.description: Acquire movement skills and understand concepts needed to engage in health-enhancing physical activity.
comments: Physical performance involves competency in a wide range of motor, non-motor and manipulative skills. Learning in this area is developmental, building simple movements into more complex patterns. Learning to follow directions and rules enhances enjoyment and success in both recreational and competitive sports. Working toward higher levels of competence, students learn how to maintain health and fitness as individuals and as members of teams.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards Incorporating the Common Core Math

9D0AE5A0DFE50131785568A86D17958E.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

9D0A8350DFE50131785468A86D17958E.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

9D0A4380DFE50131785368A86D17958E.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

comments: For example, the function A = s² giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line.
9D09FF10DFE50131785268A86D17958E.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.

9D09BB40DFE50131785168A86D17958E.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).
comments: For example, given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.

9D097830DFE50131785068A86D17958E.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.
comments: Function notation is not required in Grade 8.

For example, collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?
9D089170DFE50131784D68A86D17958E.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.

9D084C20DFE50131784C68A86D17958E.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept.
comments: For example, in a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.

9D080660DFE50131784B68A86D17958E.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

9D07C000DFE50131784A68A86D17958E.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

9D077060DFE50131784968A86D17958E.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

9D06C870DFE50131784768A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.
comments: For example, given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.

9D0682E0DFE50131784668A86D17958E.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.
comments: For example, 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.

9D064280DFE50131784568A86D17958E.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

9D060170DFE50131784468A86D17958E.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

9D05BD70DFE50131784368A86D17958E.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

9D056B10DFE50131784268A86D17958E.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

9D0503A0DFE50131784168A86D17958E.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

9D04BAD0DFE50131784068A86D17958E.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

9D047500DFE50131783F68A86D17958E.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

9D042D80DFE50131783E68A86D17958E.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.
comments: For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed.

9D03E400DFE50131783D68A86D17958E.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

9D039A30DFE50131783C68A86D17958E.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

9D033FA0DFE50131783B68A86D17958E.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other.
comments: For example, estimate the population of the United States as 3 × 10<sup>8</sup> and the population of the world as 7 × 10<sup>9</sup>, and determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.

9D02FB80DFE50131783A68A86D17958E.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

9D02B710DFE50131783968A86D17958E.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.
comments: For example, 3² × 3<sup>-5</sup> = 3<sup>-3</sup> = 1/3³ = 1/27.

9D026A30DFE50131783868A86D17958E.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

comments: For example, by truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.
9D01BDC0DFE50131783668A86D17958E.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²).

9D016DC0DFE50131783568A86D17958E.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.

9D012C90DFE50131783468A86D17958E.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

9D00A5A0DFE50131783268A86D17958E.description: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

9D005FE0DFE50131783168A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

9D0016B0DFE50131783068A86D17958E.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

9CFFC4B0DFE50131782F68A86D17958E.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

9CFF7820DFE50131782E68A86D17958E.description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

9CFF2BF0DFE50131782D68A86D17958E.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

9CFEE920DFE50131782C68A86D17958E.description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles.
comments: For example, arrange three copies of the same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line, and give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so.

9CFEA480DFE50131782B68A86D17958E.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

9CFE5640DFE50131782A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

9CFE0900DFE50131782968A86D17958E.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

9CFDC8E0DFE50131782868A86D17958E.description: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.

9CFD8620DFE50131782768A86D17958E.description: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.

9CFD4300DFE50131782668A86D17958E.description: Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

9CFCFF40DFE50131782568A86D17958E.description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations:

9CFCADB0DFE50131782468A86D17958E.description: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

9CFC1D00DFE50131782268A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
9CFBCD90DFE50131782168A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.
9CFA6B00DFE50131781D68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

comments: Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.
9CF9B480DFE50131781B68A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Physical Development and Health

A373B2D0DFE50131849968A86D17958E.description: Formulate a plan to achieve individual health goals.

A3736EC0DFE50131849868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate skills essential to enhancing health and avoiding dangerous situations.

A3732680DFE50131849768A86D17958E.description: Explain how decision making affects the achievement of individual health goals.

A372E6D0DFE50131849668A86D17958E.description: Apply decision-making skills related to the protection and promotion of individual health.

A372A560DFE50131849568A86D17958E.description: Formulate strategies to prevent conflict and resolve differences.

A3725C00DFE50131849468A86D17958E.description: Describe the effects (e.g., economic losses, threats to personal safety) of conflict and violence upon the health of individuals, families and communities.

A3720410DFE50131849368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate procedures for communicating in positive ways, resolving differences and preventing conflict.

A371B4A0DFE50131849268A86D17958E.description: Promote and enhance health and well-being through the use of effective communication and decision-making skills.
comments: From an early age, students need to know how to communicate their health needs and learn to take responsibility for their own health. They also need to know how and why personal decisions can affect their own health and well-being. Consideration for the needs of others becomes part of health promotion as well. Students who can clearly identify and communicate about health-related issues-and can make healthful personal decisions-will benefit as they grow and mature in school and into responsible workers and citizens.

A3716740DFE50131849168A86D17958E.description: Describe changes in physical health and body functions at various stages of the life cycle.

A3711E40DFE50131849068A86D17958E.description: Describe factors that affect growth and development.

A370D420DFE50131848F68A86D17958E.description: Explain immediate and long-term effects of health habits on the body systems (e.g., diet/heart disease, exercise/fat reduction, stress management/emotional health).

A37088D0DFE50131848E68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of health-related actions on the body systems.

A37041B0DFE50131848D68A86D17958E.description: Explain how body system functions can be maintained and improved (e.g., exercise, nutrition, safety).

A3700440DFE50131848C68A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain the structure and functions of the human body systems and how they interrelate.

A36FC2F0DFE50131848B68A86D17958E.description: Understand human body systems and factors that influence growth and development.
comments: To achieve healthful individual development, students need to understand human anatomy and physiology, nutrition, stages of growth and development, avoidance of harmful actions and the characteristics of good health habits. Early learners begin with basic recognition of body systems and growth stages. As students progress, they understand how systems work together and how individual actions affect health. As they themselves grow and develop, students can learn to enhance the process throughout their school years and later life.

A36F8550DFE50131848A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how environmental conditions can affect health on a large scale (e.g., acid rain, oil spills, solid waste contamination, nuclear leaks, ozone depletion).

A36F4900DFE50131848968A86D17958E.description: Explain how the environment can affect health.

A36F0960DFE50131848868A86D17958E.description: Explain social and economic effects of health problems on individuals and society (e.g., cost of health care, reduction in productivity).

A36EBFB0DFE50131848768A86D17958E.description: Describe and explain the factors that influence health among individuals, groups and communities.

A36E8240DFE50131848668A86D17958E.description: Research and report about a career involved in health promotion, health care and injury prevention.

A36DC360DFE50131848368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate basic procedures in injury prevention and emergency care that can be used in the home, workplace, and community (e.g., first aid, CPR).

A36E4410DFE50131848568A86D17958E.description: Analyze possible outcomes of effective health promotion and illness prevention (e.g., reduction in stress, improved fitness, lessened likelihood of injury and illness).

A36E0390DFE50131848468A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast communicable, chronic and degenerative illnesses (e.g., influenza, cancer, arthritis).

A36D7F00DFE50131848268A86D17958E.description: Explain the basic principles of health promotion, illness prevention and safety.

A36D2A00DFE50131848168A86D17958E.description: Understand principles of health promotion and the prevention and treatment of illness and injury.
comments: Nutrition, exercise, rest, hygiene and safety are the bases for personal, family and occupational health. From an early age, students can recognize healthy habits and understand why they are important. As students become more sophisticated in their understanding, they learn and can adopt a variety of ways to minimize illness and enhance health. Learners will be able to apply the effects of health-related actions to success in the workplace. Students who develop an effective understanding of basic health promotion can establish the foundation for achieving and maintaining personal health and well-being by making informed wellness decisions now and throughout their lives.

A36CD670DFE50131848068A86D17958E.description: Work cooperatively with others to achieve group goals in competitive and non-competitive situations (e.g., challenge course, orienteering).

A36C8AB0DFE50131847F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate cooperative skills during structured group physical activity.

A36C43A0DFE50131847E68A86D17958E.description: Complete a given task on time.

A36C02D0DFE50131847D68A86D17958E.description: Apply identified procedures and safe practices to all group physical activity settings.

A36BBDF0DFE50131847C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate decision-making skills both independently and with others during physical activities.

A36B5830DFE50131847B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate individual responsibility during group physical activities.

A36AF130DFE50131847A68A86D17958E.description: Develop team-building skills by working with others through physical activity.
comments: As members of teams, students need to fill the role of leader at times and participant at other times. Knowing how to follow procedures, accept leadership from others, participate actively and lead when appropriate will serve the student on and off the playing field. Students need to know the elements of teamwork (communication, decision making, cooperation, leadership) and how to adjust individual needs to team needs. Students also need to be able to recognize each member's contributions, including their own.

A36AB490DFE50131847968A86D17958E.description: Design and implement a personal fitness program.

A36A7810DFE50131847868A86D17958E.description: Evaluate physical fitness services, products and advertising.

A36A3B40DFE50131847768A86D17958E.description: Set realistic, short-term, health-related fitness goals based on individual profiles.

A369FE00DFE50131847668A86D17958E.description: Set goals based on fitness data and develop, implement and monitor an individual fitness improvement plan.

A369C020DFE50131847568A86D17958E.description: Prepare an individual health-related fitness profile and evaluate fitness level on each component.

A3697F00DFE50131847468A86D17958E.description: Record and interpret health-related physiological data (e.g., blood pressure, body mass index, oxygen exchange), with and without the use of technology.

A368F520DFE50131847268A86D17958E.description: Participate in various types of fitness training programs (e.g., circuit, cross and interval training) and describe the character-istics and benefits of each.

A368B830DFE50131847168A86D17958E.description: Interpret the effects of exercise/physical activity on the level of health-related fitness.

A3687B30DFE50131847068A86D17958E.description: Know and apply the principles and components of health-related fitness.

A3683A50DFE50131846F68A86D17958E.description: Achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical fitness based upon continual self-assessment.
comments: Regular physical activity is necessary to sustain fitness and health. Students need to apply training principles-frequency, intensity, time and type (FITT)-to achieve their personal fitness goals. Fitness expectations need to be established on an individual basis; realistic goals need to be based on the health-related components of endurance, strength, flexibility, cardiorespiratory fitness and body composition. By learning and applying these concepts, students can develop lifelong understanding and good habits for overall health and fitness.

A367FA40DFE50131846E68A86D17958E.description: Select and apply offensive, defensive and cooperative strategies in selected activities, games and sports.

A367B200DFE50131846D68A86D17958E.description: Develop rules and safety procedures for physical activities.

A3676500DFE50131846C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of rules, safety and strategies during physical activity.

A36725A0DFE50131846B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze various movement patterns for efficiency and effectiveness.

A366E5D0DFE50131846A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze various movement concepts and applications.

A366A500DFE50131846968A86D17958E.description: Perform skills efficiently in a variety of leisure activities, sports, creative movement and work-related activities.

A3666100DFE50131846868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate physical competency in individual and team sports, creative movement and leisure and work-related activities.

A365DFF0DFE50131846768A86D17958E.description: Acquire movement skills and understand concepts needed to engage in health-enhancing physical activity.
comments: Physical performance involves competency in a wide range of motor, non-motor and manipulative skills. Learning in this area is developmental, building simple movements into more complex patterns. Learning to follow directions and rules enhances enjoyment and success in both recreational and competitive sports. Working toward higher levels of competence, students learn how to maintain health and fitness as individuals and as members of teams.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards Incorporating the Common Core English Language Arts

A2C86770DFE50131835168A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

A2C81CB0DFE50131835068A86D17958E.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

A2C7CDE0DFE50131834F68A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., hyperbole, paradox) in context and analyze their role in the text.

A2C781C0DFE50131834E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

A2C733B0DFE50131834D68A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

A2C6DB40DFE50131834C68A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, its etymology, or its standard usage.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Fine Arts

A3116EC0DFE5013183CD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the arts shape and reflect ideas, issues or themes in a particular culture or historical period.

A3112E80DFE5013183CC68A86D17958E.description: Understand how the arts shape and reflect history, society and everyday life.

A310EB60DFE5013183CB68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how careers in the arts are expanding based on new technologies and societal changes.

A310A2A0DFE5013183CA68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the arts function in history, society and everyday life.

comments: The arts are a record of civilizations, past and present. Artists are influenced by-and influence-the times and places in which they live and work. As students learn through the arts about people and civilizations, they learn about others and themselves. Also, students learn about careers related to this goal (e.g., animator, curator, art historian, sound technician).
A3105D50DFE5013183C968A86D17958E.description: Understand the role of the arts in civilizations, past and present.

A3101020DFE5013183C868A86D17958E.description: Create and perform a complex work of art using a variety of techniques, technologies and resources and independent decision making.

A30FC2F0DFE5013183C768A86D17958E.description: Apply skills and knowledge necessary to create and perform in one or more of the arts.

A30F84A0DFE5013183C668A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate how the choice of media, tools, technologies and processes support and influence the communication of ideas.

A30F3CB0DFE5013183C568A86D17958E.description: Understand processes, traditional tools and modern technologies used in the arts.

A30EFAE0DFE5013183C468A86D17958E.description: Through creating and performing, understand how works of art are produced.
comments: Students acquire skills to produce and perform dance, drama, music and visual art. They learn to use media, tools and technologies. They learn to shape ideas and emotions into sounds, images and actions. As students create and perform their own artworks and review the works of others, they become more imaginative, strengthen their problem-solving skills and learn to respond to the creativity of others. Creating and performing are at the core of the fine arts. Students also learn about the role of the artist (e.g., dancer, painter, actor, director, scriptwriter, musician).

A30EBDB0DFE5013183C368A86D17958E.description: Understand how different art forms combine to create an interdisciplinary work (e.g., musical theatre, opera or cinematography).

A30E7F30DFE5013183C268A86D17958E.description: Understand the similarities, distinctions and connections in and among the arts.

A30E3F60DFE5013183C168A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate student and professional works for how aesthetic qualities are used to convey intent, expressive ideas and/or meaning.

A30E0050DFE5013183C068A86D17958E.description: Understand the sensory elements, organizational principles and expressive qualities of the arts.

A30DAEA0DFE5013183BF68A86D17958E.description: Know the language of the arts.
comments: Through observation, discussion, interpretation and analysis, students learn the "language" of the arts. They learn to understand how others express ideas in dance, drama, music and visual art forms. In addition to acquiring knowledge essential to performance and production, students become arts consumers (e.g., attending live performances or movies, purchasing paintings or jewelry, or visiting museums) who understand the basic elements and principles underlying artworks and are able to critique them.

A3AD0440DFE50131850668A86D17958E.description: Identify and apply the steps of systematic decision making.

A3ACB4E0DFE50131850568A86D17958E.description: Apply decision-making skills to deal responsibly with daily academic and social situations.

A3AC6910DFE50131850468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of how social norms affect decision making and behavior.

A3AC1490DFE50131850368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to respect the rights of self and others.

A3ABC890DFE50131850268A86D17958E.description: Consider ethical, safety, and societal factors in making decisions.

A3AB8700DFE50131850168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate decision-making skills and responsible behaviors in personal, school, and community contexts.
comments: Promoting one's own health, avoiding risky behaviors, dealing honestly and fairly with others, and contributing to the good of one's classroom, school, family, community, and environment are essential to citizenship in a democratic society. Achieving these outcomes requires an ability to make decisions and solve problems on the basis of accurately defining decisions to be made, generating alternative solutions, anticipating the consequences of each, and evaluating and learning from one's decision making.

A3AB4570DFE50131850068A86D17958E.description: Apply constructive approaches in resolving conflicts.

A3AB02A0DFE5013184FF68A86D17958E.description: Describe causes and consequences of conflicts.

A3AAACA0DFE5013184FE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an ability to prevent, manage, and resolve interpersonal conflicts in constructive ways.

A3AA5F60DFE5013184FD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze ways to work effectively in groups.

A3A9FF50DFE5013184FC68A86D17958E.description: Describe approaches for making and keeping friends.

A3A9C270DFE5013184FB68A86D17958E.description: Use communication and social skills to interact effectively with others.

A3A983D0DFE5013184FA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to work effectively with those who are different from oneself.

A3A942F0DFE5013184F968A86D17958E.description: Identify differences among and contributions of various social and cultural groups.

A3A8F9C0DFE5013184F868A86D17958E.description: Recognize individual and group similarities and differences.

A3A89FD0DFE5013184F768A86D17958E.description: Describe the expressed feelings and perspectives of others.

A3A83CD0DFE5013184F668A86D17958E.description: Identify verbal, physical, and situational cues that indicate how others may feel.

A3A80070DFE5013184F568A86D17958E.description: Recognize the feelings and perspectives of others.

A3A7BFA0DFE5013184F468A86D17958E.description: Use social-awareness and interpersonal skills to establish and maintain positive relationships.
comments: Building and maintaining positive relationships with others are central to success in school and life and require the ability to recognize the thoughts, feelings, and perspectives of others, including those different from one's own. In addition, establishing positive peer, family, and work relationships requires skills in cooperating, communicating respectfully, and constructively resolving conflicts with others.

A3A78030DFE5013184F368A86D17958E.description: Monitor progress on achieving a short-term personal goal.

A3A743C0DFE5013184F268A86D17958E.description: Describe the steps in setting and working toward goal achievement.

A3A70540DFE5013184F168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate skills related to achieving personal and academic goals.

A3A6C2C0DFE5013184F068A86D17958E.description: Explain how family members, peers, school personnel, and community members can support school success and responsible behavior.

A3A67DD0DFE5013184EF68A86D17958E.description: Describe personal skills and interests that one wants to develop.

A3A63AE0DFE5013184EE68A86D17958E.description: Recognize personal qualities and external supports.

A3A5F580DFE5013184ED68A86D17958E.description: Describe and demonstrate ways to express emotions in a socially acceptable manner.

A3A5A6B0DFE5013184EC68A86D17958E.description: Describe a range of emotions and the situations that cause them.

A3A55D10DFE5013184EB68A86D17958E.description: Identify and manage one's emotions and behavior.

A3A50CB0DFE5013184EA68A86D17958E.description: Develop self-awareness and self-management skills to achieve school and life success.
comments: Several key sets of skills and attitudes provide a strong foundation for achieving school and life success. One involves knowing your emotions, how to manage them, and ways to express them constructively. This enables one to handle stress, control impulses, and motivate oneself to persevere in overcoming obstacles to goal achievement. A related set of skills involves accurately assessing your abilities and interests, building strengths, and making effective use of family, school, and community resources. Finally, it is critical for students to be able to establish and monitor their progress toward achieving academic and personal goals.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Fine Arts

A2F7B520DFE5013183A468A86D17958E.description: Know and describe how artists and their works shape culture and increase understanding of societies, past and present.

A2F76B50DFE5013183A368A86D17958E.description: Understand how the arts shape and reflect history, society and everyday life.

A2F720B0DFE5013183A268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast how the arts function in ceremony, technology, politics, communication and entertainment.

A2F6DEF0DFE5013183A168A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe careers and jobs in and among the arts and how they contribute to the world of work.

A2F69B90DFE5013183A068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the arts function in history, society and everyday life.

A2F652B0DFE50131839F68A86D17958E.description: Understand the role of the arts in civilizations, past and present.
comments: The arts are a record of civilizations, past and present. Artists are influenced by-and influence-the times and places in which they live and work. As students learn through the arts about people and civilizations, they learn about others and themselves. Also, students learn about careers related to this goal (e.g., animator, curator, art historian, sound technician).

A2F60930DFE50131839E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge and skills to create 2- and 3-dimensional works and time arts (e.g., film, animation, video) that are realistic, abstract, functional and decorative.

A2F5A430DFE50131839D68A86D17958E.description: Sing or play with expression and accuracy a variety of music representing diverse cultures and styles.

A2F55DC0DFE50131839C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate storytelling, improvising and memorizing scripted material supported by simple aural and visual effects and personal background knowledge needed to create and perform in drama/theatre.

A2F51E20DFE50131839B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate body alignment; movement from center; awareness of accent, meter and phrasing; and step patterns from different dance styles and forms.

A2F4E140DFE50131839A68A86D17958E.description: Apply skills and knowledge necessary to create and perform in one or more of the arts.

A2F4A330DFE50131839968A86D17958E.description: Describe how the choices of tools/technologies and processes are used to create specific effects in the arts.

A2F46300DFE50131839868A86D17958E.description: Read and interpret traditional music notation in a varied repertoire.

A2F41EC0DFE50131839768A86D17958E.description: Describe the processes involved in composing, conducting and performing.

A2F3D120DFE50131839668A86D17958E.description: Describe the use of the primary tools (body, mind and voice) and the support tools (costumes, scenery, props, lights, make-up, sound) to convey an idea through acting, playwriting and designing a drama or theatre activity.

A2F390F0DFE50131839568A86D17958E.description: Describe how body actions, types of accompaniment, lighting, costuming and processes (e.g., reordering and refining) influence the expressive qualities of dance.

A2F35030DFE50131839468A86D17958E.description: Understand processes, traditional tools and modern technologies used in the arts.

A2F30950DFE50131839368A86D17958E.description: Through creating and performing, understand how works of art are produced.
comments: Students acquire skills to produce and perform dance, drama, music and visual art. They learn to use media, tools and technologies. They learn to shape ideas and emotions into sounds, images and actions. As students create and perform their own artworks and review the works of others, they become more imaginative, strengthen their problem-solving skills and learn to respond to the creativity of others. Creating and performing are at the core of the fine arts. Students also learn about the role of the artist (e.g., dancer, painter, actor, director, scriptwriter, musician).

A2F2C830DFE50131839268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the elements and principles in two or more art works that share similar themes.

A2F284F0DFE50131839168A86D17958E.description: Understand the similarities, distinctions and connections in and among the arts.

A2F23870DFE50131839068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the elements and principles can be organized to convey meaning through a variety of media and technology.

A2F1EA00DFE50131838F68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the elements of value, perspective and color schemes; the principles of contrast, emphasis and unity; and the expressive qualities of thematic development and sequence.

A2F1A3D0DFE50131838E68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe changes in elements and expressive qualities (e.g., crescendo, ritardando, fermata, meter, sforzando).

A2F15CE0DFE50131838D68A86D17958E.description: Understand how the elements of acting, directing, playwriting and designing combine with the principles of tension, rhythm, pattern, unity, balance, repetition and idea to communicate.

A2F11D10DFE50131838C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how elements are combined and contrasted; identify the principles of transition, variety and balance; and the expressive qualities of movement.

A2F0D820DFE50131838B68A86D17958E.description: Understand the sensory elements, organizational principles and expressive qualities of the arts.

comments: Through observation, discussion, interpretation and analysis, students learn the "language" of the arts. They learn to understand how others express ideas in dance, drama, music and visual art forms. In addition to acquiring knowledge essential to performance and production, students become arts consumers (e.g., attending live performances or movies, purchasing paintings or jewelry, or visiting museums) who understand the basic elements and principles underlying artworks and are able to critique them.
A2F086C0DFE50131838A68A86D17958E.description: Know the language of the arts.

A3B99E70DFE50131851868A86D17958E.description: Predict others' feelings and perspectives in a variety of situations.

A3B81D10DFE50131851268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how making use of school and community supports and opportunities can contribute to school and life success.

A3B7CE70DFE50131851168A86D17958E.description: Analyze how personal qualities influence choices and successes.

A3B78EC0DFE50131851068A86D17958E.description: Recognize personal qualities and external supports.

A3B74E20DFE50131850F68A86D17958E.description: Apply strategies to manage stress and to motivate successful performance.

A3B6C370DFE50131850D68A86D17958E.description: Identify and manage one's emotions and behavior.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Social Science

9A8AC120DFE50131740068A86D17958E.description: Describe how changes in production (e.g., hunting and gathering, agricultural, industrial) and population caused changes in social systems.

9A8A7710DFE5013173FF68A86D17958E.description: Understand how social systems form and develop over time.

9A8A1B30DFE5013173FE68A86D17958E.description: Describe the ways in which institutions meet the needs of society.

9A89CD30DFE5013173FD68A86D17958E.description: Describe interactions of individuals, groups and institutions in situations drawn from the local community (e.g., local response to state and national reforms).

9A897A20DFE5013173FC68A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles and interactions of individuals and groups in society.

9A8929A0DFE5013173FB68A86D17958E.description: Explain ways in which language, stories, folk tales, music, media and artistic creations serve as expressions of culture.

9A88D6C0DFE5013173FA68A86D17958E.description: Compare characteristics of culture as reflected in language, literature, the arts, traditions and institutions.

comments: A study of social systems has two important aspects that help people understand their roles as individuals and members of society. The first aspect is culture consisting of the language, literature, arts and traditions of various groups of people. Students should understand common characteristics of different cultures and explain how cultural contributions shape societies over time. The second aspect is the interaction among individuals, groups and institutions. Students should know how and why groups and institutions are formed, what roles they play in society, and how individuals and groups interact with and influence institutions.
9A886F30DFE5013173F968A86D17958E.description: Understand social systems, with an emphasis on the United States.

9A880540DFE5013173F868A86D17958E.description: Identify different settlement patterns in Illinois and the United States and relate them to physical features and resources.

9A87B480DFE5013173F768A86D17958E.description: Describe how physical characteristics of places influence people's perceptions and their roles in the world over time.

9A876EA0DFE5013173F668A86D17958E.description: Understand the historical significance of geography.

9A872740DFE5013173F568A86D17958E.description: Explain how human activity affects the environment.

9A86DD80DFE5013173F468A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationships among location of resources, population distribution and economic activities (e.g., transportation, trade, communications).

9A868E90DFE5013173F368A86D17958E.description: Describe how natural events in the physical environment affect human activities.

9A8648B0DFE5013173F268A86D17958E.description: Understand relationships between geographic factors and society.

9A8601E0DFE5013173F168A86D17958E.description: Explain how physical and living components interact in a variety of ecosystems including desert, prairie, flood plain, forest, tundra.

9A85BEE0DFE5013173F068A86D17958E.description: Describe how physical and human processes shape spatial patterns including erosion, agriculture and settlement.

9A8579E0DFE5013173EF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and explain characteristics and interactions of the Earth's physical systems.

9A852F20DFE5013173EE68A86D17958E.description: Use maps and other geographic representations and instruments to gather information about people, places and environments.

9A84DE90DFE5013173ED68A86D17958E.description: Compare the physical characteristics of places including soils, land forms, vegetation, wildlife, climate, natural hazards.

9A849300DFE5013173EC68A86D17958E.description: Locate, describe and explain places, regions and features on the Earth.

9A844020DFE5013173EB68A86D17958E.description: Understand world geography and the effects of geography on society, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: The need for geographic literacy has never been greater or more obvious than in today's tightly interrelated world. Students must understand the world's physical features, how they blend with social systems and how they affect economies, politics and human interaction. Isolated geographic facts are not enough. To grasp geography and its effect on individuals and societies, students must know the broad concepts of spatial patterns, mapping, population and physical systems (land, air, water). The combination of geographic facts and broad concepts provides a deeper understanding of geography and its effects on individuals and societies.

9A83F320DFE5013173EA68A86D17958E.description: Identify individuals and their inventions (e.g., Watt/steam engine, Nobel/TNT, Edison/electric light) which influenced world environmental history.

9A83A6E0DFE5013173E968A86D17958E.description: Describe how people in hunting and gathering and early pastoral societies adapted to their respective environments.

9A835F00DFE5013173E868A86D17958E.description: Describe environmental factors that influenced the development of transportation and trade in Illinois.

9A8311A0DFE5013173E768A86D17958E.description: Identify individuals and events in the development of the conservation movement including John Muir, Theodore Roosevelt and the creation of the National Park System.

9A82CA60DFE5013173E668A86D17958E.description: Identify environmental factors that drew settlers to the state and region.

9A827AA0DFE5013173E568A86D17958E.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world environmental history.

9A822640DFE5013173E468A86D17958E.description: Describe the various roles of men, women and children in the family, at work, and in the community in various time periods and places (e.g., ancient Rome, Medieval Europe, ancient China, Sub-Saharan Africa).

9A81DF90DFE5013173E368A86D17958E.description: Describe the influence of key individuals and groups, including Susan B. Anthony/suffrage and Martin Luther King, Jr./civil rights, in the historical eras of Illinois and the United States.

9A8197D0DFE5013173E268A86D17958E.description: Describe the ways in which participation in the westward movement affected families and communities.

9A814B70DFE5013173E168A86D17958E.description: Describe the various individual motives for settling in colonial America.

9A810BF0DFE5013173E068A86D17958E.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world social history.

9A80CA10DFE5013173DF68A86D17958E.description: Describe basic economic changes that led to and resulted from the manorial agricultural system, the industrial revolution, the rise of the capitalism and the information/communication revolution.

9A8087C0DFE5013173DE68A86D17958E.description: Describe the basic economic systems of the world's great civilizations including Mesopotamia, Egypt, Aegean/Mediterranean and Asian civilizations, 1000 BCE - 500 CE.

9A804540DFE5013173DD68A86D17958E.description: Describe the economic consequences of the first agricultural revolution, 4000 BCE-1000 BCE.

9A8000A0DFE5013173DC68A86D17958E.description: Describe significant economic events including industrialization, immigration, the Great Depression, the shift to a service economy and the rise of technology that influenced history from the industrial develop-ment era to the present.

9A7FB7A0DFE5013173DB68A86D17958E.description: Explain how individuals, including John Deere, Thomas Edison, Robert McCormack, George Washington Carver and Henry Ford, contributed to economic change through ideas, inventions and entrepreneurship.

9A7F5F30DFE5013173DA68A86D17958E.description: Describe how slavery and indentured servitude influenced the early economy of the United States.

9A7F11C0DFE5013173D968A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of economic systems.

9A7EC290DFE5013173D868A86D17958E.description: Describe the origins of Western political ideas and institutions (e.g. Greek democracy, Roman republic, Magna Carta and Common Law, the Enlightenment).

9A7E7C10DFE5013173D768A86D17958E.description: Describe the historical development of monarchies, oligarchies and city-states in ancient civilizations.

9A7E3540DFE5013173D668A86D17958E.description: Identify major political events and leaders within the United States historical eras since the adoption of the Constitution, including the westward expansion, Louisiana Purchase, Civil War, and 20th century wars as well as the roles of Thomas Jefferson, Abraham Lincoln, Woodrow Wilson, and Franklin D. Roosevelt.

9A7DECA0DFE5013173D568A86D17958E.description: Identify presidential elections that were pivotal in the formation of modern political parties.

9A7D9D00DFE5013173D468A86D17958E.description: Identify major causes of the American Revolution and describe the consequences of the Revolution through the early national period, including the roles of George Washington, Thomas Jefferson and Benjamin Franklin.

9A7D57E0DFE5013173D368A86D17958E.description: Describe how the European colonies in North America developed politically.

9A7D08E0DFE5013173D268A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of significant political events.

9A7C9AF0DFE5013173D168A86D17958E.description: Ask questions and seek answers by collecting and analyzing data from historic documents, images and other literary and non-literary sources.

9A7C4220DFE5013173D068A86D17958E.description: Compare different stories about a historical figure or event and analyze differences in the portrayals and perspectives they present.

9A7BF320DFE5013173CF68A86D17958E.description: Read historical stories and determine events which influenced their writing.

9A7BAD60DFE5013173CE68A86D17958E.description: Apply the skills of historical analysis and interpretation.

9A7B6560DFE5013173CD68A86D17958E.description: Understand events, trends, individuals and movements shaping the history of Illinois, the United States and other nations.
comments: George Santayana said "those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it." In a broader sense, students who can examine and analyze the events of the past have a powerful tool for understanding the events of today and the future. They develop an understanding of how people, nations, actions and interactions have led to today's realities. In the process, they can better define their own roles as participating citizens.

9A7B1F90DFE5013173CC68A86D17958E.description: Identify which public goods and services are provided by differing levels of government.

9A7AD1E0DFE5013173CB68A86D17958E.description: Explain how and why public goods and services are provided.

9A7A76F0DFE5013173CA68A86D17958E.description: Understand the impact of government policies and decisions on production and consumption in the economy.

9A7A1B50DFE5013173C968A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationships among specialization, division of labor, productivity of workers and interdependence among producers and consumers.

9A79C650DFE5013173C868A86D17958E.description: Explain why people and countries voluntarily exchange goods and services.

9A7980E0DFE5013173C768A86D17958E.description: Understand trade as an exchange of goods or services.

9A793F70DFE5013173C668A86D17958E.description: Describe how entrepreneurs take risks in order to produce goods or services.

9A78FD40DFE5013173C568A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain examples of competition in the economy.

9A78B890DFE5013173C468A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between price and quantity supplied of a good or service.

9A786070DFE5013173C368A86D17958E.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by producers.

9A781CE0DFE5013173C268A86D17958E.description: Explain that when a choice is made, something else is given up.

9A77DA40DFE5013173C168A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between the quantity of goods/services purchased and their price.

9A7795A0DFE5013173C068A86D17958E.description: Identify factors that affect how consumers make their choices.

9A7749C0DFE5013173BF68A86D17958E.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by consumers.

9A7687C0DFE5013173BD68A86D17958E.description: Describe how incomes reflect choices made about education and careers.

9A764580DFE5013173BC68A86D17958E.description: Explain how economic systems decide what goods and services are produced, how they are produced and who consumes them.

9A7600D0DFE5013173BB68A86D17958E.description: Understand how different economic systems operate in the exchange, production, distribution and consumption of goods and services.

9A75BC40DFE5013173BA68A86D17958E.description: Understand economic systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: Why This Goal Is Important: People's lives are directly affected by the economies of cities, states, nations and the world. All people engage in economic activity: buying, selling, trading, producing and consuming. By understanding economic systems-and how economics blends with other social sciences, students will be able to make more informed choices, prudently use resources and function as effective participants in the economies around them.

9A757520DFE5013173B968A86D17958E.description: Identify consistencies and inconsistencies between expressed United States political traditions and ideas and actual practices (e.g., freedom of speech, right to bear arms, slavery, voting rights).

9A752810DFE5013173B868A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of United States political ideas and traditions.

9A74D680DFE5013173B768A86D17958E.description: Determine and explain the leadership role of the United States in international settings.

9A749850DFE5013173B668A86D17958E.description: Understand United States foreign policy as it relates to other nations and international issues.

9A745760DFE5013173B568A86D17958E.description: Explain ways that individuals and groups influence and shape public policy.

9A7415A0DFE5013173B468A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles and influences of individuals and interest groups in the political systems of Illinois, the United States and other nations.

9A73CD20DFE5013173B368A86D17958E.description: Describe and evaluate why rights and responsibilities are important to the individual, family, community, workplace, state and nation (e.g., voting, protection under the law).

9A736E60DFE5013173B268A86D17958E.description: Understand election processes and responsibilities of citizens.

9A7317F0DFE5013173B168A86D17958E.description: Explain what government does at local, state and national levels.

9A72CBA0DFE5013173B068A86D17958E.description: Understand the structures and functions of the political systems of Illinois, the United States and other nations.

9A727B30DFE5013173AF68A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of fundamental concepts expressed and implied in major documents including the Declaration of Independence, the United States Constitution and the Illinois Constitution.

9A722D70DFE5013173AE68A86D17958E.description: Understand and explain basic principles of the United States government.

9A71D460DFE5013173AD68A86D17958E.description: Understand political systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: The existence and advancement of a free society depend on the knowledge, skills and understanding of its citizenry. Through the study of various forms and levels of government and the documents and institutions of the United States, students will develop the skills and knowledge that they need to be contributing citizens, now and in the future.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Social Science

9B22D980DFE50131754768A86D17958E.description: Analyze how social scientists' interpretations of societies, cultures and institutions change over time.

9B227100DFE50131754668A86D17958E.description: Understand how social systems form and develop over time.

9B2225D0DFE50131754568A86D17958E.description: Use methods of social science inquiry (pose questions, collect and analyze data, make and support conclusions with evidence, report findings) to study the development and functions of social systems and report conclusions to a larger audience.

9B21D940DFE50131754468A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles and interactions of individuals and groups in society.

9B219720DFE50131754368A86D17958E.description: Compare ways in which social systems are affected by political, environmental, economic and technological changes.

9B215240DFE50131754268A86D17958E.description: Compare characteristics of culture as reflected in language, literature, the arts, traditions and institutions.

comments: A study of social systems has two important aspects that help people understand their roles as individuals and members of society. The first aspect is culture consisting of the language, literature, arts and traditions of various groups of people. Students should understand common characteristics of different cultures and explain how cultural contributions shape societies over time. The second aspect is the interaction among individuals, groups and institutions. Students should know how and why groups and institutions are formed, what roles they play in society, and how individuals and groups interact with and influence institutions.
9B210BC0DFE50131754168A86D17958E.description: Understand social systems, with an emphasis on the United States.

9B20C3F0DFE50131754068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the historical development of a current issue involving the interaction of people and geographic factors (e.g., mass transportation, changes in agricultural subsidies, flood control).

9B2078C0DFE50131753F68A86D17958E.description: Understand the historical significance of geography.

9B203700DFE50131753E68A86D17958E.description: Describe geographic factors that affect cooperation and conflict among societies.

9B1FF4A0DFE50131753D68A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of human migrations and increased urbanization on ecosystems.

9B1FB050DFE50131753C68A86D17958E.description: Compare resource management methods and policies in different regions of the world.

9B1F6060DFE50131753B68A86D17958E.description: Understand relationships between geographic factors and society.

9B1EF930DFE50131753A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze international issues and problems using ecosystems and physical geography concepts.

9B1EA980DFE50131753968A86D17958E.description: Analyze and explain characteristics and interactions of the Earth's physical systems.

9B1E6790DFE50131753868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how maps, other geographic instruments and technologies are used to solve spatial problems (e.g., land use, ecological concerns).

9B1E2580DFE50131753768A86D17958E.description: Locate, describe and explain places, regions and features on the Earth.

9B1DDFA0DFE50131753668A86D17958E.description: Understand world geography and the effects of geography on society, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: The need for geographic literacy has never been greater or more obvious than in today's tightly interrelated world. Students must understand the world's physical features, how they blend with social systems and how they affect economies, politics and human interaction. Isolated geographic facts are not enough. To grasp geography and its effect on individuals and societies, students must know the broad concepts of spatial patterns, mapping, population and physical systems (land, air, water). The combination of geographic facts and broad concepts provides a deeper understanding of geography and its effects on individuals and societies.

9B1D97A0DFE50131753568A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between an issue in world environmental history and the related aspects of political, economic and social history.

9B1D51E0DFE50131753468A86D17958E.description: Analyze how technological and scientific developments have affected human productivity, human comfort and the environment.

9B1D09B0DFE50131753368A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between an issue in United States environmental history and the related aspects of political, economic and social history.

9B1CBAD0DFE50131753268A86D17958E.description: Analyze positive and negative aspects of human effects on the environment in the United States including damming rivers, fencing prairies and building cities.

9B1C7820DFE50131753168A86D17958E.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world environmental history.

9B1C35D0DFE50131753068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between an issue in world social history and the related aspects of political, economic and environmental history.

9B1BF440DFE50131752F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between an issue in United States social history and the related aspects of political, economic and environmental history.

9B1BAFC0DFE50131752E68A86D17958E.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world social history.

9B1B67A0DFE50131752D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between an issue in world economic history and the related aspects of political, social and environmental history.

9B1B1CD0DFE50131752C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how historical trends in population, urbanization, economic develop-ment and technological advancements have caused change in world economic systems.

9B1ABE70DFE50131752B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how industrial capitalism became the dominant economic model in the world.

9B1A6B40DFE50131752A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between an issue in United States economic history and the related aspects of political, social and environmental history.

9B1A2040DFE50131752968A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why the role of the United States in the world economy has changed since World War II.

9B19D900DFE50131752868A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of economic systems.

9B197650DFE50131752768A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship of an issue in world political history to the related aspects of world economic, social and environmental history.

9B190DC0DFE50131752668A86D17958E.description: Describe how tensions in the modern world are affected by different political ideologies including democracy and totalitarianism.

9B18CB30DFE50131752568A86D17958E.description: Analyze worldwide consequences of isolated political events, including the events triggering the Napoleonic Wars and World Wars I and II.

9B188710DFE50131752468A86D17958E.description: Analyze how United States political history has been influenced by the nation's economic, social and environmental history.

9B184240DFE50131752368A86D17958E.description: Describe how modern political positions are affected by differences in ideologies and viewpoints that have developed over time (e.g., political parties' positions on government intervention in the economy).

9B17FCF0DFE50131752268A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of significant political events.

9B17B6E0DFE50131752168A86D17958E.description: Explain the tentative nature of historical interpretations.

9B1765C0DFE50131752068A86D17958E.description: Analyze historical and contemporary developments using methods of historical inquiry (pose questions, collect and analyze data, make and support inferences with evidence, report findings).

9B172270DFE50131751F68A86D17958E.description: Apply the skills of historical analysis and interpretation.

comments: George Santayana said "those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it." In a broader sense, students who can examine and analyze the events of the past have a powerful tool for understanding the events of today and the future. They develop an understanding of how people, nations, actions and interactions have led to today's realities. In the process, they can better define their own roles as participating citizens.
9B16DC00DFE50131751E68A86D17958E.description: Understand events, trends, individuals and movements shaping the history of Illinois, the United States and other nations.

9B169790DFE50131751D68A86D17958E.description: Describe key schools of thought (e.g., classical, Keynesian, monetarist, supply-side) and explain their impact on government policies.

9B165320DFE50131751C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how fiscal, monetary and regulatory policies affect overall levels of employment, output and consumption.

9B160D90DFE50131751B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how and why government redistributes income in the economy.

9B15C110DFE50131751A68A86D17958E.description: Understand the impact of government policies and decisions on production and consumption in the economy.

9B156EE0DFE50131751968A86D17958E.description: Explain how technology has affected trade in the areas of transportation, communication, finance and manufacturing.

9B1526F0DFE50131751868A86D17958E.description: Analyze why trade barriers and exchange rates affect the flow of goods and services among nations.

9B14E270DFE50131751768A86D17958E.description: Explain how transaction costs affect decisions to produce or consume.

9B149DE0DFE50131751668A86D17958E.description: Understand trade as an exchange of goods or services.

9B1456F0DFE50131751568A86D17958E.description: Explain how government intervention with market prices can cause shortages or surpluses of a good or service (e.g., minimum wage policies, rent freezes, farm subsidies).

9B13EFE0DFE50131751468A86D17958E.description: Explain how changes in non-price determinants of supply (e.g., number of producers) affect producer decisions.

9B0DC9D0DFE50131751368A86D17958E.description: Explain how competition is maintained in the United States economy and how the level of competition varies in differing market structures (e.g., monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic and perfect competition).

9B0D6CF0DFE50131751268A86D17958E.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by producers.

9B0D2870DFE50131751168A86D17958E.description: Analyze elasticity as it applies to supply and demand and consumer decisions.

9B0CE4B0DFE50131751068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how inflation and interest rates affect consumer purchasing power.

9B0C9E00DFE50131750F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of changes in non-price determinants (e.g., changes in consumer income, changes in tastes and preferences) on consumer demand.

9B0C5520DFE50131750E68A86D17958E.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by consumers.

9B0BFE00DFE50131750D68A86D17958E.description: Explain the comparative value of the Consumer Price Index (e.g., goods and services in one year with earlier or later periods).

9B0B83F0DFE50131750C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of various determinants on the levels of GDP (e.g., quantity/quality of natural/capital resources, size/skills of the labor force).

9B0B37E0DFE50131750B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of economic growth.

9B0AF1D0DFE50131750A68A86D17958E.description: Explain the impact of various determinants of economic growth (e.g., investments in human/physical capital, research and development, technological change) on the economy.

9B0AACB0DFE50131750968A86D17958E.description: Understand how different economic systems operate in the exchange, production, distribution and consumption of goods and services.

9B0A6470DFE50131750868A86D17958E.description: Understand economic systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: Why This Goal Is Important: People's lives are directly affected by the economies of cities, states, nations and the world. All people engage in economic activity: buying, selling, trading, producing and consuming. By understanding economic systems-and how economics blends with other social sciences, students will be able to make more informed choices, prudently use resources and function as effective participants in the economies around them.

9B0A19D0DFE50131750768A86D17958E.description: Interpret how changing geographical, economic, technological and social forces affect United States political ideas and traditions (e.g., freedom, equality and justice, individual rights).

9B09CC20DFE50131750668A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of United States political ideas and traditions.

9B098660DFE50131750568A86D17958E.description: Analyze relationships and tensions among members of the international community.

9B094310DFE50131750468A86D17958E.description: Understand United States foreign policy as it relates to other nations and international issues.

9B08FE10DFE50131750368A86D17958E.description: Interpret a variety of public policies and issues from the perspectives of different individuals and groups.

9B08B1C0DFE50131750268A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles and influences of individuals and interest groups in the political systems of Illinois, the United States and other nations.

9B085410DFE50131750168A86D17958E.description: Analyze the consequences of participation and non-participation in the electoral process (e.g., women's suffrage, voter registration, effects of media).

9B080670DFE50131750068A86D17958E.description: Understand election processes and responsibilities of citizens.

9B07BC60DFE5013174FF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze similarities and differences among world political systems (e.g., democracy, socialism, communism).

9B0777E0DFE5013174FE68A86D17958E.description: Understand the structures and functions of the political systems of Illinois, the United States and other nations.

9B073370DFE5013174FD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze ways in which federalism protects individual rights and promotes the common good and how at times has made it possible for states to protect and deny rights for certain groups.

9B06EDE0DFE5013174FC68A86D17958E.description: Understand and explain basic principles of the United States government.

9B069E00DFE5013174FB68A86D17958E.description: Understand political systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: The existence and advancement of a free society depend on the knowledge, skills and understanding of its citizenry. Through the study of various forms and levels of government and the documents and institutions of the United States, students will develop the skills and knowledge that they need to be contributing citizens, now and in the future.

document.title: New Illinois Learning Standards – Science (NILS-Science)

7A93F86DEABB47789FB8C9F6CD4359FD.description: Develop a model to generate data for iterative testing and modification of a proposed object, tool, or process such that an optimal design can be achieved.
