9F537740DFE501317CCE68A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (e.g., because).

9F532C40DFE501317CCD68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.

9F52DF80DFE501317CCC68A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are cozy).

9F527A30DFE501317CCB68A86D17958E.description: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims; a tiger is a large cat with stripes).

9F522BB0DFE501317CCA68A86D17958E.description: Sort words into categories (e.g., colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

9F51E120DFE501317CC968A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

9F5195D0DFE501317CC868A86D17958E.description: Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g., looks, looked, looking).

9F514920DFE501317CC768A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.

9F50FAA0DFE501317CC668A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

9F50A790DFE501317CC568A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

9F4F7190DFE501317CC168A86D17958E.description: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.

9F4F14C0DFE501317CC068A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.

9F4EA180DFE501317CBF68A86D17958E.description: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.

9F4E00F0DFE501317CBD68A86D17958E.description: Capitalize dates and names of people.

9F4DB490DFE501317CBC68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

9F4D6580DFE501317CBB68A86D17958E.description: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.

9F4D11C0DFE501317CBA68A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).

9F4C4B90DFE501317CB868A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).

9F4BB240DFE501317CB668A86D17958E.description: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., Yesterday I walked home; Today I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).

9F4B6650DFE501317CB568A86D17958E.description: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (e.g., I, me, my; they, them, their; anyone, everything).

9F4B1890DFE501317CB468A86D17958E.description: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).

9F4AC340DFE501317CB368A86D17958E.description: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.

9F4A77C0DFE501317CB268A86D17958E.description: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.

9F4A22D0DFE501317CB168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

9F490F70DFE501317CAE68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

9F48C340DFE501317CAD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

9F487310DFE501317CAC68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

9F47DAC0DFE501317CAA68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

9F4734C0DFE501317CA868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

9F46D730DFE501317CA768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

9F464290DFE501317CA568A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

9F45F400DFE501317CA468A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.

9F459DC0DFE501317CA368A86D17958E.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

9F455570DFE501317CA268A86D17958E.description: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.

9F44B220DFE501317CA068A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.

9F445C00DFE501317C9F68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

9F440680DFE501317C9E68A86D17958E.description: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.

9F43BC10DFE501317C9D68A86D17958E.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.

9F437280DFE501317C9C68A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

9F432B30DFE501317C9B68A86D17958E.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 1 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups

9F425020DFE501317C9868A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

9F41FA30DFE501317C9768A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

9F41A420DFE501317C9668A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

9F40D340DFE501317C9468A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

9F4082F0DFE501317C9368A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

9F402EB0DFE501317C9268A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

9F3F9F80DFE501317C9068A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

9F3E5D80DFE501317C8C68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

9F3E1060DFE501317C8B68A86D17958E.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of "how-to" books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).

9F3DC180DFE501317C8A68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

9F3D1970DFE501317C8868A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

9F3CBB20DFE501317C8768A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

9F3C0360DFE501317C8568A86D17958E.description: Write narratives in which they recount two or more appropriately sequenced events, include some details regarding what happened, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide some sense of closure.

9F3BAD60DFE501317C8468A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.

9F3B5F90DFE501317C8368A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.

9F3A74E0DFE501317C8068A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

9F39DAF0DFE501317C7E68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

9F399020DFE501317C7D68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

9F394390DFE501317C7C68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

9F38F200DFE501317C7B68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

9F389550DFE501317C7A68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

9F383980DFE501317C7968A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

9F37E260DFE501317C7868A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

9F373410DFE501317C7668A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

9F36E7B0DFE501317C7568A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

9F369AD0DFE501317C7468A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

9F35EF30DFE501317C7268A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

9F3588C0DFE501317C7168A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

9F353440DFE501317C7068A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

9F34EDA0DFE501317C6F68A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

9F34A6D0DFE501317C6E68A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

9F341650DFE501317C6C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.

9F337080DFE501317C6A68A86D17958E.description: Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables.

9F331AC0DFE501317C6968A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.

9F32C230DFE501317C6868A86D17958E.description: Know final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.

9F321640DFE501317C6668A86D17958E.description: Know the spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs.

9F31BE90DFE501317C6568A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

9F3123C0DFE501317C6368A86D17958E.description: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds (phonemes).

9F30D3F0DFE501317C6268A86D17958E.description: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in spoken single-syllable words.

9F307300DFE501317C6168A86D17958E.description: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes), including consonant blends.

9F3002F0DFE501317C6068A86D17958E.description: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.

9F2FB880DFE501317C5F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

9F2F2300DFE501317C5D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).

9F2ED4F0DFE501317C5C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

9F2DCEF0DFE501317C5968A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, read informational texts appropriately complex for grade 1.

9F2D7D70DFE501317C5868A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

9F2D2DF0DFE501317C5768A86D17958E.description: Identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

9F2CD3F0DFE501317C5668A86D17958E.description: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

9F2C85E0DFE501317C5568A86D17958E.description: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.

9F2BE8A0DFE501317C5368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by the words in a text.

9F2B8670DFE501317C5268A86D17958E.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text.

9F2B2C70DFE501317C5168A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions to help determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in a text.

9F2A7700DFE501317C4F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

9F2A27E0DFE501317C4E68A86D17958E.description: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

9F29D490DFE501317C4D68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

9F28EFB0DFE501317C4A68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, read prose and poetry of appropriate complexity for grade 1.

9F289AC0DFE501317C4968A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

9F283E90DFE501317C4868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories.

9F27E540DFE501317C4768A86D17958E.description: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events.

9F270CA0DFE501317C4468A86D17958E.description: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.

9F26C240DFE501317C4368A86D17958E.description: Explain major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information, drawing on a wide reading of a range of text types.

9F266B60DFE501317C4268A86D17958E.description: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.

9F25AB50DFE501317C4068A86D17958E.description: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.

9F255B80DFE501317C3F68A86D17958E.description: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.

9F250920DFE501317C3E68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

9F23EDA0DFE501317C3B68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

9F23A2F0DFE501317C3A68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

9F2355D0DFE501317C3968A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

9F2303D0DFE501317C3868A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

9F22AB50DFE501317C3768A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

9F221830DFE501317C3568A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

9F21CDF0DFE501317C3468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

9F2182B0DFE501317C3368A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

9F20CC00DFE501317C3168A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

9F2073D0DFE501317C3068A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

9F202070DFE501317C2F68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards Incorporating the Common Core Math

9BFD6B50DFE5013176CC68A86D17958E.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

9BFD25A0DFE5013176CB68A86D17958E.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.

comments: Sizes are compared directly or visually, not compared by measuring.
9BFCD810DFE5013176CA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.

9BF208F0DFE5013176A468A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
9BF17DB0DFE5013176A268A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
9BF131C0DFE5013176A168A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

9BEFE480DFE50131769D68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

9BEF4C50DFE50131769B68A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: New Illinois Learning Standards – Science (NILS-Science)

CE8F2FB1E42243A48BCBAF5637905997.description: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

D9BEB9364D8D4B90B67F470F5997ECFE.description: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.

1B5F5B2C0C3141F9B23636A72A787075.description: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or a want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost.

ECC5576347C5419CA005CCC1855626DF.description: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment.

4D9EAC3136A5474A9DF551B675278832.description: Describe and graph the amounts and percentages of water and fresh water in various reservoirs to provide evidence about the distribution of water on Earth.
comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to oceans, lakes, rivers, glaciers, ground water, and polar ice caps, and does not include the atmosphere.

Clarification Statement: Examples could include the influence of the ocean on ecosystems, landform shape, and climate; the influence of the atmosphere on landforms and ecosystems through weather and climate; and the influence of mountain ranges on winds and clouds in the atmosphere. The geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere are each a system.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to the interactions of two systems at a time.
AF52E38ADF874735BEBF1C7E990DD263.description: Develop a model using an example to describe ways the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and/or atmosphere interact.

comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of patterns could include the position and motion of Earth with respect to the sun and selected stars that are visible only in particular months.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include causes of seasons.
92C266E5E58A4B1C9447FD3B4A9B67A5.description: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in length and direction of shadows, day and night, and the seasonal appearance of some stars in the night sky.

E5DC0B46252A4148ABBD01DFC9711820.description: Support an argument that differences in the apparent brightness of the sun compared to other stars is due to their relative distances from Earth.
comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to relative distances, not sizes, of stars. Assessment does not include other factors that affect apparent brightness (such as stellar masses, age, stage).

5459AD3B309A4DBA91843F93CCD131FE.description: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.
comments: Clarifcation Statement: Emphasis is on the idea that matter that is not food (air, water, decomposed materials in soil) is changed by plants into matter that is food. Examples of systems could include organisms, ecosystems, and the Earth.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include molecular explanations.

5CC01DB715BF49C9B279ECB5019BDC2C.description: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the idea that plant matter comes mostly from air and water, not from the soil.

5721B5B7952749C697E66AF657B25EB4.description: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

441D59712C294BBD807E768F543B9B6B.description: Use models to describe that energy in animals' food (used for body repair, growth, motion, and to maintain body warmth) was once energy from the sun.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of models could include diagrams, and flow charts.

005973E1F49D489E81FE7BACFD755452.description: Support an argument that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed down.
comments: Clarification Statement: "Down" is a local description of the direction that points toward the center of the spherical Earth.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include mathematical representation of gravitational force.

4095E915B2124FD4905F0D90D9E93530.description: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

9C5448A5FC304D7BBA0ADB0CA7B1094E.description: Conduct an investigation to determine whether the mixing of two or more substances results in new substances.

E5AB1178D13343BA947800D0BC49C6F9.description: Make observations and measurements to identify materials based on their properties.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of materials to be identified could include baking soda and other powders, metals, minerals, and liquids. Examples of properties could include color, hardness, reflectivity, electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, response to magnetic forces, and solubility; density is not intended as an identifiable property.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include density or distinguishing mass and weight.

420A95C090B14676803F5C226071C8CB.description: Measure and graph quantities to provide evidence that regardless of the type of change that occurs when heating, cooling, or mixing substances, the total weight of matter is conserved.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of reactions or changes could include phase changes, dissolving, and mixing that form new substances.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include distinguishing mass and weight.
Clarification Statement: Examples of evidence could include adding air to expand a basketball, compressing air in a syringe, dissolving sugar in water, and evaporating salt water.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include the atomic-scale mechanism of evaporation and condensation or defining the unseen particles.
A9F3F6F2D23840558A8EAB220616DC65.description: Develop a model to describe that matter is made of particles too small to be seen.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Social Science

919222BAB3FE4798ACA832135BF474A8.description: Analyze major contemporary cultural exchanges as influenced by worldwide communications.

90AB286DDC5A4AB4A8631F3C487C2494.description: Analyze major cultural exchanges of the past (e.g., Colombian exchange, the Silk Road, the Crusades).

1E0010E658EE4946AE343E81CF48F503.description: Understand how social systems form and develop over time.

873EAA50DFA848A08C2FA2AA0B2A5A01.description: Analyze various forms of institutions (e.g., educational, military, charitable, governmental).

B8271C962C7949A98B39F78635C7E31E.description: Understand the roles and interactions of individuals and groups in society.

F9CF3727D0D14C378642CD37366037C7.description: Analyze the influence of cultural factors including customs, traditions, language, media, art and architecture in developing pluralistic societies.

256D8C9C75A54B4E9AC6649A8FE16345.description: Compare characteristics of culture as reflected in language, literature, the arts, traditions and institutions.

comments: A study of social systems has two important aspects that help people understand their roles as individuals and members of society. The first aspect is culture consisting of the language, literature, arts and traditions of various groups of people. Students should understand common characteristics of different cultures and explain how cultural contributions shape societies over time. The second aspect is the interaction among individuals, groups and institutions. Students should know how and why groups and institutions are formed, what roles they play in society, and how individuals and groups interact with and influence institutions.
C3EC48C047DC42A0AD36D6BE49C5AEA3.description: Understand social systems, with an emphasis on the United States.

184D66137FCA4AD09E7EFC43EB84E62D.description: Explain how processes of spatial change have affected human history (e.g., resource development and use, natural disasters).

CE0ED6A35FA8423D9B85A91F8E72D0B8.description: Understand the historical significance of geography.

5E2D05BF96AA4CB7BDAFDD9AE68158BD.description: Explain how places with various population distributions function as centers of economic activity (e.g., rural, suburban, urban).

5BBB879382244A8CB3198E29FA66B79F.description: Analyze growth trends in selected urban areas as they relate to geographic factors.

3BB59D83A5C04123BC1793B71B506925.description: Explain the ability of modern technology to alter geographic features and the impacts of these modifications on human activities.

D5FA225D309A46ACB3368CF1AD49703F.description: Understand relationships between geographic factors and society.

1988B5C28F6A487CA95074D637073A45.description: Analyze trends in world demographics as they relate to physical systems.

2CEC659BAD134FC1A3CA628FE6B79B10.description: Explain the dynamic interactions within and among the Earth's physical systems including variation, productivity and constructive and destructive processes.

04BDE2FD73954DEBA94383992A7AD0BC.description: Analyze and explain characteristics and interactions of the Earth's physical systems.

9E897B917D0E44DDB645D3840CBD3A63.description: Use maps and other geographic instruments and technologies to analyze spatial patterns and distributions on earth.

38AF6976758D4B0DBE09B1219D7C6C23.description: Use mental maps of physical features to answer complex geographic questions (e.g., how physical features have deterred or enabled migration).

52FBDFCF75A648D2AF240933B20BA0C4.description: Locate, describe and explain places, regions and features on the Earth.

7BE8D9EAD461450794F0745316951330.description: Understand world geography and the effects of geography on society, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: The need for geographic literacy has never been greater or more obvious than in today's tightly interrelated world. Students must understand the world's physical features, how they blend with social systems and how they affect economies, politics and human interaction. Isolated geographic facts are not enough. To grasp geography and its effect on individuals and societies, students must know the broad concepts of spatial patterns, mapping, population and physical systems (land, air, water). The combination of geographic facts and broad concepts provides a deeper understanding of geography and its effects on individuals and societies.

AF58C38E38FA455BA5BA0300573443B5.description: Describe how migration has altered the world's environment since 1450.

C9C30546FF0A46F6B11C36ECDB21B874.description: Describe how cultural encounters among peoples of the world (e.g., Colombian exchange, opening of China and Japan to external trade, building of Suez canal) affected the environment, 1500 - present.

0F6B91DE671E4304B9B628D667C75E53.description: Describe different and sometimes competing views, as substantiated by scientific fact, that people in North America have historically held towards the environment (e.g., private and public land ownership and use, resource use vs. preservation).

303191C23B724B13972586D4CE218D9E.description: Describe the causes and effects of conservation and environmental movements in the United States, 1900 - present.

AF1947AF61F54308A8D85C56A189CF02.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world environmental history.

CBE4AFF582EC4470B097CD8C4E8279F1.description: Identify significant events and developments since 1500 that altered world social history in ways that persist today including colonization, Protestant Reformation, industrialization, the rise of technology and human rights movements.

FF336F06D2D042E98238D64D48ED7737.description: Describe unintended social consequences of political events in United States history (e.g., Civil War/emancipation, National Defense Highway Act/decline of inner cities, Vietnam War/anti-government activity).

37D85FF36E8E47C691319F9BF80307FE.description: Describe the immediate and long-range social impacts of slavery.

135412F317C8443DB6CF335BAFF77DC5.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world social history.

E3CBE2EEF30641A2A03F6CD9401315D8.description: Describe how the maturing economies of Western Europe and Japan led to colonialism and imperialism.

30C8F4C723554CF09D22699FFFCE2A76.description: Describe the impact of key individuals/ideas from 1500 - present, including Adam Smith, Karl Marx and John Maynard Keynes.

4656041070DB4E46B2817525B88F5045.description: Compare socialism and communism in Europe, America, Asia and Africa after 1815 CE.

1463D370E11B4FC3B900E81E3C410DD0.description: Describe the growing dominance of American and European capitalism and their institutions after 1500.

8BCEA90A7358494EA8EBDDBF4B25498E.description: Describe how American economic institutions were shaped by industrialists, union leaders and groups including Southern migrants, Dust Bowl refugees, agricultural workers from Mexico and female workers since 1914.

CDD2B43388C04861B93C703F1F35A9B9.description: Analyze the impact of westward expansion on the United States economy.

13558B7285144A9A92A8E44BF10A66F8.description: Explain how trade patterns developed between the Americas and the rest of the global economy, 1500 - 1840.

87E67BBDA5D24688B90AE8180178EDF3.description: Understand the development of economic systems.

55513AC024DE46EFA1A94EC363DA54FB.description: Identify political ideas from the early modern historical era to the present which have had worldwide impact (e.g., nationalism/Sun Yat-Sen, non-violence/Ghandi, independence/Kenyatta).

A72BAD1704F44ED6BB68F71E92E701D9.description: Identify political ideas that began during the Renaissance and the Enlightenment and that persist today (e.g., church/state relationships).

79A82A62586144049C40DA3761EB2686.description: Identify political ideas that have dominated United States historical eras (e.g., Federalist, Jacksonian, Progressivist, New Deal, New Conservative).

08F34D097F2A418CA23CD84FF0B0A74F.description: Understand the development of significant political events.

0D8CD4125FDA476698555FF9D5DF6084.description: Compare competing historical interpretations of an event.

D544AD8767364BE2B8F2740EE7671FEC.description: Analyze and report historical events to determine cause-and-effect relationships.

23AF78333ABF489FAB27F1952101632E.description: Apply the skills of historical analysis and interpretation.

33BBEBBF0987478389B333E604C2AAAA.description: Understand events, trends, individuals and movements shaping the history of Illinois, the United States and other nations.
comments: George Santayana said "those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it." In a broader sense, students who can examine and analyze the events of the past have a powerful tool for understanding the events of today and the future. They develop an understanding of how people, nations, actions and interactions have led to today's realities. In the process, they can better define their own roles as participating citizens.

2F187A9E44D34AC5830904AB25BD3FC6.description: Analyze the relationship between a country's science/technology policies and its level and balance of trade.

634F433C4756465CBD6DBB62E8D55656.description: Describe social and environmental benefits and consequences of production and con-sumption.

EC7A49FD5C0E4257B8529BBF20DAE87E.description: Explain why government may intervene in a market economy.

245D744973CC4B76911423E7C3AA31DA.description: Understand the impact of government policies and decisions on production and consumption in the economy.

F15ED19147264C1F999BD7B1E3ABCA21.description: Describe the impact of worker productivity (output per worker) on business, the worker and the consumer.

20FF43C18BC449169A911AAD52D3E29F.description: Describe the relationships between the availability and price of a nation's resources and its comparative advantage in relation to other nations.

52176310EE69442AAF01936507F48D41.description: Explain the meaning and importance of "balance of trade" and how trade surpluses and deficits between nations are determined.

5639E4CECED24065AB843E5001E1D6CF.description: Understand trade as an exchange of goods or services.

0860C3E75F634CDDA1BC52902A696EE6.description: Explain the importance of research, development, invention, technology and entrepreneurship to the United States economy.

35BB78CA742D4561915AD3597A5BAAF4.description: Analyze the impact of political actions and natural phenomena (e.g., wars, legislation, natural disaster) on producers and production decisions.

81C6862E08CF4DBB963D392DF8045374.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by producers.

163041AADB3F4609B31EFBCBFE2C10B4.description: Analyze the impact of current events (e.g., weather/natural disasters, wars) on consumer prices.

37BBB88F72454CFFBF99E7B4A18C484C.description: Explain the costs and benefits of making consumer purchases through differing means (e.g., credit, cash).

2D49E9A95CE64A368FAB8CC6613D6737.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by consumers.

98B3BFB6701841E3B5E35EF08469A67B.description: Explain the effects of unemployment on the economy.

C703FD334C0F4973A4D3F805D0F14B95.description: Analyze the impact of inflation on an individual and the economy as a whole.

E3C12D7A342440F6A1A0D04DB3EB44B6.description: Explain how national economies vary in the extent that government and private markets help allocate goods, services and resources.

5E1255B5FE11464C8B6F866EF68E5E1E.description: Understand how different economic systems operate in the exchange, production, distribution and consumption of goods and services.

F21369F6989E4A26B60718DD3BDF971F.description: Understand economic systems, with an emphasis on the United States.

9D857FD0DFE50131797068A86D17958E.description: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

9D851600DFE50131796F68A86D17958E.description: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number generator).

comments: For example, compare a high-deductible versus a low-deductible automobile insurance policy using various, but reasonable, chances of having a minor or a major accident.
9D84A560DFE50131796E68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values.

9D844FE0DFE50131796D68A86D17958E.description: Find the expected payoff for a game of chance.
comments: For example, find the expected winnings from a state lottery ticket or a game at a fast-food restaurant.

9D83FD40DFE50131796C68A86D17958E.description: (+) Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values.

9D83A8A0DFE50131796B68A86D17958E.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions

9D834E70DFE50131796A68A86D17958E.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value.
comments: For example, find a current data distribution on the number of TV sets per household in the United States, and calculate the expected number of sets per household. How many TV sets would you expect to find in 100 randomly selected households?

9D82EFE0DFE50131796968A86D17958E.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value.
comments: For example, find the theoretical probability distribution for the number of correct answers obtained by guessing on all five questions of a multiple-choice test where each question has four choices, and find the expected grade under various grading schemes.

9D829990DFE50131796868A86D17958E.description: (+) Calculate the expected value of a random variable; interpret it as the mean of the probability distribution.

9D824140DFE50131796768A86D17958E.description: (+) Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.

9D81E100DFE50131796668A86D17958E.description: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems

9D810FC0DFE50131796468A86D17958E.description: (+) Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

9D80BA90DFE50131796368A86D17958E.description: (+) Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

9D806640DFE50131796268A86D17958E.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

9D8010B0DFE50131796168A86D17958E.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

9D7FB7A0DFE50131796068A86D17958E.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model

9D7F5060DFE50131795F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.
comments: For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if you are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung cancer.

For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their favorite subject among math, science, and English. Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other subjects and compare the results.
9D7EEAC0DFE50131795E68A86D17958E.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

9D7E7CC0DFE50131795D68A86D17958E.description: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

9D7E2890DFE50131795C68A86D17958E.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

9D7DCF20DFE50131795B68A86D17958E.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

9D7D48B0DFE50131795A68A86D17958E.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data

9D7CE690DFE50131795968A86D17958E.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

9D7C2140DFE50131795768A86D17958E.description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

9D7BB290DFE50131795668A86D17958E.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

9D7B61A0DFE50131795568A86D17958E.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

9D7B0FE0DFE50131795468A86D17958E.description: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies

9D7ABC70DFE50131795368A86D17958E.description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation.
comments: For example, a model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model?

9D7A6830DFE50131795268A86D17958E.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

9D7A0FA0DFE50131795168A86D17958E.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments

9D78F960DFE50131794E68A86D17958E.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

9D78A500DFE50131794D68A86D17958E.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

9D77EDE0DFE50131794B68A86D17958E.description: Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.

9D779700DFE50131794A68A86D17958E.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.

9D774130DFE50131794968A86D17958E.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data.
comments: Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models.

9D76EAA0DFE50131794868A86D17958E.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

9D7690E0DFE50131794768A86D17958E.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

9D7630D0DFE50131794668A86D17958E.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables

9D75D4F0DFE50131794568A86D17958E.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

9D7579A0DFE50131794468A86D17958E.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

9D751400DFE50131794368A86D17958E.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

9D74B320DFE50131794268A86D17958E.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

9D7440E0DFE50131794168A86D17958E.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable

9D20E630DFE50131785F68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

9D208620DFE50131785E68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

9D1EF6B0DFE50131785A68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

9D1E2810DFE50131785868A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

A265EA90DFE50131828768A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

A2658100DFE50131828668A86D17958E.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

A2651B60DFE50131828568A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., euphemism, oxymoron) in context and analyze their role in the text.

A264BDF0DFE50131828468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

A2646470DFE50131828368A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

A263FF70DFE50131828268A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, or its etymology.

A263B400DFE50131828168A86D17958E.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., analyze, analysis, analytical; advocate, advocacy).

A2636780DFE50131828068A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

A2631800DFE50131827F68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grades 9—10 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

A2627670DFE50131827D68A86D17958E.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., MLA Handbook, Turabian's Manual for Writers) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

A2621DD0DFE50131827C68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

A2613A60DFE50131827968A86D17958E.description: Use a colon to introduce a list or quotation.

A260E270DFE50131827868A86D17958E.description: Use a semicolon (and perhaps a conjunctive adverb) to link two or more closely related independent clauses.

A26084E0DFE50131827768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

A2601A10DFE50131827668A86D17958E.description: Use various types of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, participial, prepositional, absolute) and clauses (independent, dependent; noun, relative, adverbial) to convey specific meanings and add variety and interest to writing or presentations.

A25F78C0DFE50131827468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A25E3510DFE50131827168A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

A25D9CB0DFE50131826F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

A25D4E50DFE50131826E68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

A25CB470DFE50131826C68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

A25C0AF0DFE50131826A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

A25BAE30DFE50131826968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A25B0360DFE50131826768A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

A25AB450DFE50131826668A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

A25A53E0DFE50131826568A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

A25A0750DFE50131826468A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence clearly, concisely, and logically such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and task.

A2596120DFE50131826268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, identifying any fallacious reasoning or exaggerated or distorted evidence.

A258EAB0DFE50131826168A86D17958E.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source.

A2587DC0DFE50131826068A86D17958E.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives, summarize points of agreement and disagreement, and, when warranted, qualify or justify their own views and understanding and make new connections in light of the evidence and reasoning presented.

A2582C90DFE50131825F68A86D17958E.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that relate the current discussion to broader themes or larger ideas; actively incorporate others into the discussion; and clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions.

A257DE50DFE50131825E68A86D17958E.description: Work with peers to set rules for collegial discussions and decision-making (e.g., informal consensus, taking votes on key issues, presentation of alternate views), clear goals and deadlines, and individual roles as needed.

A2579010DFE50131825D68A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

A2573A10DFE50131825C68A86D17958E.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grades 9—10 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

A2563770DFE50131825968A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

A255DBA0DFE50131825868A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

A25587F0DFE50131825768A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

A254E2F0DFE50131825568A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

A2549830DFE50131825468A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

A2544BB0DFE50131825368A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

A253A1D0DFE50131825168A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

A25321F0DFE50131825068A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

A25287B0DFE50131824E68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

A2523850DFE50131824D68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the research question; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

A251E730DFE50131824C68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

A2518730DFE50131824B68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

A2513420DFE50131824A68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage of technology's capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically.

A250E500DFE50131824968A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

A2509640DFE50131824868A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

A24FF4E0DFE50131824668A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

A24F9F80DFE50131824568A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

A24F5010DFE50131824468A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic and convey a style appropriate to the discipline and context as well as to the expertise of likely readers.
