Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include complex chemical reactions.

01579C40C90A4C659FF40CEC15FACB2B.description: Refine the design of a chemical system by specifying a change in conditions that would produce increased amounts of products at equilibrium.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the application of Le Chatlier's Principle and on refining designs of chemical reaction systems, including descriptions of the connection between changes made at the macroscopic level and what happens at the molecular level. Examples of designs could include different ways to increase product formation including adding reactants or removing products.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to specifying the change in only one variable at a time. Assessment does not include calculating equilibrium constants and concentrations.

FFF1EE63FAB244C19BFAC275F7709FFC.description: Apply scientific principles and evidence to provide an explanation about the effects of changing the temperature or concentration of the reacting particles on the rate at which a reaction occurs.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on student reasoning that focuses on the number and energy of collisions between molecules.

Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to simple reactions in which there are only two reactants; evidence from temperature, concentration, and rate data; and qualitative relationships between rate and temperature.

2855604729B74C0A9693253A9D40F4BF.description: Develop a model to illustrate that the release or absorption of energy from a chemical reaction system depends upon the changes in total bond energy.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the idea that a chemical reaction is a system that affects the energy change. Examples of models could include molecular-level drawings and diagrams of reactions, graphs showing the relative energies of reactants and products, and representations showing energy is conserved.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include calculating the total bond energy changes during a chemical reaction from the bond energies of reactants and products.

Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on understanding the strengths of forces between particles, and not on naming specific intermolecular forces (such as dipole-dipole). Examples of particles could include ions, atoms, molecules, and networked materials (such as graphite). Examples of bulk properties of substances could include the melting point and boiling point, vapor pressure, and surface tension.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include Raoult's law calculations of vapor pressure.
5548D2633D9A4413B6B053C4CBF24253.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to gather evidence to compare the structure of substances at the bulk scale to infer the strength of electrical forces between particles.

19678A17B1554EBB9EE13A6FC30BFAA8.description: Construct and revise an explanation for the outcome of a simple chemical reaction based on the outermost electron states of atoms, trends in the periodic table, and knowledge of the patterns of chemical properties.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of chemical reactions could include the reaction of sodium and chlorine, of carbon and oxygen, or of carbon and hydrogen.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to chemical reactions involving main group elements and combustion reactions.
Clarification Statement: Examples of properties that could be predicted from patterns could include reactivity of metals, types of bonds formed, numbers of bonds formed, and reactions with oxygen.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to main group elements. Assessment does not include quantitative understanding of ionization energy beyond relative trends.
93AD9A06A151413980C07F64260CC41C.description: Use the periodic table as a model to predict the relative properties of elements based on the patterns of electrons in the outermost energy level of atoms.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards for Social Science

9A63D540DFE5013173AB68A86D17958E.description: Describe how individuals interacted within groups to make choices regarding food, clothing and shelter.

9A638F30DFE5013173AA68A86D17958E.description: Understand how social systems form and develop over time.

9A634430DFE5013173A968A86D17958E.description: Identify major social institutions in the community.

9A62FAD0DFE5013173A868A86D17958E.description: Compare the roles of individuals in group situations (e.g., student, committee member, employee/employer).

9A629C20DFE5013173A768A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles and interactions of individuals and groups in society.

9A624A40DFE5013173A668A86D17958E.description: Identify folklore from different cultures which became part of the heritage of the United States.

9A620660DFE5013173A568A86D17958E.description: Compare characteristics of culture as reflected in language, literature, the arts, traditions and institutions.

9A61BDA0DFE5013173A468A86D17958E.description: Understand social systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: A study of social systems has two important aspects that help people understand their roles as individuals and members of society. The first aspect is culture consisting of the language, literature, arts and traditions of various groups of people. Students should understand common characteristics of different cultures and explain how cultural contributions shape societies over time. The second aspect is the interaction among individuals, groups and institutions. Students should know how and why groups and institutions are formed, what roles they play in society, and how individuals and groups interact with and influence institutions.

9A617370DFE5013173A368A86D17958E.description: Identify changes in geographic characteristics of a local region (e.g., town, community).

9A610E00DFE5013173A268A86D17958E.description: Understand the historical significance of geography.

9A60AC50DFE5013173A168A86D17958E.description: Explain the difference between renewable and nonrenewable resources.

9A605C50DFE5013173A068A86D17958E.description: Identify opportunities and constraints of the physical environment.

9A601260DFE50131739F68A86D17958E.description: Identify ways people depend on and interact with the physical environment (e.g., farming, fishing, hydroelectric power).

9A5FCA40DFE50131739E68A86D17958E.description: Understand relationships between geographic factors and society.

9A5F46B0DFE50131739C68A86D17958E.description: Identify components of the Earth's physical systems.

9A5F0180DFE50131739B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and explain characteristics and interactions of the Earth's physical systems.

9A5EB280DFE50131739A68A86D17958E.description: Identify the characteristics and purposes of geographic representations including maps, globes, graphs, photographs, software, digital images and be able to locate specific places using each.

9A5E6BC0DFE50131739968A86D17958E.description: Identify physical characteristics of places, both local and global (e.g., locations, roads, regions, bodies of water).

9A5E1C40DFE50131739868A86D17958E.description: Locate, describe and explain places, regions and features on the Earth.

9A5DCB80DFE50131739768A86D17958E.description: Understand world geography and the effects of geography on society, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: The need for geographic literacy has never been greater or more obvious than in today's tightly interrelated world. Students must understand the world's physical features, how they blend with social systems and how they affect economies, politics and human interaction. Isolated geographic facts are not enough. To grasp geography and its effect on individuals and societies, students must know the broad concepts of spatial patterns, mapping, population and physical systems (land, air, water). The combination of geographic facts and broad concepts provides a deeper understanding of geography and its effects on individuals and societies.

9A5D7A10DFE50131739668A86D17958E.description: Compare depictions of the natural environment that are found in myths, legends, folklore and traditions.

9A5D3220DFE50131739568A86D17958E.description: Describe how the local environ-ment has changed over time.

9A5CE8E0DFE50131739468A86D17958E.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world environmental history.

9A5CA770DFE50131739368A86D17958E.description: Identify how customs and traditions from around the world influence the local community.

9A5C6260DFE50131739268A86D17958E.description: Describe key figures and organizations (e.g., fraternal/civic organizations, public service groups, community leaders) in the social history of the local community.

9A5C1970DFE50131739168A86D17958E.description: Understand Illinois, United States and world social history.

9A5BD160DFE50131739068A86D17958E.description: Explain how trade among people brought an exchange of ideas, technology and language.

9A5B6DC0DFE50131738F68A86D17958E.description: Identify how people and groups in the past made economic choices (e.g., crops to plant, products to make, products to trade) to survive and improve their lives.

9A5B1670DFE50131738E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the economy of the students' local community has changed over time.

9A5AD700DFE50131738D68A86D17958E.description: Describe how Native American people in Illinois engaged in economic activities with other tribes and traders in the region prior to the Black Hawk War.

9A5A98D0DFE50131738C68A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of economic systems.

9A5A59D0DFE50131738B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the contributions of individuals and groups who are featured in biographies, legends, folklore and traditions.

9A5A1910DFE50131738A68A86D17958E.description: Explain why individuals, groups, issues and events are celebrated with local, state or national holidays or days of recognition (e.g., Lincoln's Birthday, Martin Luther King's Birthday, Pulaski Day, Fourth of July, Memorial Day, Labor Day, Veterans' Day, Thanksgiving).

9A59D750DFE50131738968A86D17958E.description: Identify key individuals and events in the development of the local community (e.g., Founders days, names of parks, streets, public buildings).

9A599100DFE50131738868A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of significant political events.

9A5942F0DFE50131738768A86D17958E.description: Describe how people in different times and places viewed the world in different ways.

9A590220DFE50131738668A86D17958E.description: Ask historical questions and seek out answers from historical sources (e.g., myths, biographies, stories, old photographs, artwork, other visual or electronic sources).

9A58C1A0DFE50131738568A86D17958E.description: Explain the difference between past, present and future time; place themselves in time.

9A5880A0DFE50131738468A86D17958E.description: Apply the skills of historical analysis and interpretation.

9A583D80DFE50131738368A86D17958E.description: Understand events, trends, individuals and movements shaping the history of Illinois, the United States and other nations.
comments: George Santayana said "those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it." In a broader sense, students who can examine and analyze the events of the past have a powerful tool for understanding the events of today and the future. They develop an understanding of how people, nations, actions and interactions have led to today's realities. In the process, they can better define their own roles as participating citizens.

9A57FA10DFE50131738268A86D17958E.description: Identify goods and services provided by government.

9A57B1C0DFE50131738168A86D17958E.description: Understand the impact of government policies and decisions on production and consumption in the economy.

9A576240DFE50131738068A86D17958E.description: Know that barter is a type of exchange and that money makes exchange easier.

9A571E40DFE50131737F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the benefits of simple voluntary exchanges.

9A56DA60DFE50131737E68A86D17958E.description: Understand trade as an exchange of goods or services.

9A5691E0DFE50131737D68A86D17958E.description: Identify limitations in resources that force producers to make choices about what to produce.

9A563790DFE50131737C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how human, natural and capital resources are used to produce goods and services.

9A55E1D0DFE50131737B68A86D17958E.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by producers.

9A558A30DFE50131737A68A86D17958E.description: Explain why consumers must make choices.

9A5542E0DFE50131737968A86D17958E.description: Understand that scarcity necessitates choices by consumers.

9A550000DFE50131737868A86D17958E.description: Describe how wages/salaries can be earned in exchange for work.

9A54BD50DFE50131737768A86D17958E.description: Identify advantages and disadvantages of different ways to distribute goods and services.

9A5477A0DFE50131737668A86D17958E.description: Understand how different economic systems operate in the exchange, production, distribution and consumption of goods and services.

9A542890DFE50131737568A86D17958E.description: Understand economic systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: Why This Goal Is Important: People's lives are directly affected by the economies of cities, states, nations and the world. All people engage in economic activity: buying, selling, trading, producing and consuming. By understanding economic systems-and how economics blends with other social sciences, students will be able to make more informed choices, prudently use resources and function as effective participants in the economies around them.

9A53E040DFE50131737468A86D17958E.description: Describe political ideas and traditions important to the development of the United States including democracy, individual rights and the concept of freedom.

9A53A2A0DFE50131737368A86D17958E.description: Understand the development of United States political ideas and traditions.

9A5364C0DFE50131737268A86D17958E.description: Identify relationships that the federal government establishes with other nations.

9A5326F0DFE50131737168A86D17958E.description: Understand United States foreign policy as it relates to other nations and international issues.

9A52E900DFE50131737068A86D17958E.description: Identify the roles of civic leaders (e.g., elected leaders, public service leaders).

9A52AA20DFE50131736F68A86D17958E.description: Understand the roles and influences of individuals and interest groups in the political systems of Illinois, the United States and other nations.

9A526730DFE50131736E68A86D17958E.description: Identify concepts of responsible citizenship including respect for the law, patriotism, civility and working with others.

9A521410DFE50131736D68A86D17958E.description: Understand election processes and responsibilities of citizens.

9A51C440DFE50131736C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the different levels of government as local, state and national.

9A517760DFE50131736B68A86D17958E.description: Understand the structures and functions of the political systems of Illinois, the United States and other nations.

9A512A80DFE50131736A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the fundamental principles of government including representative government, government of law, individual rights and the common good.

9A50E050DFE50131736968A86D17958E.description: Understand and explain basic principles of the United States government.

9A508BE0DFE50131736868A86D17958E.description: Understand political systems, with an emphasis on the United States.
comments: The existence and advancement of a free society depend on the knowledge, skills and understanding of its citizenry. Through the study of various forms and levels of government and the documents and institutions of the United States, students will develop the skills and knowledge that they need to be contributing citizens, now and in the future.

document.title: Illinois ABE/ASE Mathematics Content Standards

A842AFF975A14779AD10D9467CF8350C.description: (+) Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

9EA97FF4DD0540DF91CC3035E181126A.description: (+) Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

8C7A0736B41E4E1FB70D1770EBEA0DD4.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

7CCBF50A94E2452095854A737316759D.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

6A032C15C28D4A1B95CDA3F4509BD305.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.

0F4F0EF91FBC44E8A24BA69747A06B5C.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.

C9EA1DA3B49B481DB5AA09311A85B005.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities. For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your class on their favorite subject among math, science, and English.

FFB8C1FA37304032B0CE1B85D7BE84DC.description: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

F679F8B70C5A42B6B2635FF0E4BC78CD.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

8E2218E499C943929F68F189FE759E60.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

22D2FA0C32B145638D1D8E964EB38E17.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.

8D5C00F12D8940CBA6C45ABCC4E8B9D5.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

15928AD4E2F9404D98CEFFED8B6B0AA9.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).

ED6609CDE29F4EC1BFA68018EED1E89F.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

FEA54926B9B14DD4AC16A40CB0594174.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

0FEE87E644BB48C3A48D540FCCF240C9.description: Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects.

AD430B0504F24188A6CA119B42B2DDD1.description: (+) Give an informal argument using Cavalieri's principle for the formulas for the volume of a sphere and other solid figures.

C111A966A90E42F89AE31F3170581C6E.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri's principle, and informal limit arguments.

3C81C717038A4D9D9AB21E4C5E2E7A85.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

7DFFC49CB49E4FE6A910CEB6CFB314AF.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

0F96034202984EB687D5E30E69C215A1.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

40AB7CA353FF4503913B6498D86673E2.description: (+) Derive the equations of ellipses and hyperbolas given the foci, using the fact that the sum or difference of distances from the foci is constant.

13BC017EB8DA462887BEF76050456E17.description: Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix.

A3CBD079A36F4348B5E0E29DA3E46A57.description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

E0D094A55FE845F9B63202E33F9FEA46.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

C7ED5D43E69847C1BF1359796E5F88DC.description: (+) Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in right and non-right triangles (e.g., surveying problems, resultant forces).

EAD6FA5CC93941EB8B7199458C3BAB42.description: (+) Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.

7F62C9A1BADA4ED5A0F3B41F62462E7A.description: (+) Derive the formula A = 1/2 ab sin(C) for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

3D28240E3C6041D2BA8160AB550C476E.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

BE8723A6F6EA4921A169FEEC0C605FA0.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

4ACBCE458AA84EFD961D94432466EAD3.description: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

1C1B31B8DAFC4B8787E5675E8AF485CE.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles.

F48779DDE6824FEE80A906FA0196719C.description: (+) Prove the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent and use them to solve problems.

421C43DBEB5E4435BE7484C56276C26C.description: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant of the angle.

9C5C3766A3824C4F9977255D875A0979.description: (+) Use inverse functions to solve trigonometric equations that arise in modeling contexts; evaluate the solutions using technology, and interpret them in terms of the context.

C0B8964ACF774BF08B45A5A460270D1A.description: (+) Understand that restricting a trigonometric function to a domain on which it is always increasing or always decreasing allows its inverse to be constructed.

1E4BD439A4DD401B8767A492A974D32C.description: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

3CE969F96411471190C1B37CC8A2F641.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions.

62842B1C4CD94B1F9827E1B31C2FF38D.description: (+) Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions.

51A843F992554F098390C3E65D5E414E.description: (+) Use special triangles to determine geometrically the values of sine, cosine, tangent for π/3, π/4, π/6, and use the unit circle to express the values of sine, cosine, and tangent for π - x, π + x, and 2π - x in terms of their values for x, where x is any real number.

F45CE0F7F7ED4C05B5A21878C8C0FB7F.description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

A447AE72E4064849A685849DDBDE9865.description: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

DAC838969D524CA6A258D2DBF8912E78.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

FDCA7592B36F47FBA50500E75A870171.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

9B8B6C7E65314199B2260AFA2EDF14A4.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

18AFDDD52D1A49BEA4AD88C9E74F0648.description: For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to ab<sup>ct</sup> = d where a, c, and d are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

3958AAC0199341AF8C619D7DFC674500.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

878B37CE23354A14BD736047AD72A454.description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

6AAE4BB0B058421581BB2402BB432F03.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

1E34EC27EA254627A3A590CDD51A9BE8.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

C4A7E59E3EEF4D988452B166DB977626.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

4396CAED24C5458291959BDE81287F18.description: (+) Understand the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms and use this relationship to solve problems involving logarithms and exponents.

72881599507C4640A37B7BA6CC89480A.description: (+) Produce an invertible function from a non-invertible function by restricting the domain.

BCF2EC9EDAFC4111A826617D1FEC98FD.description: (+) Read values of an inverse function from a graph or a table, given that the function has an inverse.

C3B5351FF71F45CA8109E253A08AC437.description: (+) Verify by composition that one function is the inverse of another.

5394AF283AD64D979FDA337FD075720C.description: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse. For example, f(x) = 2x³ or f(x) = (x + 1)/(x - 1) ≠ 1

335A79BF6B3F4CF2A94F209EFC8F3FE6.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

92D6AADE078642F9AD1866DAA865295A.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

B9AA5FBCF77B4D76BE48839972C0FE35.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

3D265960809640E7B7EA9EBE9282995B.description: (+) Compose functions. For example, if T(y) is the temperature in the atmosphere as a function of height, and h(t) is the height of a weather balloon as a function of time, then T(h(t)) is the temperature at the location of the weather balloon as a function of time.

2D0838991E624E3582E05601A7A21A3D.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.

659526E9FB704B79B07C1C379CB5C57B.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

EBFB15E16FD2499C9F3ADC5913BD0D33.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.

3E6E90173DD645ECBA98B864A9D33D38.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions. For example, identify percent rate of change in functions such as y = (1.02)t, y = (0.97)t, y = (1.01)12t, y =(1.2)t/10, and classify them as representing exponential growth or decay.

7F61634AFF4746299F40483FA9BAC47D.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

0A4DBB5FE00D4C998AFB48D820139289.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

6C6538A0114E4160B12D741966F858F3.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

4B1D5419D6784D6B8863EC8C37461C50.description: (+) Graph rational functions, identifying zeros and asymptotes when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

526CA6971D414253AFA47FB6C69C73D7.description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

4E1EDA1C405147148EA8493A6EC0DF5C.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions

D221D3EA1C094B359854345FA82DFAF5.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

A31FE7E33F484780873037173D0AF5DF.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

D531D4FEDE98447890543F05B4827BF0.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. For example, if the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.

1A0F41411D4141748414D622D8E106CC.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

3E5BEB12337F4721882C51DCA9D4E16E.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

E018B4B5DC334DE18193B58777F12D7B.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers. For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n+1) = f(n) + f(n-1) for n ≥ 1.

001F3C8F1E7247FDAA2B54A29B0344AB.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

EAC745CAF6E64CA2A70DB4DD9311B6DF.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

8A9B1E5094694E94BFF640CB10253799.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

E3E81554AB74442D849682247ADCC58F.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

8F9FC3159C4E4E4499308A6DBFBEC087.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately (e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations). Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

08E27DBB16B141CEB6FB55437BFAB9BC.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

FF8AD1579A794FB1A8D3226DC90AADED.description: (+) Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists, and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).

B800B11124BD479EBE7CB8514710379F.description: (+) Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation in a vector variable.

537586661FBE4F5C9289F536A9E5847B.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically. For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = -3x and the circle x² + y² = 3

473513BCB46A41E69A14DA406033EA3B.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

FE37F6B2B9A945BB92B94B5CB781DC30.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

246DEFBBB5FB496199F38E0ED760372B.description: (+) Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

A40786940CA4482CA2D2E09E6065E46F.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

D13F8704636B4500A93DFBB7CB7F9D98.description: (+) Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)<sup>n</sup> in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal's Triangle.

F6567BD9C8DB483E8F18850CFF5D127F.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships. For example, the polynomial identity (x² + y²)² = (x² −y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

31968D2E33744658B8AC8D5D91FD4B86.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

B50FEC1A8DE046D989E923AF6A86706E.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

CDA81B97258F444BB7D0BBE7CF148494.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x – a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

0EBF2EB2299D412AAA23B0D05BF9B853.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

DE23CA9E755148E5A54ACB54BDC6948E.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

B07B55594F86493887A3FA51DA7CF528.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems. For example, calculate mortgage payments.

44454673EEAA4459A0D6AC79CF1C519F.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions. For example the expression 1.15<sup>t</sup> can be rewritten as (1.15<sup>1/12</sup>)<sup>12t</sup> ≈ 1.012<sup>12t</sup> to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

32108F5D6F7041708A7C07FC58EC16E7.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

B18DC9B76E0A4B46AE6E34EB436E79BF.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

97753EFEB0BE4B6981CE8D277AC87D20.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

E0F0395BBED6405986E0C3766EFA6AB0.description: (+) Work with 2x2 matrices as transformations of the plane, and interpret the absolute value of the determinant in terms of area.

E5F489FA9B584C7788B3CF9F813568B0.description: (+) Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors.

923BEC137B05468DA933CE99E542A5B7.description: (+) Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

44438CA68B204A44AD93CFE49DE06F4C.description: (+) Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.

6F3FD4906D994AAEB91178196C629C67.description: (+) Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions.

81E2A73D156946768C0A6FB124360F22.description: (+) Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices (e.g., as when all of the payoffs in a game are doubled).

DED527EAE8E8428197585AC729E535FA.description: (+) Use matrices to represent and manipulate data (e.g., to represent payoffs or incidence relationships in a network).

51E08518A50C4F208D76E3F5639AAD5F.description: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.

2F2D61A128CA4D7E862D5E102238D5EB.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ≠ 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against v (for c < 0).

6814B893F6C84C5D80C2258E75B825D3.description: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction; perform scalar multiplication component-wise, e.g., as c(vx, vy) = (cvx, cvy).

159A71D0F11D46818D8B809010DC4758.description: (+) Multiply a vector by a scalar.

BE0F8D6F31CE48D48695407E5C5C6C21.description: Understand vector subtraction v – w as v + (–w), where –w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector subtraction component-wise.

926680968AAE40F6BF6A8385E604D368.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.

22D4B5925FDF47388EFB7590FD252746.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule. Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.

C2FB4496DE5A4565B0C9A03241374AF8.description: (+) Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors.

67195EE4BAB74554932489C0A241B463.description: (+) Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

19563FA092284441A7B62F295D0E605B.description: (+) Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).

9AFE60A77A6D41008FFCDB973008C879.description: Represent and model with vector quantities.

BC373BBD017141E2819EABD19179E2ED.description: (+) Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

BFB94D05E32548C8996E3F1760032ADB.description: (+) Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers. For example, rewrite x² + 4 as (x + 2i)(x − 2i).

4A452DA82A9D45079DA8497BC7C6A86B.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

7B75E0FDD6FC41E69066C50BADCE7CA0.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

E10925FB85044CC48ECF2EE7186617E4.description: (+) Calculate the distance between numbers in the complex plane as the modulus of the difference, and the midpoint of a segment as the average of the numbers at its endpoints.

C3A26CF965AD48EC9F11879DF5F25D6B.description: (+) Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation. For example, -1 + √3i³ = 8 because -1 + √3i has modulus 2 and argument 120°.

D05A28CDBA694F8F86266F731F4E0397.description: (+) Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form (including real and imaginary numbers), and explain why the rectangular and polar forms of a given complex number represent the same number.

7629723EB12842569B35F4FFF507EE09.description: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane.

3BBD0179FEE84C399265B5FFF45FCC1B.description: (+) Find the conjugate of a complex number; use conjugates to find moduli and quotients of complex numbers.

1AC2F3BA0F3F4B86BD3750513EBA8552.description: Use the relation i² = –1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

A6C1D4222B184B749E9DABA379C912AB.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = –1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real.

CE4817C79AEB49A6A30E4B8A7C19CE5F.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

27C0C5A4DD89446BB0C5B7AEEDC32A27.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

D324D2C76A4E4627A4F7CA70559097A5.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

1B7C42F882D74EA1B51CBBE614BF1B7E.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

12FFD26B6CDB4A879E0D084022AF1699.description: NRS Level 6 - High Adult Secondary Education

27ABE6474E614DDDB30E33B2BFEEF010.description: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

A9BD1A42DDB345CC969E0F0CB7D8C580.description: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number generator).

ED0862B7AE5242D99CFD1F14AD72E86D.description: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values. For example, compare a high-deductible versus a low-deductible automobile insurance policy using various, but reasonable, chances of having a minor or a major accident.

C646C946AD9543EC8FE32C3BAB660B5F.description: Find the expected payoff for a game of chance. For example, find the expected winnings from a state lottery ticket or a game at a fast food restaurant.

91EEA88F00F849888D09B456D3F5E0EA.description: (+) Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values.

64DAABD01A3F414C9A96507C104906BC.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.

64ED4401452641B78E57A62049092557.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value. For example, find a current data distribution on the number of TV sets per household in the United States, and calculate the expected number of sets per household. How many TV sets would you expect to find in 100 randomly selected households?

43A195DD641F43AFABCBDF5EE611814A.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value. For example, find the theoretical probability distribution for the number of correct answers obtained by guessing on all five questions of a multiple-choice test where each question has four choices, and find the expected grade under various grading schemes.

580AA18A75534D7481E9AE061A35141F.description: (+) Calculate the expected value of a random variable; interpret it as the mean of the probability distribution.

A593E2B0E53E424DAE7DC5B1DF3E232C.description: (+) Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.

25892832F88747D3917CFC99B9EDAF3E.description: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems.

7E84E42C758C429A85633E822ECB34F5.description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

DDBE1B824A1D4E3987F41BDFA60728BB.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

03F82511939D4550848F6D0B70E427D6.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

25BA41D8B46545A5B4932560557EBACD.description: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies.

201E412F2C0B4EB1878AE3FE00C0A350.description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process (e.g., using simulation). For example, a model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model?

39C68906DB634FF48E65EDDD3D281DD0.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

DC11508E86AB4CBFA0358F834C210001.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.

2455FA874FD346D886C1B10020DA9461.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

A76902B6D98F483C9AF7AABF1DFBD602.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

441478999A2C4EB78D773C5B1D208523.description: Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.

DE6C16304EF146F8BAA2077F6CBC0A3C.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.

F86D3BE3CF0F4518B96027D641468570.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models.

6BC445AF7FCA424D9A18BB5DCE961873.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

663D09407CF440A78113210728BAD8D4.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

8D638520DF18465F90B2511BD707DE08.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

26D42D0C8AC44FDBBBD21724DA1CAA7A.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

BCFB8550755B48CEA409A78B4B787A17.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

5F8EAFD204BA495BAA85FFF234D5BEF4.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

9A4A8950BEE04F2B89F737E64FBAF85D.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

BA2F2DF25D2B4A3FA43B83BA0F1394B2.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

7CC98D7C28244C888C8022B01F4308A3.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

5480A9EC601D4521BA3F6E8D72459FA8.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

6EA1211AC196490793CAF1B265A316A9.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

5DF758B91A8F4B058134573D9BF9183C.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

ACC9ECCC9D1440E8BA5674253E74AA5C.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri's principle, and informal limit arguments.

5FB40543F1E044C8AFC48CE912C1243B.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

07E7592EBE8D45CFBD5697C240C16EAF.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles (e.g., using the distance formula).

E63B6A2F3B65499AB87EE8F75C901FE1.description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

938A2B1A53A34C5EA14306F2E4A27C0A.description: Prove theorems about lines and angles. 19C92B7595224010A24E3703FE754E45.description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

8870C711F34F411FA5CCF5123F6E7ADB.description: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.

90F55BD43F154B3BB1BD7BD6D5B6605F.description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

A7133D667B5A465BB5548E30FAA546DC.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

4AEA91BD400E4EB4976FC863C0FDD06D.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

8229C89418EC43CABB5B429E0A3366A4.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x − p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

C57067878499491DA5FA97F34C54117A.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

43774F85C2CE456691826EAD42C19436.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

F74968F7CD9942C4A99B8CBC24929802.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

E6D2F48E3A8C45E385A89ED31FC102A1.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

6B91296ED3B6462FBBF6D67C607DE5AD.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

66939BEF79F54E2D812F44F4BBA36601.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

DD173E82C9524C7DAD82FBF9D895C9B8.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.

42239199749E4055B3B2B90953052AA2.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

B5A0805896A047E19C967EDED3DF7673.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

274358309A9C47C689B1FD94CA6FC776.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

374D95935A7B47E3802A8E910444D6FC.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

8C4D29FA129F4103B991C439779F901C.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

80DF473FF9F94F52943B71C682BFBA98.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

512FE1708B114D90A66876DEC2BBCCB3.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it. For example, see x<sup>4</sup> − y<sup>4</sup> as(x²)² − (y²)², thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x² − y²)(x² + y²).

32D930B674BD47E7AC61415D5A2E6B57.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. For example, interpret P(1 + r)n as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

9BEB690869C2466BBD203B7F96048A2D.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

1FF1A8BA6F484ED7B1F8A3CEE5B7A925.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

46401ADB1A1A4C9DBCBFD3026E630B6A.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

BA65C0CE3D61428F9F15AE38C1A0C19D.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. 15308419F9E742A8BC7DC0DEFBAEEA53.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept. 479924509AA144DE967F067A52639AED.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. 3C62A1C99CA34E2DA6A431B1238EA29A.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. C0DFC2F5CFC64A5691DA8780D52F144C.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

5FD547AFDAA645A684995943CDA2CB6E.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

5CF6BC3D00C445E79F9D0012DB7CF7AE.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

B9666C693BA14138BBFC77578F2D8707.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

1B99296EA0F64943A4F2A572A61C8787.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.

9E00F7B090984BFB9622372B4297EF50.description: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

82990A5A78BF442EA979735BE6A7E92A.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers. For example, "How old am I?" is not a statistical question, but "How old are the students in my class?" is a statistical question because one anticipates variability in students' ages.

1B403E90CC65447AA3C5FF4161540391.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

7B0753D82DE0482C995703FA3374F073.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

05D7CC828FF947E3B7F3000EECC78540.description: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.

A6EBAD12B1D64A95A5B5BABE7D77521B.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

EAF426E04585471FA981034C40DECB70.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.

BF9EA7D7800244F5BA0C1142E62E8C29.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

1EFBEDC493E44D269A921B259B8B695E.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

067740E75FA04317B32AE4CA78E24607.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other.

AE03AAFB4C474EC5BFEA2167FD312986.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

9E46A9BC8DB84B09B99B56355C81238D.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions. For example, 32 × 3(–5) = 3(–3) = 1/(33) = 1/27.

C46CF5F7074040619BB632E41DEE6BE5.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

79160F134DD148AE86D0089730DCEA6D.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.

D928508171F3485E843003BD25FE16C9.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

ACB8ADA1DBBF457BBE6D1679B197E11F.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations as strategies to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies. For example: If a woman making $25 an hour gets a 10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50. If you want to place a towel bar 9 3/4 inches long in the center of a door that is 27 1/2 inches wide, you will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate can be used as a check on the exact computation.

77656BA1311D41528A05755D0DE729F9.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

953799A388D84E68B277CC096A079CCB.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related. For example, a + 0.05a = 1.05a means that "increase by 5%" is the same as "multiply by 1.05."

724DE19BA14B4A99BB8214A386530766.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

F3FA6596991B4B7299E90C17B484ADDF.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

0DFD2B0ADF094E98B0E10E4C02E937DF.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation. For example, in a problem involving motion at constant speed, list and graph ordered pairs of distances and times, and write the equation d = 65t to represent the relationship between distance and time.

37B642B9AE1A43928085F9BA8EEBD171.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

B4CBB4E420814B2CAF718F08BA5D7E6B.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.

75C73E59EBFB45138C30AC10F865AE20.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.

06469319C22C41AB80B10717295CF36F.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.

3EF95A62E34E4598B98526518BF42BA9.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.

2E51D1AAA2AB46F8A98BAC25D2141E7A.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

15C223D879C347928183D4B424A1959C.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent (i.e., when the two expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted into them). For example, the expressions y + y + y and 3y are equivalent because they name the same number regardless of which number y stands for.

63AF90849805405C840475F489776531.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions. For example, apply the distributive property to the expression 3(2 + x) to produce the equivalent expression 6 + 3x; apply the distributive property to the expression 24x + 18y to produce the equivalent expression 6 (4x + 3y); apply properties of operations to y + y + y to produce the equivalent expression 3y.

6F4276B5E4B54EB9934B0A56FE76668F.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values for their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole-number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (order of operations). For example, use the formulas V = s³ and A = 6 s² to find the volume and surface area of a cube with sides of length s = 1/2.

B1777359C9EE4475B9743E14EF9A7B6C.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity. For example, describe the expression 2(8 + 7) as a product of two factors; view (8 + 7) as both a single entity and a sum of two terms.

B3018F1B088442C7A4B4E88BA1C8D0FD.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers. For example, express the calculation "subtract y from 5" as 5 – y.

E628D9518FA148DC8B9D295B329D9ABC.description: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

732ACA1E51E246DE9B93AF517A3E4213.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents

C1BCC06F16B448D19F3D546750594377.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

A600C66C226944ABA67C3E85A3ABD2FA.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π2). For example, by truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.

FF5196287A394D9EA28B4A575AD2C01C.description: Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; the rational numbers are those with decimal expansions that terminate in 0's or eventually repeat. Know that other numbers are called irrational.

F76249E397F149ECAF8F499611B16ADC.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

E029F7EF750F46118A2A06BD7ECF7BA1.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers. (Computations with rational numbers extend the rules for manipulating fractions to complex fractions.)

E1E3F51467D945D0B0B2A1AC0FDA995D.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

3FCF00A7553C4FA694FFD9CF806534E8.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

E67D3D669BCD4A0CA280630CEFED5481.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers then –(p/q) = (–p)/q = p/(–q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

755E9E5D89644A248108149C197D0A5D.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (–1)(–1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

32C7C46CE68D4787AD92A67A5884B33B.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.

9108FC0CD28F45529355D23DF31E8B09.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

C9AAC9A6DABB409DA2B895A9601FBC05.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p – q = p + (–q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

11C2A10F4A244759806B140EB6F39A7A.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

110A82E1E1FC4971A8BD5448F9B12003.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0. For example, a hydrogen atom has 0 charge because its two constituents are oppositely charged.

CB11AAFC0F9E4E3AB2EA7F50C84E8083.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

C9F46A3C06764105ACF68235AE1F9A25.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

F06DD3959C634272BD15A861AE3170F9.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

789A181CB5FB42C8962D86D782DD395F.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order. For example, recognize that an account balance less than –30 dollars represents a debt greater than 30 dollars.

CBF241A7751B4DBDA8666EE03E3EE424.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation. For example, for an account balance of –30 dollars, write |–30| = 30 to describe the size of the debt in dollars.

C07033DD145C4DB2BB643AA67A446DE6.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts. For example, write –3°C > –7°C to express the fact that –3°C is warmer than –7°C.

80422CF57F93481AB738C30FEDC44183.description: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram. For example, interpret –3 > –7 as a statement that –3 is located to the right of –7 on a number line oriented from left to right.

735549705EB6404A826F8A4546872277.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

E38B317A2820477881041DDFA2E07C3F.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane

F7202F958E1C478D98D97FB898616288.description: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.

D6F6D6F7FE9145E290CB78EC474E88DF.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself (e.g., –(–3) = 3, and that 0 is its own opposite).

9246EEDE6908443587113FBF1919F356.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.

08038E43EBB94FAD85C43AF30B77F3FE.description: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, debits/credits, positive/negative electric charge); use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.

87031D735BBF40CE9EABC19F33A33611.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

E9717EE972D9423F9DEBA101F01B3633.description: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers 1–100 with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor. For example, express 36 + 8 as 4 (9 + 2).

BE9AB2AC9ADE4A6EB22B782F01869703.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation.

AAFD95D3CEE8493086385FEA08FCCB91.description: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.

8904EBA656094EBBB7480375FD5DE934.description: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

CB8747810BCD4BEA8D544FD338FBB65A.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions (e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem). For example, create a story context for (2/3) ÷ (3/4) and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient; use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (2/3) ÷ (3/4) = 8/9 because 3/4 of 8/9 is 2/3. (In general, (a/b) ÷ (c/d) = ad/bc.) How much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share 1/2 lb of chocolate equally? How many 3/4-cup servings are in 2/3 of a cup of yogurt? How wide is a rectangular strip of land with length 3/4 mi and area 1/2 square mi?

5E20F9601DCF4C92A4930B73E3A4C24B.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.

C57D08AF74D942249A3D98DEBA287407.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems. Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, percent error.

6D9CC595C365434398C9F73CB43631BD.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

3E70D0A94FA24A59A131EF741E5F5C72.description: Represent proportional relationships by equations. For example, if total cost t is proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn.

AB40EB4C92C945FFABE97F7DCAE64572.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

196A097ABF4B43A197D07A22FEADF339.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship (e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin).

C06B732C66794F39A99A83714C9685C8.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

5A169AAFA7CE469FB699D09E8420CF33.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units. For example, if a person walks 1/2 mile in each 1/4 hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction (1/2)/(1/4) miles per hour, equivalent to 2 miles per hour.

6078F8E41FE54F308CDAE6BFE8BE1433.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

9636FF447B4D4CA7848E273D6E0ACF87.description: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.

AA385D58187644B59C036AAED9EFBCCB.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole given a part and the percent.

27EC512FFF8449098FA5E848F8F3E17F.description: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed. For example, if it took 7 hours to mow 4 lawns, then at that rate, how many lawns could be mowed in 35 hours? At what rate were lawns being mowed?

318EF367EB514E59A8AD6BAD84F0ECFB.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.

0514781F4D1C4F6B8F77FBFA121842D8.description: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems (e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations).

753548B5CD0441DFA57451E9E23EFDCB.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0 (b not equal to zero), and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship. For example, "This recipe has a ratio of 3 cups of flour to 4 cups of sugar, so there is 3/4 cup of flour for each cup of sugar." "We paid $75 for 15 hamburgers, which is a rate of $5 per hamburger." (Expectations for unit rates in this grade are limited to non-complex fractions.)

04C8091A09A9492BB91767C7259E2FB6.description: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities. For example, "The ratio of wings to beaks in the bird house at the zoo was 2:1, because for every 2 wings there was 1 beak." "For every vote candidate A received, candidate C received nearly three votes."

1DC4E9280C5F46388790987F3E574DBF.description: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

A24480D2AFFD4E1F9549A079D278FB32.description: NRS Level 4 - High Intermediate Basic Education

6EE4F8EB3232495DB0DB19C8F9697534.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

31A3172056FA41719594E7F2F81985AA.description: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category. For example, all rectangles have four right angles and squares are rectangles, so all squares have four right angles.

67EC67D45F83476E9076274313EA8F4F.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

95F1FF886A6544C9A34C81BDD9FFA0E7.description: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

BC88F68E62CC4B15A7D9CC5746168A36.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

015ACC8F822E450B9691046E78B6311F.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

9D82287A8C6248C883A50740D0DA17E4.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

5731B1240AAC4D8E8D1B49BC1F777DA3.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

5E380C213B30426083ADBB0B708BC0D1.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.
