D42378DDE8EE491BA5760053745BEE11.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

71501A0243A947218DECB17CB0A8302F.description: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

7CA010D4BB53463FA9F07A16882DA97B.description: Apply the formulas V =(l)(w)(h) and V = (b)(h) for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems.

32AA5C5BC1F84B2EA84FE563E27083C3.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent three-fold whole-number products as volumes (e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.

363866AE59774BF4A560D44A5F118300.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real world and mathematical problems involving volume.

BB6FDFE687F8481EBFCF2635B91F8AD8.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.

BFCDBE4104E5485D97321B4D92C10434.description: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

58FF8DA5BA434E61812804BB55D111DD.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.

825873C36A27497A80EC494E6BB9BB7C.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

D2C7CAE3045344BAA95C3769F1E6DB05.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

A00D026ED11A4C3B941D814D9F2460AF.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m), and use these conversions in solving multi-step real world problems.

2D335DB858E046E1B8F7A0D4352C145A.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

7FA4A4A074824192AFC2ADF25672A696.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems (e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure).

6AF65943944049B78E5C76A0F2DB7D20.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

B92AFE45C4984320912301A4A13A1C01.description: An angle that turns through in one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

B08AF6F6C5F44840979E69EC901B6756.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

414D892FD7084E6CABC4725589A69BFE.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

07DD108F25314942B73A4CCE4DDE0A0E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

D3EC3278057A4B2CB028418D7914E5D1.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots. For example, given different measurements of liquid in identical beakers, find the amount of liquid each beaker would contain if the total amount in all the beakers were redistributed equally.

266AC3590C2B4FBABB74A12B92D66A48.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots. For example, from a line plot find and interpret the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in an insect collection.

937A87E231D84EFC8116CCB0104B18CC.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems. For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formula as a multiplication equation with an unknown-factor.

CDE37FDDD4B04ACB8FECC680A16C3D1B.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

75C065A8617D477C9C78F3116A617FC0.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb., oz.; l, ml; hr., min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table. For example: Know that 1 ft is 12 times as long as 1 in. Express the length of a 4 ft snake as 48 in. Generate a conversion table for feet and inches listing the number pairs (1, 12), (2, 24), (3, 36).

264C4978D2984D30A2C8F39FA1BE4FAE.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

28A89029D8384B19837C171BDCC795B4.description: Solve real-world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions (e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem). For example, how much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share a 1/2 pound of chocolate equally? How many 1/3-cup servings are in 2 cups of raisins?

2D802B15BE2343D1954749460C80585D.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients. For example, create a story context for 4 ÷ (1/5) and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that 4 ÷ (1/5) = 20 because 20 × (1/5) = 4

48241F84E317428EA0776412888EFE9A.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients. For example, create a story context for (1/3) ÷ 4 and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (1/3) ÷ 4 = 1/12 because (1/12) × 4 = 1/3.

87E2E4AC127B4170B4EF463AF5D47488.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions

F513BFB20E35402A81CF62FEFE65D900.description: Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers (e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem).

8B863462092740C99BFFE73685AFA17A.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than 1 as a familiar case); explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n×a) / (n×b) to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1.

F3DD3F5744604F22B5E5294A84225DAD.description: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.

301FB54727984476A75ED5776ED62FE1.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

25CA90EB26A84485A1052812F6FA5805.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b. For example, use a visual fraction model to show (2/3) x 4 = 8/3, and create a story context for this equation. Do the same with (2/3) x (4/5) = 8/15. (In general, (a/b) x (c/d) = ac/bd.)

38F2DB6B9FF842ECB69FCF0832A35EFF.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

3E154702DBDE43F19612356FFB483E4D.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers (e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem). For example, interpret 3/4 as the result of dividing 3 by 4, noting that 3/4 multiplied by 4 equals 3 and that when 3 wholes are shared equally among 4 people, each person has a share of size 3/4. If 9 people want to share a 50-pound sack of rice equally by weight, how many pounds of rice should each person get? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

513731B9E9DD4DB497DD9090949D224A.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

003BA6B4AE924BAD8EB4DB6AA85E350D.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators (e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem). Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers. For example, recognize an incorrect result 2/5 + 1/2 = 3/7 by observing that 3/7 < 1/2.

2AEB06C140464E8086810311986E5FF1.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators. For example, 2/3 + 5/4 = 8/12 + 15/12 = 23/12. (In general, a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd.)

979C56F2708D4CC5A321BC8B33F11177.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

FF1444FE4F69459689702ECF1A907E28.description: Compare two decimals to the hundredths place by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions (e.g., by using a visual model).

1B7A5B4406584F51ADB8A70BD3BF2039.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100. For example, rewrite 0.62 as 62/100; describe a length as 0.62 meters; locate 0.62 on a number line diagram.

A9E8363D00E7499FABB6CFF88A34D50A.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100. For example, express 3/10 as 30/100 and add 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100.

391817F9085F4A509A42D97A62FD58A0.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

DE0487B224B8436997E872F45BF6E3F8.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number (e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem). For example, if each person at a party will eat 3/8 of a pound of roast beef, and there will be 5 people at the party, how many pounds of roast beef will be needed? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

E46336585B4D4B3D8528EA35CC08E6D3.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number. For example, use a visual fraction model to express 3 × (2/5) as 6 × (1/5), recognizing this product as 6/5. (In general, n × (a/b) = (n × a)/b.)

C5679F11FC754EE2B53515BB1450B3B1.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b. For example, use a visual fraction model to represent 5/4 as the product 5 × (1/4), recording the conclusion by the equation 5/4 = 5 × (1/4).

271B60E6531E4CD0B11227442BD5CE9C.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

055D07C7DA954E0AB8EAD304FC895DBF.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators (e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem).

C2E76D1B287246DB979AD4E5178A9A8C.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators (e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction).

00328349064343EAA8AE50085011D87B.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions (e.g., by using a visual fraction model). Examples: 3/8 = 1/8 + 1/8 + 1/8; 3/8 = 1/8 + 2/8; 2 1/8 = 1 + 1 + 1/8 = 8/8 + 8/8 + 1/8.

5A58DA7F52A54AA6868CF11C5EC31E7B.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

096806CD78384092BB8779E0E6889928.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

E4235A2F503A408BA5B58343695CF812.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

69EF77A6C6084160A1B179BB39215D2C.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators (e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as ½). Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions (e.g., by using a visual fraction model).

3661234FC60A468EAFBBAE77E35355EE.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

82524AA9AB854685AE7DC0727B58942E.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

16917BEFC8AB43B18E114DD204919898.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

00675EFB25A24D0AB18401115395DE76.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

CA5D1B6242B743F9ABD9492E753A8898.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

85CE19B2DAA046A48AA602B50EBB0AE3.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

7796A5E6718749AAA42BB4B2345A7CBA.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

5D02B271480C4705A3D75E3EA6D88AEB.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

5294AD709B674F299B0881C3D35BF8CB.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form (e.g., 347.392 = 3 × 100 + 4 × 10 + 7 × 1 + 3 × (1/10) + 9 × (1/100) + 2 × (1/1000).

4DE66A2F1FE148AF83D7531A8D159A66.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

031DE5EEB9ED4C298798AFF45F97FDDE.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole number exponents to denote powers of 10.

49A7AFAF6EB3400F99A9AC9AD055B5AB.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

ACE86F622648424B8FE2E930B8F51F07.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

91CF5CF29E944382998BAF99097C435F.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

530DE99C4ECB473AAD0B584E37B8EA3F.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

6DE8887ACFB04CFEBA3E8B683FD5C485.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

5A8A4971FE844F1890288F1846206B56.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

15D542AD1BE9484C970AA7E589FE9920.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

031B4883917648429F1C528FC80B9CB2.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right. For example, recognize that 700 ÷ 70 = 10 by applying concepts of place value and division.

D8F9A8C40C0142CCB2D6FFCD29CBEB84.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

07383CA724FE486C89C25A5CB4460168.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

B88B312285D0409B8CAABE8E31AA703B.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane. For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 0, and given the rule "Add 6" and the starting number 0, generate terms in the resulting sequences, and observe that the terms in one sequence are twice the corresponding terms in the other sequence. Explain informally why this is so.

F40DE93CAF3046C8A13BBD2CDF032B89.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them. For example, express the calculation "add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2" as 2 × (8 + 7). Recognize that 3 × (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921, without having to calculate the indicated sum or product.

1ABB0D1A25E34DFEAE857FF417762FCC.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

3FAD39FDA3DE41A0BA065EAEAAF0176D.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself. For example, given the rule "add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.

DCD802D01A09426D90A67A78DD4A8F01.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1-100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1-100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1-100 is prime or composite.

E09BCA8D8B4142E8B58F4249BF84B7E5.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

425778B59EFE4F348E83A88D6A93DFC1.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

2AE8572A47D44187BB5221B5ADC11EFC.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison (e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem), distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

AF99A1E8325E45489F1528F9AA1BC6C7.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison (e.g., interpret 35 = 5 x 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5). Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

B67CD5FA748B4E32BCFA1FCFF580F253.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

2D7328B37CA54E43B3293721BABD194C.description: NRS Level 3 - Low Intermediate Basic Education

A0F7F6C369544210AD79AA11D5514A58.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole. For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as 1/4 of the area of the shape.

1BC6BF19DE8D43DEB7BE8EB54184DDA8.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

2CFC2BED988842F58CDBC824ACE63973.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

18A8629871EC4BF495884D973BDCBD6C.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.

0B7E1FDFEB45407486F08106A5A787DB.description: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes. Sizes are compared directly or visually, not compared by measuring.

37623DDF6ED84194B353A53FDDC19D11.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

528EC2DF73E34A0EAEEB44B3F8ECFBF6.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

69F9AED899D14864AF8A000616999548.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

712E504D1D3B46F597344BEE45DD5DF6.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

E484464245D94092A7A8F24297FF9FB4.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

1D9CDD0BE9EB4384AC29BFC660245C4E.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

393B4D83FE244793841F735FCAFD340A.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

5CDA87D8FA184E9BB16B8CAC1A754881.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

507D98D232EA4362AC6B013389A8122C.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

433592307A1C4B75AB683E1F77808596.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

18271004D52D42729D4F23DC2E728136.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

4C6C7D6602B44896A0F23B5B610E93B6.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

1E6D9B3C137D4CE78C8FCC39FA1423EB.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

302C8AE0D6BF4C86BD55E0CF81EDA930.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units (e.g., by using drawings such as a beaker with a measurement scale to represent the problem).

7A138FBAC7564165891AE331A3104435.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes (e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram).

6B98CCAAC5394023AF3DB1D6F7DF598F.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

997E43892994450886BD38E27273034E.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units - whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

07772C00E6854BE69F8D3C5A017360E6.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs. For example, draw a bar graph in which each square in the bar graph might represent 5 pets.

C534C16D60AC42648C688B4DB8C8E8DD.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately. Example: If you have 2 dimes and 3 pennies, how many cents do you have?

1DC25FF968EA4F84A37C709E0E496D3F.description: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

EBB8C29103C64738904CED3F3F9B5BA6.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2… and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

A7511AF51AE342E79BF1A0683D2A8C36.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units (e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem).

661B6AA33D034565B30A26BF67891441.description: Relate addition and subtraction to length.

EB753620FD13403CB38CE7BCF68D885D.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.

C50A6D14DBEF4DB6A9386268DDD97017.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

284FF551FDE14D1DAD2722BE4BA8CEFE.description: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.

29F70A7E6C0541A59D082AB4C520CD88.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.

D441DB7FE4EB41E796254D93D2A48AD5.description: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.

C3E13912A81448C88E0FAB1D488DB80A.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole.

53576C4D9BE54F679F2F177D062C05D6.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers. Examples: Express 3 in the form 3 = 3/1; recognize that 6/1 = 6; locate 4/4 and 1 at the same point of a number line diagram.

6D0686DD4497432A92E9049C3584695E.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions (e.g., 1/2 = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3). Explain why the fractions are equivalent (e.g., by using a visual fraction model).

CBEB0EA2059842E3916A04C79426CC65.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size or the same point on a number line.

7C0EC4DCC4304086A285EFA3E2156A14.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

7BC8A65026E549068CA74BEFA7CE6AB0.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

F07907C24BD7424F936FE54177704A3B.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

21B93C9661D54C6E83793AEA2148DBA8.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

D2AE0DB174E740B394ECE74F550EEB90.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

B85FCA2422564C7E9ADC222D3485F89A.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

5F2475F899D54F13AF4D27F31178DDB7.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10–90 (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

BAF92BC9B98E4238B034B1BE3DC9D84C.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

19685347389D4E3781E322DBD40F3247.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

350AEBE2FD3242E7845846BDA953EE1B.description: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations. (Explanations may be supported by drawings or objects.)

37859E9176814C77AEA40C5366923BEF.description: Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100–900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100–900.

E5EEAD24CC2546FCB487BC4B2095B952.description: Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.

ED5B067729C84C4D97BF752E9B4C38B1.description: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

323F04E6441F4A34A103CE6B90494BBF.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract and to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

A7B3AAE82DF9427F9DFA8CD806473476.description: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

F0E20818764D425AABEED13C98111FA6.description: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

793A48D90FA24CF089AC0CEE113304CF.description: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

6A14DC20269148B4B7EDA330101FA41E.description: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a "hundred."

755E2BF688CF419DA3395B9A5275AE5A.description: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones (e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones). Understand the following as special cases:

B2F9D5628A46464981CB10E0F14AF151.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

4641FFA3151945249D792A1F7DDE30D2.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations. For example, observe that 4 times a number is always even, and explain why 4 times a number can be decomposed into two equal addends.

764D58653D2741A4958D7B6C010998B9.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding. This standard is limited to problems posed with whole numbers and having whole number answers; students should know how to perform operations in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (order of operations).

402E20C4AC7D4C39A6CE218FF497DA82.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

4739EAA301AD4E57B6EE57A64AE2E7B1.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 ×5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. Know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

02B96EBF0E594DFEBFD40E28028C3370.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem. For example, find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8.

A704F31C6B954DB88A5B66F7D3EFFC9A.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide. Examples: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known (commutative property of multiplication). 3 × 5 × 2 can be found by 3 × 5 = 15, then 15 × 2 = 30, or by 5 × 2 = 10, then 3 × 10 = 30 (associative property of multiplication). Knowing that 8 × 5 = 40 and 8 × 2 = 16, one can find 8 × 7 as 8 × (5 + 2) = (8 × 5) + (8 × 2) = 40 + 16 = 56 (distributive property). Students need not use formal terms for these properties.

A7CCEF583D454F048EFD0C15B9FC66CB.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

A850C197648640539F487803B7758471.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers. For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 × ? = 48, 5 = ? = 3, 6 × 6 = ?

F3995E47C1544A06965A51B65E2F9882.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities (e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem).

3A28F827D6144C0BAD63BAEEFC6E8FC1.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers (e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each). For example, describe a context in which a number of shares or a number of groups can be expressed as 56 ÷ 8.

6903125087BB43D5B4394676E88E871B.description: Interpret products of whole numbers (e.g., interpret 5 x 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each). For example, describe a context in which a total number of objects can be expressed as 5 x 7.

18D50F13B8D047588C2820E86C758278.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

27CC581BF2334771B820B505BF86CE95.description: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns; a meeting write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.

384A19EBDB2744FE8FE8CE1DFE62D316.description: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members (e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by 2s); write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.

73A0064679354E099F519DC0D8280629.description: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.

E852888738CB480BA720D5A22B2550F6.description: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. Know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.

DA876859D3AB49AE9A207BFFFBBC715C.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and Checking grocery comparing, with unknowns in all positions receipt against (e.g., by using drawings and equations purchases with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem).

0EC1BFD47EC741ADBEE0CA1D7322ACD5.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

E0B6846AAC19442F93CE8B73BED3B3FE.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

814FF0A8759642C89BD3118126DAD078.description: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape. Students do not need to learn formal names such as "right rectangular prism."

CB3DA1E0564E4C51AC74265CAEE066FF.description: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.

EFD721EC0F24458389E0D950EF7F6AAF.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

E63919EB8074475281828256B367815C.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes. For example, "Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?"

7575E4A58DEE4106955E85F3F9E81134.description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components and drawing shapes.

0A5D23BF1EA045149CF5C7D2B9D89478.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/"corners") and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

E344465365CF4D7E8BC960D0B502A52A.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.

F2F93B04396C4B8497E63C8C9D568C4F.description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, "flat") or three-dimensional ("solid").

4958931B30CF41A192E3B979DE8190EF.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

CD1C5F2D38CA4482B497FEFAEB46C563.description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

68A408754A0E4DFDBD6C678623D395FF.description: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).

A1407EDFB13E4D628682D7B41B326241.description: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.

9B0C91A5855445C7A6AF72CDE8036DA8.description: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.

6CC59F7427EC43379909EB63DA39DA50.description: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps. Limit to contexts where the object being measured is spanned by a whole number of length units with no gaps or overlaps.

23B5E9EC04D84683A95297F092257326.description: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.

F8013C1A91DD483B8E93A8575269E99B.description: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.

343916BD532D4819A87763ECB70B263B.description: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count.

E49A917109C2455492E9F176EC5680EF.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.

86EC386FC15842269565BFA4128C6B61.description: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has "more of"/"less of" the attribute, and describe the difference. For example, directly compare the heights of two people and describe one person as taller/shorter.

E7A020D302854FBEAFF90295AAED70B5.description: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.

05482BD8F7C0441EB0EA232E77E8C4C5.description: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10–90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10–90 (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

9386D46B067742D88896E4C8A69CEEFF.description: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.

7270AC41A3B844C9A30305AAF52F1CB5.description: Add within 100, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.

D2CA9E0887DE4C08946715063ACEBEEB.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

5C18958CAD0A413CAB4995F078C94406.description: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <.

186CE91F531B431999D7B39AF1E278EB.description: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).

77C70C992B2948E2A4E7062B68FDC98B.description: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

BE45622908CC4D6AA5A8B7EC51756AFE.description: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones—called a "ten."

ACA4867C76134A2391ADA3AF48DE36B8.description: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:

498A2B6A8D7641288AD6D8A40A3A0536.description: Work with numbers 11-19 and tens to gain a foundation and understand place value.

41A8115531144D66AF4F65F39C7D2593.description: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.

516631F5A68D48A8960859DA8E214A9E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

1DEABFA7290A4EDA937C6C662447BC05.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers. For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 + ? = 11, 5 = ? – 3, 6 + 6 = ?.

31ACA6D4A31441C58BFA17F9D32EDACC.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false. For example, which of the following equations are true and which are false? 6 = 6, 7 = 8 – 1, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2.

41C9561FA60F4E83ABCC6BB4A6078DA9.description: Work with addition and subtraction equations.

00400F88D4B14F42B9F545FEF0406B9A.description: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 – 4 = 13 – 3 – 1 = 10 – 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 – 8 = 4); and reading equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

2E809FB8DBC34C998E2C83C88CB743CC.description: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).

D536AAD051C14064AB0B61F5CE0D27CC.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem. For example, subtract 10 – 8 by finding the number that makes 10 when added to 8.

4583744E76F1423DA00E53C8D9215BC1.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract. Examples: If 8 + 3 = 11 is known, then 3 + 8 = 11 is also known (commutative property of addition). To add 2 + 6 + 4, the second two numbers can be added to make a ten, so 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12 (associative property of addition). Students need not use formal terms for these properties.

D86D3A62F6024160B34E21D94767ED82.description: Understand and apply properties and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

E6FD77454E294D5DA96A29E0336B4F0B.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20 (e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem).

8FA5EE59726A404CBD7D588100343064.description: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions (e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem).

AAD1169AEC0F4CFEB5FFBF3B930C1CC5.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

ADCDF2ABE2E64F278331C489CE16EFF5.description: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number (e.g., by using objects or drawings), and record the answer with a drawing or equation.

F6044F00BA1046E7818E1716E2350668.description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way (e.g., by using objects or drawings), and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).

75872E26AB8F43C386C87174FC9E5183.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10 (e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem).

2A8564B362114BF1AD636C907E406B87.description: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), and acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations. Drawings need not show details, but should show the mathematics in the problem.

61A7FE44F2174979BD53861143B04158.description: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.

33FD6D08028A420799A8F645312DA8BC.description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.

CB1089DD08CB4903AEF65F6A43F36638.description: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group (e.g., by using matching and counting strategies). Include groups with up to ten objects.

A014B25A63154E72A6B85109AF742B8D.description: Count to answer "how many?" questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1–20, count out that many objects.

12374AF97E2A4044B8A7F98BF1FB4655.description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

B482CBDA63F743098C22B13450F29119.description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.

2A7A4AC698E4483BA8CE01D8F4045EEF.description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.

9D61CD11231A4CC7A156807D2971755D.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

A06C2DED586248DB892CB1C5ED8FAB9E.description: Count to tell the number of objects.

4EB3E12B11C34A16A6EC6BDFA91EBB78.description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

8BBF9A15A15B4CD4992FA93D056734E2.description: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).

F41FB3F0482A463FB216989CB6D26F2E.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

003EBC5821C8484FBC4757A4046580CE.description: Know number names and the count sequence.

ABB8022DC4AD4EC2B7351839216A3779.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

E5FB6C2280044CE1A4203AC61585A887.description: Look for and make use of structure.

9EEF3E6A1FBF42CDBB74D857233DDA67.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

19F350FF6E394522B16456C3371F6FD7.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: New Illinois Learning Standards – Science (NILS-Science)

A54774EB544A4400A2B7F316DBD2EDDD.description: Analyze data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of how each performs.

1BF27A586C1242C3BC71DA2807E659FD.description: Develop a simple sketch, drawing, or physical model to illustrate how the shape of an object helps it function as needed to solve a given problem.

87480054D1E64A62B3BC803CE0F2AD46.description: Ask questions, make observations, and gather information about a situation people want to change to define a simple problem that can be solved through the development of a new or improved object or tool.

8035BF811E874084A3E59BFE3669050B.description: Obtain information to identify where water is found on Earth and that it can be solid or liquid.

74189ADF3A814CAEA95C232CCD001619.description: Develop a model to represent the shapes and kinds of land and bodies of water in an area.
comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include quantitative scaling in models.

2489228ADBA5473EB76A019CA8453400.description: Compare multiple solutions designed to slow or prevent wind or water from changing the shape of the land.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of solutions could include different designs of dikes and windbreaks to hold back wind and water, and different designs for using shrubs, grass, and trees to hold back the land.

ED897FA745DF401C89DA6638D974CD45.description: Use information from several sources to provide evidence that Earth events can occur quickly or slowly.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of events and timescales could include volcanic explosions and earthquakes, which happen quickly and erosion of rocks, which occurs slowly.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include quantitative measurements of timescales.
Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the diversity of living things in each of a variety of different habitats.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include specific animal and plant names in specific habitats.
FF59DE9E3D054BC0941DB7BC74113F13.description: Make observations of plants and animals to compare the diversity of life in different habitats.

5035D66977B543ABA6748EB1A13097C0.description: Develop a simple model that mimics the function of an animal in dispersing seeds or pollinating plants.

7A0B34A57B7E47D6B51758460F4A8EBC.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine if plants need sunlight and water to grow.
comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to testing one variable at a time.

2CE7712194604F99A67E44CD026114D2.description: Construct an argument with evidence that some changes caused by heating or cooling can be reversed and some cannot.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of reversible changes could include materials such as water and butter at different temperatures. Examples of irreversible changes could include cooking an egg, freezing a plant leaf, and heating paper.
Clarification Statement: Examples of pieces could include blocks, building bricks, or other assorted small objects.
8A206F3A584049FA95D84EC037CE804C.description: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account of how an object made of a small set of pieces can be disassembled and made into a new object.

8141722C6EB042A184FA1DEA33F32412.description: Analyze data obtained from testing different materials to determine which materials have the properties that are best suited for an intended purpose.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of properties could include, strength, flexibility, hardness, texture, and absorbency.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment of quantitative measurements is limited to length.

09B407A911AD4FDA8C8A19BC8CABEFE0.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to describe and classify different kinds of materials by their observable properties.
comments: Clarification Statement: Observations could include color, texture, hardness, and flexibility. Patterns could include the similar properties that different materials share.

document.title: Illinois ABE/ASE Reading Content Standards and Benchmarks

6C141E0F46FA425D961984CB6DAA1A62.description: Apply environmental reading to life skills (e.g., a brochure on workplace medical benefits and/or a consumer guide about long distance phone service).

9BD490E3737E442D9697DE24506988F6.description: Identify the writer's style (e.g., repetition of a key word, use of a string of opposites) used to convey ideas.

5FC4FCB7D930499AB7C8E7B667A5AD5D.description: Differentiate between fact and opinion in order to make decisions by comparing and contrasting facts.

2B9769D2BE3E4AA08643C14EE8100FB3.description: Analyze a character in a fictional passage by identifying the character's appearance, behaviors, actions, and dialogue with other characters.

BFBF96CF6AD14021AF6814253EB57779.description: Locate information on a given topic in several types of reference materials (e.g., dictionary, Internet, newspaper).

F60C827AD6E14F0187E7A388D91DF902.description: Make generalizations from implicit ideas (e.g., first paragraph of The Declaration of Independence).

72E91B0BF26E4CDC96491DC4A92B706A.description: Determine a character's motivation in a play by examining the character's dialogue, actions, and stage directions.

A7A4E592333C4EC08C1E9508EBE765F9.description: Identify phrases or words that the author used to create an image or mental picture in a poem.

AC02F831254E438C96012F5045191769.description: Identify the moral of a short story or a play.

76963E059D334B2797360B663E98E594.description: Compare and contrast the personalities of two characters in a story.

A237DABDFE3C4F8A99135A1A1E87355E.description: Identify directly stated and implied main ideas based on stated and suggested information.

4070C0F1F04E45AB82B6B2501BF263D6.description: Follow complex instructions or directions that include conditionals (e.g., if and then statement) and multiple steps.

D78590625C724BBB840E77FECF4FA997.description: Demonstrate understanding of specialized vocabulary from the content areas (e.g., science, social studies, and Constitution).

ABD8036683424D628E0972F27D2EBA79.description: Apply environmental reading to life skills (e.g., read a campus catalog, read instructions from a job-search-focused website).

03763564376C4CF0ACE9AC16DA66C159.description: Use a graphic organizer to demonstrate the importance of and relationship between ideas (e.g., Venn diagram, webbing, and mapping).

31DC9539146149DDB09141AC1F8235BA.description: Identify opinions, propaganda, and bias within written publications (e.g., newspapers, political cartoons).

D3D0887D37C442CEAEFBC76936E34EB3.description: Recognize differences in structure, content, and tone of various texts.

7F377B2D60734AD18256B0CD8D72A34A.description: Identify relationships between similar documents (e.g., order form and invoice) and compare information for accuracy.

05C35752ED864A149F66E3E18B52DAB5.description: Follow directions necessary to perform a moderately complex sequential task.

12230A55F5D240A4A907187A17902937.description: Interpret information in context (e.g., medical, occupational, parenting) and apply that information to a new situation.

C2DE6C7A91984C908E8D77FCC55C7E1E.description: Identify and interpret common figurative language (e.g., simile, metaphor, hyperbole) found in a literary work or poem.

D6FE630E233E4ED6A71D973D46BBDC22.description: Identify the elements of a plot (e.g., beginning, exposition, middle-complications and climax; end-resolution) within a literary work.

CC854FBB8A064F95B1287A642BE93853.description: Identify the central idea or theme of a literary work (e.g., short story, drama, poetry).

3EF092C66ED641EBB2C672BF9843058D.description: Read a technical manual or a legal document and explain a sequential process about a complex and unfamiliar work procedure.

9F89A5FD99DB44CEB48B3A98BA601D0A.description: Identify and restate in own words the implied main idea from symbols used to represent a person, place, or thing (e.g., political cartoon) or main idea of a multi-paragraph passage.

57BB6491582D4D07ACD6C4F563BF7BB9.description: Demonstrate understanding of synonyms, antonyms and different applications of the same word (multiple meanings).

2F7AAC7B7D98474E99B4B04C2884F896.description: Demonstrate understanding of language structures by focusing on idioms, expressions, colloquialisms and literary structures.

713CFA0DFCE64CD4A32B29F965A8191F.description: Apply environmental reading to life skills (e.g., read and summarize a brief message addressed to a group of co-workers, read simple directions for a fax or computer to perform the sequence of tasks).

F5094FFE983D4FE59D87FC52B849BCAE.description: Begin to identify and interpret similes and metaphors.

15DE79BCD54542519588BC9B7451BE3F.description: Determine the appropriate reading strategy to acquire specific information (e.g., rereading, skimming, and scanning).

9C58CEEF74CD4661939169263609889E.description: Demonstrate an awareness of the difference between the use of English in formal and informal settings.

508FFCB00DFE4046BC6FB78235800D14.description: Clarify understanding of non-fictional passages by creating outlines, graphic organizers, logical notes, summaries, or reports.

E3A172394D5546ABBC5B4963776EB3D8.description: Integrate information from texts, charts, and graphs to draw a conclusion.

DC12AC57A88E433DB26C2516F0956295.description: Determine the meaning of persuasive language and faulty logic used in print and visual material (e.g., advertisement).

F4D1F68478574AB9A9BD362A74768A91.description: Identify features that distinguish fiction, drama, poetry, fables, and legends.

210069A8B2A64A358F7002DA5DCB1E60.description: Predict probable outcomes from knowledge of events obtained from a reading selection.

CC210AE8A9624F5BACD2F4FB3B1F57DB.description: Be able to summarize what has been read.

7AA4B9F8E83D411F87060A81921CA5BE.description: Identify cause and effect implied in a paragraph.

677E53E492D64F0CBBA59326BE977751.description: Identify the implied main idea and supporting details from an instructional level passage.

C6C2F115CFB0416C8B597D448D7EF9D1.description: Determine author's purpose (e.g., to entertain, inform, and persuade) from a variety of written pieces (e.g., newspaper article, travel brochure, and store catalog).

6BBF292C34094F05827B513C394A05ED.description: Select, explore, and evaluate sources, such as a dictionary, Internet, magazine, and newspaper, to obtain and to evaluate information for a specific task using research as serves the student's purpose.

063085A3954F4C83A5671BE783110AAE.description: Identify and use the structural features of newspapers, magazines, and editorials.

DFC8C15DF958446E9CCFF9000F1B46B0.description: Read and interpret information in newspapers, and periodicals.

7112D72E2B994C68B885D5334F64137D.description: Demonstrate an awareness of the difference between the use of English in formal and informal settings (e.g., formal vs. slang use in a job interview).

E2EB8E4F1CC74603BDE4325327BB608F.description: Recognize and understand clipped and shortened words (e.g., exam-examination).

3CE7D3A68A8C4EFE8B48D4A3EAEAE638.description: Identify idioms and their use in passages.

8FCC3BA597F349B3BF322B06A2168FF9.description: Identify and interpret basic figurative language (e.g., similes, metaphors, pun, and alliteration).

31B74A0DEAC7416AACBF443D65E489EB.description: Use a dictionary to locate the meaning of words used in a statement.

12D8E1EC2DDE4E27B3EAD640B43D50C0.description: Apply environmental reading to life skills (e.g., read nutrition charts).

2021CD32AD0A4A26906B297573636DE9.description: Read instructional level narrative and expository text aloud at a conversational rate with expression and accuracy.

902E0D0BF99B48E4B012C1AB454CC2E3.description: Determine the sequence of events in a written passage.

594F54C3595E400790C9CAE337274E1A.description: Skim for overall understanding and scan for keywords and ideas.

F61B726A670E492797FF79A7EA887065.description: At instructional level, formulate questions while reading text.

FC924EAC3E6C4B5EABE6045A3F24738B.description: Identify and apply appropriate strategies to aid comprehension (e.g., graphic organizers, outlining).

1F20F483D1F54DFBBC88D68EC0FC249E.description: Make inferences about short passages at grade-level (e.g., identifying correct multiple choice answers or writing short answers to questions).

4636513A0F79475B83C2C3C3A2C34381.description: Determine the appropriate reading strategy to acquire specific information (e.g., rereading, skimming, and scanning).

D462FF9B5DF14C32A4492D0AD243529F.description: Locate pertinent information in multi-paragraph passages and apply it to answer a question.

5E5925B35C3E49DFB95168A24BCF2628.description: Summarize the main idea of a passage by answering who, what, when, why, and how questions.

document.title: Illinois Learning Standards Incorporating the Common Core English Language Arts

A208AAC0DFE5013181BB68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

A2085B80DFE5013181BA68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., bullheaded, willful, firm, persistent, resolute).

A2080690DFE5013181B968A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words to better understand each of the words.

A207A8E0DFE5013181B868A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g. verbal irony, puns) in context.

A2073E50DFE5013181B768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

A206DFA0DFE5013181B668A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

A2069010DFE5013181B568A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

A2064060DFE5013181B468A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., precede, recede, secede).

A205EF20DFE5013181B368A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

A20599B0DFE5013181B268A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words or phrases based on grade 8 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

A204D310DFE5013181B068A86D17958E.description: Use verbs in the active and passive voice and in the conditional and subjunctive mood to achieve particular effects (e.g., emphasizing the actor or the action; expressing uncertainty or describing a state contrary to fact).

A20457B0DFE5013181AF68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

A2034650DFE5013181AC68A86D17958E.description: Use an ellipsis to indicate an omission.

A202F3E0DFE5013181AB68A86D17958E.description: Use punctuation (comma, ellipsis, dash) to indicate a pause or break.

A202A280DFE5013181AA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

A2024F00DFE5013181A968A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb voice and mood.

A2017E80DFE5013181A768A86D17958E.description: Form and use verbs in the active and passive voice.

A2010EA0DFE5013181A668A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of verbals (gerunds, participles, infinitives) in general and their function in particular sentences.

A200BC30DFE5013181A568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A1FF9820DFE5013181A268A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

A1FEB740DFE5013181A068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

A1FE5470DFE50131819F68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

A1FD7E50DFE50131819D68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

A1FCC200DFE50131819B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

A1FC7540DFE50131819A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

A1C23D30DFE5013180F268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.
