document.title: Illinois Culturally Responsive Teaching and Leading Standards

C3B260D7688E4F26BA38EA9639251D3E.description:
Ensure classroom and building decorations are inclusive of all students throughout
 the building or within the community or city at large.

9066BEB84D4045D98291450913AC3FAD.description:
Verify that course materials are representative of all students, including materials
 for centers, stations, labs, classroom libraries, etc.

39434BAF037340FF9EFB6D123050A5D7.description:
Ensure linguistic diversity is represented throughout the building and seek ways to
 reflect representation of world languages.

73B86BA94F8F47418B5F50C5263D0C4A.description:
Uphold systems of support that create, promote, and sustain a welcoming and
 inclusive community.

606E375414834B3980C869E5E42CD998.description:
Student Representation in the Learning Environment – Culturally responsive teachers and
 leaders ensure the diversity of their student population is equally represented within the
 learning environment. In turn, all members of the student population feel seen, heard, and
 affirmed. Exceptionally well-versed culturally responsive teachers and leaders provide
 exposure to underrepresented or misrepresented minority groups, even when they are not
 present within the population of their school and community at large. The culturally
 responsive teacher and leader will:

842623389A0D42DA91374869B7D3853C.description:
Consider a broader modality of student assessments, such as performance
 portfolios, essays, multiple choice, State exams, oral examination, community
 assessments, work experiences, social justice work, action research projects, and
 recognition beyond academia.

BE79208DD307466A99E8EDE8A125E6E6.description:
Promote robust discussion with the intent of raising consciousness that reflects
 modern society and the ways in which cultures and communities intersect.

D437AFFBAFEC49A48996C67454EABC22.description: Use a resource tool to assess the curriculum and assessments for biases.

40B5E655CD484A4DAF1F93C8A9248E55.description:
Ensure teacher and students co-create content that encourages critical thinking
 about culture and includes counternarratives to dominant culture.

92E0DDA51B2E446799586BEDE59E03D8.description: Ensure text selections reflect students' classroom, community, and family culture.

4A5AC9AA1775421C85B7EF033817B852.description:
Implement and integrate the wide spectrum and fluidity of identities in the
 curriculum.

08B337DFC8AE4015B6107C664D10301E.description:
Assess one's story through multiple vantage points to gain a whole narrative that
 includes all sides of parties involved.

15A83FD8DEBC4D3DA8D593246679E764.description:
Embrace and encourage a balance of viewpoints and perspectives that leverage asset
 thinking toward traditionally marginalized populations.

4F67E18B75B046F5A7BDDB8E003011EB.description:
Ensure assessments reflect the enriched curriculum that has embedded student
 identities.

C8961A7494D64D48BCF02B63F7AB3993.description:
Employ authentic and modern technology usage inspiring digital literacy
 through an equity lens.

65AD42604F5043DC98E91255FB6033FA.description:
Identify and articulate the purposeful ways in which marginalized communities
 are represented in curriculum, including print, digital media, and other
 classroom resources.

9A0D16B802CD4C09A79849A56B1FFC9C.description:
Content Selections in all Curricula – Culturally responsive teachers and leaders intentionally
 embrace student identities and prioritize representation in the curriculum. In turn, students
 are not only given a chance to identify with the curriculum, they become exposed to other
 cultures within their schools and both their local and global communities. The culturally
 responsive teacher and leader will:

8136C66A866642B3BE7E870952DF9C98.description:
Collaborate effectively over time with the local community and community
 agencies, when and where appropriate, to promote a positive environment for
 student learning.

FAB4CB732E4841FA8B779FD030CAFA33.description:
Communicate and provide appropriate techniques and materials to support and
 enrich student learning at home.

02377B6FCFE942718447C4329EB9E1E1.description: Welcome communication from parents and reply in a timely manner.

279421D4C21945E1B854EC62718C4719.description:
Invite family and community members to teach about topics that are culturally
 specific and aligned to the classroom curriculum or content area.

9F52E05113004C0C8E3ACE98078F743C.description:
Foster students' cultural understanding and connection to the surrounding
 community.

C4C3F4B667094036BA3BCAC1E2F4BB17.description:
Develop relationships with families and the community outside of the classroom
 setting.

E8ECBBCFF62D49B681861A15CF9CE286.description:
Use best practices that are culturally responsive to value students and their families'
 cultural traditions when recognizing, motivating, encouraging, and supporting
 student success and growth.

26DD178B9A2345F1A66C919B7B94AD7D.description:
Continuously learn and build cultural knowledge that families and the community
 bring to the school community to nurture and foster relationships and inform
 student learning experiences.

8030734D2032407F9B8ED05596E76D82.description:
Forge ongoing participation with families and community members to meet the
 diverse needs and interests of students.

7EFCB6489C58445A96A1B9C98C5CAF38.description:
Actively seek multiple perspectives and contribution from families and the
 community and invite them to actively share their opinions, feedback, and concerns
 that impact the school community.

4130DF34722F418B86B17F2CBBC4E515.description:
Regularly interact with students, families, and communities in both English and home
 language through methods of their preference.

EEA972B73B7F4CC0BC467308C809C2A8.description:
Family and Community Collaboration – Culturally responsive teachers and leaders will
 partner with families and communities to build rapport, form collaborative and mutual
 relationships, and engage in effective cross-cultural communication. The culturally responsive
 teacher and leader will:

C8B57D26091746D09082A40BDC04E99D.description:
Give students space to solve their own problems, negotiate their advocacy needs,
 and present their perspectives.

F11B7154A1F6495596B76F8166281F57.description:
Communicate high expectations to which all students can be held and urge students
 to lead as student advocates appropriate to the students' age and development.

2741496BA61C42F7BB13155A3171E9FC.description: Research and offer student advocacy content with real world implications.

89756FDFE96348ED81EE8B5435CA0EEA.description: Create a risk-taking space that promotes student advocacy.

35578B9DA4F44B33B0B76A6543390E0B.description:
Help students identity actions that can be taken to apply learning to develop
 opportunities and relationships for alliances.

A419BA3D95194628AE4E5A1C818AF164.description:
Include students in the creation of an inclusive learning community with more
 opportunities for student expression.

EC96EEF064DA4D9EB858586D44A23FD9.description: Offer guidance to students on how to develop a self-advocacy plan to inform decisions and choices.

8ECEC423C80440F79165A1ABE911A9D1.description: Emphasize and connect with students about their identities, advocacies, and self-        interest.

6C682265D42847E59784B9BF695A6162.description: Leveraging Student Advocacy – Culturally responsive teachers and leaders will support and create opportunities for student advocacy and representation in the content and classroom. The culturally responsive teacher and leader will:

9D93739E3FFF4E81A09A61C8C7385C29.description: Persistently solicit student feedback, value that feedback (resist defensiveness), and adjust based on that feedback.

DE1F9A47905B43B286BF0C38791C3CA9.description: Create and embed student leadership opportunities into the student experience (e.g., peer-led discussion, student-led workshops, and student- run schoolwide initiatives).

A158134D6A2A44818B50BCFFC44CB82F.description: Co-create, with students, the collective expectations and agreements regarding the physical space and social-emotional culture of the classroom and school.

2FAD525327124C9DA715748C50579F27.description: Consistently solicit students' input on the curriculum (e.g., interests, people, or concepts).

6CFD68D3CAC54343B6D5B56957F17457.description: Make authentic connections between academic learning and students' prior knowledge, native language, culture, and values.

577145027DFD4E6BBCB75B1EFB1A6B10.description: Encourage and affirm the personal experiences (family, community, culture, etc.) students share in the classroom.

078558C6A51844DAB38DB4F6E175419C.description: Students as Co-Creators – Culturally responsive teachers and leaders who fundamentally believe all students are capable center learning around students' experiences and position them as co-creators, with emphasis on prioritizing historically marginalized students. The culturally responsive teacher and leader will:

94ECA5688D004D80981813F84AB3CC35.description: Set holistic goals for students that accommodate multiple ways of demonstrating strengths and success, (e.g., alternate academic achievement metrics, growth indicators, leadership, character development, social- emotional learning competencies, and school values).

A9FE8BFF33404EDF933C49F355A8FDC4.description: Provide multiple opportunities for parents to communicate in their language and method of preference, to the greatest extent possible.

FA0D3665F62B4315B27B234B6B011D4A.description: Share the classroom systems and policies (expectations, agreements, recognition and incentive practices, etc.) used in the classroom with students' families and align them to the values and cultural norms of those families.

0CB985C732954A50B0DDDD261AF749A7.description:
Provide parents with information about what their child is expected to learn,
 know, and do at his or her grade level and ways to reinforce concepts at home.

F9CF4BD5D0C94F0B95FB357C72A24587.description: Develop positive, strength-based partnerships with students and their families by learning about them, soliciting their opinions, and valuing their expectations, especially with those marginalized by schools in the past.

0546E61990174834B8CF887B8B00AEE7.description: Engage with students’ families and community members outside of the classroom to develop a more holistic understanding of the students’ lived experiences.

6E86CD66358B4F448CF978810AB7E300.description: Learn from and about their students’ culture, language, and learning styles to make instruction more meaningful and relevant to their students’ lives.

AC702C07780B410FB6E639CF306B2251.description: Students as Individuals – Culturally responsive teachers and leaders view and value their  students as individuals within the context of their families and communities. The culturally  responsive teacher and leader will:

E7DC192BF1A843EF9296F2833E3F2B50.description: Understand how a system of inequity reinforces certain suppositions as the norm.

84E7C975415A43829F814A1A69771914.description: Understand how a system of inequity creates rules regarding student punishment that negatively impact students of color.

AEF7C0F790434F7B91190450DC9640D9.description: Be aware of the effects of power and privilege and the need for social advocacy and social action to better empower diverse students and communities.

FAEE90E019B14C529635254F8FF03283.description: Understand how current curriculum and approaches to teaching impact students who are not a part of the dominant culture.

04C69EBE002B4BE084388F5D6C5F54AC.description: Know and understand how the system of inequity has impacted them as an  educator.

BD997753DC8341C7B3A7DCE3E2415E77.description: Collaborate with colleagues to determine how students from different backgrounds experience the classroom, school, and district

7DA84DB5E1D14F8DB0182940E21ACF91.description:
Understand the difference between prejudice, discrimination, racism, and how to
 operate at the interpersonal, intergroup, and institutional levels.

7EAAA8F1414D4F9B8E358CEEB91CF401.description:
Systems of Oppression – Culturally responsive teachers and leaders understand that there
 are systems in our society especially, but not limited to, our school system, that create and
 reinforce inequities, thereby creating oppressive conditions. Educators work actively against
 these systems in their everyday roles in educational institutions. The culturally responsive
 teacher and leader will:

7B416C43F3524960865DAA411EA7417B.description:
Assess how their biases and perceptions affect their teaching practice and how they
 access tools to mitigate their own behavior (racism, sexism, homophobia, unearned
 privilege, Eurocentrism, etc.).

65F9D7E529E24D878354A2217A258E2B.description:
Critically think about the institutions in which they find themselves working to
 reform these institutions whenever and wherever necessary.

0C36100A49474C649D2A9A92AFA9D589.description: Educate themselves about students’ communities, cultures, and histories.

D16ED7A9493448688933EA433886BF34.description:
Recognize how their identity (race/ethnicity, national origin, language, sex and
 gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, physical/developmental/ emotional
 ability, socioeconomic class, religion, etc.) affects their perspectives and beliefs about
 pedagogy and students.

41FD10F4B2BD4110B6D8C0223496295E.description:
Explore their own intersecting identities, how they were developed, and how they
 impact daily experience of the world.

CC23E641EEA543358387E83B235724EC.description:
Engage in self-reflection about their own actions and interactions and what ideas and
 biases motivated those actions.

F1D5D1CD59364DA4A944C63B54479727.description:
Include representative, familiar content in the curriculum to legitimize students’
 backgrounds, while also exposing them to new ideas and worldviews different from
 their own.

49B498CE8E4A4572AD9C0ABDE620E6DB.description: Know about their students and their lives outside of school, using this knowledge to  build instruction that leverages prior knowledge and skills.

BBE2461C0699423696F25A5523917054.description:
Approach their work and students with an asset-based mindset, affirming the validity
 of the students’ backgrounds and identities.

1E82361B91C14AD686317FA0B45DBC29.description:
Understand and value the notion that multiple lived experiences exist, that there is
 often not one "correct" way of doing or understanding something, and that what is
 seen as "correct" is most often based on our lived experiences.

36A939D818A242D08CA71995926759FE.description:
Self-Awareness and Relationships to Others – Culturally responsive teachers and leaders are
 reflective and gain a deeper understanding of themselves and how they impact others,
 leading to more cohesive and productive student development as it relates to academic and
 social-emotional development for all students. The culturally responsive teacher and leader
 will:

progress in using languages for enjoyment,
enrichment, and advancement.

globalized world.

home and around the world

explain, and reflect on the nature of language

and their own.

with cultural competence

understanding

support in controlling behavior, e.g., holds caregiver’s hand
when crossing the street

6A0123C0B8464B9F961C301D422D9278.description:
Increasingly reacts appropriately to adults’ facial expressions,
tone, and affect, before acting on an impulse

5FBC664B5D5040F18BCEAECF2350BC71.description: Increases the use of private speech in everyday play and interactions

364DEAE2204A4B6CABDFB4F3AED4F38A.description:
Begins to respond to caregiver’s cues and modifies behavior,
e.g., does not touch the forbidden object, once recognizing the
caregiver is discouraging the action

D4AF98B507E24CED92CA3E379DA174FF.description: Communicates “no” to self when reaching for forbidden objects

BE19EF4F7AE5403FAF88C9625DD383DD.description: Communicates “mine” when another child takes a toy away

5AF39B9AB544475FA11A51889FEF1C00.description:
Completes a forbidden action regardless of referencing a
caregiver’s reaction, e.g., looks toward their caregiver before
touching the forbidden object and then touches it anyway

A38B488245C1482093207953B0825207.description:
Chooses between two options, e.g., “You can have the red ball
or the blue ball”

6A24C9E2359D4A878726C92E0728C832.description:
Has difficulty channeling excitement, e.g., screams, jumps,
squeezes, bites

A3EE535C0DA64344966FCA688C54CA12.description:
Reads cues and body language of caregiver(s) and familiar
others to guide reactions and behaviors in novel and uncertain
situations

345C7245790D4D25AD3150E6D4BE17AF.description:
Explores environment while unaware of boundaries and limits,
e.g., crawls toward a shelf and attempts to climb it

220D92495E9B4A71A9F88543EA9369B8.description:
Shows curiosity and limited restraint when exploring the environment, e.g., reaches for objects that adults or other children
are holding

18BE1054D33A4306B2BBF12BDA3A29F0.description:
Physically explores environment through touch, e.g., sucking,
gnawing, hitting, pulling, banging

5AAB5FC4AA644F398198F18CE17DA666.description:
Uses physical movements to disengage from interaction, turns
head, averts gaze

C37BDEE26C4F4C30B0176D94223E3DC4.description: Cries when hungry, tired, uncomfortable, or bored

223D1EBF39F3457F80D781040B0EF78B.description:
Children demonstrate the emerging ability to manage and adjust behaviors in accordance with social and cultural
contexts.

EFF9C87B010C4F95A4F1FB23BF015840.description:
Transitions between what he or she is engaged in and what is
happening in the background, e.g., makes a comment in regard
to a conversation happening between another child and adult,
while engaged in completing a puzzle

CC3854EA86424049BDE0D2A373F0221B.description: Wait time increases, e.g., participates in turn-taking activities

67F8EB91AB4A4B749306FF7B04CF5F35.description:
Plays independently before moving on to a new activity, e.g.,
engages in block play, reads a book

A63C2A8320F74C9C8F729838527DE7CB.description:
Uses self-talk to extend play, e.g., says “now sleepy” to the baby
doll after feeding it a bottle

75BAEF42C43B45528F9D7ECAE63171D0.description:
Attention expands and stays focused on an activity or object
even when distractions are present

97B2D8B2F9DC44B694902E9F65261CB8.description:
Attends and stays engaged to often reach a goal, e.g., places all
the shapes in the shape sorter

7ABC5FD208FB415B959EB1D53B14C1C1.description:
Remains focused for longer periods of time while engaged in
self-initiated play

ED5D34FCEF8943D4BDEC654676AB7173.description:
Works on solving increasingly difficult activities, e.g., attempts
to solve a simple, three-piece puzzle

CFBF37C9EC1A46D0B410CD921FE81C04.description:
Works to find solutions to simple problems and/or obstacles,
e.g., attempts to climb onto a piece of furniture in order to
retrieve a toy

0B6BE8B9E2B14156997C8A807D82E81C.description:
Relies on routines and patterns to maintain an organized state in
order to focus

B57ABC41D7CD47CEA597E379809E67FE.description: Shifts attention from adults to peers

68FDC7CC32AB4F858E046D48D072ACD2.description:
Focuses on one object or activity for a brief period of time, even
with other objects close in proximity; still easily distracted

266C4F995BB7463B8B9460EFF7B975F6.description:
Maintains more advanced levels of engagement, e.g., repeats
actions over and over when enjoying the reaction and result of
the experience

6380510FEBC646E5B7406F2B48641B83.description:
Engages in joint attention with a caregiver, e.g. joins in looking
at the same object or shifts gaze to where someone is pointing

58FC419AEEE14744A3355D2D7D1A01F2.description:
Plays with one object for a few minutes before focusing on a
different object

803418F53CCB4F638E819409AEDF000A.description: Focuses attention on novel objects and familiar caregiver(s)

8AA9F3D09A11414288AE5D715F13AC10.description:
Explores environment through senses, e.g., touches and mouths
objects

7808DE1316DD47DB87E9168BC5023829.description:
Initiates and briefly maintains social interactions with adults,
e.g., establishes eye contact, coos to receive attention

DD58260CCDFE47C1907037F24EA33518.description: Focuses on objects in the environment during alert states

A44E750761C44F91A220E94C4D7EB98C.description:
Children demonstrate the emerging ability to process stimuli, focus and sustain attention, and maintain engagement in
accordance with social and cultural contexts.

6E86849552E64997ADEC0CDEAD528909.description:
Holds on to a special object during certain times of the day, e.g.,
blanket, picture, book, stuffed toy

CEA092E72B0B43D2BCE3611AFED2DC89.description: Expresses emotions through the use of play

AE690DE9BB874F15BAF35F61BABBD980.description:
Seeks caregiver support when feeling overwhelmed by emotion;
may reject support as well

6C7CEACF7B1243E2A99549BC2D6693A4.description:
Engages in pretend play to manage uncertainty and fear, e.g.,
plays doctor and gives someone a “shot”

73B6EAC7E1B74FD48E3253A9FDD7330A.description: Communicates wants and needs verbally, e.g. “pick me up”

A3E2073792204B9682AB06B5D08FF2DC.description:
Begins to use “private speech” in order to assist in regulating
their emotions, e.g., utters “bear, where is bear” to self

1252B79E54A44C7285DBD9A0A69558C5.description:
Uses verbal and nonverbal communication to signal the need for
their caregiver, e.g., calls by name, crawls into a familiar adult’s lap

61FC92958D0B4713BD9E3AE4DA332A67.description:
Uses play to sort out feelings and gain control over them, e.g.,
projects feeling onto an object, grasps a ball and hugs it tightly
to chest when excited

A250BE71D7004CD7ADB0ECF6D06610E2.description:
Uses caregiver’s facial cues and body language to assist in novel
and uncertain situations, e.g., sees a dog for the first time and
uses the adult’s smile as a cue to cautiously pat the dog

B2AFA6E60E1D48A5A0AB60303D4D5AFB.description:
Uses comfort objects, e.g., a stuffed animal or blanket, to help
calm down

3851482CD1CC4BCC94349CCAE010A2AB.description:
Seeks out caregiver through physical actions, e.g., reaches for
the caregiver’s hand or moves closer to them when frightened

844D71B8342B4F7496324B7DCABA6E62.description: Prefers physical proximity to familiar adults in unknown situations, e.g., follows caregiver when he or she leaves the room

85D4DF3B44514CE08062ED03A537E714.description:
Uses social referencing in uncertain situations, e.g., looks at a
caregiver’s face for reassurance in the presence of a new person

8102539D22954AC58CB0679E3262AEA0.description:
Able to self-soothe more effectively, e.g., sucks thumb, holds on
to stuffed toy

D64887D661D942A39335E91D123C7B0A.description: Communicates needs to an adult, e.g., points, shakes head

C0D5F55738BD42CF9AD5381146616462.description:
Vocalizes and uses facial cues to get caregiver’s attention, e.g.,
cries, gazes, initiates eye contact

760B64596C7249F9BDA3259A4D2E49A3.description:
Begins to use self-soothing strategies, e.g., sucks on hands,
grasps an object in order to calm self

E9BB73995C0045A1B0102B2C4D10FE16.description:
Able to use cues to signal overstimulation , e.g., turns head,
gaze aversion

D9EF9F5A9CA6494DB2087D88D240DE0A.description: Signals needs by sounds and movement

94396704C08F49008F1DAE5ED22E2CBE.description:
Children demonstrate the emerging ability to identify and manage the expression of emotion in accordance with social
and cultural contexts.

CD8A39AE9F7C4403B59DC83449659E0D.description: Demonstrates a readiness to begin toilet training

BBE28558D4154BA8A80E27C7E70BD6D3.description:
Manages overstimulation in a more organized manner, e.g.,
disengages, walks away

7EBBB8AC6B834683848C2DE9375B6852.description: Communicates needs more thoroughly, e.g., “I am hungry”

E7A0BA354DC1496EBA6AA967A7B34610.description:
Recognizes patterns throughout the day, e.g., grabs a pillow and
blanket after lunch, when it is nap time

08585343E8314E1185342D5F879BF0D9.description:
Uses movement to express an emotion, e.g., jumps up and down
when excited, stomps feet when upset

72C8BE7A57B049C4A83660A1E5E80086.description: Calms down in order to sit and read a book with a caregiver

D43DC449C2DE485F9D880D038CC116F7.description:
Begins to have an awareness of bodily functions and begins to
demonstrate an interest in toileting, e.g., recognizes a “potty”

8C931D01FFCE4CF7AC030B5ECDACACC6.description:
Communicates needs with one or two words, e.g., says or
gestures “milk” for “I want milk”

179A86C9454448D6A0A0DF627D6687BB.description:
Becomes frustrated and displays regressive behaviors when
overstimulated, e.g., temper tantrums

CC888820D4FE448A98342548DC008453.description:
Uses gestures and symbolic actions to demonstrate feelings and
needs, e.g., lays head on caregiver’s lap when tired

B49BFF5826E84767A3CDEAE11C9545E4.description: Increased desire for independence and control

CAD36B2B076949A89891331446CD231E.description:
Begins to exhibit certain behaviors when overstimulated and/or
unfocused, e.g., becomes aggressive, lashes out, bites

484EED063F9C42808C3EBEB53D0BD0C5.description: Communicates with a wide range of signals as crying diminishes, e.g., smiles, gestures, uses words

4F15E2475B7F4CCCAF2886686EA9F008.description:
Increasingly organized and consolidated internal schedule for
sleep/wake, elimination, and feeding, e.g., decreases the number
of naps but extends the length of the naps

8A7E9AB7745942B4AE0B03ED76942A84.description:
Demonstrates consistent sleeping and feeding times throughout
the day

83A70A397B324E9CAFD5DAF61039A90E.description: Uses sucking to assist in sleeping

3D1D55B6E75D49B8AE493F170D99338A.description:
Disengages when overstimulated, e.g., turns head, glances away,
falls asleep, spits up

AE90A17B51544A598FFF1C17E4A14E68.description: Signals for needs, e.g., cries when hungry, arches back in discomfort

44CC8B3C7CC645A3B681373845452CF3.description:
Begins to demonstrate a pattern in sleep-wake and feeding
cycles

56D14EA795B44A0D9E2F375DE24ADB07.description:
Children demonstrate the emerging ability to process stimuli, focus and sustain attention, and maintain engagement in
accordance with social and cultural contexts.

standardSets.title: Developmental Domain 1: Social and Emotional Development
standardSets.subject: Early Learning Guidelines: Birth to Age 3 (2012-)

document.title: Illinois Early Learning Guidelines For Children Birth to Age Three

E27E4D190589421F8F479350D6C1DBD4.description:
Shares in and shows an emotional response for peers’ feelings,
e.g., may show concern for a child who is hurt, or smile for a
child who is happy and jumping up and down

93CD2C92C6DA4633BC82916C01B3ACD8.description:
Responds to a child in distress in an attempted manner to make
that child feel better, e.g., gives a crying child a hug, uses soothing words, or uses distraction

B20FC26FDF1546D589D6E3F294BE2AA7.description:
Communicates how other children may be feeling and why, e.g.,
states that a peer is sad because his or her toy was taken away

7967AFB4A7FE44FCBB509C785C26F08F.description:
Shares in and communicates simple emotions of others, e.g.,
“mama sad”, “papa happy”

5DC978BA38514430904868DC669A45C7.description:
Demonstrates awareness of different emotions and feelings
during play, e.g., rocks a baby doll and whispers “shhh”

DC75E43D6A5C40B3948C7005C071B589.description: Recognizes some of his or her own emotions, e.g., grabs a comfort object when sad

9D2A96D9610A4913B357032603453495.description:
Imitates comforting behaviors from caregiver(s), e.g., pats or
hugs a child when upset

46B4727748CD4B079D7166ED24C2FE0A.description:
Begins to have a greater awareness of own emotions, e.g., says
or gestures “no” to refuse, squeals and continues to laugh when
happy

07610405874F450DB3F18E756C9BC8DB.description:
Shares in both positive and negative emotions with caregiver(s),
e.g., shares in wonders, amazement, delight, and disappointment

41A753489F3C4368A850BABFAA01BDEA.description:
Reacts to a child who is upset by observing or moving physically
closer to the child

818D45346255496B8A1A8F07CC0D77BC.description:
Uses social referencing with caregiver(s) when in uncertain
situations, e.g., glances at a caregiver’s face for cues on how to
respond to an unfamiliar person or new situation

B5734598290D4C028BB8FBCB9BA189FC.description: Smiles with intention to draw out a smile from a familiar other

8E5E10A215DE4BE7BBDE1FE52288E2EE.description:
Begins to share in simple emotions by reading facial and gestural
cues, e.g., repeats activities that make others laugh

0B49577FD117411590844E7B13308749.description: Shows signs of separation anxiety, e.g., protests when a caregiver leaves the room

D8A6E76AD8E24CA3A0B1EC0AAE66F4DD.description:
Responds to interactions from caregiver(s), e.g., smiles when
caregiver smiles, looks toward a caregiver when he or she
shakes a rattle

C20A71CA4E9B4AA5BC824C055D57E0D5.description: Cries when hearing another infant cry

2D455A1F1B4247A1AB62AE37534AC78B.description: Watches and observes adults and other children

A1CEF689A05143B5829CBBC100F5DD8B.description:
Children demonstrate an emerging ability to understand someone else’s feelings and to share in the emotional
experiences of others.

2FF66722BF534F25B89C1F320A918D0F.description: Begins to engage in more complex play with two or three children

770F01B8305C4637969EA20742424127.description:
Communicates with other children in different settings, e.g.,
talks to a peer during snack time, or hands a peer a book

BCD861F874E6466599CAF9626EC30AD2.description:
Becomes frustrated with peers, e.g., yells “no” if a peer tries to
interfere in something he or she is engaged in

A2F6CE0BC2984AE39535C0BF3115C880.description: Demonstrates a preference toward select peers

F6712BC4082C4041886B01AAC3088F41.description:
Demonstrates a preference for parallel play, e.g., plays next to
other children with similar toys with little or no interaction

D29B037E9B3E4956BB3AF8D8D3D12B1E.description:
Begins to engage in simple reciprocal interactions, e.g., rolls a
ball back and forth

FFAFE232580743FCA7E9159163BD498E.description:
Expresses frustration when another child takes something away
from him or her, e.g., a toy

A1F8FF0ECD4141ED8EC4A28E31913AEB.description: Gestures in order to communicate a desire to play near a peer

81F3DE783BD74646899E75709FBBE2AF.description:
Begins to engage in parallel play, in closer proximity to other
children but no interaction is attempted

54A98CBD600D4CBB99B93FBF6A9651F9.description: Engages in a simple, reciprocal game such as “pat-a-cake”

92DCE7C18888492E8A53A210250BAAA7.description: Imitates actions of another child, e.g., rolling a car

F7193A28927A4FDAA7FF7D2D5B319B37.description:
Shows interest in another child by moving closer, e.g., rolls,
crawls, or walks toward the child

E090B582DD24446C92F99CBB2BE8C4A4.description: Attempts to imitate actions, e.g., bangs a toy

C4B88E841B674FA38AE69FD34E1217D6.description: Reaches out to touch another child

43AC4854ABE64760AB09BE3F766BE5CC.description: Cries when hearing another child cry

124866BAA915463B8171082019D2C989.description: Shows interest in both familiar and unfamiliar peers

58E2BF1453E7491EB8A0E9D479F296F3.description: Observes other children in the environment

75C84A8B59D44B629A927D3B90B32916.description:
Demonstrates effort to interact and engage, e.g., uses eye
contact, coos, smiles

9925802E34A64DDAB45E4A9985DD0341.description: Children demonstrate the desire and develop the ability to engage and interact with other children.

7E4592026C86483BA514AE562AF3F80B.description:
Begins to understand concept of possession, e.g., “yours,” “hers,”
“his”

456FC49ED37D42D4AF277E86BC973447.description:
Communicates feelings, e.g., may say “I’m sad,” or stomps feet
when mad

36AB1A6C3333459B84E71933E153D066.description: Demonstrates preferences, e.g., “I want the green cup”

6A746A095BD44B31B0953AB7A470DC28.description:
Begins to show an interest in describing physical characteristics,
e.g., “I have blue eyes”

73EF8BC9864541878C60675EDE1E6D7E.description: Incorporates roles of family members in play

A704F3DFB1B0427087B1DFCC5AB338F3.description:
Asks for help from familiar adults but pushes away and refuses
help

AECDAA0BE27D47A7BC7ACB9BE8691FCD.description: Names people in his/her family and shares stories about them

E14E4E18D0AC4F45BEBC77C340A8D087.description:
Asks for help from familiar adults but may begin to attempt to
complete tasks autonomously

E1844CE3C347428084BB6C0CA7B244FB.description: Points to self in images and other types of media

8F76B72068F1453894BF217B8F011CB7.description:
Demonstrates understanding and use of concepts through words
such as “mine,” “me,” and “you”

A338BBB1516749189D663097B6E430B9.description: Refers to self with gestures and language

DEA35FE3157C4008ABD1E734FDA88EF0.description: Able to express his or her name

D580999D4DEE48A1A307D6A3690B462A.description:
Demonstrates awareness of self, e.g., touches own nose in the
mirror

2BF2F8F54F41487EBF7B66149A2188D0.description:
Points to and identifies body parts on him or herself, e.g., points
to eyes when asked, “Where are your eyes?”

D38E6FCFC6F244088BFA7946B50A9D4A.description: Uses social referencing to guide actions and begins to test limits

65D23DE484C242878AA5529260E89333.description: Uses gestures and some words to express feelings, e.g., “no”

BD1EF51A4FE24A3CBC3F9C1599CE67CC.description: Demonstrates interest in looking in mirror

436F0DA8F4D947CB9F381D849D0E4004.description: Responds with vocalizations or gestures when hears name

994C87104F91421B813803CBAEF1D785.description:
Engages in joint attention with familiar others, e.g., shares in
looking and engaging with objects and people

C7E707558E9143DFA50B36F96A82CBDA.description:
Shows awareness of significant people by calling them by name,
e.g., “papa”

D7F3FF4055BF42BFBE38E2CBCC9D8318.description:
Demonstrates separation anxiety, e.g., cries when caregiver
leaves the room

26F6F844E2E747E3B7FF542E6976D7CC.description:
Begins to display the beginning of joint attention, e.g., points to
objects and people

27A1571027D840DAAB207965C9B404AD.description:
Initiates interactions with others, e.g., imitates actions, plays
peek-a-boo

B63E642AAC134C18B955980B6C4A54AC.description:
Recognizes and prefers familiar adults and siblings, e.g., leans
toward caregiver when being held by someone else

78F0541B52ED48E2B75DDE65759D2DC6.description:
Recognizes own name, e.g., looks up, or turns head toward a
person who is saying his/her name

0DC43767D508478DA94F2701FE17CF30.description: Explores his or her own hands and feet

306EC0D9510A476AA9005ED99A206939.description: Demonstrates interest in faces and voices of others

5B06791A7E0946E48CFBAA3CC3C1C3BA.description:
Demonstrates desire to control or make decisions independent
from adults

314A35202EFF462E9B59EB9E7B50799F.description:
Communicates thoughts, feelings, questions, and plans to both
familiar and unfamiliar adults

DB25E08473374620A7C6260E5C6D8461.description:
Initiates activities that are meaningful in the relationship, e.g.,
brings over a favorite book to be read together

85355F5617504441A7324D6C7BAAD410.description:
Imitates adult roles and activities through pretend play, e.g.,
goes grocery shopping, or prepares a meal

0D6400B866944064825432E9AD0AC951.description:
Imitates a familiar adult‘s actions, e.g., waves hands around
while pretending to talk on the phone after seeing caregiver
make those same actions

59E21C426C88449ABDB5C81BABB8D294.description:
Responds to guidance, e.g., places the shape into the shape
sorter after caregiver demonstrates how to

6BD7A3DD8DD14ADA8645AD4E2DDE2515.description:
Seeks adult assistance with challenges but may refuse help and
say “no”

8E7D647E1E454D52BC4217E85E5BEDD2.description: Builds emotional connections with other familiar adults, in addition to primary caregiver(s)

F1E1029A941E42FB8377B934087644EF.description:
Draws a familiar adult into an interaction, e.g., hands a book or
toy to engage in together

47B1E4B4D84341179F84F836D9F900AB.description:
Uses “social referencing” when encountering new experiences,
e.g., glances at a caregiver’s face for cues on how to respond to
an unfamiliar person or unknown object

3B4C3EFCE56E4F9D83F378F224A00301.description: Uses key adults as a “secure base” when exploring the environment

D2C6F895615E405280431D349DD1D33F.description:
Engages with adults during play, e.g., bangs on a toy drum and
repeats action after an adult completes the same action

218AD85C8C3F4299B6237FF259361581.description: Looks for caregiver’s response in uncertain situations

DFC9431605064970BCDF556DEA923682.description:
Begins to engage in simple, back-and-forth interactions with a
familiar adult, e.g., plays “peek-a-boo,” babbles in response to an
adult speaking and repeats this interaction

30AA6000C4F04B8DA1247B78DEE0A500.description:
Demonstrates preference for familiar adults, e.g., reaches hands
out to signal for caregiver(s)

DF8E03E7E4D54A73BAAA21CB1B59C4EC.description:
Engages in social interactions with adults through smiles, coos,
and eye contact

4A90C54C9513470D984AA19BE21C8797.description: Attempts to engage both unfamiliar and familiar adults

B85E4BC57A3445B9B161DEAA93F953B6.description:
Uses signals to communicate needs, e.g., crying, body language,
and facial expressions

0E2916B560D34E8190D8FDFE4835C247.description: Children demonstrate the desire and develop the ability to engage, interact, and build relationships with familiar adults.

10E6FFFA17124F49B6E6A9ED7C583950.description:
Engages in play to express emotion, e.g., draws a picture for a
caregiver because he or she misses them, hides a “monster” in a
box due to a fear

2EB97BCDAE984077940215BCCD12EDCB.description: Begins to express complex emotions such as pride, embarrassment, shame, and guilt

0838034AB8EB4882990B16AF46C52FA2.description:
Acts out different emotions while engaged in pretend play,
e.g., cries when pretending to be sad, jumps up and down for
excitement

1A23C45653F94E1299A5A00DAF827881.description: Attempts to use words to describe feelings and names emotions

C2206FA4D95C486894677A1734066982.description:
Expresses wonder and delight while exploring the environment
and engaging others

78AE3D09E6A748B59424ECBFCE17FAD0.description: Attempts to use a word to describe feelings to a familiar adult

1D9805DA8D624144BFE8241F97A7E84F.description: Expresses pride, e.g., smiles, claps, or says, “I did it” after completing a task

49037A6D677E4A70B34BBE86BEEA2A4C.description:
Demonstrates anger and frustration through a wide range of
physical, vocal, and facial expressions, e.g., temper tantrums

F567C90AEDEE4B1EA3A7F43C5299FC05.description:
Recognizes and expresses emotion toward a familiar person,
e.g., shows emotion by hugging a sibling

DEA4966642464AD8928D60C4BBE2FCEE.description: Shows anger and frustration, e.g., cries when a toy is taken away

04FF50C92547403EAEE155847DBAB982.description:
Expresses fear by crying or turning toward caregiver(s) for
comfort

BB671E31A2CB477B83FAB8B39F095E67.description:
Expresses wants with intentionality, e.g., pushes an unwanted
object out of the way, reaches for a familiar adult when wanting
to be carried

68B00A9D77C740C781D11944A563CE86.description:
Demonstrates discomfort, stress, or unhappiness through body
language and sounds, e.g., arches back, moves head, cries

A1DC3091B0354E199310D3B70E999C8C.description:
Expresses emotions through sounds and gestures, e.g., squeals,
laughs, claps

E037E0F12120447894F8E07FAA72E981.description:
Uses facial expressions and sounds to get needs met, e.g., cries,
smiles, gazes, coos

0901C3A375BC499B8E13DE55C9968DB6.description: Children demonstrate an awareness of and the ability to identify and express emotions.

89E18B60B4F54D8686A98C8F4086D572.description:
Separates with assistance from attachment figure with minimal
anxiety

397284D8B3594710828FB1974C53B7D3.description: Communicates thoughts, feelings, and plans to familiar adults

082A6693ACC84C09922AD5B4EFE2B694.description:
Initiates activities that are meaningful in the relationship, e.g.,
brings over a favorite book to be read together

298DCA835F474236B02C76411403B592.description:
Uses glances and words to stay connected, without having to be
physically near or touching the caregiver

6725C2B1211B458D87227139DB0B6492.description:
Actively seeks emotional responses from caregiver(s) by waving,
hugging, and crying

FBC713ECD03D4E9CAE66C4DCE7A1E96C.description:
Plays physically farther away from primary caregiver with
increasing confidence; moves closer as needed

37E6AD8FA44B4A4BB45925482C307A58.description:
Uses imitation and pretend play to make sense of relationships,
e.g., uses a toy to “brush” hair, or feeds and rocks a doll

42DDF31441E94618A9D70EED3FE6B176.description:
Shows an emotional connection with familiar adults other than
the primary caregiver

225A611EE61C4290832451ED31EF550E.description: Initiates and maintains interactions with caregiver(s)

DBB1488AA0224EFFAB849BAEF0D4B2FA.description:
Seeks comfort from caregiver(s) and/or a familiar object, e.g.,
blanket, stuffed animal

75B222FD02A5433884E2E88AB479B10F.description:
Exhibits stranger anxiety and concern in presence of an
unknown person or a new situation

EBE42C6AC0D2444B9F8EBAA25FA66525.description: Uses key adults as a “secure base” when exploring the environment

7F1DFE2D33694B53B16BB315BB6188B6.description:
Uses social referencing with caregiver(s) when in uncertain situations, e.g., will glance at caregiver’s face for cues on how to respond
to an unfamiliar person or new situation

A106182E98C74DD8A41920F461EC26CA.description:
Attempts to change the situation when separation anxiety occurs,
e.g., follows caregiver(s) when he or she leaves the room

7DD9B2E43535406F969F7DD3B6EF567E.description: Distinguishes between primary caregivers and others

8573FBDA093245E082D5B60C4672562E.description:
Exhibits separation anxiety , e.g., does not want to be held by
another person when being held by primary caregiver

BFD7D65E16F141B9A2BDF012183F5113.description: Imitates familiar adults’ gestures and sounds

08B13CF676D4407A9DA925685FEA845C.description: Seeks comfort from a familiar caregiver

431886A159744BA18A109853EF5D2046.description: Responds to caregiver(s) by smiling and cooing

99D54A1E645B4ED69D8CDCF8543C8EE2.description: Establishes, maintains, and disengages eye contact

C12639CF315B48ED8A09483F464E032C.description:
Children form secure attachment relationships with caregivers who are emotionally available, responsive, and
consistent in meeting their needs.

F6F407EDD44346C1A7C8569CC82AD8E8.description: Attempts to put on shoes and socks without help

C0441FC3F8214A829A4DE00E23B43775.description:

wants to sit on “potty”

A9DC74BBDE2B4C5286F4A92FA5E2FDBF.description: Uses nonverbal and/or verbal communication to specify needs

85AFB0B74B8A4E4AA5868035C66C4204.description: Makes choices pertaining to dressing and eating

FEA617B1909146F6BBB64DF7884E0178.description: Performs some self-care tasks regularly and mostly independently, e.g., brushes teeth, washes hands, places cup in sink

5505630CB7CA4C3B9FB851DFC949695F.description: Undresses independently but still needs assistance with dressing

32C32109FAAF40E48085625AB46E5DEB.description: Attempts to brush teeth with support

CB58AF67BD8641ACB2FD5F6555E993C2.description: Starts to indicate needs with gestures or a word, e.g., tugs diaper when wet, says “milk” when thirsty

243ACEE8C0874DDBB7CA5BA6A28259CE.description: Shakes head to demonstrate no; pushes objects away

5771548D0CCF44C697FC9B2C4EB8BCFC.description: Attempts to feed self with a bottle

object or person

both in the actual environment and in play, e.g., walks carefully
when holding a pretend tea cup

D8AAC3B43DA048A489932FDC4DA04D41.description:
Adjusts approach to unknown objects, e.g., presses harder on a
lump of clay

CF37380EBE804EBB8BF100678DE20CE6.description: Imitates familiar adults when coloring; draws lines and/or circles

6A2E5BD322F24911B8A76E720A736BAA.description:
Adjusts approach to environment, e.g., changes volume of voice
to adjust to noise level in the environment

9B0B3BD847D349E0A0A2449DAB8B6DFC.description:
Recognizes situations that need to be approached cautiously,
e.g., walks slowly with a cup of water, or with food on a plate

61FCB03833414BCC99F1A002095B5F38.description: Enjoys physical play, e.g., wrestling, tickling

6730B0629D6D4A51A24491B26A607991.description:
Plays with water and sand tables; explores by pouring, digging,
and filling

109CAF1FE7C74D09856E2EEAB031B0D3.description:
Adjusts manner of walking depending on the surface, e.g., walks
carefully across gravel

ABAF634D01604703B46A38F83E23EAC9.description:
Becomes aware of obstacles in the environment, e.g., crawls
around the table to get the ball

6219DEB01CD94C3EBE43D98BE45A2CD3.description:
Begins to show a preference for or aversion to particular sensory activities, e.g., pulls hand away from unfamiliar objects or
unpleasant textures

534141E04DEA493498B972A26FA74D0C.description:
Begins to manipulate materials, e.g., pounds at play dough,
squeezes finger foods

6689874AD6824F138F483A2E0EEAC07D.description: Recognizes familiar objects and begins to demonstrate favoritism for certain toys

4F340D3F76974E978616A40FD4EA49B5.description: Feels the sensation of being touched and looks around to identify the source of the touch, e.g., person or object

611EE3D1C1B74C44BA49A1AAFA12D20B.description:

leads to seeing colors and seeing objects from a distance

4A1649B572D245658BE9EABB43BCB517.description: Attempts to mimic sounds heard in the environment

17465E2474904D7A91C3DDF4431E0E2B.description: Explores objects through senses, e.g., mouths, touches objects

1C0F4A5EA8364312A2AD405152BACAFA.description:

hearing a loud noise, turns head toward light

70AB66518638403BBB312D2D7C712D22.description: Children demonstrate the ability to distinguish, process, and respond to sensory stimuli in their environment.

161FC3590AE645D2B056FAEE548D7A23.description:
Uses hand-eye coordination in a more controlled manner, e.g.,
completes puzzles, strings beads together

30AB53C47ED841B996B3AC03E0FE3573.description: Scribbles with intent and begins to draw circles and lines on own

BD4CDB9E5AF542F9AEEC16E6FF64C675.description:
Attempts to help with dressing self, e.g., snaps buttons, pulls
zipper, puts socks and shoes on

3CB3CEAAB73B496A9479336F47CDAD61.description: Begins to use more complicated hand movements, e.g., uses eating utensils independently, stacks blocks

0A5E1D57FAE34E4D81BA5BB349989E22.description:
Controls placement of objects in a more effective manner, e.g.,
stacks blocks in a more orderly fashion

45579CA2ECF8478DAD24EB61B2722E54.description: Begins to imitate lines and circles when drawing

1B4A9B8D305146F2821371BDF340DD73.description:
Uses simple tools, e.g., scooper to scoop sand or water, crayon
for scribbling

B71D68FF88AF46758D01CC955513D501.description:
Uses baby sign to communicate various concepts, e.g., “all
done,” “more,” “water”

C73AC791118F4616AB054B9FC43BDC48.description:
Attempts to fold various types of materials, e.g., paper, baby
blanket

6B650598CC5B40C1ADA547158F3F7F71.description: Participates in finger plays, e.g., moves hands to imitate caregiver’s hands when singing “Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star”

AAA294267AAD462BB24599D6B6A50027.description:
Coordinates increasingly complex hand movements to manipulate objects, e.g., crumples paper, connects and disconnects toy
links, flips light switch on and off

AC75B47F11CC473E8FF19964FC27664C.description:
Uses hands in a purposeful manner, e.g., turns the pages of a
board book, drops objects into a bucket

D755905AB3AF4D0AADE2303BA7520B40.description: Begins to use simple baby signs (if exposed to baby sign language), e.g., moves hands toward each other to signal more

1BDF9CA942614E92891C2CD310635523.description: Uses pincer grasp, e.g., picks up a Cheerio with thumb and forefinger

0B697E884918473BBCDC90700B71516B.description: Holds a small object in each hand; bangs them together

5EC50863115E4E22B3784EECBCD437D7.description:

9BF3E59A23F0472A8B2EE0E5F1A22F1F.description: Transfers an object from one hand to the other

5CCF6340BF2F467EBE746794E6FF3A96.description: Opens hands when in a relaxed state

9BE27DEFEB104B68B18EFBAA2BB1AF5A.description: Children demonstrate the ability to coordinate their small muscles in order to move and control objects.

5C92E5FFBAAC46B5A0443115638FAEB8.description: Walks on tiptoes, walks backward, and runs

A8443E80DE2A476487C663411BD6609E.description:

B15C5F06A2D6475486012F3458FD72A9.description: Rides a toy by using his or her hands or feet

FB1F8E0AC3AF4773B38B0EE56B67B82F.description: Kicks and attempts to catch a ball

Holds objects or toys while walking, e.g., pulls a car by a string

Attempts to climb objects, e.g., furniture, steps, simple climbing
structures

0AD6AF01FFC240FB84AA3CDF7E846238.description: Gets into a standing position without support

9EBDE0702256496FA0BEF8EC7971773A.description: Briefly maintains balance when placed in a non-supported standing position

368D32C7265E4BC084F8256A90292EB8.description:
Cruises while holding on to furniture, e.g., walks around crib,

Moves objects with large muscles, e.g., pushes a toy car with

12177EF93F144A65B4880DA9C772FF93.description: Rocks back and forth on knees

8192D2933A0B4A72B6DD2DE63DAF5C3F.description: Moves from hands and knees to a sitting position

3B6DBF14138D42D996D60005A047738B.description: Children demonstrate strength, coordination, and controlled use of large muscles .

with caregiver

D0714BD10C054879A5961894C99FC916.description:
Attempts to engage in early forms of turn-taking with caregiver,
e.g., coos and stares at caregiver

D4384198633C457CA009EE06B258F4E6.description:
Uses sounds, cries, facial expressions, and body language to
convey needs

1BE00625315349A1AF90ABAD66F083E9.description: Children demonstrate the ability to engage with and maintain communication with others.

3523B9F818064C3FB91D380B456D38A5.description:
Reminds younger peers of rules, e.g., holds hands with a
younger peer while walking outside

7A6A79CCC70147CF8330A548F84F061E.description:
Remembers and begins to apply past experiences to future
situations, e.g., walks carefully and slowly when there is snow
on the ground

B02FE9B554C243D690D71BFF053DDE3E.description:
Communicates to an adult if something is wrong, e.g., a peer is
hurt or missing

30EC96529DD84AFF89CA614226356C59.description:
Pays attention to safety rules but still needs supervision to keep
self safe

A25FF6FE4AFD49D582045E4F29B97028.description:
Imitates adults’ actions during play, e.g., tells baby doll “no
touch” when walking by the pretend stove

651587E8A17D4E17AA7BF1218F1CEDF4.description: Responds to warnings and begins to change behavior accordingly, e.g., moves away from the outlet after caregiver communicates “no”

D6DF5ADA7C0A42BFA78CF1FA9185133C.description:
Understands when “no” and “stop” is communicated through
either words or gestures

807F7014F1F34E0EB929529676EC4CB1.description:
Responds to warnings and changes in tone of voice; needs
assistance and redirection to stop unsafe behavior, e.g., looks
up after hearing a stern “no” but does not necessarily stop the
behavior or action

C9054165CFEE4441A6DFA3150E7FD34F.description:
Hesitates and demonstrates caution in new and/or changing
situations, e.g., stops crawling when reaches the edge of an
uneven surface

21B75E0005E74A98911DBDE531D1E2F5.description: Responds to cues from caregiver in uncertain and unsafe situations

18C0629E0B1B46D78154CEE097226E31.description: Actively climbs to reach for wanted objects during play

B5E9CD882E2843CA852200018DB4D626.description:
Uses social referencing to assess uncertain situations, e.g.,
looks at a caregiver for social cues as to whether or not to
proceed

DE2A648DFCB448D4A6B49D74D5520F5B.description: Demonstrates trust in caregiver(s), e.g., reaches for adult, comforted when soothed, looks for caregiver in novel situations

2C42DC507F4C4CACB99013115C1A7BC3.description: Uses physical movements to explore environment, e.g., reaching, sitting, rolling

ABA3B964808040DEBECC975765F5B3B0.description:
Demonstrates interest in own body, e.g., stares at hands,
mouths feet, pokes at belly button

4DDDF7292119441482CB6015A91971C9.description:
Signals needs through reflexes and sounds, e.g., demonstrates
rooting reflex when hungry, cries when uncomfortable

E593EBBF70D94ACEBBCDB4A0E15D93B4.description: Children demonstrate the emerging ability to recognize risky situations and respond accordingly.

659DDB26427440799BAF4E835262EC23.description:
Engages in processes to reach an outcome, e.g., mixes three
different colors of paint to see what color emerges

8278E69C717E47639CE32519E8A5DD14.description:
Draws on past experience to describe and communicate about
observations and experiences, e.g., knows what happens when
one blows on a candle, discusses what happens to snow when
the temperature is warmer

03CCA4DAE95843B490C7CB078DB755EB.description:
Identifies various attributes of objects, food, and materials, e.g.,
color, shapes, size

E2BEEE0F5A254DC9A472E08135D1295F.description:
Begins to identify characteristics of animals, e.g., “The dog
barks”

3FF8F82B09C74440885F5A7872DFCBB6.description:
Uses motion and sound to represent an observation, e.g.,
“snake, ssssss!”

3628D54832DD4BF3AC0C7C4B5F49BD9B.description:
Attempts new tasks during familiar activities, e.g., plays at the
water table, and instead of using hands, tries to use head to
make the water move

2428F8D5336B4B0288FAEC5A7D717801.description: Begins simple categorizing, e.g., cats and dogs are animals

C6DA2A04F053427AB7AE2E168E486A41.description:
Shows interest in own body; may know names for certain body
parts

D757F5E5ABC14BED8344B39E9700DD90.description: Experiments with different textures found in the outside environment, e.g., runs fingers through dirt, crumbles dry leaves

9280AA6281B54CD19FF87ABE04D54634.description:
Repeats actions that attracts his or her attention, e.g., drops
object onto floor to hear the sound it makes

7CE8A8EA6F094A05BADB5187D4745335.description:
Actively explores objects and experiences their properties
through the different senses, e.g., color, texture, weight, taste

1F66C991F4B54BEE8117AB89A9FA2AC5.description:
Uses all of his or her senses to explore and discover new things,
e.g., reaches out to touch rain or snow

EE4E3984002F46588A3D90C59C89052A.description:
Actively explores new objects found in the environment, e.g.,
mouths, pats, grasps

CB164C9910A84D71A6506B36F7C32B8B.description: Engages in social interactions with familiar adults

A482026E6846497CB43FF7B4CAF50F71.description: Observes people and objects in his or her environment

9284D3ECB45540188D08B3A1555DDB45.description: Children demonstrate a basic awareness of and use scientific concepts.

13D0A3F4267D48A6BD2FEA0078C0FDF1.description:
Uses descriptive words when communicating about others, e.g.,
“She ran fast,” “He is short,” “Look how far away I am”

24A7B6BF4E6E40A8A3B987C6EAEB8D17.description:
Assigns meaning to numbers; understands the concept of a
small number or big number, e.g., communicates “wow” when a
caregiver shares that he or she is 35 years old

9D980C7848D3442DADB9540B1A5A148A.description:
Begins to identify quantity comparison, e.g., “Which group has
more blocks?”

21A4237DFDEC4341A038DF0322375C04.description:
Begins to count objects; may count objects twice and/or skip
numbers

1F0FE00795C04E9C93BC43B6333D1450.description:
Understands progressive number order, e.g., recites the number
series to ten

E05605797E0241F19E79940042D8A97C.description:
Begins to use descriptive words for people in a more complex
fashion, e.g., “he big,” “she baby”

FCBD31EA94A143B8AABB245314A7B8AE.description:
Begins to use “one,” “two,” and “three” to identify very small
quantities without counting them

750FE45B436B4A8CACA59CE88E7C3E48.description: Uses nonverbal gestures to demonstrate understanding of quantities, e.g., holds up two fingers to express two of something

19933FF70D02428CABE340CA6B80306C.description:
Communicates amount of familiar objects, e.g., sees two apples
and says, “two”

17D15090A02C478C96B36EF9B75E67D1.description:
Begins to use number words to label quantities, even though
incorrect

4C237E0789C4400099396D1B20BFB702.description:
Begins to understand descriptive words and apply attributes
to people, e.g., points to himself when asked, “Who’s a big boy?”

F418CBC10D11413686DD5F761D793965.description:
Uses nonverbal and verbal communication to express more
complex concepts, e.g., “some,” “again,” “all done”

E809877C3A2443E896F1ACD7D238B9FE.description: Imitates counting, e.g., climbs stairs and mimics “one, two”

72A657CD84DE4BFE889FA871083E7D76.description:
Understands the concept of “more” in regard to food and play;
signs or says, “more”

00520EDFF9D14AFBA9B9214720DBCED7.description:
Holds on to more than one object at a time, e.g., grasps a rattle
in one hand, and reaches for block

2747D6014D6845CABB9AE30E031064FF.description:
Expresses desire for more through facial cues, sounds, gestures,
and actions, e.g., bangs, opens mouth, points, reaches

A4D65A62EBAA4D86AFFC0458F1550151.description:
Explores objects one at a time, e.g., mouths one toy and drops it
to grab hold of another, or drops toys in a container

AEFECB85F42B4E38B51AD425E495A5AF.description:
Uses sounds and body language to signal for more, e.g., begins
to cry when finishing a bottle of milk and is still hungry

BA192EDE86814289B19BEF322292B3BB.description: Children demonstrate awareness of quantity, counting, and numeric competencies.

6447321CBF374AF89BF329C471B81FA2.description:
Expresses cause and effect in certain situations, e.g., “I fell down
and now I have a boo-boo.”

6BAF124930AA4508A3A1107E48952424.description: Applies past experiences to new situations

567B5E4791D945DF8D2907FC291133DB.description:
Makes a prediction of what will happen next in a sequence of
events

1A27E41DC1A84A289CBE3367A82C2366.description:
Recognizes actions and objects and can generalize meaning,
e.g., sees someone opening an umbrella and can attribute that
to the fact that it may be raining

B774995C65D243D4B2B89CE0FCB888B7.description:
Begins to understand certain behaviors are related to certain
contexts, e.g., behaves differently at childcare than at home

322364FD518F4EFFB4CC01DD3D19B6CB.description:
Understands functionality of objects, e.g., mop is used to clean
the floor

B7F6078022E34B259059EF5FB69C8C4B.description:
Starts to predict the consequence of simple and familiar actions,
e.g., knows that flipping the light switch will either turn on or
turn off the light

B9CC80F593FC4DA399F930EC8CF272F9.description:
Repeats actions over and over to cause desired effect, e.g.,
dumps out a bucket and refills it with objects

702B279498EE44CC9BB6B62D79794966.description:
Imitates adult’s body language and simple actions, e.g., puts
hands on hips or pretends to brush crumbs off table

409911A5BC504BDB925399005807DE2D.description:
Uses different actions for an intended result, e.g., builds tower
with blocks and then knocks it down with his or her hand,
repeats the activity and uses his/her head to make the tower
tumble

A2D7077DEBC04A8C912EF9D5AADBA99A.description:
Attempts different ways to move an object to see what happens,
e.g., rolls a ball gently at first and then hard to see how fast and
far it will move

15731B68375A42E496EFC4C92D91F977.description:
Uses objects as they are intended, e.g., pretends to drink milk
out of a toy bottle

841FE6DEA90E4395A614308E631CB22B.description: Looks for and finds an object that has fallen

751FC1B44A5C4186847740D549C09698.description:
Repeats similar actions on different objects, e.g., shakes stuffed
animal in the same manner as a rattle to hear noise

307BA44EA3B242A898CA9DE796745843.description:
Uses nonverbal and verbal communication to generate
responses from caregiver(s), e.g., coos, reaches, laughs

F9A5B26A501347A58CC6F057543D032C.description:
Children demonstrate the ability to use knowledge, previous experiences, and trial and error to make sense of and
impact their world.

62689705CCD94D8F9F381247F9FAC0DC.description: Plays dress-up and invites caregiver(s) to play along

D65E272E576C443BBC6D81B1601B5602.description:
Uses imaginary play to cope with fears, e.g., puts monster in a
closet

91E53F3438F44981B7A076F83285C8C8.description:
Builds increasingly complex structures and expands upon them,
e.g., uses smaller blocks to build taller towers, lines up materials
and adds other components to create a “road” leading up to the
tower

157B0E750B3743CC8B9C2299EA2B74D7.description:
Identifies and discusses characters that are meaningful to him
and her

C8090B6A749A4F5581FF5A910B0CC2D2.description:
Selects movements that reflect mood, e.g., jumps up and down
when excited

E7B8A810FF1C410FBEC3C7067980E4D0.description:
Creates artwork; focuses and enjoys the process rather than the
final product

04B6CD48508A4DF5876384A4728F7ABC.description:
Enjoys breaking down what he or she has built, e.g., knocking
over a stack of blocks with his or her arm

4329B62723DD4564BD436008B10B0D1E.description:
Builds by using different objects and materials, e.g., lines up
cars, stacks small boxes

AB72E31074D246A899773FEAC4EA53AD.description: Enjoys using instruments while listening to music

C59DACB1F1C945B7B1AEFF422DB0D366.description:
Engages in more intricate pretend play, e.g., uses a toy banana
as a phone

675969A60F354FE29ACAFA5A478E5E93.description: Imitates basic movements during an activity, e.g., places beanbag on head

6ACFBFF9313540678DE0998C59800A0C.description: Engages in art activities such as coloring or finger painting

76E05745126D4BA78C3B1A50F912EE75.description: Participates in music activities by performing some accompanying hand movements

4FFC99DD9C10411DBDCAE962C4B5ACC8.description: Begins to stack large blocks with or without support

108F67F4282F43DB84BDA213A4E67CAE.description:
Begins to use symbolic play while interacting, e.g., holds a play
phone to ear and has a “conversation” with grandma

AE4739203B6348068247EFC2D52E7577.description: Enjoys familiar songs and word rhymes

7CCC4F4E4B2244A2AC9F723FB54531D0.description: Manipulates objects, e.g., turns, shakes, bangs

782CB03D6BCC4A598A4012D05B634129.description: Demonstrates interest in sounds, songs, music, and colors

3AC28E944469462F99C1EEFD39231588.description:
Participates in interactions with caregiver(s), e.g., observes,
smiles, coos

9C705885099B4945AFB493E0FB6A6D23.description: Actively explores sensory objects in the environment

F02A1AB2F4DB4A97864E09C3BEAB0221.description: Children demonstrate the ability to convey ideas and emotions through creative expression.

4E4E4BE45FAD4BEBAF79B5740F2B2930.description:
Takes on different adult roles during play and uses appropriate
mannerisms, e.g., pretends to be the teacher and speaks in a
more adult-like voice, while pretending to read a book to
students

B056606301C7403C9A90C762A6CA0FD4.description:
Projects feelings and words onto stuffed animals, e.g., “The
horse is sad”

860ED46ADF114B9A9C04F60002832D10.description:
Communicates descriptors of people or objects that are not
present, e.g., says “My mommy has blue eyes”

7DE35DFBF2804FD8AE683E7DE5B63E4E.description:
Builds in sequencing while engaged in play, e.g., beginning,
middle, and end

8FE3EF4976F94A3DA3D61B981D861FF3.description: Assigns roles to peers while engaged in imaginary play

924F12ECD62D4D2B815BD40B6873265F.description:
Communicates labels to familiar objects and/or people, e.g.,
says “dog” when seeing four-legged animals

B6391D1AA98E4FD88B7259A0CFDB7E61.description:
Identifies or names his or her drawings, e.g., points to scribble
and says, “mama and dada”

A99317E8B8DD4098B6AD5342CF385602.description:
Engages in pretend play with familiar objects and experiences,
e.g., places baby doll in stroller and pushes the stroller

CD45B52823194618A876F1CEF05D7363.description: Finds objects after they are hidden in close proximity

4693C501BC964AEBA57709609460F95E.description:
Pretends one object is really another by using substitution, e.g.,
a napkin for a baby’s diaper

B9595F90AD9F44E4AC1AC1C8E7173152.description: Recognizes familiar people and/or objects in photographs

9D973EC279E449D9900C839E3DB2C2A0.description:
Engages in simple pretend play, e.g., pretends to drink tea from
a pretend tea cup, pretends to feed baby doll with toy bottle,
uses a toy block as a phone, pretends to talk to mama

EB93BC0037394FA7B0DC287E276CEFBE.description:
Imitates adult’s actions, e.g., bangs a drum with a rattle, after
observing an adult complete the action

32A27F6AD25E49818895933DD1A63FD5.description:
Demonstrates object permanence , e.g., realizes objects and
people still exist, even when they are not physically visible

10189B49D03D46DF8CB3B95708265C21.description: Locates an object that has been partially hidden

D6686882D2AF455DBB504682983115F3.description:
Physically manipulates objects, e.g., twists and turns toys, drops
items

D46C15CB646548E3B519B5593C8475AC.description: Interacts with caregiver(s) and the environment

799CC8BBC066445BA614EA9E8E340A6D.description: Uses senses to explore objects, e.g., observes, mouths, touches

AFD776988217405F995C0765CFB73E29.description: Children demonstrate the understanding of concepts, experiences, and ideas through symbolic representation .

F40E937C4CED46B8B4320A41B26FABA7.description:
Actively uses body to change where he or she is in relation to
objects, e.g., climbs to sit on the couch

50114B93355846649E05150249310695.description:
Completes simple puzzles with less trial and error, e.g., can
match a puzzle piece to its correct slot by identifying the size
and shape by simply looking at it.

20DAAD659D774B5ABADE3825801CB167.description:
Recognizes where his or her body is in relation to objects, e.g.,
squeezing in behind a chair

0731BB0AEBEF4BFEAEE82C62CE57CD43.description: Uses words and gestures to describe size of objects

9095A6D6B6E54FE5A7080948FB7886FF.description: Begins to understand simple prepositions, e.g., under, in, behind

8258DDB1CE76469A92430EF2815F20C8.description:
Recognizes the proper direction of objects, e.g., will turn over an
upside-down cup

16B75E2DBCDA49BD874BBE290A80BF1B.description:
Uses simple trial and error to complete simple puzzles, e.g.,
matches piece, orients and attempts to turn to make a puzzle
piece fit

E417DC23C0D3412A9A27E880448ADCE0.description: Understands words that characterize size, e.g., big, small

356C7192B45D4232A649B947C44C3505.description:
Discriminates between small and large objects, e.g., uses one
hand or two hands in a variety of ways

56E63FFFCD354CA7959836819465D683.description: Drops objects such as toys and watches them move

C259FA39C2FD44EFAB5C3A255B408350.description:
Begins to identify physical obstacles and possible solutions
when moving around, e.g., crawls around a chair instead of
under it

B9B7252D550D44F0877883065614E369.description:
Puts objects in a bucket and then dumps them out; repeats this
action

0101CA85135A43B4A91ACF0745DF9C4C.description:
Focuses attention on an object in motion and follows it, e.g.,
watches a toy roll away after it falls

AE5AC5AC6CBC415ABCBB8A387DC99B5E.description:
Explores through the use of different senses, e.g., begins to
mouth and/or pat objects

B63C4E6A3E00459BB84F59CAA91B8AAD.description:
Observes objects and people in the immediate environment,
e.g., looks at own hands and feet, tracks caregiver with eyes,
turns head toward sounds

7788A5103C5C4C5485E803C971484328.description: Children demonstrate an awareness of how objects and people move and fit in space.

E18BA90626FA4A6B9E30D93A5E94AD89.description:
Translates past knowledge to new experiences, e.g., recalls a
trip to the dentist, and narrates and acts out each step of the
experience on a peer during play

8A1724C9630241F8AB0DEC8736A4859F.description:
Uses play to communicate about previous events or experiences,
including the sequence of events that took place, e.g., a friend’s
birthday party

215A84865FAA4D8E9DB8FF8092F7252E.description:
Carries out routines independently without being reminded what
comes next in the daily routine.

6EF181B309CF40E5BA5DBF44BDABB74C.description: Shares with adult what happened in school that day

06A85D00CAF54E439CB57D49B2018ABB.description: Searches for objects in different places

BDE4112C17444A47B0B6FA9CA95E2B67.description:
Recalls an event in the past, e.g., a special visitor, or a friend’s
birthday party

9E4A57B2EA5B40F0957F2BC00AA84B9E.description:
Remembers several steps in familiar routines and carries out
these routines with little or no prompting

01F9D86AA03F485184E785072D6C2FBF.description:
Anticipates what event comes next in his or her daily routine,
e.g., sits down for a morning snack after a music activity

4315A9CCFBCC48FAAAAF84B2892600E2.description:
Searches for objects in their usual location, e.g., finds their
favorite book on the bookshelf

DD9266F3E1754DE0837EC0F68622FD60.description:
Shows awareness of non-present, familiar adults, e.g., while in
childcare, asks for mom and dad throughout the day

74581F00E9164D369E56884165ABD12D.description:
Finds hidden objects, e.g., lifts a blanket to uncover a toy after
seeing the caregiver hide it

5E13CF1322F645E086587FBC9289E49E.description:
Remembers that objects and people still exist even when they
are no longer physically present, e.g., looks around for parent
when parent leaves the room

1764450925D54ED3AACFB7FAFFEC539A.description: Finds an object that it is partially hidden

2F2A1E0383824D2CA59CA3757C5885AE.description:
Anticipates familiar events, e.g., reaches for bottle and brings to
mouth

DD8BE2E6AA9A4AE681B34608B153BC50.description: Turns toward familiar voices, sounds, and/or objects

60CFE3932737468E83438338DDCF21B6.description: Children demonstrate the ability to acquire, store, recall, and apply past experiences.

E5C6A130BBB04614B8C9910CB0EE4978.description:
Identifies categories, e.g., able to point out all the animals within
a picture even with different types of objects represented

9E52BD192AD443829017D3739CDE2D8F.description:
Purposefully arranges similar objects, e.g., divides plastic blocks
into a red group, a blue group, and a yellow group

C0DD453F3C0143E9B606AEC31C166E7A.description:
Uses symbolic representation during play, e.g., grabs a hair
brush and uses it as a telephone

7AB3B3E189624898ABA7B4B3FBA5EC8A.description:
Begins to arrange objects in a line, e.g., lines up toy cars, one
after the other

3FEAEAF1F9594E1597BC685CCB17B7A0.description:
Identifies characteristics of objects and people when named,
e.g., colors

54E9C265C38041D0959C466AA90339C1.description:
With assistance, groups a few objects by similar characteristics,
e.g., color, shape, or size

22611BAB02434005ACE69715FD07E177.description: Begins to identify characteristics of the object, e.g., “red ball”

6CC6F17A6F0E4172B82C9E68BBD3C4E3.description:
Uses an object to represent another during play, e.g., uses block
as a phone

AB7B67755D5E409CBDA515A10BBB412A.description: Begins to identify and name objects and people

CA68041837504299B4D4993BAC5931CA.description:
Pretends to use objects in their intended manner, e.g., holds a
play phone to ear and engages in a conversation by babbling

75D7939E57EC4E93ACEF943CABD0E721.description:
Focuses attention on objects, people, and sounds for increasing
amounts of time

0E7C6970EE3C4AEA8F4D6A2FE8F6DB3F.description:
Identifies and indicates objects and people in pictures, e.g.,
points

243DD084A361464DBD95DF57741A3024.description:
Uses physical actions while exploring objects, e.g., rolls a ball
back and forth on the floor, purposefully throws object repeatedly onto floor to be picked up

99D68C1156654E279236A486FC07F85E.description:
Develops object permanence, aware that an object still exists
even when it is not physically visible, e.g., pulls the blanket off
the pacifier, cries when caregiver leaves the room

451E9AE16A5249E2BE9805418FF4B074.description: Focuses and begins to distinguish between familiar and unfamiliar objects, sounds, and people

AC03A8B00111466FBB3959B89F830AC3.description:
Attempts to repeat an action, e.g., pats the table and tries to pat
it again

37D070FE50404DE89F509588F07C0E8F.description: Actively explores the environment through the five senses

51CA95696AB24F5A9109351482AF013E.description: Begins to focus on objects, sounds, and people

E97AF85B62204D2295C7A6AC07E599EC.description: Children demonstrate the ability to connect pieces of information in understanding objects, ideas, and relationships.

693E5376CEC34C4BA6347EE8B3345711.description:
Creates an art project and creates a simple story to accompany
the artwork

551CFF326F6643C8B48ECB170AC09787.description:
Expresses inventive ideas to peers while playing; becomes directive, e.g., “You will be the police officer and you have to wear
this.”

26EB7B3A054B4E48B85479AC7EFC4CE5.description:
Takes on familiar roles during play, e.g., cooks in the pretend
kitchen

Demuestran comprensión de los verbos y los
adjetivos de uso más frecuente, al relacionarlos
con sus opuestos (antónimos) (ejemplo: salirentrar; perder-ganar; alto-bajo; grande-pequeño).

EA8992D55CFD4C5189D5D11E8111D52E.description:
Clasifican objetos comunes en categorías
(ejemplo: formas, alimentos) para obtener un
sentido de los conceptos que representan las
categorías.

5DCE51D60A19470A8804DBB0A9E2A257.description:
Con sugerencias y apoyo, exploran las relaciones y
matices en los significados de las palabras.

D5A7AA89980A4231A9F674E68AC9E43C.description:
Usan las inflexiones y los afijos de uso más
frecuente (ejemplo: re- bi-, -ita -ito, -ota –ote)
como clave para el significado de una palabra
desconocida.

EA68C21BF39C4A8E95ADA252BC876B67.description:
Identifican y aplican correctamente nuevos
significados relacionados a palabras ya conocidas
(ejemplo: saber que el zapatero es la persona que
vende o arregla zapatos).

AC11BD7DA0A24B8ABC25BFF62725C30B.description:
Determinan o aclaran el significado de palabras y
frases desconocidas y de palabras de significados
múltiples, en base a la lectura y el contenido
académico de kindergarten.

968040721FBE4F5580D0C2B26A6A1501.description:
Reconocen el acento escrito (acento ortográfico)
en palabras sencillas y ya conocidas (mamá, papá,
José).

E03E6FA20AA946BEB25C9B065976A4E9.description:
Deletrean fonéticamente palabras sencillas,
usando el conocimiento de la relación entre
fonemas y grafemas.

15BC5E92177E4105A2D0A09406B11FC2.description:
Escriben una letra correspondiente para lamayoría
de los sonidos consonánticos y vocálicos.

D38C00C142454F51B0AC7A4EE149C9A9.description: Reconocen y nombran la puntuación final.

68D8F24469904763BA62521934E68D3B.description:
Emplean la mayúscula en la primera letra de una
palabra al inicio de una oración.

36272810C7104ADA8280511F2FE888CD.description:
Demuestran al escribir dominio de las normativas del
español para el uso de las letras mayúsculas, signos
de puntuación y ortografía.

6C519CB1824441F0934EEFB505E90932.description:
Utilizan los artículos determinados eindeterminados
notando la concordancia de género y número con
el sustantivo (ejemplo: el perro, los libros, la mesa,
las sillas, un niño, unos niños, una niña, unas
niñas).

1630597B58EF4DF4ACC34B3ACA474B0F.description:
Producen y elaboran oraciones completas en
actividades compartidas de lenguaje.

A382534FA64A4A2CA4D972B141B21066.description:
Emplean las preposiciones de uso frecuente
(ejemplo: con, en, de, por, para).

616777C8B9F3430D8A031CDCBE96A3D4.description:
Comprenden y utilizan las palabras que denotan
interrogación (ejemplo: quién, qué, dónde,
cuándo, cómo y por qué).

5E8C6804A7AC4D71BE021AABA578AC35.description:
Forman el plural de sustantivos regulares al
añadir /s/ o /es/ (ejemplo: perro, perros; mantel,
manteles; rey, reyes).

5529D97F489A43BD9F080B2BF4D0016D.description:
Usan sustantivos y verbos que se utilizan con
frecuencia incluyendo los verbos ser y estar,
empleando la concordancia correcta.

968FC7F28CF64071A8D3474686707126.description:
Escriben con letra de molde la mayoría de las
letras mayúsculas y minúsculas.

9FD77A41B359478CA0B28A2F605CA7BD.description:
Demuestran dominio de las normativas de la
gramática del español y su uso al escribir y al hablar.

D24D3F3CF3734AEA99B0505CE40B86DC.description:
Hablan en forma audible y expresan sus
pensamientos, sentimientos e ideas con
claridad.

BA7E8A2845D849BEA06035EBC14F9A56.description:
Añaden dibujos y otros medios visuales a las
descripciones según deseen para ofrecer detalles
adicionales.

0340D526A2364BE8A6E76AB69CEAC6D5.description:
Describen a personas, lugares, cosas y
acontecimientos que les son familiares y, con
sugerencias y apoyo, ofrecen detalles adicionales.

9F3D7516E8434BA6AADC95CB07164E3D.description: Presentación de conocimientos y de ideas

775818C0B6FB4AB593F8E47598AFF3F5.description:
Hacen y contestan preguntas con el fin de solicitar
ayuda, obtener información o aclarar algo que no se
entiende.

FD23380F2F074F30AA47934C1A35ECE5.description:
Confirman la comprensión de un texto leído en
voz alta o la información presentada oralmente o a
través de otros medios de comunicación, al hacer y
contestar preguntas sobre detalles clave y solicitar
aclaraciones si algo no se entiende.

064E4C6EF02648DCB1488602E27C4A1A.description:
Continúan una conversación a través de múltiples
intercambios.

583AB2C60A174C63B4BE0E23C36DD73C.description:
Siguen lasreglas acordadas para participar en
conversaciones (por ejemplo: escuchar a los
demás y esperarsu turno para hablarsobre los
temas y textos que se están tratando).

2D5FAB3FCA444D32B0EDFA8CB8AD74F7.description:
Participan en conversaciones colaborativas con
diversos compañeros y adultos en grupos pequeños
y grandes sobre temas y textos apropiados al
kindergarten.

D0F8A099F1D94BD2B4C3073262F9AC1D.description:
ESTÁNDARES DE AUDICIÓN
Y EXPRESIÓN ORAL

B9259D99FF5746AB98A490E04AF50069.description:
Con la orientación y el apoyo de adultos, recuerdan
información de experiencias o recopilan información
de diversas fuentes que se les ofrece para contestar
una pregunta.

C72461AF83FA4A46A4ABA68D1603D80C.description:
Participan en proyectos compartidos de
investigación y escritura (por ejemplo: exploran una
serie de libros de un autor favorito y expresan su
opinión sobre ellos).

5E9C470B8F3045628F5985B255E2AD0C.description:
Investigación para la formación y presentación de
conocimientos

F5D17E7BDBEC4CB0804872DC1824A2D2.description:
Con la orientación y el apoyo de adultos, exploran
una variedad de herramientas digitales para producir
y publicar escritos, incluso en colaboración con sus
compañeros.

F1E8591E5C1A4F52BEC3B558EB6016AE.description:
Con la orientación y el apoyo de adultos, responden
a las preguntas y sugerencias de sus compañeros y
añaden detalles para mejorar la escritura según sea
necesario.

12EC93DB583D4AE9A612BE1EFC171300.description: Producción y redacción de la escritura

985757B66AED4CDFA08B5C7F9792C85A.description:
Usan una combinación de dibujo, dictado y
escritura para narrar un acontecimiento único o
varios acontecimientos vagamente enlazados.
Hablan de dichos acontecimientos en el orden en
que ocurrieron y proporcionan una reacción a lo
sucedido.

876209900B9248AAA5614B8FDD3BDFFE.description:
Usan una combinación de dibujo, dictado y escritura
para redactar textos informativos y explicativos
en los cuales dicen sobre qué están escribiendo y
ofrecen algo de información acerca del tema.

ED89322A337A4C30ADE93D470AE24380.description:
Usan una combinación de dibujo, dictado y escritura
